**Done 2026-10-28 (a recording is joined to its calendar invitation, and the attendees stop being a guess):**

Richard, on a recording that had been transcribed, filed and registered the day before: *"Somehow you didn't pull in the meeting attendee in the calendar invite. Will you make sure that when you correlate a recording to a meeting in the calendar that it adds those people as attendees?"*

── THE MEASUREMENT, BEFORE ANY CODE ───────────────────────────────────────

A Plaude export named `10-23_Ber_Wilson_meeting_w_Brent_Bennett.mp3`, read out of the Drive intake folder. Its `meetings` row, on the live database:

| | |
|---|---|
| attendees recorded | **5** — Richard White, Damon, Reef Capital, Casey Evans, Brent |
| attendees the model originally extracted | **12** — including J.P. Morgan, New York Life, Maverick, Exos, Taurus, Tenzer, Fly & Jay |
| people actually in the room | **2** |
| `party_id` on the "Richard White" slot | `c46979df…` — which is **Ber Wilson, `is_organization = true`**. Our own company, wearing a person's name |
| meeting date | **2026-10-27**. The conversation was on the **23rd** |

And sitting on both executives' calendars, four days earlier, an API call away: **`Ber Wilson meeting w Brent Bennett`, 2026-10-23 12:30, attendees `moose@berwilson.com`, `brent@getbennett.com`, `tuaone@berwilson.com`** — all three accepted, all three with addresses.

⚠ **ONLY ONE OF FIVE RECORDING DOORS HAD EVER LOOKED AT THE CALENDAR, AND EVEN IT DID NOT WRITE WHAT IT FOUND.** The Meet importer matched an event and handed the invitees to the model as `seedAttendees`. A seed is a hint: it survives onto the row only if the recap repeats it. The other four doors — Drive audio, voice memos, an iPhone call note, an uploaded mp3 — each carried a comment saying, in almost the same words, that nobody could be known structurally. Three of those comments were written on different days by different passes, which is §12's hardest fork to see. For any recording made during a meeting that was on the calendar, all four were simply wrong.

⚠ **AND THE DATE DRIFTED FOR A REASON THAT WAS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR.** `recordedAtFromName` requires `20\d{2}`, so `10-23_…` has no year and the parser rightly refused it rather than reading two digits as a date — exactly what its docblock argues for. Drive's `modifiedTime` then stood in, which is the day somebody dragged the file in. No parser fix would have helped; the invitation is the only hard date in the chain.

── WHAT WAS BUILT: `src/lib/meetings/calendar-match.ts`, ONE JOIN FOR FIVE DOORS ──

**Two joins, both facts, neither a similarity score.**

- **title** — exact once normalized, or containment either way, and containment only where the shorter string carries **three significant words**. Measured first: of **203 events** on the two executive calendars in 2026, **43 carry three tokens or fewer and 33 of those are one recurring personal event** ("KAVA Talks"); "Vultr Pregame", "Partnership Discussion" and "Meeting w/ Hannah" are the same shape. A two-word subject inside a long filename is a coincidence. The stopword list is deliberately tiny and holds no place names (§12) — `Meeting w/ Hannah` reduces to one significant word and is refused.
- **clock** — a recording that starts inside an event's own span IS that meeting. This is the join for **voice memos**, the source with the worst titles and the best times: every memo on the phone is still named with an ISO timestamp, so the title join can never fire there, and `createdAt` is the recorder's own.

⚠ **A SYMMETRIC CLOCK SLACK BROKE ON THE FIRST REAL CALENDAR IT MET.** 23 October holds `Prep for Ber Wilson meeting w Brent Bennett`, 12:15–12:30, ending exactly as the meeting starts. With ±20 minutes of slack a 12:35 recording was "contained" by both, the ambiguity rule refused the pair, and the clock join returned nothing for the very meeting it was written for. Back-to-back blocks are the normal shape of a worked calendar. Two fixes, each independently right: the span is **half-open `[start, end)`** with slack only *before* the start (a recording STARTS once, so the only honest allowance is for pressing record early), and the clock join **skips an event with no invitee but its organizer** — prep blocks, focus time, travel, lunch. A solo block has no room to report, so letting it compete could only ever cost a real match.

⚠ **A CLOCK-ONLY MATCH MUST AGREE WITH WHAT THE CALLER ALREADY KNOWS.** Conclusive for a voice memo of a meeting; merely plausible for a phone call, which is most often taken *during* blocked time. So where a source hands in somebody it is sure of — iOS's `Call with <name>` — the invitation must contain them, or the overlap is logged as a coincidence and discarded. A title match needs no such corroboration; it is already a second signal.

**The invitees are ASSERTED, not suggested.** New `assertedAttendees` on `MeetingRecordInput`, unioned at the one choke point every door already goes through (`unionAssertedAttendees` in `record.ts`) — **on the address first and the name second**, because an email is the one key on a meeting row that cannot be two people (§12) while a name off a transcript is "Eric" or "Ber Wilson Executive". Where a slot already exists the invitation wins on `party_id`, `email`, `team_member_id` and name, and the model keeps `role` — *"GC principal"* is real information the calendar does not carry. That rule is exactly what corrects the Ber Wilson-the-company id off Richard's slot.

`MeetingAttendee` gained **`email`** (jsonb, no migration), and `tsc` named all four literal sites that had to learn it — which is the point of a required field.

── THE SIZE BOUND, AND WHY IT IS A BOUND AND NOT A CLASSIFIER ─────────────

The first dry run put **14 strangers** on a voice memo recorded during KAVA Talks, and an Apple iMIP proxy address on another. Invitee counts across the 203 events:

`0:96  1:2  2:13  3:18  4:22  5:6  6:1  7:2  11:2  12:4  14:28  17:1  34:1  76:6  78:1`

⚠ **THERE IS NO CLEAN GAP.** Twelve is `Ber Wilson/TensorIQ/Elite Solutions`, the prefab factory tour and both Vultr calls — real meetings whose attendee lists are worth having. Fourteen is twenty-eight occurrences of one community event. §12 warns that two identically shaped things fall either side of any number you pick, and 12 against 14 is precisely that. So the rule is deliberately **not** "refuse the event": above `SMALL_MEETING_INVITEES` the invitees who **already resolve to a contact or a colleague** are still asserted and only the strangers are dropped. A big deal call keeps its people; a webinar adds nobody to the directory queue. KAVA Talks went from 14 asserted to 2.

⚠ **AN OPAQUE ADDRESS DROPS THE ADDRESS, NOT THE PERSON.** Three `…@imip.me.com` addresses are live on this calendar and **one of them is the organizer of a real meeting, who is our own Eric** — so filtering the invitee out lost a colleague from a meeting he called. Instead the address is discarded (asserting it as an email would be worse than having none, because everything downstream trusts an address exactly) and the display name is resolved against the directory under the same exact-name-plus-uniqueness rule `linkAttendees` uses. Eric now links. And one person gets one row whether they are on the invitation twice or not at all — keyed on the contact where there is one and the name where there is not, or `syncAttendeeActivity` logs the meeting on their profile twice.

── THE SECOND HALF OF "MAKE IT MORE ACCURATE": THE PROMPT ─────────────────

⚠ **THE TWELVE-ATTENDEE LIST WAS THE PROMPT DOING WHAT IT WAS TOLD.** `meeting-intake` asked for *"every distinguishable person (and organization) present **or referenced**"*. That one phrase makes the field a mix of the room and the market — and the field feeds `meetings.attendees`, every attendee's profile feed, and the `/contacts` → From calls queue, all three of which ask "who did we speak to" and none of which asks "who came up". Split at **prompt 1.3**: `attendees` is now the people actually in the conversation, with companies pushed into each person's `company`; a new `mentioned` list carries everybody talked *about*.

⚠ **AND FIXING THE PRODUCER DID NOT FIX THE CONSUMER** (§12). `counterpartyName` in `from-recording.ts` — the gate on §11's 10-19 amendment, the one that decides whether a recording may create a deal — hunts the first organization in `attendees`. After 1.3 those live in `mentioned`. It now reads both, because every session staged before today has them in the old place and every session after has them in the new one.

── THE BACKFILL, AND WHAT PROVING IT IDEMPOTENT FOUND ─────────────────────

Every door is idempotent on `drive_file_id`, so the **eleven** recordings already registered would never be read again — the fix would have applied only to the twelfth. `scripts/backfill-meeting-calendar-attendees.mts` matches each against the calendar and unions through the *same* function the live path uses. It adds and corrects; it never deletes, because a human confirmed some of these lists and somebody can be in a room uninvited.

The clock came free: a voice memo's `source_title` **is** its ISO instant, because the phone names every memo that way. A Drive export's name gives one where the exporter wrote it. A Notes call keeps neither, so it may only join on its title — and `Call with Eric Tuaone` matches nothing, correctly.

**4 of 11 matched. The target recording: date 10-27 → 10-23, Richard's slot re-pointed from the company to the man, Brent carrying his address, Eric added.** The three remaining names on it — Damon, Reef Capital, Casey Evans — are prompt-1.2 artifacts a human confirmed, left in place and reported.

⚠ **AND THE SECOND RUN REPORTED 1 CHANGED, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON A REAL BUG WAS FOUND.** A live invitee on this calendar is named **`"Huge "`** with a trailing space. `parseAttendees` trims on the way out of jsonb, so the untrimmed asserted name could never equal what had just been stored, and the pass rewrote that row on every run — forever, quietly. §12 asks for exactly this test and this is what it caught. Trimmed at the source; second run now reports **0 changed**.

**Verified end to end against the live calendar and directory**, not only in tests: the title join resolves the real file name to the real event and all three invitees to real contacts; the clock join resolves a timestamp-named memo to the same event past the prep block; a recording named `New Recording 7` matches nothing. 771 tests pass (+41), lint holds at the frozen 23, build green. **DEPLOYED**

**Done 2026-10-27 (the UI audit, the remainder — and two items whose deliverable was NOT building them):**

── /investors: THE PAGE READ AS BROKEN BECAUSE IT WAS EMPTY ────────────────

⚠ **IT HAD ITS OWN `Stat` COMPONENT, WHICH IS WHY NOTHING DONE TO `StatTile` EVER REACHED IT.** A local copy with its own card shell, its own label style, an 18px figure where the shared tile uses 30, and a coloured dot on three of its four tiles. So when `StatTile` learned earlier the same day that a genuine zero should render muted, this page carried on showing **three tiles reading "$0" at full ink weight** — giving "nothing has happened yet" the same emphasis as "$12B". That is §5.3's whole point: the same unit on four pages, four slightly different ways. ⚠ The dots went with it and nothing was lost: the tranche bar carries that legend explicitly a few lines above, and three of four tiles coloured is the failure `StatTile`'s own comment names — when every tile is coloured, colour has stopped signifying.

⚠ **AN UNTOUCHED TRANCHE IS NOW DRAWN AS A SHAPE WAITING TO BE FILLED.** With nothing committed — every tranche of every raise today — all four segments rendered as identical flat `bg-muted` bars, and the audit read the control as broken rather than as empty: *"a dark track with no visible fill"*. A dashed outline says the structure is real and the money has not arrived; a solid track says the widget did not load. Same information; the difference is whether a reader trusts the page.

And *"No commitments yet"* stopped repeating on all seven investor cards, each with its own divider above it. That made the most repeated element on the page a sentence saying nothing had happened — which the page's own KPI tiles already report in full and the stage chip on each card says more precisely.

── /dashboard ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**The rail is sticky and capped.** It began ~460px down the page — a void beside the KPI tiles and the pipeline chart — and then ran roughly 1,500px PAST the bottom of the main column, so the two halves of the morning read shared almost no vertical space. Verified by scrolling `<main>` 1,200px and watching the rail travel 944 and then stop at 88, with its own `overflow-y` capping it at 751px so it no longer sets the page's length. ⚠ `lg:` only — on a phone the rail is the next section down, and a sticky element in a single column pins over the content it belongs under.

**The objectives grid picks a column count that leaves no orphan.** At a fixed `xl:grid-cols-3`, four objectives render 3 + 1 — a lone card on its own row under a full one, which reads as a layout accident. The rule: of the two candidate widths, take the one whose last row is FULLEST (4 → 2 columns, 5 → 3, 6 → 3), preferring 3 on a tie. ⚠ Two LITERAL class strings, never `grid-cols-${n}`.

**The Intelligence Brief shows its first line when collapsed.** It was a title, a refresh icon and a chevron — the most expensive thing the platform produces, presenting as a disclosure widget, with the reader having to open it to learn whether it was worth opening. ⚠ Markdown furniture is skipped when picking that line: the brief opens with its own `# Heading`, and a preview reading "# Portfolio brief" tells a reader nothing the panel's title did not.

── /jobs, /intake, /attention ──────────────────────────────────────────────

/jobs was `max-w-3xl` left-aligned in a 1,451px frame with the composer and the run list stacked; two columns now. ⚠ **Its three example prompts were ALREADY clickable and never looked it** — no border, no resting affordance — and they are the page's entire onboarding. Cards now, on `bg-muted/40` NOT `bg-card`, because the composer is itself a Panel on `bg-card` and a card-coloured child would have shown nothing but its border; the card-shell ratchet failed the build at 227 and was right to.

/intake went `max-w-3xl` → `max-w-5xl`: five of its six tabs are queues and staged lists, and the proposal tab had already opted out to `max-w-6xl` while the rest were never revisited.

── §5.2: ONE OWNER FOR THREE IDENTICAL FILTER ROWS ─────────────────────────

`ProjectFilters`, `InvestorFilters` and `OpportunityFilters` were three copies of one component — same shell, same `setParam` over `URLSearchParams`, same `w-auto` select, same clear affordance — differing only in which facets they listed, and `OpportunityFilters` hand-rolled its select class so its controls were a different height from the identical row two pages over. 301 lines became `UrlFacets` plus three facet lists.

⚠ **THE AUDIT ASKED FOR ONE BAR ACROSS SIX PAGES AND THAT WOULD HAVE MADE TWO OF THEM WORSE.** /contacts and /leads filter with multi-select chips carrying counts, which is strictly better for those pages than a row of selects. The convergence that was real is the three that were already the same thing written three times.

── THE SELECT CHEVRON: 140 CONTROLS, UNDER A COMMENT PROVING IT COULD NOT HAPPEN ──

⚠ **IN TAILWIND v4, LAYER ORDER BEATS SPECIFICITY.** `globals.css` drew a themed chevron on every collapsed `<select>` and reserved `padding-right: 1.875rem` for it inside `@layer base`, beside a long ⚠ note arguing the rule was safe because `select:not([multiple]):not([size])` is (0,2,1) and beats a `.px-3` utility at (0,1,0). **The arithmetic is right and the conclusion is wrong**: Tailwind v4 emits utilities into a real `@layer utilities` declared after `base`, and the cascade resolves LAYER before it looks at specificity at all. Measured on /projects: every filter select computed **`padding-right: 10px`**, not 30, with the chevron sitting on the last letter of "All Statuses" and "All Stages". App-wide, for months. The rule is UNLAYERED now — the one mechanism that actually wins — and the computed value is 30px. ⚠ The general lesson is about WHICH ARGUMENT a load-bearing comment makes: a specificity calculation written before the codebase had cascade layers stays arithmetically correct and stops being true, so it reads as verified long after it is.

── TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT ───────────────────────────────────────

⚠ **§5.4's SAVED VIEWS.** The audit calls them "the Attio-defining feature" and notes the data model supports them. It does. But `ProjectFilters` carries a long note on the `localStorage` filter replay that was REMOVED from this page: it made a bare `/projects` render DIFFERENTLY for each executive **with no way for the sender of a link to tell**, and re-rendered the list under the reader after hydration. A named view in per-reader storage reintroduces exactly that property, and the remedy already recorded in that comment — *bookmark the filtered URL* — is SHAREABLE, which a saved view would not be. Not building it is the deliverable, and the reason is recorded in `OPEN-ITEMS.md` rather than left as a silent gap.

⚠ **§5.3's DELTA LINE.** *"↑ 4.2% vs last month"* needs a comparison the platform does not store — there are no historical portfolio snapshots. The audit's own instruction is to omit the line rather than ship a placeholder, so this is a schema question before it is a UI one: a `portfolio_snapshots` table taking one row a week would make it half a day of interface.

── THE DENSITY TOGGLE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Phase 4 landed two row heights one step short of what the audit asked for, and said so rather than quietly missing them. This is the resolution, and it is not a compromise: **both targets are reachable, as a CHOICE rather than as a decision taken on the reader's behalf.**

| surface | comfortable | compact | above the fold |
|---|---|---|---|
| /decide | 82px | **54px** (audit asked 64) | 9.9 → 15.1, +53% |
| /contacts | 56px | **48px** (the audit's number exactly) | 14.6 → 17.0 |

The argument each way, stated once: /decide's third line is the MODEL'S REASONING, and it is what makes the banner above the list — *"138 of 140 can be accepted without opening them"* — a defensible offer rather than a leap. Hiding it by default trades the queue's safety for nine rows without asking. Hiding it on request is a reader who has decided they already trust it. /contacts at 48px crushes a 20px name over an 18px subtitle; at 56px it does not. Neither of those is a layout problem — they are preferences, and preferences belong to the person reading.

`compact:` is to row height what `dark:` is to colour: one `@custom-variant` reading one attribute on `<html>`, set by the same pre-paint script that sets the theme. ⚠ **It is set there and not in an effect for the same reason the theme is** — reading it after mount renders the page once at the default and again correctly, which on a 397-row list is a visible jump. ⚠ **And `:where()` keeps specificity at zero**, matching `dark:`: without it every compact rule would outrank the base utility it is meant to sit beside, and a one-off override on a single row would stop working.

⚠ **FOUR FILES NAME THE STORAGE KEY AND NONE OF THEM IMPORTS FROM THE OTHERS** — the toggle writes it, the pre-paint script is a string inside a `<script>` tag, and both screenshot harnesses seed it because Chrome runs on a fresh profile every time. That drifted within the hour of being written: `shoot.mjs` gained `BW_SHOOT_DENSITY` and `measure.mjs` did not, so a "compact" contrast sweep came back with the COMFORTABLE numbers — **591 text nodes on /decide in both runs, when compact hides a line per row and cannot produce the same count.** A flag that changes nothing reads exactly like a page that is already fine; the tell was the two runs agreeing to the node, which is the same shape as §12's "a probe that is broken and a page that is broken produce the same number". `conventions.test.ts` now holds all four files to the same key for both `theme` and `density`, and asserts the variant exists at all — proved by deleting it, since every `compact:` class in the tree is inert without it.

── /company: THE WEAKEST PAGE, AND IT WAS NEVER A STYLING PROBLEM ──────────

The audit: *"The ABOUT field dumps raw text including ──────── ASCII rules, three presidential quotes, and a pitch deck. It is rendering unparsed… the single most unfinished-looking thing in the app."*

Measured: `company_profile.about` holds **14,579 characters over 156 lines** — eighty-underscore horizontal rules, three presidential quotes each with an attribution on the line below, bulleted figure lists (*"• $39.5 billion planned in the Utah and Nevada corridor"*), and eight section headings (*The Platform*, *The Numbers*, *Where We Build*). All of it rendered as ONE `<p className="text-sm leading-relaxed whitespace-pre-line">`.

**The structure was in the text the whole time and nothing read it.** `src/lib/utils/prose.ts` parses it into `rule | heading | quote | list | paragraph`; `ProseBlocks` renders them. Pure and tested, with every fixture a real line from the field.

⚠ **TWO OF THE RULES EXIST ONLY BECAUSE OF LINES THAT MUST NOT MATCH.** A heading is ≤5 words, ≤50 chars, with no `|`, no `:` and no terminal stop — without all four tests, *"Ericson Tua'one | Founder and CEO | South Jordan, Utah"*, *"Document Control: BW-BRG-2026-012"* and *"Three presidents. One mission. Ber Wilson is building it."* all become titles. An attribution attaches only to a quote that is directly above it and not yet attributed — without that, any em-dash sentence in the body becomes somebody's byline. A heading also may not open with a dash, which is what a SECOND attribution under an already-attributed quote otherwise becomes.

⚠ **AND THE FIRST VERSION JOINED WRAPPED LINES, WHICH THIS CORPUS DOES NOT HAVE.** Its paragraphs are single lines of up to 190 characters, and a heading is followed IMMEDIATELY by its paragraph with no blank line between — so joining merged every section's two paragraphs into one. The test that caught it was a fixture I had written myself rather than taken from the corpus, which is §12's own trap experienced from the inside: *a fixture that builds the field directly cannot catch a producer that never fills it.* One line is now one paragraph, and the test says why.

Also on that page: **the empty 80px photo dropzone was the first thing on the company's own profile**, above its legal name, its address and everything a reader comes for — the most prominent element on the screen was an invitation to fill in something nobody asked for. It now sits below the record it illustrates (still rendered: a surface hidden because it is empty is hidden exactly when someone needs to fill it). The page took `PageHeader` and widened from `max-w-3xl`.

**Done 2026-10-27 (the UI upgrade spec, Phases 1–3 — and the instrument that found what a screenshot passes):**

Richard handed over a written UI audit of the live build — "raise the surface quality to Attio / Domo / Linear tier without diluting the product's density or its voice" — phased, with acceptance criteria, and one standing instruction: *"If an item conflicts with something you find in the codebase that I could not see from the browser, follow the codebase and note the deviation."* That instruction earned its keep eight times.

── PHASE 1: THE BUGS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

⚠ **ONE MISPLACED CHARACTER MADE 138 BUTTONS INVISIBLE, IN BOTH THEMES, THROUGH A GREEN SUITE.** `/decide` wrote `bg-primary elev-1/10 text-primary`. The `/10` belonged to `bg-primary` and landed one token to the right, on `elev-1`. Tailwind generates no `elev-1/10`, so the modifier evaporated — and the fill it was meant to soften stayed at FULL accent under ink of the same token. Rust on rust, zero contrast, on the Accept button of every row in a 136-row queue. Typecheck green, build green, 730 tests green, both classes plainly visible in the source.

Measured with a new probe: **138 of 611 text-bearing elements on /decide computed an ink within 24/765 of the fill behind them. After the fix: 0.** Then swept 19 further routes in both themes — 0 across ~7,000 nodes.

Fixed by naming the variant the string was spelling: `soft` on `<Button>`, the accent twin of the existing `destructive`. Two assertions hold both halves of it, each proved by planting the original bug back: an opacity modifier only ever rides a COLOUR utility, and no token is both the fill and the ink. ⚠ The first version of the opacity check returned **1,243 hits, every one an import path** — narrowed from "contains a slash" to the SHAPE of a modifier (one slash, at the end, a number after it).

⚠ **§3.2 DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THE REAL BUG WAS BIGGER.** The audit reported the sidebar's System parent navigating to a 404. No `/system` href exists anywhere: the parent is already a `<button>`, and `nav.test.ts` already proves every destination is a real route. What WAS real was the other half. `pageTitle` never read `alsoMatches` though `navItemActive` always had — the same path, two modules, two answers — and its fallback was `'Ber Wilson'`, which is a real destination's own label. **Nine routes therefore named the company profile while you stood somewhere else:** /review, /documents/unfiled, /proposals/intake, /settings/contact-roles and the four governance registers, plus every 404. All nine now name themselves, the fallback is `'Not found'`, and a test walks `src/app` to prove no chromed route reaches it.

**§3.3**: /tasks already had a faithful skeleton (a session after the audit snapshot added it). /commitments had a title, a bar and ten blocks standing in for a header, a two-line description, five count chips, two toggle groups, a sort, a search field and two headed card sections. Rebuilt from the ledger's own measurements, and its `Section` took `<Panel>` so the two cannot drift. ⚠ `animate-pulse` is already 2s in Tailwind v4 — the audit's "set it to a slow 2s, not the default" was already true.

── THE INSTRUMENT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`scripts/ui/measure.mjs` + `probes.mjs`, the companion to `shoot.mjs`: same CDP plumbing, same theme assertion, for the questions a screenshot passes. Probes: `contrast`, `type`, `touch`, `landmarks`, `numerals`, `focus`.

**Building them found five ways to measure nothing**, and every one was caught by the EXAMINED count rather than the hit count — which is the entire reason each probe reports what it looked at:

1. The palette computes to `oklab()`, so a regex pulling numbers out of the computed colour read an OKLab LIGHTNESS as a red channel: 25 false hits on perfectly legible muted text. Colours are now resolved by painting them on a 1×1 canvas.
2. Climbing the DOM for "the first opaque background" found the 1px `bg-critical` *today* rule on /timeline as the fill for its own label — a label sitting 4px to the RIGHT of it. The ancestor must CONTAIN the text's box.
3. `\d` inside a template literal is not an escape JavaScript recognises; it collapses to a bare `d`. `/\d/` reached the page as `/d/` and matched the LETTER d, so "Today", "On Hold" and "West Wendover" came back as figures. (A backtick in a probe's own comment is the same trap with teeth — it stops the file parsing.)
4. A CSS walk that recursed on `if (rule.cssRules)` skipped every style rule in the document, because Chrome's nested-CSS support gives each `CSSStyleRule` a (usually empty) rules list. It found **0 focus selectors on a page with 54**, and therefore reported all 436 controls as unstyled.
5. `document.elementFromPoint` only answers for coordinates inside the VIEWPORT. Hit-testing 448 controls returned null for everything below the fold, which the test read as "does not reach" — reporting the same 279 failures whether the bug was fixed or not. **A probe that is broken and a page that is broken produce the same number.**

── PHASE 2: FOUNDATIONS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**§4.1 — the type scale.** The audit's premise held exactly: on /decide **581 of 611 text nodes (95%) render at 13px/400 or 14.5px/500 and exactly ONE is larger**; /commitments 1,384 of 1,472; /contacts 1,572 of 1,736. Hierarchy was being carried entirely by colour, and colour was doing six jobs. Four ROLE tokens join the ladder — caption 12, title 18, display 28, metric 30 — each carrying its own weight, tracking and line-height, so a caller writes `text-display` instead of re-deciding three properties per page. `PageHeader`'s h1 took it, **overriding this file's own argument from the day before** for 20px; that argument was made without measuring the page underneath it, where a 20px title over 14.5px body is a 1.38× step.

⚠ **DEVIATION: `--text-sm` STAYS AT 14.5px** against "the 14.5px value is an artifact — normalise to 14px". `globals.css` records the bump as a deliberate readability call for a tool read all day, and the audit's own goal is HIERARCHY: body and secondary are 1.5px apart today and 14px makes that 1px. The gap that was missing was above these two, not between them.

⚠ **AND THE ROLES VANISHED THE HOUR THEY SHIPPED.** `text-*` is ambiguous — `text-sm` is a size, `text-foreground` is a colour — and tailwind-merge separates them with a BUILT-IN list of size names. Every new role landed in the colour group, so `cn('tnum mt-1 text-metric', 'text-foreground')` deleted the size and the dashboard's four KPI figures rendered at the inherited **16px instead of 30**. Fixed with `extendTailwindMerge`; `TYPE_ROLES` and `globals.css` are now held to each other by an assertion, because the failure mode is invisible in every other check.

**§4.2 — the accent, six jobs down to one.** The tone system already separated status from category; only the RENDERING didn't, so a sector chip and a "needs attention" chip were the same object in different hues. Category tones are now OUTLINE and status stays FILLED — one word in one file, reaching every sector, lane and role chip. ⚠ And **four of seven sectors were wearing STATUS tones** (`government: info`, `infrastructure: caution`, `real_estate: positive`, `institutional: neutral`): that is what the audit saw as "Gov't and Tech are both blue" — two blues from two different vocabularies, arriving beside each other by accident. Seven sectors, seven category tones, one each. The sidebar's selected row gave up `text-primary` for `foreground` plus a 2px accent rail; steel's next-step control gave it up for a state that is not a status at all.

⚠ **THE PIPELINE BARS COULD NOT TAKE `--chart-1..5` AS ASKED.** Seven stages, five hues — the ramp would CYCLE, and a cycled categorical hue is indistinguishable from the slot it repeats. Stages are also ORDERED: swapping Bid and Closeout changes the meaning, which is the test for ordinal rather than nominal, so they take one hue in monotone lightness steps. Declared as `--ordinal-1..7` and validated against the four ordinal checks in BOTH themes — monotone, every adjacent gap ≥ 0.06 ΔL, light end 2.10:1 / 2.30:1 on the `--muted` track it is drawn on, hue spread ≤ 3°.

⚠ **It was sage (hue 150) for about ten minutes and that was a STATUS COLLISION** — `--positive` is hue 152, so a desaturated green bar beside a `positive` chip would have read as "this stage is GOOD". Moved to 190, and the chroma came down from 0.075 to 0.05 with it, because teal below L 0.37 leaves sRGB at that chroma and the bottom two steps **clipped to nearly the same colour** — silently destroying the monotonicity the whole ramp exists for, in the arm nobody checks second. ⚠ And the five `--chart-*` tokens were read by **ZERO classes in src/**: a declared palette with no consumer.

**§4.3 / §4.4 — already done, measured not assumed.** Dark elevation was already real shadows (0.30 alpha at elev-1, done 10-26), `--font-mono` is already exposed, and tabular numerals already covered **1,434 of 1,450 figures across four pages** — not "all currently proportional and visibly ragged". The five real misses were the commitment ledger's count chips.

**§4.5 — focus.** Measured: **298 of 436 controls on /decide, 31 of 41 on /projects, 54 of 95 on /tasks had no focus style of their own.** The idiom was never the problem — 396 `focus-visible:` call sites honour it — the ~70% of controls nobody had got to was. One enumerated `:where(…):focus-visible` floor in `@layer base` takes all three to 0 in both themes, at specificity zero so every utility still wins. ⚠ Written first as a BARE `:focus-visible`, which never reached the compiled bundle at all: present in the file, absent from the CSS, no error anywhere.

**§4.6 — the 44px tap target.** ⚠ **SEVENTEEN CALL SITES EACH COMPUTED THEIR OWN OVERLAY INSET FROM THE CONTROL'S SIZE, IN THEIR HEAD.** The idiom is right — grow a small control's hit area with an absolutely positioned overlay rather than padding, because padding shifts the row under the next tap — but it is only correct if both numbers are. /decide's checkbox carried a comment reading *"44px hit area via an overlay"* above `size-3.5` with `-inset-3`: 14px plus 12px either side is **38px**. A comment claiming a control that is not there is worse than no comment. One `tap-target` utility, `max(100%, 2.75rem)`, derives nothing and is correct at all seventeen and at the next one. Measured at phone width, controls below the floor went **279 → 133 on /decide, 33 → 2 on /tasks, 707 → 10 on /commitments**.

**§4.7 — absence.** Only **3 render sites, not 19** — the 19 are rows from one code path, and all three carry a ⚠ comment citing §12 against the em dash. The table column takes the dash anyway, muted: the CLIENT column beside it already rendered absence that way, and two adjacent columns answering the same question differently is the worse failure. The cards keep the words, because a card has no column to be read down and no neighbour to agree with.

── PHASE 3: SHARED COMPONENTS ──────────────────────────────────────────────

**§5.1 — the page header.** Measured: **46 `page.tsx` files render their own `<h1>` in 14 distinct spellings** — `text-lg font-semibold` ×19, `text-xl font-semibold` ×9, three different `text-2xl`s, one `tracking-widest uppercase` — against 3 files using `PageHeader`. ⚠ And **/opportunities and /investors had no masthead at all**: both opened on a filter row, with nothing naming the page but the 14.5px locator in the app chrome.

Seven surfaces converted — /decide, /attention, /leads, /commitments, /opportunities, /investors, /objectives — each with `text-display`, the description capped at `max-w-2xl`, and at most one filled action. The cap is the fix for the audit's "/decide and /leads run their intro paragraph the full 1,451px": that is ~190 characters a line, about three times the width prose stays readable at, on the two pages whose writing is doing the most work. `PageHeader` gained an `icon` SLOT (not a free `ReactNode`, so a page cannot put a 40px glyph on the masthead), because the chip was the part each page re-invented.

/decide's held-back count became an `info-surface` callout. It had rendered as plain muted prose directly under the page description — same size, same colour, full width — so the one actionable FACT on the page outside the queue read as more preamble.

**§5.5 — the boards.** ⚠ DEVIATION: /opportunities ALREADY collapsed its empty columns. What neither board did was keep the label readable: at 96px with `truncate` the four empty stages read **"Due Dilig…"** and **"Evaluat…"** — a column whose only remaining content is a cut-off word, which is worse than the wide empty column it replaced. Both boards now TURN the label, `writing-mode: vertical-rl` in a 3rem rail. /steel went from five of six columns empty at a fixed 15rem — **1,200 of its 1,451px spent on the absence of deals** — to two populated columns and five legible rails; all nine of /opportunities' stages now fit in frame, where four used to be off the right edge.

⚠ **TOP-ALIGNED, THOUGH CENTRED LOOKED RIGHT IN THE CODE.** A column is as tall as the fullest one — measured 944px against an 863px viewport — so a centred label sits below the fold and the rail reads as an empty box with nothing in it. The span was centred to the pixel inside a 930px wrapper and invisible anyway. ⚠ And the WRAPPER stays horizontal while only the span turns: `items-center` centres along the INLINE axis, so putting `writing-mode` on the element that does the centring flips the axis it centres on.

/opportunities' column header stopped printing "Not set" over "none of 4 priced". One deal in thirty carries an `estimated_value`, so that pair was the most repeated element on the board — two lines of chrome per column, saying nothing twice.

── THE TAIL ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

⚠ **THE PROJECTS TABLE HEADER CARRIED EVERY STICKY CLASS AND STUCK TO NOTHING.** `sticky top-0 z-10 bg-muted/60 backdrop-blur-sm`, present and inert. Two separate scroll containers were swallowing it, both invisible: `overflow-x-auto` on the table's wrapper (CSS cannot scroll one axis and leave the other visible — `overflow-x: auto` computes `overflow-y` to `auto`, and a sticky child resolves against its nearest scroll container), and `overflow-hidden` on the `<Panel>` around it, which counts the same way. Measured: the wrapper's scrollHeight === clientHeight === 917, while the real scroller — `<main class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto">` — ran 1,182 over 815 and carried the rows straight past the header. Now `max-lg:overflow-x-auto` (sideways scroll only where the table is genuinely wider than the viewport) and `isolate` on the Panel. Verified by scrolling `<main>` 367px and watching the header move 216.

A zero metric now renders muted at the metric's size (§4.7): three of four tiles on /investors read "$0" at full ink weight, which gives "nothing has happened yet" the same emphasis as "$12B". ⚠ `.skeleton-shimmer` was REMOVED after counting its users: **0**. It declared a two-theme gradient animation that nothing referenced, and pinned four oklch values literally rather than reading the palette — so a re-skin would have left it behind in the old neutrals. ⚠ And `eslint` never ignored `.next-verify`: `.gitignore` names it, `eslint.config.mjs` did not, so CLAUDE.md's own compile-without-shipping recipe makes the next lint run report **27,909 problems against a frozen baseline of 23**.

── WHAT THE DEVIATIONS ADD UP TO ───────────────────────────────────────────

Eight items in the audit were already done, already different, or could not be executed as written: the /system 404 (no such href), /tasks' skeleton, `animate-pulse`'s duration, dark elevation, `--font-mono`, tabular numerals, /opportunities' column collapse, /investors' secondary action — and the chart ramp, which seven stages and an ordered dimension make a different problem from the one the audit saw. Against that, the audit's three biggest claims — the invisible buttons, the flat type scale and the focus gap — were all true and all understated.

**Verification:** 737 tests pass; lint 23, unchanged, none in the touched files; contrast swept across six routes in both themes, **0 invisible elements in 5,657 text-bearing nodes**. Five new assertions, each proved by planting its violation back. Deployed in three parts, each built, kickstarted and asserted with `tailnet-setup.sh` + `lmstudio-check.sh`.

**Not done, and recorded in `docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md`:** §5.2 (one shared filter bar for the six pages that each render their own), §5.3 (the KPI tile's delta line and converging /steel and /investors onto `StatTile`, which only `HealthPanel` uses today), §5.4 (column resize / reorder / visibility, saved views, a multi-select bulk bar), all of Phase 4's page-by-page list and Phase 5's polish. Each is a build rather than a convergence, which is why they are a separate decision rather than a silent omission.

**Done 2026-10-27 (the third attempt: dark mode back, 274 buttons, and the layout he was actually asking about):**

Richard: *"I still want Dark Mode. I am not seeing different button shapes, layouts, etc that make this look more modern and polished. Legit can't see what you did other than put it in light mode by default."*

Both halves fair, and the second one is the important one.

⚠ **REMOVING DARK MODE WAS AN OVER-READING.** *"It doesn't need to be dark themed"* is permission, not a request, and it was taken as licence to delete a feature. The real bug was the stored preference silently overriding a changed default, and that was already fixed. Dark is back, the toggle is back, light stays the default. **The lesson is narrow and worth keeping: when a sentence licenses a removal, the removal still needs its own reason.**

### ⚠ THE BUTTONS WERE THE COLOUR BUG AGAIN, EXACTLY

Measured: **34 files import `<Button>`. 274 button class strings are hand-rolled.** So when 10-26 raised the primitive's sizes and padding — explicitly *"to stop buttons looking visibly timid next to the chunky primary actions that make Jobber and Attio feel like products"* — that change reached 34 files and missed 274 buttons. The same shape as the 2,214 raw colour classes that made two palette re-skins invisible, one layer up: **A PRIMITIVE ONLY STYLES WHAT USES IT.**

The divergence from the primitive's own declared shape:

| | hand-rolled | `ui/button.tsx` |
|---|---|---|
| radius | `rounded-md` ×264 | `rounded-lg` |
| height | `h-8` ×98 | `h-9` |
| type | `text-xs` ×120 | `text-sm` |
| lift | `elev-1` on 2 filled | on all |

Two button radii on every screen, and neither matched `Panel`. Converged by codemod (`scripts/codemod/button-shape.mjs`): 307 radii, 117 heights, 142 type sizes, 130 lifts. ⚠ Scoped to strings that are unambiguously a control — `inline-flex` + a height + a surface — because `inline-flex … rounded-md` alone also describes chips, avatars and icon wells, which must not grow. `h-7` (the primitive's own `xs`) and absolute touch targets are left alone.

### The layout, which is what he actually asked about

⚠ **TWO PASSES HAD MOVED COLOUR TOKENS AND CONTROL STYLING AND NEVER TOUCHED HOW A LIST IS SHAPED.** `/projects` offered a Kanban board and a grouped card list — **both of them card layouts**: one record per tile, four or five facts each, most of the screen spent on padding, four records visible at 1512×950. Every reference app in the brief leads with a **table**: one row per record, every column comparable down the page. Measured on the real portfolio: **12 records visible instead of 4.** That is the difference between an admin panel and a BI tool, and no amount of radius or shadow substitutes for it.

`ProjectsTable` is the new default view — sortable columns, a sticky header, a stage dot carrying the funnel's one real signal into every row, and `rolledPipelineValue` so a program's figure is still its leaves'. The board stays: a bid funnel genuinely is a board, and the 10-26 drag primitive lives there.

⚠ **THE STORAGE KEY IS NEW ON PURPOSE (`bw.projects.view.v2`).** Everyone who has ever opened that page has `'pipeline'` written in localStorage, so changing the DEFAULT would have reached nobody who uses the application — **which is precisely how the theme change failed to land four hours earlier.** A new key is the only way a default applies to existing readers. Same bug, same day, caught the second time.

### The harness lied, and now it does not

`BW_SHOOT_DARK` set the theme by navigating to `/dashboard#set-dark`, which is not a thing: `chrome --headless --screenshot` runs none of your script, so it can never reach `localStorage` before the pre-paint script reads it. **The flag existed, read plausibly, and was never once run** — which is how six screenshots were taken in the one theme the user was not in. Rewritten over the DevTools Protocol: open a tab, seed the key, reload, capture. ⚠ **And it now ASSERTS the theme applied before saving a frame**, because the failure being fixed is a switch that claimed to work.

### ⚠ The ratchet earned its keep twice in one session

`conventions.test.ts` failed the build for `StatTile` and again for `ProjectsTable`, both hand-rolling `rounded-lg border border-border bg-card elev-1` — a new shared primitive is exactly where the 228th copy of the card starts. Both use `<Panel>`.

It also, correctly, went up to 236 when the buttons converged: a secondary button is `rounded-lg border border-border bg-card`, byte-identical to the card-shell pattern. **Raising the baseline was the easy move and would have made the ratchet mean less than it did before.** The scan was NARROWED instead — a class string carrying `inline-flex` and a height is a control, not a surface — and measured against the tree before and after, it returns **227 both times**, proving the convergence added no cards and that the old 231 was four buttons miscounted. The baseline came DOWN.

**Done 2026-10-27 (the overhaul was invisible, and the half-measure is why):**

Richard, an hour after the overhaul shipped: *"literally nothing look any different. I asked for a complete overhaul..."* — the second time in two days.

⚠ **HE WAS IN DARK MODE, AND THE ENTIRE OVERHAUL WAS DONE ON THE LIGHT PALETTE.** Proven by diff, not inferred: between `7bbdb08` and the overhaul commit, the `.dark` block's `--sidebar` (`oklch(0.165 0.016 55)`), `--background` (`0.205 0.012 88`) and `--card` (`0.255 0.012 88`) are **byte-identical**. Every colour that moved was in `:root`. So the rail, the canvas and the cards — the three surfaces that are 90% of the screen — did not change at all for him.

⚠ **AND THE HALF-MEASURE IS WHAT PUT HIM THERE.** His instruction was *"It doesn't need to be dark themed."* The overhaul read that as *default to light* and removed only the `prefers-color-scheme` fallback, leaving the pre-paint script still honouring a stored `theme: 'dark'`. Anyone who had ever touched the toggle — once, months ago — stayed in dark for ever, and now had no signal that anything had been done. **A theme default is not a theme decision.** Changing what a new visitor gets does nothing for the only two people who use the application.

The alternatives were ruled out before changing anything, because "nothing is different" has four plausible causes and only one of them is worth acting on: no service worker exists, the HTML is `Cache-Control: no-store`, the CSS chunks are content-hashed (so a stale stylesheet is impossible), and the new pre-paint script was confirmed byte-present in the live response. That left exactly one explanation, and the diff above confirmed it.

**The fix is not a better default.** The stored key is no longer read and is cleared on load; the toggle is gone from the user menu, because a control that appears to work and does not survive a reload is worse than no control. The `.dark` block stays in `globals.css` — `tone.test.ts` measures it, and deleting a whole palette to turn a feature off is not reversible — but nothing in the application can reach it. **Bringing dark back means designing it, not re-enabling it.**

⚠ **THE GENERAL LESSON, AND IT IS ABOUT VERIFICATION, NOT CSS.** The session built a screenshot harness specifically so the work would be looked at, took six screenshots, and still shipped something the user could not see — because **every screenshot was taken in the theme being redesigned, and the user was in the other one**. A harness that can only render the happy path is a harness that confirms what you already believe. `BW_SHOOT_DARK` existed in `shoot.mjs` from the first commit and was never once run.

**Done 2026-10-27 (the complete UI overhaul — and the measurement that explains why two re-skins could not be seen):**

Richard: *"I want a complete overhaul of the UI. It doesn't need to be dark themed. I want it to look modern like Attio, Domo or some other leading business intelligence dashboard. The colors can look like Ber Wilson, but I would like the layout, and look to be modernized. Do a complete overhaul."*

⚠ **THE FIRST THING THIS SESSION DID WAS BUILD A WAY TO LOOK AT THE APP, AND IT PAID FOR ITSELF IN FOUR MINUTES.** Three consecutive sessions (10-26, 10-26, 10-27) shipped palette and layout work without once rendering the result; the 10-27 entry says so in its own words — *"Three rounds shipped with NO screenshot."* The blocker was always auth: every route but `/login` sits behind `middleware.ts`, so headless Chrome lands on the sign-in card whatever URL you give it. **§12 already held the key and nobody had connected it: `next dev` does not load the root `middleware.ts`.** So a dev server on :3001 renders every page with no session at all — `curl /dashboard` returns 200 — and `chrome --headless --screenshot` can walk the whole app. That is now `scripts/ui/shoot.mjs`. The very first screenshot, of `/login`, showed a **navy radial gradient** on the first screen of the product.

### What the measurement found, before anything was changed

⚠ **2,214 RAW TAILWIND COLOUR CLASSES ACROSS 135 FILES — AND THAT IS WHY THE BRAND PALETTE "COULDN'T BE SEEN".** 10-26 re-derived the whole palette from Jobber's Atlantis tokens; 10-27 re-derived it again from the Ber Wilson logo. Both were real, both were correct, and both were nearly invisible, because **most of the application's colour never consulted a token**. `text-red-600 dark:text-red-400`, `bg-amber-50 dark:bg-amber-950`, `text-slate-500` — six parallel palettes with their own hues, their own contrast and their own hand-maintained dark mode, running beside the measured one. 950 of the 2,214 were `dark:` variants that exist only because a raw colour cannot carry a theme. This is §12's *"a token themes only what READS it"* at a scale nobody had counted.

⚠ **`<h1>` IN 20+ DISTINCT SPELLINGS, AND NO PAGE-HEADER COMPONENT.** `text-lg font-semibold`, `text-xl font-semibold leading-tight`, `text-2xl`, `text-base font-semibold`, one in `tracking-widest uppercase text-slate-900`. Nothing wrong with any of them individually — that is the point. No owner, so no two pages opened the same way.

⚠ **AND THE APP CONTAINED ZERO DATA VISUALISATIONS.** 97 pages of lists, cards and counts. Richard named Domo; the honest reading of that is that a BI dashboard shows a SHAPE, and this one could only show totals.

### The overhaul

**Light is the default, and the system preference no longer decides.** The pre-paint script fell back to `prefers-color-scheme`, so on a Mac set to dark — which both of these are — the app opened dark however it had been designed, and **the light palette every re-skin was measured in was the theme nobody ever saw.** Now only an explicit stored `'dark'` turns it on. Dark mode still exists and is still tested; it is a choice in the user menu.

**THE RAIL IS LIGHT, and this is the single largest move.** It was a dark slab at L 0.225 beside a light app — the one thing every reference Richard named does *not* do. Attio, Linear, Notion and Domo all run a light rail one step below the canvas and let the CONTENT be the brightest plane. A dark rail is the signature of an admin panel, and it was also carrying the app's only large area of colour, so the eye went to the furniture instead of the data. Three planes now, chrome → canvas → content: **rail 0.922, canvas 0.963, card 0.995**, ΔL 0.041 and 0.032, both clearing the 0.03 floor `tone.test.ts` asserts. Flipping it inverts the rail's ink and its wordmark (`/logo-dark.png` is a cream lockup — invisible on a light rail), and `themeColor` with it.

⚠ **`--primary` GAINED A FOURTH SURFACE AND THE TEST DID NOT KNOW.** The active nav row is now primary-coloured text *on the rail*, a pairing no assertion covered while the sidebar was dark. L 0.52 was tried — it reads brighter — and landed at 5.77:1 on a card, under the 6.0 bar `contrast.test.ts` holds this token to. **The bar was not lowered to fit the colour; the colour went back to 0.50 and the test grew the rail as a measured surface** (§12: when a reason moves, the assertion gets stronger, not deleted). 0.50 → 6.29:1 on fill and card, 5.07:1 on the rail.

**The serif is gone.** Every `<h1>` was set in Newsreader. A serif masthead over a data table is the tell of a document, not a dashboard; Attio, Linear and Domo all set headings in the body face and separate them by weight and tracking. `--font-heading` now resolves to the sans stack and Newsreader is no longer loaded.

**The login page is the canvas.** Hue 260, inline, reading no token — the first screen of the product and the one surface two consecutive re-skins could not reach. Rebuilt as `bg-background` with a single wash of `--primary` through `color-mix`, so it follows the palette by construction.

**The codemod: 1,844 classes mapped, 675 redundant `dark:` variants dropped, 0 raw status-family classes left.** `scripts/codemod/tokenise-colours.mjs`. It converts only the families `tone.ts` declares as STATUS (red→critical, amber/yellow→caution, emerald/green→positive, blue→info, the neutral ramp→foreground/muted/border) and leaves every CategoryTone — violet, indigo, cyan, sky, teal, rose, orange — exactly as it is, which is tone.ts's own documented decision. The second half is the real win: once mapped, a `dark:` twin of a status token is redundant *and worse than redundant* where it was written as an arbitrary alpha (`bg-caution-surface … dark:bg-caution/15`), overriding in one theme a token whose whole job is to carry both.

**New primitives.** `PageHeader` + `HeaderMetrics` (one masthead idiom, deliberately 20px and not 30px — it buys back the vertical space 10-26's density change spent). `StatTile` + `StatGrid` + `Sparkline` — inline SVG, no charting dependency, because the demonstrated need is a 100×24 polyline and Recharts is ~90KB plus a client boundary. `StageMix`, the app's first chart: pipeline count and value by stage, proportional bars from CSS widths, server-rendered.

**The KPI band lost its four pastel icon chips.** Each tile carried a 36px rounded square in its own hue — primary, violet, emerald, amber. §12: when every row is red, red has stopped signifying; four tiles in four colours is the same failure wearing pastel, and it meant the one tile genuinely warning could not be picked out from the three that were fine. The tiles are plain, and `tone` colours the FIGURE only when the figure is the problem.

⚠ **AND THE BAND MOVED ABOVE THE FOLD.** It sat third, below two tall panels, so on a 1512×950 screen **the state of the portfolio was below the fold on the page whose job is to show it.**

**Every view switcher stopped shouting.** Screenshots, not grep, found this: three filled blocks in one row on the dashboard — two near-black tab groups and a terracotta sort control — none of which was the page's actual button. On `/contacts`, two more beside the real "Add Contact". Nine switchers across six files now use the track-and-pill idiom: a grey track with the selected segment lifted to the content plane. §12 on this exact token: *"Keep it scarce: it means 'this is the action'."*

⚠ **THE CODEMOD FOR THAT WAS TOO BROAD AND NINE OF ELEVEN HITS WERE REVERTED BY HAND.** Syntax told it which strings were selected-states; it could not tell which sat in a TRACK. The others were loose filter chips on the canvas, where a pill has nothing to lift off — `--card` is ΔL 0.045 from `--muted`, not enough to say "selected" when the chips are a hand's width apart. A near-black chip is legible and legitimate there, and was never what broke the hierarchy. **The rule is narrower than the regex: a pill belongs to a segmented track.** Written into the script for whoever re-runs it.

### ⚠ The bug the codemod shipped, and the test that now catches it

**`bg-slate-900 text-white` became `bg-muted text-white` — white on near-white, in 13 controls.** The neutral mapping read shade 900 as "the dark end of the ramp, therefore the `dark:` half of a tinted surface". It is not: in light mode that pair is a **dark fill** — a print button, a numbered bullet. Thirteen controls rendered invisible. **Typecheck green, build green, 729 tests green.** Found on a screenshot of `/login`, where the footer was still `text-white/40` from the navy page.

Nothing could have caught it except looking, and looking does not scale to 97 pages. What scales is the structural rule underneath, now `conventions.test.ts`: **the app has two inks and two fills and they pair one way round** — `bg-foreground` takes `text-background`; `bg-card`/`bg-background`/`bg-muted` take `text-foreground`. Any class string pairing a light fill with a light ink, or a dark fill with a dark ink, is a rendering bug whatever it looks like in source. `text-white` counts as a light ink deliberately: it is theme-blind, so on `bg-muted` it is wrong in *both* themes. The test also caught `MapView`'s `bg-foreground … text-background dark:text-foreground` — light ink on a light fill in dark mode.

**`StatTile`'s first draft was failed by the Panel ratchet**, correctly: it hand-rolled `rounded-lg border border-border bg-card elev-1` inline, which is exactly where the 232nd such shell would have started. It uses `<Panel>`.

### Verified

730 tests (one new), typecheck clean, lint at the frozen 22-problem baseline (§9), and — for the first time in four sessions — **screenshots of `/dashboard`, `/projects`, `/contacts`, `/tasks`, `/leads` and `/login`, looked at**. ⚠ A dev-mode screenshot under-represents the rail: with no middleware there is no session, so `getViewer()` returns null, the role falls back to `member` and most nav rows are filtered out. The chrome and the content are faithful; the nav row count is not.


**Done 2026-10-27 (the palette was never Ber Wilson's — the brand was in the logo the whole time):**

Richard, after the Jobber-register re-skin shipped: *"I can't see a single
change. I asked for a radical overhaul of the system. Wanting this to look
modern and clean like Attio or Jobber. I want the color scheme to match Ber
Wilson's colors."* And on dark mode: *"Make it look like Ber Wilson. Doesn't
need to be so dark."*

**He was right twice, and the second one is the finding.**

⚠ **FIRST, "I CAN'T SEE A CHANGE" WAS CHASED AND THE OBVIOUS ANSWER WAS WRONG.**
The stylesheet is served `immutable, max-age=31536000`, which looked like the
whole story — until building the PREVIOUS `globals.css` to a throwaway dist dir
showed the chunk name *does* move with its content (`0u~4z8wyq9u-~.css` →
`0eo7m8l10pv87.css`). Cache-busting works. The page is `no-store`, points at
the new chunk, there is one server, there is no service worker, and
`.rounded-lg{border-radius:var(--radius)}` proves the utilities are wired to
the tokens rather than merely declared beside them. **Production was correct
and the change was simply too timid to see.** Measuring the deltas said so
plainly: dark `--background` went `#070707` → `#080706`, `--card` `#101010` →
`#11100e`. One value per channel. I had set dark chroma to 0.004 and then told
him the canvas was "within a hair of Atlantis" — true of the LIGHT canvas, and
he works in dark. That was an over-claim, and his "not a single change" was a
fair description of what shipped.

⚠ **SECOND, AND WORSE: THE ACCENT HAD NO BASIS IN THE BRAND.** `globals.css`
called `oklch(0.42 0.145 262)` *"Ber Wilson's blue"* and the 10-17 entry
defended keeping it over a near-black. Nobody had checked. Sampling the logo
PNGs in `public/` — the asset the sidebar renders every single page — gives:

| | hex | oklch | role in the mark |
|---|---|---|---|
| terracotta | `#ca6e55` | `0.637 0.123 36` | dominant |
| sage | `#709a8e` | `0.652 0.049 175` | secondary |
| ochre | `#c4994a` | `0.708 0.110 81` | tertiary |
| cream | `#ede6d3` | `0.925 0.026 90` | the field |

**Warm, earthy, southwestern — and the app was cool navy on neutral grey.** Two
sessions had re-measured that blue against four thresholds without once asking
where it came from. *A token's name is not evidence; the brand asset is.*

**The palette is derived now, not picked.** `--primary` is the brand hue 38 at
the lightness a sweep found clears 6:1 as link text AND carries cream at 4.5:1
— L 0.50 light, 0.72 dark, which compile to `#a14122` and `#e7876a`. The
neutrals moved to the cream's own hue 88 at real chroma, so the canvas is
`#f2ecde` rather than grey with a rumour of warmth. Dark lifted off near-black
per Richard: canvas L 0.13 → 0.205 (`#191711`), cards → `#25231c`, and the dark
sidebar ΔL *improved* to 0.040 from the 0.035 it had been sitting on against a
0.03 floor.

⚠ **AND THE RAIL WAS PAINTED BY A HARDCODED GRADIENT, NOT BY ITS OWN TOKENS.**
`.sidebar-gradient` and `.sidebar-nav-active` carried literal `oklch(… 260)`
navy, so every `--sidebar-*` token could be re-themed and the rail would not
move one pixel. That is precisely why the first pass left a navy rail against a
warm app and read as "nothing changed" on the most prominent chrome on screen.
Both are `color-mix()` over the tokens now, so the rail cannot drift again.
**Same class of bug in three more places**, each a surface a re-skin could not
reach: `::selection` was blue, the skeleton shimmer was neutral grey over warm
surfaces, and `themeColor` was `#1a1b2e` in BOTH themes — the phone's browser
chrome. `--chart-1..5` were byte-identical across light and dark, which
`tone.test.ts` already names as the cautionary tale it cannot catch because
nothing renders them yet; they are the brand's three plus two derived.

⚠ **ONE BOUND MOVED AND IT IS WORTH BEING HONEST ABOUT.** `MAX_CHROMA` in
`contrast.test.ts` went 0.015 → 0.032 — a bound I had written myself four hours
earlier. The justification is not "it was in the way": the bound tracks the
palette it measures, and the brand's own cream is 0.026, so 0.015 would have
forbidden the company's actual colour. The principle is untouched — one hue,
bounded, no accidental tints — and the hue check is what does the real work.

**Measured, both themes:** body 16.97 / 14.04, muted 6.54 / 6.84, accent 6.11 /
6.06, every status ink ≥ 5.59 on its own surface, every ΔL ≥ 0.040. 729 tests,
100 render checks, lint unchanged at 22. Verified by fetching the live
stylesheet over the tailnet after the kickstart: `--background:#f2ecde` /
`#191711`, `--primary:#a14122` / `#e7876a`, `--sidebar:#231a14`.
⚠ **No screenshot — the Chrome extension disconnected and then reported zero
connected browsers**, so three rounds of visual work shipped without eyes on
it. That is the standing weakness in this whole sequence and it is why a
too-timid change survived a full deploy.

**Done 2026-10-26 (the aesthetic overhaul — and Jobber publishes its design system, so the values were read rather than guessed):**

Richard, after seeing the drag-and-drop land: *"I can see there is some drag and
drop capability now, but what about the UI aesthetics? I want this to look like
jobber or a leading edge modern CRM. That can entail a complete button, color
overhaul etc... if you haven't already been planning that, tell me and I will
start a fresh chat to get the aesthetics right."*

**The honest answer was no — I had steered him AWAY from this four hours
earlier**, arguing the monochrome palette already *was* the modern register and
getting agreement on "interaction-first, direction C stays". That was right for
the drag work and it explicitly deferred the look. He is now asking for the
look, which is the half 10-17 said was his to judge.

⚠ **JOBBER PUBLISHES ATLANTIS, SO THIS DID NOT HAVE TO BE A MOOD BOARD.**
`atlantis.getjobber.com` 403s a fetch, but `@jobber/design` is on npm and its
`dist/color.css`, `foundation.css` and `semantic.css` are served by jsDelivr.
Reading them reframed the whole job:

- `--radius-base: 8px`, `--radius-large: 16px` — **twice ours** (`--radius: 4px`).
- `--space-base: 16px` on a 4px step — against our `--spacing: 0.22rem`.
- `--shadow-low` / `--shadow-base` / `--shadow-high`: **real, layered, present** —
  against our `--elev-1/-2: 0 0 0 0 transparent`.
- `--color-taupe: hsl(43, 18%, 92%)` — a **warm** canvas, not a neutral grey.
- `--color-grey*`: **0% saturation**, exactly like ours.
- `--color-interactive` is one saturated green; `critical`/`warning`/`success`/
  `informative` each carry `surface` and `onSurface` siblings.

⚠ **THE SEMANTIC LAYER IS ALREADY WHAT WE HAVE.** Their `interactive` /
`critical` / `warning` / `success` / `informative` / `inactive` maps one-to-one
onto our `primary` / `critical` / `caution` / `positive` / `info` / `neutral`,
down to the surface+ink pairing. **The architecture needed nothing.** What
differed was four values and a missing component — which is a very different
project from "a colour overhaul", and is why measuring first mattered again.

**So the gap was never colour.** Jobber's palette is *less* chromatic than
ours; it reads friendly because of radius, air, lift and warmth. Put to Richard
as three options with the trade named — polish costs rows per screen — he took
the full direction and told me to choose and ship rather than build a gallery.

**What changed, all of it in tokens.** `--radius` 0.25rem → **0.5rem** (one
line re-rounds every card, button, input and dialog, because the whole ladder
derives from it). `--spacing` 0.22rem → **0.25rem**, reversing 10-17 and costing
~13% of the rows on a screen, accepted deliberately. `--elev-1/-2` from
`transparent` to two-layer shadows modelled on `--shadow-low`/`--shadow-base`.
And the neutrals took a deliberate warm cast on one hue — the light canvas
compiles to **`#f4f1ec`**, within a hair of Atlantis's own `#f0ece3`.

⚠ **TWO ASSERTIONS HAD TO BE OVERTURNED, AND OVERTURNING THEM WELL WAS THE REAL
WORK.** They were not obstacles; they were 10-17's decisions written down, and
§12 says a workaround's recorded reason must be re-tested before it is
inherited. Both were re-tested:

1. `contrast.test.ts` asserted `parsed.c === 0` on seven neutrals in both
   themes. Its stated reason — *"a slightly blue grey is invisible in isolation
   and obvious in aggregate"* — is a rule against ACCIDENT, and exact-zero is
   the cheapest statement of it, not the truest. It now asserts the neutrals
   **share one hue** and stay under a chroma bound, which is **strictly stronger
   against the original bug**: two greys at chroma 0.01 on different hues used
   to be unrepresentable, and now fail loudly on the hue.
2. `tone.test.ts` asserted `--elev-1`/`--elev-2` were literally
   `0 0 0 0 transparent`. That reason — a shadow on every card turning a
   181-document list to mush — **depended on the density, which moved in the
   same change**. It now asserts the ladder is ORDERED and caps the resting
   rung, because the failure mode was never "a shadow", it was "a shadow loud
   enough to repeat two hundred times".

⚠ **AND THE REWRITTEN LADDER TEST FAILED ON ITS FIRST RUN, CORRECTLY, WITH THE
WRONG REASONING.** Its first metric summed every alpha in a shadow, which
reported the dark `--elev-2` (two tight layers, 0.35 + 0.28) as heavier than
`--elev-3` (one wide-blur layer at 0.6) — the opposite of what the eye sees,
because summing ignores blur and spread. The failure was real and the metric
was wrong; max-alpha orders them honestly with no blur maths. Then **fifteen
planted violations** proved both rewrites still catch what the originals caught
— including the case that showed my own expectation was wrong rather than the
check (the "just a little lift" bug trips the ORDERING rule before the cap, so
a separate heavy-but-ordered case was added to exercise the cap at all).

**The button overhaul Richard asked for by name.** Sizes up a step — the
default was `h-8` = **28.2px** at the old spacing, visibly timid; it is 36px
now, with padding to match (`px-2.5` on a primary action was the tightest thing
on screen). The primary carries `elev-1`. ⚠ **A SIXTH VARIANT WAS NAMED BECAUSE
IT ALREADY EXISTED:** `bg-foreground text-background` appears in **65 files**,
including a byte-identical retry button in **42 of the 55 `error.tsx` files** —
an unnamed variant in 65 places is a button style nobody can restyle once.
⚠ And the per-size `rounded-[min(var(--radius-md),10px)]` caps were deleted
from four places: at a 4px radius `--radius-md` was 3.2px, so the `min()` had
never once bound anything.

⚠ **THE MOST VISIBLE WRINKLE WAS A BLOCKER SOMEBODY WROTE DOWN AND LEFT.**
**140 raw `<select>` elements** render OS chrome on a themed page — the thing
that looks most unfinished in every screenshot — and `field.tsx` explained
exactly why: *"`appearance-none` would take the native arrow with it and this
app has no popover Select to replace it"*. True, and the fix was never a
popover: it was to BRING a chevron. One base rule in `globals.css` now themes
all 140 at once, with no component churn, no behaviour change, and the OS
picker still opening on a phone, where it is the better picker.
⚠ **Specificity is doing two jobs there**: `select:not([multiple]):not([size])`
is (0,1,1), which beats the `.px-3` utility at (0,1,0) — without the `:not()`
each control's own padding would win and the option text would run underneath
the chevron.

⚠ **AND THE BOARDS WERE SHOWING A PLACEHOLDER AS THEIR MAIN FIGURE.** Measured:
**1 of 20 projects and 0 of 10 opportunities carry an `estimated_value`**, and
`formatValue(null)` returns `'—'`. §12 calls a bare em dash at a value's own
weight a failed render, and it was on essentially every card on the
opportunities board. `ProjectCard` had already solved this in words ("No value
set"); `OpportunityCard` had not, so the two flagship boards disagreed about
what "no value" looks like. A render check now guards it, with the empty-column
spacer deliberately exempt, and five planted cases prove it catches a bare dash
without tripping on a dash inside prose.

**Verification.** 729 tests, **100 render checks** (up from 90), lint unchanged
at 22, typecheck clean. Every contrast and ΔL threshold re-measured through the
same reader `/settings/ui` uses: body 20.17 / 17.91, muted 8.41 / 7.10, accent
8.63 / 7.02, every status ink ≥ 5.59 on its own surface, ΔL card/canvas 0.038 /
0.045. ⚠ **The dark sidebar sits at ΔL 0.035 against a 0.03 floor** — five
thousandths of headroom — so the dark canvas lightness was deliberately left
untouched while warmth was added around it. ⚠ **And the artifact was checked,
not just the source:** the new build was served on port 3100 against production
on 3000, and its compiled stylesheet fetched and grepped — `--radius:.5rem`,
`--spacing:.25rem`, `--background:#f4f1ec`, real `--elev-1`, the chevron rule
present, and every old value absent. A planned screenshot comparison was
abandoned when the Chrome extension disconnected twice; the compiled-CSS check
is the stronger evidence anyway, since it reads what the browser will receive.
