**Done 2026-10-26 (the CRM research Richard asked for, and the finding that his two asks pull opposite ways):**

Richard: *"I want you to research the most modern CRM's like Jobber or other
emerging leaders to help completely redesign the UI. Our UI can have colors,
drag and drop features and really anything to make it more intuitive and user
friendly. Do an analysis and perform a complete overhaul that makes us look
like the a modern tech company."*

⚠ **MEASURING FIRST TURNED A PALETTE JOB INTO AN AFFORDANCE JOB, AND THE
RESEARCH IS WHY.** The UI had been deliberately redrawn **nine days earlier**
(10-17, five phases), from the same question — *"How can I enhance the user
interface and the user experience to make it truly impressive?"* — with three
measured directions put to Richard and **C** chosen: zero-chroma neutrals, one
chromatic role, hairline borders, no resting shadow, 12% tighter density. That
entry closed by naming exactly what was left over: *"whether the accent stays
scarce enough to mean 'this is the action' … That is Richard's to say."* This
session is him saying it.

But the research contradicted the instinct rather than confirming it. **The two
references that read most as "a modern tech company" are the monochrome ones:**
Vercel is *"extreme restraint — a monochrome system where color equals
meaning"*, Linear is *"dark-first, quiet chrome, famous for what it leaves
out"*, and even **Jobber** — the one Richard named — is described as *"modern
and clean with a **neutral** colour palette, uncluttered"*, winning on being
learnable in 1–2 days. Attio is the colour-forward one, and what every Attio
review actually praises is **interaction**: *"switching a list from table to
kanban or calendar feels instantaneous"*, *"drag-and-drop updates were instant,
even with large deal volumes"*. So adding colour would have moved the platform
AWAY from the register Richard was asking for. Put to him as three options with
the measurement attached; he chose **interaction-first, monochrome stays**, and
all four scope items.

**And the affordance gap was real, measured, and embarrassing in a specific
way.** Five board surfaces: **three hand-rolled copies of native HTML5 drag**
(`SteelPipelineBoard`, `ObjectivesBoard`, `OrgStructureBoard`) and **two with
no drag at all — `/projects`'s pipeline board and `TeamTaskBoard`, the two
highest-traffic boards in the application**, both scoring a literal `0` for
`draggable`. The pattern existed and had never been applied where it mattered
most, which is §12's "a shared renderer wired to one surface is worse than no
shared renderer" in both directions at once. `Segmented` — the table⇄board
switch that is Attio's single most-praised feature — was defined **locally
inside `SteelPipelineBoard`**, reachable by one of the five.

⚠ **ALL THREE EXISTING COPIES WERE POINTER-ONLY, AND THE STEEL BOARD SAID SO IN
ITS OWN FOOTER:** *"On a phone, open a deal to change its stage."* The
limitation had become documentation instead of a bug — absent on the device
Richard carries, absent for a keyboard entirely. So the new primitive is built
**keyboard-first with the pointer as a second caller of the same reducer**; built
the other way round, the keyboard path has to reconstruct "where am I" from
mouse coordinates. A tap is the third caller: tap the handle to HOLD a card,
tap a lane to drop it, which is the only reason this works on a touch screen at
all.

**What shipped.** `src/lib/ui/dnd.ts` — pure, server-safe, 32 tests. The React
skin in `src/components/ui/board.tsx` (`useBoardDnd`, `BoardLiveRegion`,
`DragHandle`, `BoardHint`), `Segmented` lifted into `src/components/ui/`. Then:
**drag a deal between stages on `/projects`** (desktop board and the mobile
stacked list); **an opportunities pipeline board** behind a Pipeline⇄Cards
switch; **drag a task onto a person to reassign it** on `/tasks`; **reorder the
Now objectives in place on the dashboard**; and the steel board migrated off its
own copy.

⚠ **`OPPORTUNITY_PIPELINE` HAD EXISTED ALL ALONG AND HAD NEVER BEEN RENDERED AS
A PIPELINE.** Six ordered stages in `src/lib/utils/opportunities.ts`, read by the
detail layout, the milestones page and `records/live.ts` — and by nothing that
draws a board. `/opportunities` was a flat grid, so the one surface where the
order of those stages IS the information did not show it. A producer with no
consumer, the exact mirror of the §12 line about a consumer written for a
producer that never existed.

⚠ **THE SAME SHAPE ON THE DASHBOARD, AND EVERY PIECE WAS ALREADY BUILT.**
`NowObjectives` is a **numbered** list, so its order is a claim — and the only
way to change that claim was to navigate to `/objectives` and drag it there. The
numbers come from `sort_order`, the dashboard reads the FULL `now` bucket with
no LIMIT, and `/api/objectives/reorder` already took exactly the payload a
reorder produces. Three surfaces' worth of machinery, never joined up.

⚠ **THE GESTURE HAD TO REFUSE WHAT THE SCHEMA CANNOT SAVE.** `objectives`
carries `sort_order`; **`projects`, `opportunities` and `tasks` carry no order
column** (verified against `database.ts`). So a within-lane reorder on those
three would animate, hold optimistically, and snap back on the next server
render. `reorderable` therefore defaults to **false** — the safe answer, since a
board that forgets to opt in loses a nicety where one that forgets to opt out
tells the reader something untrue — and the vertical arrows are refused outright
rather than faked. The steel board gets `false` for a second reason: its
within-column order is DERIVED (next-step date, then value), so a hand-dragged
position would be overwritten by the next sort, not the next fetch.

⚠ **AND THE HINT HAD TO COME FROM THE SAME PLACE AS THE KEYS.** `BoardHint`
first took its own `reorderable` prop, to be kept in sync with the hook by hand
— a hand-written enumeration beside a registry, which §12 says drifts, and
whose drift here is a sentence naming a key that does nothing. Only the hook
knows both the flag AND the lane count, and a **one-lane** reorder list has no
horizontal move at all: the dashboard says *"the up and down arrow keys"*, the
stage boards say *"the left and right arrow keys"*, and a render check asserts
the dashboard does **not** say "left and right".

⚠ **THE §12 TAILWIND-MERGE TRAP IS EVERYWHERE IN A DRAG, AND THE OLD CODE HAD
ALREADY PAID FOR IT.** A held card and a drop target both want a signal, and
every card already owns a `bg-*` and most own a `border-l-*` urgency tint — so
every new signal is a **ring**. The steel board's old drop state was
`border-primary/60 bg-primary/5` *in place of* the resting background, which is
why its branch had to re-state the muted and normal cases to avoid deleting
them; a ring needs no such branch.

⚠ **AND THE HANDLE COULD NOT GO WHERE IT LOOKED LIKE IT SHOULD.** A `<button>`
inside an `<a>` fires BOTH — the trap that forced `/attention`'s rows from Link
to div — so on every card the handle is a **sibling** of the anchor, and
`PipelineCard` was restructured from "the card IS the Link" to a wrapper holding
both. The first draft also hung the handle's reveal on `group-hover:`, which is
wrong twice: hover-reveal is the bug, and the five boards spell their group
names differently (`group/card` vs bare `group`) while `group-hover/${name}:`
cannot be built by interpolation. It now depends on no group at all.

**Three findings that are not code.** (a) `/api/projects/[id]/stage` **did not
validate the stage against the enum** — fine while its only caller was a
`<select>` rendered from `STAGES`, and not fine now that a drag, a key press and
a tap write that column, with lanes built from a URL parameter. §12: a value
outside an enum fails the WHOLE query (`22P02`), which would have surfaced as a
500 reading "invalid input value for enum". (b) `/api/objectives/reorder` has
**no viewer check at all** and uses the service-role client — middleware is the
boundary per §8, so not a hole, but it is the only one of these routes shaped
that way. (c) The 10-17 density change's tap-target lesson had a survivor: the
`Segmented` control was `h-7`, which is `calc(var(--spacing) * 7)` = **24.6px**,
well under the 44px floor.

**Verification. ⚠ AND THE REPO HAD NO WAY TO DO IT.** CLAUDE.md's own runbook
records that `npm run build` **IS** the deploy here — the launchd job is
`KeepAlive: true`, so replacing `.next` kills `next start` and launchd boots the
new build within the minute — which makes "does this compile" indistinguishable
from "ship it". `next build` has no `--distDir` flag (checked against
`--help`), so `next.config.ts` now reads an optional `BW_DIST_DIR`; unset, the
spread contributes no keys and the config is identical, so the runbook is
unchanged. Two sharp edges, both found the hard way: **the path is resolved
against the project root even when absolute** (`/tmp/x` wrote **151MB to
`<repo>/tmp/x`**, inside the working tree, while reporting a clean build), and
**`next build` rewrites `tsconfig.json`**, appending the dist dir's generated-
types glob and reformatting the file — a real diff two sessions sharing this
repo could stage by accident. Both are now in the config's own comment, the
verify dirs are gitignored, and `git checkout -- tsconfig.json` is part of the
documented command rather than an afterthought. ⚠ A third: writing that glob
INTO the comment truncated the block comment — it contains the two characters
that end one — and `tsc` reported an unterminated template literal 16 lines
further down, naming neither the cause nor the line.

⚠ **AND ONE CHECK I WROTE COULD NOT FAIL UNTIL A PLANTED VIOLATION PROVED IT.**
The new render script asserts no bare `focus:` reaches the markup; the first
version carried `(?<!group-)(?<!-)` lookbehinds, written to let
`group-focus-visible:` through — which it never needed to, because `\bfocus:`
requires the colon immediately after "focus" and so cannot match
`focus-visible:` at all. What the lookbehinds DID do was **excuse
`group-focus:` and `peer-focus:`**, which are bare-focus variants with exactly
the same defect. Found by planting fifteen violations against the three
structural checks, not by re-reading the regex.

**729 tests** (697 + 32 new, all named and confirmed to run) and **90 render
checks** over every column shape, every optional field absent, the empty board,
and the three structural promises `tsc` cannot see: no `<button>` inside an
`<a>`, no spacing-derived tap target, nothing rendering as `NaN`/`undefined`.
Lint unchanged at **22** (13 errors, 9 warnings) throughout. Production build
compiles, exit 0, 283 routes — first against a throwaway dist dir, with the
live `.next` verified untouched at its pre-session mtime and the app still
answering, and then **DEPLOYED** on Richard's word: commit `7cb440a`, pushed,
built (13.5s, 283 routes, exit code captured from an UNPIPED build),
`launchctl kickstart -k` explicitly rather than trusting the KeepAlive cycle,
and both assertions green — `tailnet-setup.sh` (all three endpoints, env
matches the live hostname, no platform port off loopback) and
`lmstudio-check.sh`. Verified by serving: the page over the tailnet references
the new `BUILD_ID` (`jXMhFXu_ibDFTsxrfvxIA`), and the listener on `:3000` is
the new child.

⚠ **AND THE KICKSTART LEFT AN ORPHANED `next-server` THAT I NEARLY KILLED.**
`ps` showed two servers: the new job (19:57:38) and a `next-server` from
**16:42:21 reparented to `ppid 1`** — the shape §12 teaches as the LM Studio
orphan, and `launchctl list` showed the job's last exit as `-9`, so the
SIGKILL had taken the npm parent and left the child. It looked like a leak
worth reaping, and the case for reaping got stronger on inspection: it held
**two ESTABLISHED connections to LM Studio**, and `lms ps` read
**PROCESSINGPROMPT with the orphan as the only client** — which is exactly
§12's *"killing the client does not stop the generation … everything queues
behind it. Reload to clear."*

**It was the wrong read, and one more hop settled it.** Resolving the orphan's
INBOUND sockets named two live callers: `curl` **82407** (`cron-job-runner`,
47 minutes in) and **87725** (`cron-email-sweep`, 24 minutes in), both on a
3500s timeout and both still waiting. Next had kept the old server up to
**drain in-flight requests** — a graceful drain, not a leak, and the LM Studio
work was the email sweep's own, not a dead client's. Killing it would have
aborted two real cron runs to tidy 5MB of RSS. **An orphan is defined by
having no one waiting on it, so resolve the sockets to PIDs before reaping
one; `ppid 1` says the parent died, not that the work did.**

**What is deliberately NOT done.** `OrgStructureBoard` (1,668 lines) still has
its own copy: it is a **tree**, where a drag means re-parenting a node in a
hierarchy, and forcing that into a lane model would be the wrong shape rather
than a shared one. `ObjectivesBoard` keeps its copy too — its reorder
persistence is correct, complete and already handles the same off-by-one, so
rewriting working drag logic ranked below giving it to the boards that had
none.

**Done 2026-10-26 (the letter to T-Mobile — and researching it corrected my own diagnosis):**

Richard: *"Email T-Mobile's postmaster to clear the sender reputation."*

**Sent.** 15:31 PDT from `info@berwilson.com` — deliberately the mailbox the block names, which is also the proof we control it — to **`abuse@t-mobile.com`**, cc `postmaster@t-mobile.com`, accepted by their Proofpoint MX with no bounce from either role address.

⚠ **THE ADDRESS WAS LOOKED UP, NOT GUESSED, AND THAT WAS THE POINT OF NOT FIRING IT OFF IMMEDIATELY.** `abuse@t-mobile.com` is the **ARIN-registered `OrgAbuseEmail` for T-Mobile USA's TMO2 netblock** (`whois -h whois.arin.net "n 208.54.0.0"`), not a plausible-looking role address. A web search offered the same string with no provenance; the registry is the authority. Their own MX is `*.gslb.pphosted.com` — Proofpoint, the same vendor as the `cloudfilter.net` filter that is rejecting us, which is worth knowing because it means one party sees both sides.

⚠ **AND THE RESEARCH OVERTURNED THE DIAGNOSIS I HAD GIVEN RICHARD HOURS EARLIER.** I had told him `AUP#MXRT` was *"an acceptable-use rate/reputation block on our sender"* and offered *"clear the sender reputation with T-Mobile"* as one of three options. **`MXRT` is "Maximum Rate Exceeded" — a rate threshold. The reputation half was my inference and it was wrong**, which means the task as literally specified ("clear the sender reputation") asks for something that may not exist. The letter asks what the code actually signifies instead of asserting a cause, which is the only honest version of the request.

⚠ **THEN THE VOLUME KILLED THE RATE EXPLANATION TOO, AND THAT BECAME THE LETTER'S LEAD.** Measured from the sender's own Sent folder rather than from the bounces: **15 messages to `tmomail.net` and 72 messages in total** from that mailbox in 30 days — under one text every two days, no burst larger than two in a minute. Nothing at that volume reaches a rate threshold. What *is* shared is the egress: Google Workspace sends from a **shared** outbound range (`209.85.220.41` on a live sample), carrying traffic for an enormous number of tenants. **If the `MXRT` counter is keyed on the sending IP rather than the sending domain, we are collateral and nothing we change at our end clears it** — so the letter asks which it is, and offers to be corrected.

⚠ **A DNS READING THAT LOOKED DAMNING WAS CORRECTED BY THE WIRE.** `dig TXT google._domainkey.berwilson.com` returns nothing and no common selector resolves, which reads as *no DKIM at all* — and I nearly reported that. Reading a delivered message's `Authentication-Results` instead: **`dkim=pass`, `spf=pass`, `dmarc=pass`** — but signed `d=berwilson-com.20251104.gappssmtp.com`, Google's **shared fallback** key for tenants that never configured their own. So the mail authenticates while the domain has no DKIM reputation of its own. Real hygiene, filed as optional in [`OPEN-ITEMS.md`](OPEN-ITEMS.md) rather than sold as the fix, because it is not the cause here and email delivery is already proven. **§12's rule earned again: verify a DNS absence against what the receiving server actually said.**

⚠ **AND A VENDOR CLAIM WAS NEARLY REPEATED AS FACT.** Three sites asserted `tmomail.net` *"was shut down in December 2024 — accepted upstream and silently dropped, no text arrives and no bounce is returned"*, which would have made the whole letter pointless. **All three sell email-to-SMS replacements.** Checked instead of believed: `tmomail.net` publishes two live MX records, a real SPF record, and its MX answered us with AUP codes that same day. **Then Richard settled it from the one place it could be settled — his own phone: the texts DO arrive, at least sometimes.** That closes the item standing since 10-19 (*"say whether the texts arrived — your phone is the only test there is"*), confirms the gateway delivers intermittently, and is why the request was worth sending at all.

**On not sending it blind.** The letter is signed in Richard's name and goes to an outside carrier, so it was built as a Gmail **draft** in `info@` first, then sent with `drafts/send` — the one call that transmits the reviewed bytes rather than a rebuilt copy. He was asked two things before it went: whether the texts had ever arrived (which decides whether any of this is worth asking) and whether to send or read first. He said send.

Nothing in the platform changed; no code, no tests. **SENT**

**Done 2026-10-26 (the platform was paying for reasoning it threw away — and the measurement said which passes may stop):**

Richard: *"Is there anything we could do to more fully take advantage of our built in LLM capabilities or our connection to Gsuite?"* An open question, so the first deliverable was a measurement rather than a feature, and it came back lopsided: **Gsuite is already well exploited; the local model discards ~90% of everything it generates.**

⚠ **THE COST WAS INVISIBLE BECAUSE NOTHING COUNTED IT.** `qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b` reasons before it answers and LM Studio returns that reasoning in a SEPARATE `reasoning_content` field, which this platform has always dropped on the floor. `tokens_out` counted it; nothing separated it. Dividing the logged answer's character count into the token total over 30 days (3,982 calls, 55.3 GPU-hours) gives the share of each generation that was reasoning:

| prompt | n | completion tokens | answer (est) | **discarded** | sec |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| thread-summary-1.0 | 954 | 2,486 | ~274 | 89% | 45.3 |
| doc-summary-1.0 | 612 | 2,002 | ~155 | 92% | 41.3 |
| lead-triage-3.0 | 608 | 3,076 | ~275 | 91% | 50.9 |
| fit-assessment-2.1 | 526 | 2,949 | ~390 | 87% | 47.0 |
| commitments-1.0 | 366 | 3,117 | ~96 | **97%** | 56.8 |
| intake-predecide-2.0 | 119 | 1,432 | ~77 | 95% | 25.4 |
| drive-filing-1.1 | 95 | 1,378 | ~43 | **97%** | 22.3 |
| commitment-chase-1.0 | 94 | 2,803 | ~43 | **98%** | 36.2 |

**28.3 of those 55.3 hours sit in the six mechanical prompts.** LM Studio serves ONE request at a time, so that is not an abstract cost — it is the queue a human waiting on Ber AI sits behind, and it was demonstrated mid-session: a `doc-summary` cron was running back-to-back 40s calls and every probe in this session queued behind it.

⚠ **`createThinkFilter()` WAS A NO-OP ON EVERY CALL AND LOOKED LIKE THE ACCOUNTING.** It strips `<think>` tags from `content`; LM Studio never put one there — zero in 3,982 logged calls. Kept anyway, with the comment corrected to say so: §2 says a chat model is swappable at will, and a model whose template LM Studio does not recognise puts its reasoning in `content` where only that filter catches it. Removing a control because today's configuration does not exercise it is how §12's workaround rule gets earned twice. What it could never do is COUNT, which is now `reasoningChars` on `LocalChatResult` and `ai_queries.reasoning_chars`.

⚠ **THE COLUMN IS NULLABLE WITH NO DEFAULT, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** NULL means "logged before this existed"; `0` means "ran with reasoning off". A `0` default would have retro-dated 3,982 rows as having done no thinking and the before/after this column exists to make would have read as already won.

**Three mechanisms tried, one works, and it is binary.** `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}` does nothing here (80.4s, reasoning still produced — and SLOWER than the default). `/no_think` in the prompt does nothing (35.1s, 1,023 tokens). `reasoning_effort: 'low'` is not a middle setting (39.0s / 859 tokens against ~37s / ~900 for the default). `reasoning_effort: 'none'` works: **0.3s and 6 completion tokens** against 37.3s on the same classification. Hence one value on `PromptReasoning`, not a scale.

Proven through the platform's own code path, not just curl — one real obligation extraction over `COMMITMENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`: **49.2s / 3,043 tokens / 10,836 chars of reasoning → 2.9s / 157 tokens / 0.** 17x, and the reasoning accounting lines up with the table above (10,836 chars ≈ 2,700 of the 3,043 tokens, 89%).

**So the knob shipped first, defaulting to today's behaviour, and then the measurement said no.** `reasoning?: 'none'` and `jsonSchema?` on `LocalChatOptions`, both ABSENT by default so the request is byte-for-byte what it was; `PromptReasoning` (`'think' | 'none'`) declared beside each prompt's own version constant, because whether an answer survives without thinking is a property of the PROMPT and a per-call answer would drift between the several callers a prompt grows. `wireReasoning('think')` returns `undefined` — ⚠ **deliberately no way to spell "think" as a wire value**, so an unmeasured prompt cannot pin a server default that later changes.

⚠ **THE DOCUMENT PASS NEEDED THE CHOICE TO *TRAVEL*, NOT TO DEFAULT.** `runDocumentAiPass` takes its prompt as a PARAMETER, and one of its fourteen callers overrides it (`/api/opportunities/documents`, `opp-doc-summary-1.0`). Defaulting `reasoning` to the doc-summary declaration would have applied one prompt's measurement to another nobody measured — §12's "every source that can reach it needs an arm". An overriding caller defaults to `'think'`.

**`scripts/measure-reasoning-off.mts` — and ⚠ THREE OF ITS OWN BUGS WERE THE INSTRUCTIVE PART, every one a §12 rule earned again by the thing written to enforce it.**

⚠ **(1) It printed `corpus 1000 calls` for a task holding 1,283.** PostgREST truncates at 1000 silently and `.limit(2000)` does not beat it. A script reading a truncated set is worse than none, because it is believed. Paginated.

⚠ **(2) It scored `doc-summary` on a field that prompt has never produced.** `DocSummary` is `{summary?, confidence?}` and nothing else; `decisionFields: ['doc_type']` compared ∅ against ∅ and would have reported **8/8 agreement having examined nothing.** Now a declared field neither arm returns ABORTS the task and names it, and a prompt with no verdict field prints both answers for a human instead of claiming a rate.

⚠ **(3) THE WORST ONE, BECAUSE IT INVERTED A RESULT.** Commitments scored `matched 0, only-on 0, only-off 0` — both arms finding NO obligations — as AGREE. Five of the eight pairs were empty both ways, so the reported **"agreement 5/8" was 4/5 vacuous**: on the three pairs that held any content at all, reasoning-off agreed **0 of 3**. A pair where neither arm produced anything is now excluded from the denominator and reported separately.

**The design decision worth keeping: BOTH ARMS RUN NOW, never against the logged answer.** The obvious harness replays a stored input and diffs the stored response — and that is wrong here, because the system prompt is not logged (only the user message is), so a disagreement could not be told apart from a prompt rewrite since. The stored corpus supplies only the INPUT. ⚠ And the inputs it can supply are biased SHORT, because `logAiQuery` truncates `query_text` at 2,000 characters and roughly half of every task's corpus is over it — printed on every run beside the corpus's own distribution, because a clean result licenses reasoning-off for the lengths sampled and no further.

⚠ **AND A KILLED CLIENT DOES NOT STOP THE SERVER, WHICH COST THE MIDDLE OF THIS SESSION.** Generation here is deliberately UNBUDGETED — no `max_tokens` is sent (Richard's call 2026-07-11, "the local model is free") — so a trivial prompt at `JUDGEMENT_TEMPERATURE` fell into the repetition loop `gemini.ts` already warns about and generated without bound. Killing the probe freed the client and llama-server **kept going**: `lms ps` read `GENERATING` with nothing attached, every later request queued behind an answer nobody would ever read, and three separate probes timed out looking exactly like a hung script. Cleared with `lms unload` + `lms load -c 131072 --parallel 1`, then `lmstudio-check.sh` to confirm the documented state. **Never kill a client mid-generation on this box; and a `max_tokens` ceiling is the real fix.**

**AND THEN THE MEASUREMENT REFUSED MOST OF WHAT THE PLAN EXPECTED TO SHIP.** Eight real logged inputs per prompt, both arms run in the same session against the same current prompt:

| prompt | agreement | latency | tokens | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| thread-summary | **5/8** | 42.6s → 4.9s (8.7x) | 2,493 → 268 | **keeps reasoning** |
| commitments | **0/3** (5 empty both ways) | 29.3s → 1.5s (20.0x) | 1,732 → 36 | **keeps reasoning** |
| drive-filing | 7/8 | 24.5s → 2.3s (10.8x) | 1,570 → 54 | human arm below |
| intake-predecide | **8/8** | 19.9s → 2.3s (8.6x) | 1,207 → 85 | **flipped** |

⚠ **`thread-summary` FAILED ON THE FIELD THAT MATTERS MOST.** `deal_name` held 8/8, but `relevance` went 7/8 with its one miss in the expensive direction — reasoning-on said `operational`, reasoning-off said **`noise`**, and a noise verdict is a thread never read again (§12 already records 48 threads left unsearchable by exactly that column). One in eight at 954 calls a month is ~119 threads silently dropped. `counterparty` was 5/8, losing *"LiveSafe USA"* and *"Caseut"* to null, and `people`/`key_facts`/`open_items` came back consistently thinner — the fields feeding contact creation and the reduce phase. ⚠ **This also killed the obvious follow-up before it was built:** a cheap reasoning-off TRIAGE pass with full extraction only for the 34% of threads that are not noise would be a 2.2x win on 12.1 GPU-hours a month, and 7/8 on `relevance` is not a gate worth building on.

⚠ **`commitments` WAS THE CLEAREST FAIL, AND THE REPORTED NUMBER HID IT.** On the three pairs holding any content, reasoning-off **invented obligations reasoning-on did not find** — *"Ensure all future communications state that proposal numbers are approximate"*, owner *"Bear Wilson"* (misspelled), at **0.95 confidence** — and on another it **flipped `side` from `them` to `us`**, which is §12's own recorded bug: resolving `side` wrongly says someone owes themselves. 20x faster and unusable.

⚠ **REASONING-OFF IS SYSTEMATICALLY MORE CONFIDENT, WHICH IS THE WRONG DIRECTION FOR A CONFIDENCE GATE.** Seen on every task reporting one (0.7→0.85, 0.9→0.95, 0.75→0.85). Confidence is what holds a doubtful answer back: `FILING_CONFIDENCE` sends an unsure document to `_Unsorted` rather than into a tree the team trusts, and `AUTO_DISMISS_CONFIDENCE = 0.85` is what lets a dismissal act with no human. No sample crossed either bar — but a pass that is wronger AND surer has worse brakes.

⚠ **`doc-summary` HAS NO VERDICT FIELD, AND WITHOUT REASONING IT WROTE A SUMMARY OF A DOCUMENT IT HAD NOT BEEN GIVEN.** Six pairs read by hand. Handed a 31-character input (a file name, no extracted text) reasoning-on correctly refused — *"the submission contains only a patent filename… no actionable intelligence can be extracted"* — and reasoning-off **fabricated the document**, inventing an assignee: *"a US patent for managing construction project data, involving parties such as inventors and assignees like Autodesk, Inc."* On a parcel schedule the two arms counted **26 against 24**. A fabricated summary is the worst available failure for this field, because `list_documents` presents a document BY its summary, so the agent would cite the invention as evidence.

⚠ **AND THE HUMAN-VERDICT ARM IS WHAT CAUGHT `drive-filing`, WHICH AGREEMENT HAD PASSED AT 7/8.** Agreement cannot say which arm was right, so the one task where a human later ruled got scored against the human: a document with `filing_confirmed_at` set is one somebody looked at and said "it is right where it is", and `drive_folder_path` says where. The logged input carries `DOCUMENT FILE NAME:`, so the row joins back with nothing reconstructed — the candidate list in the message is the one the model actually saw. ⚠ A file name matching two documents is SKIPPED, not guessed (8 were), and 3 more were filed outside the candidate list; the honest population is **8 cases**. Result: **reasoning ON correct 6/8, reasoning OFF correct 4/8.**

⚠ **ITS FAILURE MODE IS *TIDYING*, WHICH IS WHY THE PROMPT'S OWN RULE EXISTS.** The real folder is `Dueschesne County Rail Corridor` — misspelled in Drive. Reasoning-off "corrected" it to `Duchesne County Rail Corridor`, which is not a candidate, so `coerce` throws it away and the document lands in `_Unsorted`. The prompt already says *"copied EXACTLY from the candidate list, character for character. Do not reword, re-case, pluralise, or tidy it"* — and §12 has the general form: a prompt can only ASK.

**AND THAT IS WHERE THE `jsonSchema` HALF STOPPED BEING SPECULATIVE.** The plan shipped it on the theory that a schema is "what makes reasoning-off safe", with no caller — which §11 calls complexity without demonstrated need and §12 calls decoration. The human arm supplied the need: tidying is a failure a prompt can only ASK to prevent, and an enum of the candidate folders removes the option at the sampler. A third arm was added and measured:

| arm | correct against the human | answers outside the candidate list |
|---|---|---|
| reasoning on | 6/8 | 0 |
| reasoning off | 4/8, then 5/8 on a re-run | 1 |
| **reasoning off + candidate enum** | **6/8** | **0** |

So `drive-filing` holds `'none'` **only paired with that schema**, built per call from `decidable` because the candidate list is per record, with `null` as a member because "none of these is clearly right" is an answer the prompt asks for. ⚠ No type can express that pairing, so `reasoning.test.ts` asserts it: if the declaration reads `'none'`, the enum must be at the call site. ⚠ **And n = 8 with a run-to-run spread of ±1, so "6/8 against 6/8" means indistinguishable at this sample size, not equal.** It is held anyway on two grounds that do not depend on the sample — the enum structurally removes the one systematic failure found, and `coerce` already rejects an out-of-list answer, so the worst case is `_Unsorted` rather than the wrong folder of a tree the team trusts.

**WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED, AND IT IS A THIRD OF WHAT THE PLAN PROJECTED.** Three of six prompts hold `'none'`: `intake-predecide` (8/8), `commitment-chase` (better prose without it), `drive-filing` (with the enum). Three keep reasoning: `thread-summary`, `doc-summary`, `commitments` — which are the three biggest, 1,932 of the 2,240 calls. **~2.2 of 58.9 GPU-hours a month, about 4%**, against the 28.3 the opening measurement made look available.

⚠ **THE HONEST HEADLINE IS THAT THE MEASUREMENT REFUSED THE WORK, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS THE ASSET.** `reasoning_effort: 'none'` is not a free 9x; on this model it trades accuracy for latency, and it trades it worst exactly where the volume is. But `ai_queries.reasoning_chars` now makes the cost legible instead of inferable, and the harness is re-runnable in one command — which matters because §2 says a chat model is swappable at will and all of this is a property of THIS model. The next `LOCAL_AI_MODEL` gets re-measured, not re-argued.

**ON THE OTHER HALF OF THE QUESTION — GSUITE — THE DELIVERABLE WAS A RETRACTION.** Surveyed every scope and every Google module: 3 mailboxes swept, the Drive knowledge sync, Docs + PDF composition, the two-way task Sheet, the contacts push, the Meet importer, the hourly audio folder. It is well used, and the unexploited pieces are each already decided.

⚠ **I PROPOSED SWITCHING THE KNOWLEDGE SYNC TO DRIVE'S `changes.list`, RICHARD APPROVED IT, AND THEN READING THE CODE SHOWED THE PREMISE WAS FALSE.** The claim was that a file a teammate moves or deletes in the shared Drive goes unnoticed. Both sync phases already reconcile: `syncDriveKnowledge` builds a `seenIds` set from the full walk and retires everything absent (`drive-sync.ts:433-444`, with `superseded_by_hand` and a restore path), and `syncProjectFolders` does the same. It is live rather than merely present — **69 documents retired, 13 of them automatically, most recently 10-22.** A delta feed would be strictly WORSE: it cannot retire what it never sees, and a lost page token stops noticing with nothing reporting it. The full walk over 154 documents IS the reconciliation. Dropped, and said so rather than building the approved thing.

**Also checked and deliberately not touched.** `upsertCalendarEvent` still has zero callers and `calendar.events` is still granted on all three mailboxes — Richard declined calendar publishing on 10-15 (*"he does not want calendar clutter"*), and the volume would have been small anyway: of 55 future-dated leads only **4** are undecided. `email-attachment-1.0` returning non-JSON on 9 of 9 calls is `jsonMode: false` working correctly, not a bug — checked before reporting it.

Recorded in OPEN-ITEMS rather than fixed blind.

**Done 2026-10-26 (email becomes the channel that must arrive, and the only delivery check in the system that PROVES rather than infers):**

Richard, after being shown the T-Mobile block found earlier the same day: *"Make email the channel that must arrive."* Option (c) of the three offered.

**What this is NOT: a fallback.** The two channels now have different STANDING, and that distinction is the whole change. Email is sent FIRST and its failure is the pass's failure — what a cron reports, what `notification_log` records as `failed`, what a health card goes red over. Text is still sent, because it is instant and it is on the phone, but its failure is a NOTE and never a failure. ⚠ **Folding a blocked text into the verdict would mark a morning that WAS delivered `failed`, and the next re-run would then send it twice** — which is why `PairResult.error` carries the email's error and nothing else, documented on the field itself.

Four passes were text-only or text-first: `task_week`, `task_due_today`, `record_alert`, `document_ready`. ⚠ **ONE SHARED SENDER, NOT FOUR EDITS** — `notifyPair` in `src/lib/notify/pair.ts`, because §12's rule is that a convention every caller has to remember is the one that goes missing in the route added next year, and four copies of "email first, text best-effort" is four places for that standing to drift. `agent_answer` already paired (10-23) and already sent email first, so it needed only the sender fixed.

⚠ **AND THE RECIPIENT LIST WAS THE REAL BUG, FOUND BY READING THE LOOP RATHER THAN THE DOCBLOCK.** `record_alert` iterated **`textTargets()`** — so an empty `PEPPER_TEXT_TARGETS`, a malformed entry, or simply a person with no handle meant **NOBODY was told that a recording had created a deal**, and the pass said so in a note nobody reads. That is the dependency exactly inverted: the transport was deciding the audience. Once email is the channel that must arrive, the list is the PEOPLE (`loadPepperMembers`) and a handle is an optional extra. The claim row's `team_member_id` stopped being nullable at the same time, since the member is now how the loop is keyed.

⚠ **THE SAFETY CHECK CAME BEFORE THE FEATURE, AND IT HAD TO.** This adds an email from Pepper into `moose@`/`tuaone@` **every weekday morning** — the swept deal mailboxes. That is the 2026-10-09 failure precisely: 131 of 481 open commitments were Pepper reading her own morning notes, compounding daily. Proven, not reasoned about: fetched the real delivered thread and ran `prefilterThread` over it → `SKIPPED — Written by the platform (no human message on the thread)`. `isPlatformMail` keys on the assistant seat's **ADDRESS**, so no display name can reopen it, and a human reply rescues the thread. **This is also why the mail goes as `info@` rather than `moose@`** — sending as Richard's own address would leave that guard resting on the display name matching `PLATFORM_SENDER_NAME`, which §12 says is not a contract. The `agent_answer` email had exactly that weakness and was moved to `info@` in this change.

⚠ **EMAIL CAN BE ASSERTED POSITIVELY, AND THAT ASYMMETRY IS WHY THE DECISION IS SOUND.** `text-delivery.ts` (10-21) can only ever report the ABSENCE of a bounce — evidence, never proof, because a gateway returns no receipt. The platform holds a credential for the RECIPIENT'S mailbox, so `reportEmailDelivery()` looks in the inbox the message was sent to and finds the thing itself. **It is the only delivery check in this system that proves rather than infers**, and it took three corrections to be worth reading:

1. ⚠ **IT FIRST REPORTED `found 5` AGAINST `claimed 1`** — counting every other thing `info@` had ever sent that mailbox, so it would have passed on mail with nothing to do with the notification. **A check that cannot fail is worse than no check.** Anchored the window at the most recent claimed send.
2. ⚠ **THEN IT CORRECTLY SAID `missing` FOR ERIC** — a `task_week` logged `sent` at 06:45 with no email in his mailbox, because that run predated the change and was TEXT ONLY. A verdict must not be computed over rows that predate the fact it tests. Keyed the filter on the recorded **`channel`** rather than a cutover date, so it needs no maintenance and stays right if a kind ever drops back to one channel.
3. ⚠ **AND `agent_answer` HAD TO COME OUT OF THE ASSERTED SET** — verified against the table, not assumed: its rows carry `team_member_id = NULL` and are keyed on the message id, because that pass needs per-CHANNEL idempotency rather than per-person. Listing a kind the check cannot structurally see is the same "cannot fail" trap in a third place. The omission is named in the constant's docblock with its reason, as is `lead_handoff`'s.

**The health page now has two cards where it had one, and only one of them can go red.** `Text Delivery (best-effort)` is capped at `warn` — a carrier block is a known accepted condition now, and §12 is explicit that when every row is red, red has stopped signifying. `Email Delivery (must arrive)` carries the obligation.

⚠ **AND THE FIRST LIVE EMAIL EXPOSED A §12 VIOLATION I HAD JUST WRITTEN.** Subject `Your week: 7 tasks with a date` landed above a body saying `5 of yours due this week`, because `taskCount` is `thisWeek + overdue` and the body reports those two APART, which is correct. **Two different quantities must be named apart and never summed**, and one quantity must have one definition or the reader trusts neither. The subject carries no count at all now; the body owns the numbers.

**Verified live, end to end rather than by dry run.** Forced a real `task_week` run: both executives `emailed: true, texted: true`, then read it back from each recipient's own mailbox — `From: "Pepper" <info@berwilson.com>`, the five dated tasks, the link, signed. **Eric's week-ahead is the message T-Mobile permanently rejected this morning; it is now in his mailbox.** 695 tests, typecheck clean, lint clean. **DEPLOYED**

**Done 2026-10-26 (who Pepper's texts come from, and the carrier block that was rejecting them):**

Richard: *"Make sure that when notifications are texted to Eric or myself, that they come from info@berwilson.com signed as 'Pepper'."*

⚠ **MEASURING FIRST SPLIT ONE ASK INTO A HALF ALREADY DONE AND A HALF NOBODY HAD CHECKED — AND THE SECOND WAS NOT THE ONE ASKED ABOUT.** The instruction reads as one change. It is three things, because a carrier delivers them independently and any one of them can be the only one that survives: the envelope, the subject (which a gateway renders into the delivered message), and the body's signature (the only one a carrier cannot strip).

**The envelope was already right, and the way to know that was to read the sent mail.** Not the code — the code's default is only a default, and `PEPPER_TEXT_FROM` being unset is indistinguishable from it being set correctly until something reads the wire. All 11 Pepper gateway sends in `info@`'s own Sent folder over 30 days read `from: {"name":"Pepper","address":"info@berwilson.com"}`. So that half needed no change and is now **pinned by a test** (`gatewaySender()`), because an unset variable deciding an identity is how one drifts with nobody editing it.

⚠ **ONE COMPOSER OF FOUR SIGNED ITSELF, WHICH IS WHY THE ASK WAS MADE.** `record_alert` has pushed `'— Pepper'` since 10-19 — it was built from an instruction that said to. The three live passes added since (`task_week`/`task_due_today`, `document_ready`, `agent_answer`) each went out unsigned, and the SQL says so: of the texts in `pepper_outbound_texts`, only the three `record_alert` bodies match `ilike '%pepper%'`. A convention held in a composer rather than at the choke point is a convention the pass added next year will not have (§12), so `signAsPepper()` now runs inside `sendText` and covers every pass there will ever be.

**Two details in that signer are the whole of it.** ⚠ **It signs BEFORE the body is hashed.** The self-loop guard works by hashing what goes out and having ingestion drop what it finds in `pepper_outbound_texts`; signing after the hash would put a body on the wire that hashes to something the ledger does not hold — the 2026-10-09 failure (131 of 481 open commitments were Pepper reading her own notes) rebuilt by a signature. One value is hashed, recorded and sent. ⚠ **And it is IDEMPOTENT, matching a WHOLE LINE rather than by containment**, which is what preserves `record_alert`'s deliberate shape: it puts its signature ABOVE the record's link, *"where a single tap lands"*, so a blind append would both double the signature and move it to the bottom. Containment would have been wrong in the other direction too — prose that merely says “— Pepper” mid-sentence is not a signed text, and reading it as one ships an unsigned one. The subject moved `'Ber AI'` → `'Pepper'` in the same change: `Ber AI` is the system's name, and the first thing a text should answer is who is speaking. Rendered all four live shapes end to end afterwards — one signature each, record_alert's link still last.

⚠ **AND THEN THE REAL FINDING, WHICH RICHARD DID NOT ASK ABOUT: T-MOBILE IS REJECTING THESE TEXTS.** Reading `info@`'s Sent folder to verify the From header also turned up **seven `Delivery Status Notification` messages from `mailer-daemon` in the same 30 days** — six Delay and, on 10-26 itself, one **Failure**. Every one carries the same string from T-Mobile's own MTA (`tmo-west.mx.a.cloudfilter.net`):

```
452 4.1.0 <info@berwilson.com> server temporarily unavailable AUP#MXRT
```

Per handle: **Richard 9 sent / 3 delayed / 0 failed; Eric 4 sent / 3 delayed / 1 permanently failed.** It names `<info@berwilson.com>` — our SENDER, not the handles — which is why it hits both executives, and `AUP#MXRT` is T-Mobile's acceptable-use rate/reputation block rather than a transient fault. Gmail retries a delayed message for 21–46 hours, so the real behaviour of this channel is: some arrive, some arrive LATE (a 06:45 task reminder landing the next afternoon is worse than silence), and at least one arrived never.

⚠ **THE PLATFORM HAD KNOWN FOR DAYS AND THE VERDICT WAS COMPUTED FOR NOBODY.** `reportTextDelivery()`, built 10-21 for exactly this, returns `bounced` for BOTH handles when run — it works, it is correct, and it names the diagnostic string. It reaches two places: `/settings/health`, which has to be opened, and `describeTextDelivery()`, which rides the morning note — **one of the channels held since 10-21 because the content was not useful**. So the §12 rule this very channel wrote — *assert DELIVERY, not configuration* — was discharged, and then the assertion's only unprompted reader was switched off. **A check whose report rides a held channel is a check nobody runs.** Not fixed in code, because nothing in code fixes a carrier block; filed as the newest row in [`OPEN-ITEMS.md`](OPEN-ITEMS.md) with the three calls (clear the sender's reputation with T-Mobile; move to an A2P vendor, which means bodies leaving the box against the 07-07 cutover; or accept text as best-effort and make email the channel that must arrive).

| relevance | linked | threads | attachments | imported |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| noise | no | 191 | 331 | **0** |
| operational | no | 129 | 267 | **0** |
| deal | no | 102 | 211 | **0** |
| deal | yes | 78 | 263 | 86 |

Not documents, not mail chunks, not a queue, not a health card. ⚠ **A TARGET ON THE EXISTING PASS, NEVER A FORK.** `importThreadAttachments` is ~250 lines of measured fixes — a per-message cursor that survives a kickstart, a failed byte fetch that HOLDS the cursor so the file is retried rather than lost, content-hash dedupe performed AFTER the fetch because a name is not evidence of sameness, mail-chrome rejection by NAME because `isInline` is not sufficient, and the sibling test that stopped one thread's attachments fanning onto three records. A second copy for unparented mail would have inherited none of them and would have been invisible as a fork, because it would not have looked like one — it would have looked like a sibling module for a new source (§12). So `ImportDestination` is a three-arm union and the three destinations differ only in which table the row goes in, whether a record id is on it, which watermark advances, whether siblings exist, and whether a Drive copy follows. Each is a branch of five lines or fewer, which is the test for whether it should have been a parameter.

⚠ **THE CURSOR COULD NOT BE FAKED WITH A PLACEHOLDER LINK**, which was the first idea. `thread_links` means "this conversation is about this record" and is read by the router, the apply pass, retrieval's filing filter, the confidentiality filter and `reapOrphanedLinks`; a row pointing at nothing would need special-casing in every one, and the one that forgot would read a non-existent record as a real filing. ⚠ **THE CHECK CONSTRAINT WAS FOUND BY RUNNING IT, WITH `tsc`, THE BUILD AND 682 TESTS GREEN.** The first live run refused every insert with `documents_scope_check`: that constraint enumerates what a document is OF — a project, an entity, company knowledge, a reference, a meeting, a steel deal — and had no member for "off deal mail, parent not yet decided". A CHECK is invisible to the typechecker, the build and the suite alike. ⚠ **AND `is_reference` SATISFIES IT AND IS STILL THE WRONG ANSWER**, which was the second idea: that flag means *a human uploaded this to READ it*, backs the /intake reading shelf (30 rows, newest first) and gates `/intake/document/[id]`, so routing 809 mail attachments through it would have pushed every genuinely uploaded document off the list and quietly changed what the shelf means. A purpose flag and a parentage state are two different questions. So `documents.awaiting_filing`, set by the import and cleared by `refileDocument`/`excludeDocument` — one positive discriminator rather than an inference across three nullable columns, which also leaves the 13 pre-existing parentless rows (from elsewhere, never a filing question) untouched. ⚠ The excess-property check then refused the shared `excludeDocument` patch, correctly: `opportunity_documents` has no such column.

⚠ **65% OF DEAL MAIL WAS WITHHELD FROM RETRIEVAL, AND THE GATE JUDGED PROSE.** 1,277 of 1,895 summarized deal threads were `relevance='noise'` and excluded by `email_threads_pending_embed`. Sampling them, the gate's correct rejects are genuinely correct — eSignature notifications, calendar accepts and cancellations, out-of-office replies, a Drive folder-share notice, a work order for a 2019 Toyota 4Runner. But the wrong ones share one unmistakable shape: **a three-word body carrying eight to fourteen files.** `Requested information` (14 attachments), `Powers Mines` (11), `Fwd: Steel pricing` (8 across four messages), `Fw: Deeds` (5), `bplan and financial model` (4), `Fwd: ALABAMA FERRY FIELD` (4), `Data Center Discussion` (3 messages). The summarizer reads PROSE, and the most document-dense threads in the corpus have almost none of it.

⚠ **AND THE CONTRADICTION THAT PROVED IT: 18 of those threads were ALREADY FILED to a record by the router**, which had matched them on an identity — a solicitation number, a learned identifier, an asserted alias — while the summarizer called the same thread noise. Two passes over one thread returning opposite verdicts means at least one is wrong, and only one of them looked at a fact. So the widening is on two FACTS and never on another model's score, the same shape as the record-creation rule in `from-recording.ts`: an attachment (`>= 1`), or a real back-and-forth (`message_count >= 3`, because a notification never gets two replies). Both `coalesce`d — ⚠ both columns are nullable and `null >= 1` is NULL, which is not true, so an uncoalesced comparison would have withheld exactly the rows it was written to admit and reported it as an empty result rather than an error.

⚠ **NO CURSOR CLEAR WAS NEEDED, AND REACHING FOR ONE WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WRONG INSTINCT.** A withheld thread was never STAMPED — `embedded_at` is filtered in SQL, never written, precisely so the question can be re-asked for free — so all 335 already carried a NULL cursor and the view returned them the moment it was replaced. Verified immediately: 0 pending before, 334 after, with no UPDATE against any row. **The live sweep then drained it with no rebuild at all**, because a view is database state rather than build state: watched at 20-second intervals, `view_pending` 40 → 31 → 22 while `indexed_deal` went 843 → 852 → 861. Final: **667 → 883 deal threads indexed**, 897 still withheld, and all 228 attachment-bearing noise threads now carry chunks.

⚠ **THE VOICE-MEMO DOOR HAD BEEN SHUT SIX DAYS AND ONLY THE HEALTH PAGE KNEW.** `CloudRecordings.db-wal` had not been touched since 10-19 06:37 and Voice Memos.app was not running on the Studio — iCloud syncs it only while it runs. Messages and Notes were both up, so those doors were fine; this one was shut by nothing more than an app having been quit. The sweep detects it correctly and prints it in its own log notes, and `probeVoiceMemos` reports it on `/settings/health` — neither is a channel anybody reads on a given morning, and Pepper's outbound notes are held, so the detection was right and the outcome was still six lost days. ⚠ **A CHANNEL WHOSE SETUP CANNOT BE AUTOMATED IS A CHANNEL THAT IS OFF** (§12, proven over seven days of `Couldn't find shortcut`), and "remember to leave Voice Memos open" is exactly that kind of manual step — so it is a `KeepAlive` launchd agent rather than a line of documentation. ⚠ **BY BUNDLE ID, AFTER THE DISPLAY NAME FAILED:** `open -a "Voice Memos"` returned `Unable to find application named 'Voice Memos'` (the bundle is `/System/Applications/VoiceMemos.app`, no space) **while `launchctl list` still reported the job LOADED** — a job that is loaded and failing looks exactly like one that is working, and only its own error log said otherwise. `com.apple.VoiceMemos` is the identifier that survives a rename or a localisation. Loaded, app up, snapshot kicked, probe `failed` → `ok` with the store 0h old.

⚠ **AND §12's OWN WAL RULE HAD NOT REACHED EITHER LOCAL-SOURCE PROBE.** The rule is already written down — *a FILE's mtime is not its DATA's clock where the writer keeps a write-ahead log; take the newest mtime across the set* — and both `probeVoiceMemos` and `probeIMessageSweep` were still statting the `.db` alone, whose mtime is the last CHECKPOINT. Measured: `CloudRecordings.db` 10 days old against a `-wal` of 6, so the health page reported **251h against a real 155h** — overstating a real outage by four days, on the one check whose entire job is to be believed. Overstating is as corrosive as missing it: a check that cries wolf louder than the truth is one nobody reads on the day it is right. Fixed as ONE shared `snapshotAgeMs()` helper, because two copies are exactly how it drifted into existence. Voice memos now 155h → 0h, iMessage 2h and `ok`.

**The disposition half of Richard's question had a different answer: `/decide` is the best-built thing here and needed no ergonomic work.** Per-class accept with the destination named in the button, batch tick, one confirm on accept, free reversible dismiss, optimistic with a trailing refresh, and it reports the cost of leaving each row — distinguishing "not indexed" from "indexed with its thread". The problem was entirely what never reached it: there was no class for mail carrying unimported files, so the 809 were not a chore anybody was behind on, they were invisible. It gains a third document class, `unparented`, ⚠ **named apart from the other two because the costs are opposites**: an unfiled company document is ANSWERING, wrongly, for every project-scoped question; a misfiled one answers for the WRONG DEAL; one of these answers for NOTHING. One label for three quantities is how a reader stops trusting any of them. The badge, `countDecideItems` and `summarizeDecideQueue` all gained the lane in the same change — `DecideSummary.unparented` is REQUIRED, so `tsc` named the one fixture that needed it.

⚠ **AND THE HELD COUNT NEEDED A REAL DOOR, NOT JUST A NUMBER.** `/decide` only ever offers a row it can NAME a destination for; everything `matchDocument` cannot place is held out so the queue can reach zero. On the first live import that was **4 of 4** — `BW MNDA (with Non-Circumvention)` names no record and neither does a `Quit Claim Deed`. Held is the right verdict for a MATCHER and the wrong place to stop for a HUMAN, who knows which counterparty the MNDA was for: these rows do not need a better matcher, they need a PICKER. So `/documents/unfiled`, a thin page over the SAME reader (`loadCompanyKnowledge('unparented')` — a scope parameter, not a sibling module), the same matcher and the existing refile route. ⚠ Deliberately NOT `CompanyKnowledgeBase`, though it renders the same type: that component carries `DOC_TYPES` of capability statements and past performance and a `guessType` that reads file names for "cap state", none of which means anything for a counterparty's term sheet — a shared renderer wired to a surface it does not fit is worse than no shared renderer.

**Three checks were wrong before the code was, and each one looked like a real failure.** ⚠ **`grep -c "coalesce"` against `pg_get_viewdef` returned 0** because Postgres prints `COALESCE` uppercase — the view was correct. ⚠ **The verification script's own recovered-arm assertion decayed into a vacuous pass within the hour**: it read the pending VIEW for an attachment-bearing thread, which works only while the backlog is undrained, and once the sweep caught up the view was empty BY DESIGN. Re-pointed at the OUTCOME (are these threads indexed?), which stays true permanently — a count that is only meaningful before the fix has landed is not a regression test. ⚠ **And that rewrite then hit PostgREST's 1000-row truncation**, silently: one thread holds many chunks, so `.in(thread_id, <200 ids>)` asked for a couple of thousand rows and got exactly 1000, which showed as "98 of 200 not indexed" and read as a real failure of the gate. psql said 228 of 228. A verification script reading a truncated set is worse than none because it is believed, and this one very nearly was. Paginated with `.range()`.

**Verification.** 682 tests (6 new, on the migration as the real artifact since the predicate lives in the view and has no TypeScript copy to call — ⚠ with comments stripped first, or the test measures its own documentation, and **a violation planted twice to prove each arm still fails**). Lint 22, the documented baseline. Idempotency proven the way §12 asks: the pass pinned to threads it had already read reports them gone from the queue — 419 → 412 pending, the four read threads absent, no file imported twice. The render exercised directly for every interpolated value with no `NaN`/`undefined`/`Infinity` reaching the markup — ⚠ checking only values that pass the component's own guards, because a check that stringifies a guarded value reports a bug the reader could never see. ⚠ And a comment claiming `loadTargets()` returns leads was corrected once checked: it selects from `projects` and `opportunities` only, so the narrowing is a type obligation rather than a filter on real data — a comment claiming a control that is not there is worse than no comment.

**Live result:** 6 documents imported and summarised off mail that had never yielded a file — a `$150K Contract for a NI 43-101`, `Ber_Wilson_People_Strategy_Proposal`, two MNDAs — 411 threads and ~800 files still owed, draining at 25 threads an hour through the new `unparented` sweep phase. Deployed: committed, pushed, built (exit 0 captured unpiped), kickstarted explicitly rather than probed against the process being replaced, both tailnet listeners asserted, LM Studio matching its documented config.

**Done 2026-10-25 (ask it and walk away — the notification decided by attention rather than by a stopwatch, and three things the first live answer exposed):**

Richard, having had the limits explained: *"So have we made it as powerful and capable as we can while protecting major code changes (which I would be ok with, but I know claude Opus is a superior model)? Please expand its capabilities if you can think of anything. For Ask AI, I need to be able to close it while it thinks. I don't want to wait while it finds answers. It should send an in app notification when complete and an email. Make sure these are providing the best user experience possible."*

## What was already there, which is most of it

**MEASURING FIRST TURNED THIS FROM A BUILD INTO A ONE-LINE CHANGE AND THREE BUGS.** Before writing anything:

- The run has always survived the asker leaving — `nothing here reads request.signal` is a comment in the route, put there deliberately.
- `agent_messages.run_state` + `run_started_at` is a reattach point, and `pollForAnswer` is one poller with two callers.
- A toast already fired when the dock was closed.
- `notifyAnswer` already texted a pointer and emailed the whole answer, and `notification_log` showed **8 `agent_answer` rows sent** — so it was live, not theoretical (the 10-23 session had found 0 and could not tell whether it worked).

**So the gap was one decision, and it was answering the wrong question.** The email was gated on a 90-second stopwatch, set against a measured 73s median on the stated premise that *"a fast answer is one you are still looking at"*. Richard's instruction makes that premise false: the intent is to walk away from EVERY question. **Measured the same day: 40 of 72 answers — 56% — came back under 90 seconds.** On the majority of questions, closing the dock meant being told nowhere at all.

## Attention is a fact, not a guess

The new question is "was anybody watching", and two independent sources answer it:

- **The connection, in ONE direction only**, which is why the parameter is `false | null` and never `true`. A DROPPED connection is proof nobody is there. An OPEN one proves nothing — ⚠ **`AskBerAIDock` stays mounted while CLOSED** so the conversation survives ⌘J, which is right, and means the stream is still held by a dock the asker walked away from ten minutes ago. Open reports `null` and falls back to the clock, which is exactly the old behaviour and therefore no regression for anybody.
- **The browser, properly**: dock open AND tab visible. Either alone is not enough. It reports to `/api/ai/agent/answers`, and ⚠ **`notifyAnswer` was already idempotent on `notification_log`'s `unique (kind, dedupe_key)`**, so both paths firing sends once — machinery that already existed and needed nothing.

⚠ **A BADGE, NOT AN INBOX.** An in-app notification inbox was built here and deleted on 2026-09-24: 52 rows in eight days and **zero** ever read or dismissed. The lesson is not "no in-app signal", it is that a second place to go is a place nobody goes. So: one count on the header button already in use, reading `agent_messages.seen_at`, cleared by opening the dock. ⚠ **Never `localStorage`** — §12, browser storage for content that lives in the database is not a cache but the only copy the page can see, and the entire premise here is that the answer arrived where the browser was not. ⚠ **And every existing answer is backfilled as seen**, or the badge would have launched announcing 72 historical answers, and a badge nobody believes on day one is one nobody reads on the day it is right.

**Proven live before anything else was touched:** a question asked with the dock closed came back in **69 seconds** — comfortably under the old bar, so previously silent — and sent both the email and the text, with the header reading **"1 answer ready"**.

## Then the feature's own first answer was wrong, and that found three more things

Asked *"how many contacts are tagged flightech-delegation"* it replied **"Zero contacts are tagged flightech-delegation — the tag doesn't appear to exist in the system"**, against a database holding **232**.

⚠ **THE AGENT COULD NOT SEE TAGS AT ALL.** `search_parties` neither filtered on `tags` nor returned them, so an entire import batch was invisible to the thing meant to answer about it. **The identical shape to `relationship_notes` two days earlier**: a column that exists, is populated, and has no retrieval path reaching it (§12). Adding a `tag` parameter is the fix; keeping the 53 role keys out of the declaration while putting tags in it is deliberate, because a tag is a free string a human typed and a role is a registry.

⚠ **AND FIXING IT NAIVELY MADE IT MUCH WORSE, IN A WAY ONLY MEASURING SHOWS.** Raising the row limit to 200 so a group query could answer "how many" — while still returning the full record — produced a **240,000-character tool result, about 60,000 tokens, nearly half the 131,072-token window, in a single call**, because each of the 232 contacts carried its ~700-character biography. That is what turned a count into a five-minute answer. Measured with `JSON.stringify(result).length` rather than estimated. A count does not need 232 biographies: a GROUP now returns names and the exact total, a NAMED search still returns everything. **240k → 13.9k characters, a 17× cut, with the count still exact.**

⚠ **AND THE COUNT IS COUNTED IN SQL, NEVER `data.length`.** §12 says never make the model count rows, print the count; `count: data.length` is worse than that, because it is confidently wrong the moment the limit bites — a tag holding 232 would have answered "200" and read as a fact. There is now a `head: true` exact count beside the rows, and a `note` telling the model to say the count rather than the length of the list.

⚠ **"ARTHUR FORD" FOUND NOTHING FOR `Arthur James Ford`.** Pre-existing — a phrase ILIKE cannot span a middle name — and the delegation import turned it from an edge case into the common one, 233 contacts filed under full legal names nobody would type. Falls back to requiring EVERY word on the name; any-word would hand back a stranger who merely shares a first name, which is the §12 failure that resolved "Cliff" to an unrelated academic.

## And a deploy was locking the dock for half an hour

⚠ **FOUND BY TRYING TO TYPE INTO IT.** An agent turn runs inside the web process, so a `launchctl kickstart` kills it before either verdict is written and the row stays `running` forever. The staleness horizon has to be the FULL time budget, because a 16-minute answer is real and has happened — so a run killed one minute ago still looks live for another twenty-nine, and the dock disables its input while it believes a run is in flight. Ask Ber AI sat unusable with *"Checking still working…"* against a process that no longer existed.

**A run that began BEFORE this process did cannot be running IN it.** That is a fact rather than a threshold and needs no tuning, which is why it beats shortening the window — a change that would instead abandon the slow answers the window exists to protect. ⚠ **Derived from `process.uptime()`, not `new Date()` at module scope**: the latter is the time of the first import, which under Next's lazy loading can be well after the process began, and every millisecond of that gap is a window where a genuinely live run looks dead and gets abandoned.

⚠ **AND THE DOCK-EVENT CONVENTION TEST REFUSED THE NEW EVENT, CORRECTLY.** The exemption is NAMED and then PROVED — each typed dispatcher must export its event constant, asserted — rather than the check being loosened to accommodate it (§12: a legitimate exemption gets named with its reason, never absorbed by raising the baseline).

676 tests (+3), lint 22 at baseline, 101 types / 100 live tables. Four commits, all deployed and all verified in the browser on the live host.

**Done 2026-10-24 (a roster no door could ingest, and then the door — Jobs, the working assistant):**

Richard, on a .docx with a Hebrew filename sitting in Downloads: *"Is Ber Intelligence smart enough to ingest a document like this to import contacts into our system? If so, where do I upload that?... I am just trying to understand the limits of what I can ask the local LLM to do."* Then, having been told: *"I want to import all of these contacts yourself, then I want you to either open up the doors for the qwen model... perhaps we have a separate area where we submit unique requests that use the full breadth of the LLM."* Then: *"I want this separate part to really accomplish any task I give it. Might be scrubbing through data or really any tasks that one might want to task AI to do. Lets make this like an additional assistant to Pepper that isn't built strictly around intelligence."*

## Part one — the roster

**Flightech Delegation | Participant Biographies, 18–22 October 2026.** 233 participants across nine city delegations (Chicago 43, Atlanta 32, Houston 28, San Francisco 27, Washington 25, New York 22, Miami 19, Los Angeles 19, Boston 17), each a headshot, a full name, a ~700-character biography and a source line. 183,000 characters, 225 embedded images.

**THE FIRST DELIVERABLE WAS A FACT ABOUT THE DOCUMENT, NOT A ROW COUNT: it carries no email address and no phone number. Not one, across all 233.** So these are a searchable who's-who and not a contact list anybody can write to, and that was said BEFORE importing rather than discovered after — against a rolodex of 163 that had just spent a session merging 11 duplicates. Richard read it and said import all 233 anyway, which is his call to make and was made with the fact in hand.

**THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION AS ASKED WAS NO, AND THE REASON MATTERS.** Three contact doors exist and the file fits none: **Cards** takes photographs (right shape — batch, stage, review — wrong input); **People** takes a typed list of at most 12 names and then reads *our own mail* for each, which is useless for 233 strangers who have never written to us and whose biography is already in hand; **Document** files it as knowledge and creates no contacts. The limit was never the model. Every automated path here is a deliberately built pipeline with a human confirm, so "can it do X" nearly always means "has a door been built for X".

**THREE THINGS THE PARSE CAUGHT THAT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE SHIPPED WRONG.** The parser asserts rather than hopes, and each assertion fired on real data:

- **A bio that is only a title line.** `Kristen Strezo Somerville City Councilor At-Large`, 48 characters, same shape as David Stapp's. Not malformed — the threshold was.
- ⚠ **TWO PEOPLE SHARE ONE EMBEDDED PHOTO.** `rId10` is referenced by both David Birnbaum and Henry Gilbert; 218 embeds, 217 distinct. Nothing in the document says which of them it depicts, so **NEITHER gets it** — a valid photograph of the wrong person is precisely the failure §12 names, and two missing headshots is a smaller loss than one stranger's face on a live contact. Those two want a photo by hand.
- **The "delegation" was being read off the wrong line.** The `Source:` footer mostly says `Flightech_Participant_Bios_Washington_Cancellation_13-10-2340.docx` — the compiler's own file name, not the person's city. Reading the city HEADERS instead turned five apparent delegations into the real nine.

**TITLE AND COMPANY CAME OUT OF THE BIOGRAPHY, NOT THE WEB.** The evidence was already in hand; asking the open web about 233 strangers would be slower, rate-limited (the Gemini key is free tier, 20/day) and less reliable than the paragraph their own organiser wrote. Batched eight at a time — 233 serial extraction calls is hours of LM Studio time for a job whose unit of work is two short strings — and **batching is the thing that mis-aligns silently, so each bio carries an index the model must echo back WITH the name, and a row whose name does not match the one sent is discarded.** Measured over the whole corpus: **233 of 233 read, 0 unmatched**, ~63s per batch of eight, 221 titles, 199 companies, 11 with neither (the title-only bios). Spot-checked against the source before committing the hour: `Robert "R.Lee" Lee Flowers` came back `company: null` rather than guessing *Edward Jones* from *"a decade as an Edward Jones client"*, which is the behaviour the prompt asked for and the one that is hard to get.

⚠ **THE DEDUPE MATCHER WAS WRONG FOR THIS SOURCE, AND THE COST IS INVERTED FROM THE USUAL ONE.** A false match here does not merge two people — it **SKIPS** one, losing a row with nothing reporting it. The dry run produced three fuzzy hits and **two were wrong**: `Christopher Frankland → Christopher Johnson` and `Kevin Jeremiah O'Shea → Jeremiah`, each decided on a first or middle name alone. (The third, `Ericson Hugh Tua'one → Ericson Tua'one`, is right — **Eric is in this delegation**, which is worth knowing on its own.) `matchDirectory`'s fuzzy arm is calibrated for a door that also carries an email address and an employer to narrow with, and this document carries neither: §12's rule is that when a matcher serves a new KIND of source you enumerate the signals that source can never carry.

⚠ **AND THE SURNAME RULE ALONE WAS STILL NOT ENOUGH — ONLY THE LIVE RUN SHOWED IT.** With surnames required to agree whole, the first apply skipped **`Pia van Benthem` as a duplicate of `Klaus van Benthem`** — two real people in the same delegation. A surname is a family, not a person. The first name must agree too: equal, or a prefix of something longer with a three-character floor so `J` cannot match both `James` and `Jennifer`. The same filter applied to the AMBIGUOUS branch turned a refusal into the right answer — `Mark William McCoy` came back ambiguous between `Mark William Van Leuven` and `Marc William Haddle`, three different people sharing a MIDDLE name, and once the candidates are filtered by the name rule there is no competing candidate and he is simply somebody new. **A dry run cannot find this class of bug; only applying can.**

⚠ **AND THE WHOLE IMPORT WOULD HAVE BEEN POINTLESS, FOR A REASON THAT PREDATES IT BY MONTHS.** `relationship_notes` — where a biography lives, filled on 98 of the 151 pre-existing contacts — was **the one substantive field on a contact that no retrieval path could reach**. `search_parties` matched `full_name`, `company` and `title` only; `embedPartyEnrichment` selected the row without it. So 233 people whose entire value is their biography would have been unanswerable, and so were the 98 before them. This is the shape §12 names for a document with a NULL `ai_summary`: present, stored, and invisible to the thing meant to read it. Both now read it, proven live on both paths afterwards — `"aviation e-commerce"` returns Neil Glazer (PilotMall), and vector search for `"who works on artificial intelligence for defense customers"` returns Henry Gilbert (Athena AIC) at 0.546 and Arthur Ford (Director of DoD Sales, MixMode) at 0.527.

**Landed: 232 contacts** — 220 with a title, 198 with a company, 213 with a headshot pulled out of the .docx and normalised through `sips` into the public `avatars` bucket, every one of the 232 indexed. One skipped: Eric. Every row carries `flightech-delegation` plus its city (`delegation-chicago`…), which is the undo handle — they select together and the existing bulk archive reverses the run in one press. The audit log names Richard rather than "system", because `createAdminClient` takes an explicit actor and a trail whose every row reads "system" answers nothing. **The re-run after the name fix reported exactly 2 new and 231 already present**, which is the two-run idempotency proof §12 asks for.

⚠ **THE BIOS ARE NOT COMPANY KNOWLEDGE AND WERE DELIBERATELY KEPT OFF THAT SHELF.** `is_company` documents are claims about Ber Wilson's own capabilities and feed `assessFit`; a delegation roster is not. The biographies live as `party_enrichment` chunks on the contacts, which is the corpus that answers "who is this person" without polluting the one that answers "can we win this".

⚠ **AND THE BOX WAS PAGING THROUGHOUT** — 104MB free, 17.6GB of swap — so the chat model was unloaded before the 232-contact embedding pass (§12) and reloaded after. `lmstudio-check.sh --fix` cannot load a missing embedder, the one failure it cannot repair, so that was done by hand. Swap came back at 10.6GB, better than it started.

## Part two — Jobs

**THE TENSION IN THE ASK WAS REAL AND RESOLVING IT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN.** "Really accomplish any task" and a typed write vocabulary are only in conflict if the gate is *how open-ended the task is*. It is not. **The gate is MUTATION.**

- **Reading and reasoning: unlimited.** 60 rounds, an hour of wall clock, every read tool the agent has. The output is a report, and a wrong report costs a re-read.
- **Writing: a closed vocabulary of five verbs, applied on a human's press.** Not because the model cannot reason — it read 233 biographies today without a single mis-alignment — but because **the dangerous output of a capable model is not a wrong answer, it is a PLAUSIBLE EDIT**: one that looks right in review, lands on 200 rows and is noticed six weeks later. There is deliberately **no delete verb**.

That is also why the agent's own doors stay shut. Richard's standing note on Pepper replies already said it: parse the instruction and route it through the functions that carry the whitelist, never hand the agent a pen.

**`/jobs`, NOT an Intake tab.** The first recommendation was `/intake?tab=job`; it was wrong once the scope became "any task". Intake means *things becoming records*, and a data-scrub that produces a report is not that.

⚠ **THE LOOP IS SHARED, NOT FORKED — AND COPYING IT WAS THE OBVIOUS MOVE.** `runAgentLocal` holds ~130 lines of mechanics that are exactly what a job needs, and §12's hardest-to-see fork is two SIBLING MODULES written days apart, neither of which looks like a copy. Everything in that loop was paid for by a real failure in /intel: the closing round with no tools (a turn once shipped its own narration as the answer), the un-tooled retry (Qwen can spend a whole generation inside `<think>`), the oldest-tool-results trimming (append, never rewrite — the KV prefix cache is 21x). A second copy would have had to pay for each of them again. So it moved to `src/lib/ai/tool-loop.ts` and both callers use it; `agent.ts` went 623 → 487 lines with no behaviour change, 644 tests green across the move.

**What a job adds on top is three things a chat turn does not need:** a **checkpoint after every round** (work fired off after a handler returns dies with the next kickstart, and `npm run build` IS the deploy — a 40-minute job must not be lost because somebody shipped); a **proposal tool** instead of write access, which validates the moment the model proposes and hands the refusal BACK into the conversation so a bad operation costs one round rather than being discovered by the human at review; and a **much larger budget**, because an audit over twenty records is twenty reads and that is the job rather than a sign of trouble.

**The state machine carries a clock.** `heartbeat_at` moves every round, and `working` paired with a stale heartbeat is how a reader tells a long healthy job from one a deploy killed — §12: an in-progress status is the shape that cannot settle itself, so there is no DB latch (a kickstart would make one immortal) and the runner reclaims on the clock instead. `claimNextJob` is a CONDITIONAL update, never read-then-write, and refuses a second concurrent job outright because LM Studio serves one request at a time.

⚠ **`tsc` REFUSED A VERB THE SCHEMA CANNOT PERFORM.** `tag_records` offered `parties`, `projects` and `opportunities`; a check across the whole schema says **`parties` is the only table in the database with a `tags` column**. A proposal that validates and then fails at the write is the §12 shape where a refusal reads as an absence.

⚠ **AND THE SWEEP-DEFERRAL TEST EARNED ITSELF AGAIN.** It refused the new cron route until it was classified — "these cron routes are in neither list: job-runner". A job stands aside for a live Ber AI question, and it is the clearest case of any pass on the box: a job is work somebody HANDED OVER, /intel is somebody sitting there waiting, and nothing is lost by yielding because the next tick claims it.

**Proven live, not just built.** A real job through the whole path: queued → claimed → 2 rounds, 3 `search_parties` calls, 69s → `done` with a 1,721-character report and **zero operations**, which is correct for a question. The report named two real people with their biographies quoted, and then said something better than either: *"The construction search returned 10 results, but none of those contacts have the word 'construction' in their actual biography. The matches were driven by company names."* It distinguished "there are none" from "the tool matched something else", which is exactly what the prompt asks for and what a confident wrong answer would have hidden.

⚠ **TWO THINGS ONLY RUNNING IT COULD FIND.** The report rendered as **raw markdown** — `**bold**` and `|---|---|` on screen, which reads as a failed render. `BriefMarkdown` already existed and `AgentChat` has used it since the agent shipped (§12: grep for a renderer before building one) — **and its own docblock listed pipe tables among the faults that the 2026-10-17 round did not fix.** So /intel has been showing raw `|---|---|` to a reader for as long as the agent has been answering, found only because the job prompt asks for "prose and short tables" and then got them. Tables added, guarded on the SEPARATOR line rather than the pipes, because prose contains pipes. ⚠ **And a rebuild alone did not ship the fix**: the `until curl` readiness probe answered against the OLD process before `KeepAlive` cycled it, so the page served stale markup and looked like the fix had failed. **A readiness probe that passes against the process you are replacing proves nothing** — an explicit `launchctl kickstart` is what landed it.

```
moose@berwilson.com ×5, tuaone@berwilson.com ×5   our own two executives, as mailboxes
"Ber Wilson" ×5, "Ber Wilson Lead", "…Executive Team"   our own company, in a person field
```
