**Done 2026-10-19 (the ledger was overwhelming, and three of its four causes were defects):**

Richard: *"We are getting too many commitments make it overwhelming to sift through. How can we get rid of stale ones, sort by date created and other things to make it easier to sift through them?"*

**Measured first, and "too many" was not mostly staleness.** 244 open commitments — across only **125 conversations**, so the list was nearly 2× longer than the number of things actually in play. 213 of 244 carried no due date, 176 hung off no record, and 203 sat on threads already silent a week or more. The aging pass was working (158 already retired, nothing past 45 days except chase-grace and two reopened rows); the threshold was simply loose. Three separate defects were doing the rest of the damage.

**(1) The sort was backwards, and the module said so in writing.** `readOpenCommitments` ordered `due_date asc nullsFirst:false` then `created_at` **ASCENDING** — oldest first — while the header on `list.ts` has claimed *"every open row, newest attention first"* since the day it was written. With 87% of rows undated the deadline key decided almost nothing, so the page was effectively oldest-first and anything found this week sat at the bottom of a 244-row list. §12's rule about a comment describing a control that is not there, in this repo's own highest-traffic queue. Fixed with a `sort` option on the choke point (`due | newest | oldest | activity`), defaulting to `newest`, exposed as a URL-backed control. ⚠ `activity` cannot be ordered in SQL — the key lives on the embedded thread and PostgREST will not reliably order a filtered read by an embedded column — so it is sorted in memory over a set already bounded at 1000, with nulls last in both directions rather than rendered as the extreme.

**(2) 30 of 164 "Waiting on" rows were our own work.** The extraction prompt sets `side` and `owner_name` as independent fields and nothing cross-checked them, so *"Draft and send MOU to TensorIQ for legal review — Ericson Tua'one"* and *"Make initial $50,000 payment — Richard White"* sat in the follow-up column. 20% of what read as a chase list was the executive's own to-do, and the chase pass would have composed a counterparty nudge for it. ⚠ **`attribute()` in `pepper/attribution.ts` already DIAGNOSED this exact bug** — its docblock reads *"lands on Richard's waiting-on list as something Richard owes himself"* — and worked around it at READ time by refusing to resolve the name when the side is `them`. That keeps the row off the wrong desk and leaves it in the wrong column, which is the half the reader sees. `src/lib/commitments/side.ts` is the write-time fix the workaround stood in for: `them` → `us` when `resolveOwnerName` (reused, not rewritten — §12) resolves the owner to a team member, one direction only, because the extractor errs toward `them` deliberately. Wired into extraction and reported as `sideCorrected`; 30 existing rows backfilled, with the second-run-reports-nothing assertion inline in the script.

**(3) ⚠ The duplicate fold was built, measured, and thrown away — the measurement is the finding.** 125 threads producing 247 rows looked like an obvious fold, and `commitmentSimilarity` (the overlap coefficient, already used for same-thread dedupe) folded 31 of 244 when swept. Reading the pairs killed it: **"Sign the MNDA" ≡ "Sign the NDA"**, **"Sign and endorse the LOI" ≡ "Sign the LOI"** across two *different deals*, and "Sign the MNDA" ≡ "Sign and send the grid edge MNDA". The coefficient is `shared / min(size)`, so **a short phrase is a perfect subset of every longer phrase containing it**, and "Sign the MNDA" is a subset of half the ledger. This is §12's four-blank-MNDAs-for-four-counterparties trap exactly: folding would have silently settled one counterparty's NDA by ticking another's. Swept the alternatives — identical key + same record gives **1** pair (too strict to build), Jaccard ≥ 0.8 any record gives **18**, all genuine. Shipped as a **flag, never a fold**: Jaccard (which does not reward being a subset), and a chip the reader can act on. Marking is safe even where it is wrong; merging is not. **~18 rows saved was never the lever anyway** — the aging threshold and the sort were.

**(4) The threshold, on Richard's call: 45 → 21 days.** Swept against the live corpus rather than chosen: 30d retires 35 (barely moves it), 21d retires 76, 14d retires 123 — and 14 stays ruled out by `aging.ts`'s own standing argument that a fortnight is an ordinary gap in a land deal. 21 keeps that argument intact: still two full chase cycles past the 21-day chase bar, so every row closed has had a follow-up composed and a further week of silence after it. ⚠ **A latent bug went live with the change:** `agingVerdict` never looked at `due_date`, so a counterparty who said "by the 30th" and then went quiet would be retired exactly on schedule — the one row that would have chased it. Zero of 158 retired rows had a future date at 45 days; **eleven do at 21**. §12's rule that a threshold change can break a filter it never touched. Guarded, with its own `skippedFutureDue` counter rather than folded into the others, because it is the one keep-reason that says the row is *live*.

**Also shipped:** a `thread quiet Nd` marker on each row from 14 days (amber past the 21-day bar), because the age of a *row* cannot distinguish an obligation on a live negotiation from one on a conversation that stopped — 125 of 244 rows now carry it. ⚠ **And a third `useRouter` split in three days**: `renderToStaticMarkup` threw *"invariant expected app router to be mounted"*, exactly as it did for `AttentionList` on 10-17 and `OpportunityNotes` on 10-18. `CommitmentsLedger` is now the router-free half and `CommitmentsClient` the thin wrapper — at three occurrences this is the house pattern, not a one-off. ⚠ **The verification caught what review did not:** `thread_last_at` came back populated on **0 of 244** rows because the embedded select was widened on the two history paths in `list.ts` and not on the main one in `read.ts` — so the `activity` sort was silently falling back to `newest` and every quiet-marker was absent, while the page rendered perfectly and `tsc` was clean. ⚠ Also re-tested, not inherited: `dry-aging.mts` carries a note prescribing DEFAULT imports for `src/lib` modules, which is true under `tsx` and **false** under `deploy/register.mjs`, where a default import fails outright.

**Result: 244 → 198 open, "Waiting on" 164 → 116**, with 29 more retiring as their chase grace expires. 634 tests pass (12 new on the side correction, including all four spellings of Eric's surname), 28 render checks across four sort orders and every absent-field shape, lint unchanged at 23. (DEPLOYED + PUSHED)

**Done 2026-10-19 (the upload door, one copy of the phases for three sources, and `projects.sector` has no default):**

Richard, confirming the text gateway works and settling how recordings arrive: *"I am only going to drop the file in that general folder without any labels on it. You will have to deduce from the transcript where it belongs. If you want to add an upload MP3 button on the 'update' area of projects and opportunities, we can have that be a fallback to make sure our recording associates to the appropriate record."*

**What already existed, and why it was not enough.** The Meetings tab has carried a recording upload since it was built, and the honest finding is that it is a *different and smaller* pass: `runMeetingTranscription` downloads the attached audio, transcribes it, writes a summary **only if the field is blank**, and files the transcript as a document. It stops there. No thread, so no passages in the obligation ledger; no commitments; no tasks; nothing on the record's feed. That is §12 twice in one place — two doors for one artifact where only one owns an index, and *"a destination that does not carry what creating carries reads as losing the work"*. So the new door is not a second upload; it is the SAME pass with the record as a parameter.

**One copy of the phases, for what are now three sources.** The sequence after a recording becomes a thread — route, apply, embed, extract obligations, promote the internal ones, count what *these* threads produced — was written out in `voicememos/sweep.ts` and again in `driveaudio/sweep.ts`, ~85% identical with every difference in note wording. It is the fork §12 calls hardest to see, and this family has already paid for it once (`fileMeetingFromThreadLinks` was a bug fixed in one sweep and not the other). Extracted to `src/lib/audio/phases.ts`; both sweeps now call it, and so does the upload. The two sweeps lost 90 lines between them. ⚠ The per-source note wording stays per-source and is passed in, because the advice genuinely differs: a memo gets renamed on a phone, a Drive export gets dropped in a folder, and an upload was already filed by the person doing it (so it gets no advice at all — an unfiled upload is a fault, not a habit).

**The assertion is the whole feature.** `runRecordingPhases` takes `assertions`, written as `linked` links BEFORE routing runs, because `routeThreads` respects an existing `linked` link and skips guessing for that thread entirely. An upload therefore cannot land on the wrong deal: the record is a parameter, not a match. The Drive folder's subfolder hint now travels the same seam rather than writing its own link inline.

**And the gate is deliberately not run.** The voice-memo sweep reads every memo on a personal phone and must judge which are private; a file a person chose and attached to a named deal has already been judged by the only party entitled to. A `noise` verdict DISCARDS the transcript, so running the classifier here would let a model overrule a human's filing decision.

⚠ **`projects.sector` IS NOT NULL AND HAS NO DEFAULT — found because the verification could not create its own scratch project.** §12 says a field the caller never mentioned must be OMITTED rather than nulled, since an explicit NULL does not fall back to the column DEFAULT — and that rule has an unstated precondition: **omission only works where a default exists.** `status` and `stage` have one; `sector` does not. So the morning's promotion pass, for any referenced record the model labelled `project` whose sector the call never stated, would have hit `23502` and reported it as a skip with a Postgres message inside. The fix is **not** to pick a sector: the enum has no "unknown" member and a guessed sector reads on the record as something somebody established. A conversation that never said what KIND of work a deal is has not given enough to open a project, so it stays staged with that sentence as the reason. ⚠ **This also corrects the backfill measurement from earlier today**: its one surviving candidate (`Pennsylvania Project`) was a `project` kind with no sector, so the honest number for that dry run is **zero records**, not one.

⚠ **And a new recording door needs an arm in THREE separate prefix switches, of which only one is obvious.** The live verification passed fifteen checks and failed one — the meeting sat `scope='unfiled', project_id=null` while its thread was correctly `linked` to the chosen project — and it took two runs to find the real cause, because the first fix was the wrong one:

1. `meetingRefFromThreadId` maps a thread id back to the key its `meetings` row is stored under. It knew `voicememo:`, `driveaudio:` and `note:`. **Fixed first, and the check still failed.**
2. `threadSource` is the actual root cause. `fileMeetingFromThreadLinks` opens with `if (source !== 'call' && source !== 'recording') return { moved: false }` — so an unrecognised prefix falls through to `email` and **the entire filing step is skipped in silence**, with no error and no note. Mapped to the existing `recording` member rather than a new one, which is what the docblock three lines above it already advises: a new member would mean an `update_source` enum migration plus a new arm in every switch that handles this one.
3. `LOCAL_THREAD_PREFIXES` answers "there is no Gmail thread behind this row", which keeps a synthetic id out of a live Gmail fetch. Added — though the list's *other* job, the redaction filter, cannot fire here since this path runs no work/noise gate.

§12 verbatim, now for the third time: *when a function branches on where something came from, every source that can reach it needs an arm, not just the one being added today.* **The missing test is the lasting fix** — three assertions that loop over every recording door at once and check all three switches agree, so the fifth recorder is cheap. A prefix discriminator is a registry with no type behind it, so nothing makes the compiler ask. The predicate lives in `src/lib/audio/upload-ref.ts`, a module with no imports, because `attach-recording` and `thread-source` both need it while `upload.ts` imports `attach-recording` — putting it in `upload.ts` closes a require cycle the app tolerates and a script does not.

**Measured, and whisper is not the expensive part.** A 40-second test recording took **177.9 seconds end to end**. Whisper is a few seconds of that; the rest is the model passes this path deliberately runs — thread summary, recap, obligation extraction — on an LM Studio that serves one request at a time, so each also queues behind anything else running. Those costs are roughly constant per recording rather than proportional to its length, so a long call is whisper's extra time on top of a ~170s floor. `maxDuration` is therefore **600, not 300**: at 300 a real hour-long call would have been cut off *after* the records were written, showing the caller a failure for work that succeeded. The UI copy says three minutes and that the tab can be left open, because a spinner with no explanation gets cancelled halfway.

**What a successful upload produced, on live data:** 419 characters transcribed, a thread with an `upload:` fingerprint and a provenance line naming the record and the uploader, a `linked` link reading *"uploaded onto Zzz Scratch Verification by Richard White"*, indexed passages, **1 update on the record's feed, 3 obligations and 2 tasks**, a meeting row carrying the transcript, and the promotion gate running and correctly creating nothing (the record already exists — gate 1 doing its job).

**Smaller things.** The audio itself is **not** kept: `documents.project_id` has no opportunity sibling (an opportunity's files live in `opportunity_documents`), and storing hundreds of megabytes per call on a box that already swaps buys an archive Drive is already holding. The route reads the record BEFORE writing anything and calls `canAccessRecord` — §12's measured finding that 22 of 61 one-table write routes carried no record check, precisely because a request carries only an id. It sits at `/api/records/recording` so the role gate's non-method-aware prefix match cannot reach it from `/api/records/milestones`, and it is admin-only by default-deny. One component serves both record kinds rather than the opportunity side getting the thinner copy again. No separate "Recording" entry in the Log menu: the upload panel opens beside the composer from the same `?new=1`, so a second entry would be two doors to one surface.

**Verification.** 4 new unit tests on the prefix discriminator (including that it is not mistaken for either sibling door, and that two uploads of one file get DIFFERENT fingerprints — deliberately the opposite of the Drive door, where the file id is the guard, because here a re-upload is how a person corrects a wrong record), 10 render checks on the upload panel across both record kinds, and a **live end-to-end script using real macOS TTS speech through real whisper** (`scripts/verify-recording-upload.mts`) that creates a scratch project, uploads onto it, asserts sixteen things and then removes the thread, links, passages, obligations, meeting, update, tasks and project it made. Both rewired sweeps dry-run clean. The third run of that script is **16 of 16**, with `meetingsFiled: 1`. **622 tests pass**, lint unchanged at 23, build exit 0.

**Done 2026-10-19 (Gemini's Meet notes were already flowing — and running the gate over them found it was 100% wrong):**

Richard: *"I have gemini automatically transcribing and taking notes in my Google meet. Doesn't all that save and show to you in that folder? Can't you adequately pull and populate from that information? I want you to do this with call recordings we upload to the drive and the google meet recordings that auto save to the drive."*

**He was right about the premise.** `listMeetTranscripts` reads `GOOGLE_DOC` files whose names carry Meet's artifact markers, and it has preferred `… - Notes by Gemini` over `… - Transcript` since the day it was written (a Gemini note contains the transcript, so keeping both would stage every call twice). Live: **6 Gemini notes documents, all imported** — 4 in moose@ (Tensor Uintah Basin, Rebecca/Merlin visit, TensorIQ/Elite Solutions ×2) and 2 in tuaone@ (Ber Wilson chat W Taylor, Ber Wilson / Zenthium). The Drive-upload half was wired to the promotion pass the same morning. So the gap was narrower than the question assumed: **the Meet path did not run the new gate**, and nothing had ever re-read what was already staged.

⚠ **First, a count that had been lying on every run.** The importer reported *"2 recording(s) have no transcript beside them"* while both of those recordings (239MB and 751MB) sat in the same folder as their own imported Gemini notes. `meetArtifactKey` stripped `Notes by Gemini` and `Transcript` and **not `Recording`**, so `… - 2026/10/12 09:00 MDT - Recording` kept its tail and could never equal the notes document's key — and the caller had tried to compensate by stripping a file EXTENSION (`.mp4`), which Drive does not put in `name` at all. Fixed in the one function that defines the key, with the sibling enumeration in `meetingTitleFromFileName` aligned and both pinned by tests. tuaone@ went 2 → 0; the one that remains is genuine (see below).

**Then the gate was wired into the Meet importer — the same `promoteAndAlert`, not a third copy.** A Gemini notes document is a transcript with the recap already attached, so the only thing that differs from a voice memo is where the words came from. `sourceRef` is `meet:<fileId>`, so a reader of `auto_created_from` can tell which door a record came through. It runs whether or not the TITLE filed onto a record, because a call titled for one deal routinely names another.

**And then the measurement that matters.** `scripts/promote-staged-meetings.mts` runs the gate over every meeting already staged — 18 of them, recapped before the gate existed, their `extraction_result` sitting in `email_intake_sessions` with the per-deal paragraphs and dated tasks the gate reads. No model call, no Drive read, no transcription. Dry run by default, because a backfill is the one shape of this pass that can create several records and send one text about all of them.

**It would have created 9 records and every single one was wrong.** Two distinct failures, both §12's shared-industry-word rule, in the gate I had shipped four hours earlier:

- **One document became the fact behind eight deals.** `searchWords` included the COUNTERPARTY's words, so a single `Tensor MNDA (with Non-Circumvention)` "proved" *Uintah Basin Project*, *Alberta Project*, *Weber Data Center* and *Deer Creek Public Infrastructure*. A signed NDA with Tensor is evidence that we signed an NDA with Tensor. It says nothing about whether the Alberta project is real.
- **The vendor's own boilerplate was in the haystack.** Gmail titles these *"eSigned Document **Ready**: …"*, and *West Virginia Power-**Ready** Site* matched a **template** on that word — a document that by its own name is about no deal at all.

**Three rules were tried and the corpus killed the first two.** (1) any distinguishing word → 9 creates, all wrong. (2) EVERY distinguishing word, counterparty excluded → 3, still all wrong, because `distinguishingWords` correctly drops the vocabulary every record shares ("data", "center", "project", "site") and so *Tensor Site* and *Tensor IQ Data Center* both reduce to the single word `tensor`, which is the counterparty's: "every word" and "one shared word" are the same test on a two-word name. (3) ⚠ **"…and the counterparty is new to the register" was measured BEFORE being built, and does not discriminate at all** — `Tensor IQ` is named by **0** projects and opportunities, exactly like `Synetra`, so it would have kept both false positives.

**What survives is strict and threshold-free: the document must be NAMED AFTER the deal.** The record's whole name, contiguous, once punctuation is flattened. `synetra` ⊂ `bw mnda synetra with non circumvention docx` passes — the case this gate exists for, a first MNDA with a counterparty whose name IS the deal. `tensor iq data center` ⊄ `tensor mnda` does not, and that deal stays staged for a human, which is where it already was, so nothing is lost. A long name (`Weirton — Cleveland-Cliffs (WV)`) can never be created this way, and that is correct: it already exists. The subject's vendor wrapper is stripped first (`documentNameFromSubject`), preferring the quoted file name where Gmail supplies one.

**9 → 3 → 1, with the Synetra case passing at every step.** The one survivor is `Pennsylvania Project`, created off the STRUCTURAL fact (a dated task whose own `record_hint` names it: *"Submit LOIs for Pennsylvania & Chicago Projects by 2026-10-08"*) — mechanically correct, and almost certainly **Steelton**, which is the Cleveland-Cliffs site in Pennsylvania and which the same meeting refused as already existing. That is a resolver limitation, not a gate one: a deal referred to by its state shares no word with its record's name. **So the backfill is deliberately NOT applied** — 1 probable duplicate is not worth 0 new records, and the 42 "nothing but intent" refusals are the correct answer for calls about deals we already have.

⚠ **The honest shape of this: the structural fact fired once in 18 meetings and the two fuzzy facts fired nine times, all wrong.** They survive because the Synetra case is real and the strict form passes it — but the ratio is the warning, and the dated-next-step fact is the one to trust.

**Not built, measured first.** One Meet recording is genuinely uncovered: `fxw-xtyp-jrb (2026-06-16 18:51 GMT)` in info@, **2.5GB**, from June, titled with a Meet code and with no notes beside it. Transcribing it means downloading 2.5GB and decoding it on a box with 187MB free and 8.3GB of swap in use, for a four-month-old call in the assistant mailbox whose title names nobody. Every other Meet recording is covered by its Gemini notes, which is the whole point of having notes switched on. So a video-transcription path would be built for a hypothesis — §12, measure before building.

**615 tests pass** (21 new on the identification rules, each pinning one of the real false positives, plus 4 on Meet's file-name suffixes), 30 live-database checks, lint unchanged at 23, build exit 0.

**And the channel the whole feature depends on had never delivered a message.** `notification_log` holds 10 `pepper_text` rows and the log is ten consecutive `Couldn't find shortcut "Pepper Text Richard"` / `"Pepper Text Eric"` — `shortcuts list` confirms neither exists.
