The TensorIQ exclusive-general-contractor clause still comes back from `search_correspondence` at relevance 0.753, attributed *"attachment: BerWilson_TensorIQ_Master_Strategic_Partnership_Agreement_v6.5.docx"* with the thread, its six participants, the date and a Gmail link — better provenance than the document chunk carried. `Due Diligence Letter.docx` is still listed by `list_documents` with its summary and `has_full_text: true`, and still reads through `get_document_content`. A staged `.xlsx` the mail index could not have read was picked up by the reconcile and embedded from its stored text (85 left alone, 1 embedded, 0 failed), then removed. `runSweep({ phases: ['embed'] })` carries the reconcile with it. And with **West Wendover** marked `confidential`, its mail-indexed `West Wendover Quantum Playbook Power Solution.pdf` was withheld from `searchCorrespondence` while the one surviving passage proved to be an **unfiled** thread — the documented pre-existing behaviour (*"filing it is what protects it"*), not a regression. Worth recording that `withoutProtectedThreads` now carries sole responsibility for 85 documents' text, where two filters used to cover it.

**Then the jam itself, which was a UI change.** `DocumentsTab.tsx` was 764 lines of flat list with no grouping, no filter and no search — while every row already carried `drive_folder_path` and printed it as a badge. §12 has this exactly: *check whether the data is already on the row before calling a list "an extraction problem"*. Grouped on the **whole** path rather than its first segment, because `Diligence/Rail & Transportation` (100) and `Diligence/Environmental` (8) are different shelves holding different questions and folding them into one "Diligence" would reproduce the list being replaced. `_Unsorted` sorts first — the classifier was not confident, so those rows are asking for a decision — and the unfiled sort last, named in words rather than shown against a bare dash. Run over real data: **Weirton 187 → 9 shelves, Steelton 179 → 12**, every document in exactly one, asserted. The filter lives in the URL, so a filtered view is something you can link, reload and send to Eric, and the back button undoes it.

⚠ **THE TYPE FILTER COULD NOT HAVE FILTERED FOR 163 OF THE DOCUMENTS IT WAS FILTERING.** `documents.doc_type` has no CHECK and no registry — the lead promoter, the Drive classifier and the mail import each write words of their own — and the component's local `DOC_TYPES` array had **already drifted once**, with a comment inside it recording the patch ("Both are written by lead promotion … and were missing here, so neither could be filtered for"). It was still missing six: `capability` (138), `capability_statement` (11), `reference` (6), `transcript` (4), `site_plan` (2), `quote` (2). This is the 10-14 `/decide` rule landing one component over — a hand-written enumeration beside a registry drifts, and a ⚠ comment saying so does not stop the sibling drifting. The chips are now derived from the doc_types actually on the record: there is no registry to derive from, so **the rows are the registry**. The curated array survives for the upload picker alone, which is the one place a short human-facing list belongs.

Also found while in the file: the badge printed the raw column through `capitalize`, so 11 documents read **"Capability_statement"** at a reader — now `enumLabel` (§12). And the server page had no `.limit()` against PostgREST's silent 1000-row cap, so a data room past that would simply have stopped listing with nothing saying so; it now asks for one more than it shows and says so when the extra row comes back. `shelveByFolder` went to `src/lib/documents/shelve.ts` rather than staying in the client component — a helper a test may want must not be exported from a `'use client'` file — with 5 tests, including that a blank or whitespace path never becomes its own nameless shelf and that the order is stable under reordered input.

**Corrected in flight:** a build warning went 3 → 4 after the `system-health` import and I attributed it to that change. It is nondeterministic Turbopack NFT tracing — the warned route set differs between two builds of identical code, and the route I claimed to have fixed still appeared in the build that supposedly fixed it. `system-health.ts` already imported `google-drive`, so it always pulled that layer in. The constant still moved to an import-free `src/lib/documents/status.ts`, which is where a value read by four modules belongs, but it did not fix a warning.

**Not done, deliberately:** the diligence data rooms are the real volume (480 documents, 5,532 chunks) and are left whole — that is what the record is *for*; grouping makes them readable and nothing is withheld from retrieval. Teaching `readAttachmentText` to read xlsx/pptx was left alone because the reconcile already indexes those as documents, which is the right answer and not a move of the work. And the "903 email attachments never imported" item is **833 on 426 *unfiled* threads, 381 of them on `noise` threads** — a filing backlog, not an import one, since the import only ever walks filed threads. Reworded rather than worked. Still true that there is no attachment manifest anywhere: only `email_threads.attachment_count` and the names of files actually read, so "which attachments do we hold" cannot be answered without Gmail round trips.

361 tests pass (5 new). Lint unchanged at its 23-problem baseline. (DEPLOYED + MIGRATED + PUSHED)

**Done 2026-10-14 (a document belongs to the deal it names, not to every deal its thread did):**

Richard: *"Its seems like some documents are getting filed in the wrong projects. There might also be duplicates or old versions of the same document. How can we keep it cleaner and more accurate"*

Measured before building anything, and the halves of that sentence turned out to be very different sizes.

**The duplicates half is already solved and the measurement says so.** 64 rows carry a `superseded_at`, 50 of them with a reason naming the file they duplicate, all byte-identical and found by hash — the 10-09 hashing work doing its job. Near-identical VERSIONS on a project are 7 groups over 17 rows, and five of the seven are trivial (a `.docx`/`.pdf` pair of one playbook, an `Alaska_..._Brief (1).pdf`, three `invite.ics` copies). Cross-project byte-identical copies were 16 hashes over 41 rows — and that number turned out to be the whole of the real problem, pointing straight at the other half.

**The misfiling half has exactly two causes, and one of them is a bug.**

*Cause one: one thread, three deals.* 7 of 180 project/opportunity links are multi-record. Every one of those links is CORRECT and human-made at `certainty='linked'`, `confidence=1`: the threads are titled "Assignment Doc for Steelton, Weirton and Riverdale", "Site DD for Steelton, Weirton and Riverdale", "PA, WV & IL", "Whiskey - Zorro". The filing was right. **The fan-out was the bug:** `importThreadAttachments` runs per LINK, so each of the three records independently imported every attachment on the thread, and the per-record hash dedupe cannot see it because the three copies sit on three different records. So `Dynegy Power Supply Attestation_Project Steelton.pdf`, `PPL_Power Confirmation Steelton Sept 2026.pdf`, `PSA Agreement Steelton.pdf` and the Harvest Time rapid response were all on Weirton AND Riverdale.

The guard asks each FILE which of the thread's deals it names, before the byte fetch — so a file belonging to a sibling costs no Gmail round trip at all. It reuses `bestMatch` with the target set restricted to the thread's own records, which is safe because every score there is absolute (overlap between the document's tokens and one record's) and only the ambiguity check compares records to each other. A narrower set therefore asks a narrower question with the same evidence and the same refusal to guess. What does the work is the human-asserted aliases already on those records — `Project Steelton`, `Cleveland-Cliffs Steelton`, `215 S Front St`, `Cliffs-Weirton`.

Run against the real threads, it splits `Whiskey - Zorro` perfectly — all four one-pagers to their own deal — claims twelve Steelton files for Steelton, and correctly leaves `Sites-Due Diligence-10.1.2026 (Site DD for Steelton Weirton and Riverdale).xlsx`, `Assignment Agreement .doc`, `BW MNDA (with Non-Circumvention).docx` and the TensorIQ partnership agreement on all three. **A file naming none of the deals, or all of them, still goes to all of them.** That is the load-bearing half and it has its own test: a shared workbook genuinely belongs on three records, and picking the top score there would put it on one and hide it from two. Two files stay undetectably wrong — `362626.0300-SV01-ALTA-20261002-DRAFT.pdf` is one site's ALTA survey and its name says only a job number.

*Cause two: sibling deals sharing a word.* Nine IAN acquisition documents (two patents, the SBIR compliance set, the teaming agreement) had collected on **Myton Development**, and six Myton Rail filings on the same record. "Myton" is shared by two projects and an unrelated data-centre pursuit, which §12 already records as the reason the two-token bar exists.

**The queue for what already landed.** `/decide` gains a **Wrong deal** row per document whose own name points at a different record than the one it sits on: **38 documents, 384 indexed passages answering for the wrong deal.** Human-confirm, Richard's call when asked — the alternative was auto-refiling at ≥0.99, and moving a document overwrites a filing a human may have made. The row names what it costs to leave it ("52 indexed passages answering for Weirton instead of Steelton"), the accept button names where it would go, and dismissing it writes `filing_confirmed_at` because a queue computed from the records cannot otherwise reach zero.

One matcher now serves three callers — the company-knowledge queue, this one, and the sweep — extracted out of `unfiled.ts` into `src/lib/documents/match.ts`. Forking `documentName` was the alternative and would have given the sweep a matcher with no folder-path signal and no identifier extraction, which is most of what makes it work.

⚠ **A ONE-WORD PROJECT NAME IS UNREACHABLE FROM ANY DOCUMENT, and 38 documents were sitting in that hole.** `bestMatch` needs two shared tokens, or the whole name plus a shared contact — a single word being "either a distinctive brand or a common place, and nothing in the name says which". A DOCUMENT HAS NO CONTACTS BY CONSTRUCTION, so for a project called **Tooele** the corroborating half can never be true and the project could never be matched. The result: 38 of 52 documents under `Corporate /M & A/Tooele Ber Wilson Steel House Factory/` had no proposal at all, including a **134-chunk Phase 1 environmental report**, a **79-chunk USACE W9126G26D0003 award**, an Army lease and a 2026 title commitment — all answering as Ber Wilson *company knowledge*, which is ORed into every project-scoped question and handed to `assessFit()` as "RELEVANT BER WILSON EVIDENCE". This is the `Corporate /M & A/` shelf the 09-30 session flagged as "52% of company chunks; 21 have a one-click home, the rest need a look": the rest did not need a look, they needed the matcher to be able to see the record. Not fixed by weakening the rule — that re-opens the Myton ambiguity — but by the mechanism already built for it: **asserting the folder's own name as an alias**, which the alias branch exists to allow because it requires the WHOLE alias present. One alias took the shelf from 14 proposable to **51 of 52**, and the whole company queue from 34 to 71 rows carrying **650 chunks** that would leave the company corpus.

⚠ **`.in()` WITH 1000 UUIDS IS A 37KB URL AND KONG REFUSES IT** — `URI too long`, on the reaper's first live run against 550 lead links. A PostgREST filter travels in the query string, so the 1000-row RESPONSE cap and the URL LENGTH cap are two different limits and one `PAGE` constant cannot serve both; 200 ids is ~7.4KB. **It failed closed** — the guard that bails rather than treating an empty record set as truth meant nothing was deleted — but the leads check had silently not run. The same latent trap was in `countChunksByDocument`, which passes its whole id list; chunked there too.

⚠ **TEN `thread_links` POINTED AT A DELETED PROJECT SINCE 9 SEPTEMBER, AND NOTHING COULD EVER HAVE FOUND THEM.** The existing drop is a side effect of HAVING WORK TO DO: a link is only examined when its text cursor is behind or its thread carries attachments. All ten were caught up on text (`applied_message_count = message_count`) with no attachments on their threads, so they were never selected, never examined, never dropped — immortal and invisible, and no foreign key can catch them because `record_id` points at one of four tables. They were matched to "Stockton 225 housing development" at 0.67–0.75 on the name. Not harmless either: they made two live Stockton threads look multi-record to the new attachment guard, which is why that guard counts its siblings AFTER resolving them, not before. `reapOrphanedLinks` now runs once per apply phase across all four kinds.

⚠ **`isFileable` HAS ALWAYS KNOWN A CALENDAR INVITE IS NOT A DOCUMENT — IT WAS ONLY EVER ASKED WHEN FILING TO DRIVE**, after the `documents` row already existed. So the row was created, summarised and listed on the record, and only the Drive copy was spared. 39 `.ics` rows across both document tables, 4 of them three- and four-deep on one record. Set aside with two `noname` PNGs (66,624 bytes each, byte-identical, which is why the deduper retired one and left the other — `CHROME_NAME` requires an extension) and the two `image001/002.png` that `isMailChrome`'s own docblock names. 44 rows, 2 chunks: these were answering nothing, so the win is a documents tab that is not 6% calendar invites. Door closed at intake.

⚠ **THE PLAN WAS TO EXCLUDE 44 IMAGES AS NOISE, AND READING THEM FIRST KILLED IT.** The option offered to Richard said "44 images, 14 .ics and 2 'noname' polluting chunks and retrieval". The images are **15 scanned 2007 bridge inspection sheets on Weirton, 20 scanned survey plats on Helper, the Millard County zoning amendment exhibit for Daves Farms, and two Alaska claim maps** — real diligence documents the Apple Vision OCR path had read. Excluding by mime type would have destroyed their chunks. §12 again, including when the rule is being applied by the session that wrote it down: the bloat has never once been where the rule assumed.

⚠ **THE FILTER CHIPS ON `/decide` ARE A HAND-WRITTEN LIST, ONE STRUCTURE OVER FROM A ⚠ NOTE ABOUT EXACTLY THAT BUG.** The note above `counts` records it being fixed there — a kind-keyed structure beside the registry, missing the registry's newest key, rendering "Unfiled document NaN". `counts` is now seeded from `KIND_META`; the chip row still spelled out five of six kinds, so `misfiled` got a count and no chip and its rows could not be filtered to. Both derive from the registry now, and `KIND_META`'s declaration order is the reading order.

**Also found:** `opportunity_documents` had neither `excluded_at` nor `filing_confirmed_at`, so the first version of the filing audit ran green and reported all 103 of those documents clean — PostgREST answered `42703` and the caller read `data` as null. A broken query and a clean corpus are the same number on screen. Migration `20261014000003` adds both columns plus `excluded_reason`, and `refileDocument`/`excludeDocument`/`confirmDocumentFiling` take a `DocumentSource` that defaults to `documents`, so every existing caller is unchanged. The opportunity side then needed its own chunk operations — `chunks` points at those rows through `opportunity_document_id`, so counting one on `document_id` returns 0, and zero reads as "never indexed", which is the one answer that makes a misfiled document look harmless. With both halves readable the honest audit is 38 misfiled of 738, 4.3%, and **482 with no match at all — the common and correct outcome**, because a title commitment names a parcel and an owner and never the deal.

**Verification:** 356 tests (5 new on the sibling guard, including the one asserting a three-site package stays on three sites); `tsc` clean; `next build` exit 0 captured unpiped; both one-shots idempotent on a second run (44 → 0 excluded, 10 → 0 links reaped). ⚠ The authenticated HTML render of `/decide` is NOT verified — the browser could reach neither the tailnet host nor localhost from this session. The data path is verified directly against the live database, `tsc` enforces `Record<DecideKind, …>`, and the chip and count maps now derive from that registry, but somebody should open the page.

**Richard's one tap:** `/decide` now holds 71 company rows (650 chunks leaving the company corpus) and 38 wrong-deal rows (384 chunks). Not scripted deliberately: a scripted refile logs to `activity_log` as "system", and §12 requires `actorAdminClient()` for a user-initiated mutation — the whole value of a filing decision is that it is attributable.

**Done 2026-10-14 (an in-person meeting gets a door, and it is the iPhone's own recorder — not a button in the app):**

Richard asked for a Record Meeting button at the top of Ber Intelligence, above the calculator: *"That way Eric and I can quickly open the app and record a conversation we are having. When that recording ends, that call gets parsed through and updates the relevant projects with the details."* Then, mid-build, the better question: *"I understand that I can record a phone conversation on iphone, it lands in notes and BI will get those. I am talking about what is the best way to capture in person meetings... I just don't want the audio lost due to screen lock/sleeping or things of that nature."*

**The button was the wrong primary door, on the one device he wants to use.** On iOS, locking the screen or leaving Safari suspends the page and WebAudio capture stops — exactly the failure he named, and it arrives silently at the end of a meeting rather than at the start. Voice Memos holds a system background-audio entitlement and records through a locked screen for hours. Otter and Plaud were excluded on a different ground: they transcribe in their own cloud, and raw conversation audio about live deals leaving the box is what Grok Bot was removed for on 10-11.

**Measured on the box before planning, because three of the four facts were not what they looked like:**

```
Full Disk Access          LIVE — bw-snapshot copied chat.db at 11:35 today.
                          The failures in snapshot.err.log are stale (10-12 15:35,
                          before the signing fix), and 09ab3a4 signs with a stable
                          identity so a rebuild no longer voids the grant
Notes audio               ON DISK — "Call with Eric Tuaone.m4a" and four others
Voice Memos container     EXISTS AND IS EMPTY — 4.0K, no CloudRecordings.db
                          anywhere. The app has never been opened on this Mac
whisper                   reads m4a already (afconvert), ~32x realtime, and the
                          16-minute call measured 29.7s with the chat model resident
```

Richard's four calls, taken before any code: read **every** memo with the summarizer as the gate (zero taps on the phone) rather than a nominated folder; stay on the **existing 4×/day** snapshot cadence; **file the certain, stage the rest**; and **defer** the in-app button until this path is proven in a real meeting.

**What was built is a source and a gate, not a pipeline.** `CloudRecordings.db` and its `.m4a` files join `bw-snapshot`'s allowlist; a reader, a transcriber and a sweep sit on top; and from there every step is the one the mail sweep already runs. A memo is transcribed on-box, written as an `email_threads` row prefixed `voicememo:`, and summarized — and the verdict is the fork:

```
noise  → transcript nulled, chunks deleted, copied audio DELETED, memo skip-listed.
         The row survives as the tombstone, so it is never read again
work   → route → apply (the write-up lands on the deal it names, `linked` only) →
         embed → commitments → internal tasks, AND a `meetings` row with the recap
         staged for a one-tap confirm at /decide
```

That is what makes "every memo" safe without a folder: a note has no participants, which is why automatic classification measured useless there (30% of 334 notes matched a record name, essentially all falsely), but a recording is SPEECH, so the same pass that judges a text conversation business-or-not can judge it. The precedent is the text sweep, which already forgets a private conversation the moment it is classified.

**⚠ THE PROVENANCE BRANCH HAD BEEN EXTENDED THREE TIMES AND EVERY FIX MISSED THE OTHER SOURCES.** Texts got an arm on 10-11; notes and calls got one on 10-14 after the Helper project's feed was found reading **"Email — Call with Eric Tuaone"**, false in both halves; a voice memo would have been the fourth. Four separate readers were each branching on the same question with their own predicate, which is precisely what let each fix be local. They are now one closed union in `src/lib/email-sweep/thread-source.ts`, over an exhaustive switch, so **adding a source makes the build fail until every reader has an arm** — and it did: the first `tsc` run after writing it refused `'recording'` because `database.ts` predated the migration. Two live bugs fell out of the collapse:

- **`importThreadAttachments` was fetching Gmail for note and call threads.** It bailed on `isIMessageThread` alone, so a `note:` id went to a real mailbox as a thread id — a round trip that can only 404, inside a try/catch, reporting nothing.
- **`commitments/chase.ts` was drafting replies to them.** Same test, same gap: `createDraft` against a synthetic thread id, and because the catch stores the composed text anyway, the row looks identical to one that was never eligible.

**⚠ AND THE REDACTION GATE WAS `imessage:`-ONLY, which is the one that would have mattered.** `redactPrivateTexts` filtered on that prefix, so under "read every memo" a personal recording's transcript would have stayed in `raw_markdown` — searchable by /api/thread-links — permanently. It is now `redactPrivateLocalThreads` in `email-sweep/`, covering every local prefix, deliberately not mail (a noise email is still a business record, and nobody's private life is in `moose@` the way it is in their Messages or their voice memos).

**⚠ NULLING THE TEXT IS NOT ENOUGH WHEN THE SOURCE IS SOUND, and deleting the file alone is a loop.** The transcript is the derivative; the m4a copied into a directory the app process can read is the original, and `bw-snapshot` would copy it straight back within six hours. So a discarded memo is also **skip-listed** — and the list is keyed on the audio FILE NAME rather than the recording's identifier, which is the one place these two programs disagree on purpose: the identifier→file mapping lives in the database, and giving the Full-Disk-Access binary a SQLite client to follow it would widen the one thing that must stay narrow. The list can only ever remove files from the copy set, so its header's promise that no input widens its reach is intact.

**⚠ MY OWN PLAUSIBILITY WINDOW WOULD HAVE DATED A MEETING TO 2053, and the test is what caught it.** The known failure here is Apple's: `ZCREATIONDATE1` is null for all 353 notes and a sentinel fallback dated that corpus to 1970. So the reader rejects an unreadable date rather than defaulting — but the first window was 2005-2100, and the obvious guard ("reject 1970") is aimed at the wrong end. Apple has shipped "seconds since 2001" and "seconds since 1970" in adjacent columns of the same table, and reading the second as the first produces a confident date 27 years in the FUTURE, not an obviously broken one. A recording cannot have happened after today; the window now closes at now + 2 days of clock slack. 9 tests over a synthetic store, including Recently Deleted by both signals, the un-renamed title fallback, and an unrecognised schema that must hand back the real column list rather than an empty answer.

**⚠ `summarizePending` HAD NO THREAD FILTER WHILE `routeThreads` HAS HAD ONE SINCE 10-08** — and this sweep needs the verdict, not just the side effect. Summarizing "whatever is newest" is usually the same rows, but an hourly mail sweep running concurrently can take a memo first, and then the gate reads a verdict belonging to someone else's thread. Same shape on the other end: `applyThreadUpdates` with no `linkIds` drains the whole queue, so the sweep would have reported every unapplied mail thread on the box as its own work.

**⚠ AND THE §13 ROW SAYING CLAUDE.md WAS 1,300 CHARACTERS FROM SILENT TRUNCATION WAS STALE BY 45,929 OF THEM.** The 10-12 split moved §12's full text to `docs/HARD-WON-RULES.md` and halved the file; measured today it is 104,071 characters with §12 at 21.9%. The row asking Richard which rules to retire is answered for now and has been corrected — a hand-written status paragraph drifts exactly like a hand-incremented count.

Also shared rather than forked (§12): the recap-and-register pass moved out of `notes/call-record.ts` into `meetings/record-local.ts`, which both transports now call. What stays in the call path is the only part genuinely about a phone call — iOS writes the counterparty into the title, so both ends are known structurally, without a similarity score. An in-person recording names nobody, which is the whole difference between the two callers. `notes/call-attach.ts` became `meetings/attach-recording.ts` for the same reason.

**Two habits worth more than any of this code**, both told to Richard rather than built: say who is in the room, the date and the deal name in the first ten seconds — whisper runs `-nt -bs 5` with no diarization, so the recap can only attribute what the audio says — and rename the memo after the deal, because `resolveMeetingTarget` matches a learned title or an exact record name deterministically, which is the difference between the write-up landing on Steelton by itself and waiting for a tap.

**Deliberately not built:** the in-app button (deferred by decision; the segmented-upload design is understood — ~60s segments transcribed on arrival, so a crash costs at most the last minute — and the Mac is where it would be trustworthy); transcript timestamps, which would help a reader jump through a 60-minute meeting but change a shared pass and add ~15% to every context; diarization, which nothing on this box has room for; and a new table, because `email_threads.fingerprint` already answers "have I seen this memo".

**Then it was run end to end against a SYNTHETIC store rather than waiting for Richard's first real meeting** — a `CloudRecordings.db` built with Apple's column names, and audio generated with macOS `say`, so the whole chain could be exercised before anyone depends on it. Both branches, cleaned up afterwards.

**The work branch, on a 62-second recording naming no existing deal** (deliberately — a real record name would have written onto a real project's feed):

```
whisper            62s of audio → 2.05s                      (30x realtime)
whole chain        2m50s wall clock, sequential
thread             relevance 'deal', 941 chars, 1 chunk embedded → quotable by Ber AI
meetings row       "Bramblewood Quarry Site Review", scope unfiled, status draft
  decisions        "Land acquisition price is capped at $4.2 million."
                   "Walk away if the new power feeder cost exceeds $2 million."
staged recap       pending, source_title = the memo's own name (the filing key),
                   model's rewrite kept separately, 4 attendees, 1 task
commitments        2, both side='us'
tasks              2, created with NO human confirm (§11's narrow exception) —
                   and "by Friday" resolved to 2026-10-16, which it is
routing            no record matched, so NOTHING was written to any project, and
                   the report says so in words rather than reporting silence
meeting_attended   1 row, against Richard's own contact
```

That last line matters: the 10-14 session found `meeting_attended` had never fired for any meeting, ever. It fires for a voice memo, from the owner override — nobody has to be named in the audio for the person who recorded it to be on the record.

**The noise branch, on a 20-second recording of a fictional conversation**, judged `noise` by the summarizer with no tuning: `raw_markdown` NULL, 0 chunks, no `meetings` row, no staged session, the row surviving as the tombstone carrying `{"relevance":"noise"}` and the reason string. Which is where the first real defect turned up.

**⚠ THE SWEEP REPORTED A DISCARD IT HAD NOT PERFORMED.** It printed "transcript, chunks and audio discarded" while the m4a was still on disk and the skip list had never been created. Two causes, both worth the finding: the note was composed unconditionally, and `discardMemoAudio` resolves an identifier to a file name by **re-reading the store at its default path** — which in the test was not the path the sweep had been handed. §12 already holds this rule twice over ("a pass that reports what it did must read before it writes", "name the reason beside the number") and I wrote the lie anyway, in the one place where the claim is about privacy. Now: `discardMemoAudioFiles(fileNames)` is the honest primitive and the SWEEP calls it, because the sweep is holding the row and never has to resolve anything; the resolving path survives for the inline call from `summarize-phase`, which only ever has a thread id, and it **counts what it could not name** rather than logging it. The report prints deletions and skip-listings separately and flags anything unmatched. 5 more tests.

**⚠ AND THE COMMITMENT AND TASK COUNTS WERE THE QUEUE'S, NOT THE RECORDING'S.** `extractCommitments`, `embedPendingThreads` and `promoteInternalCommitments` take no id filter and did not need one — whatever else is pending is work the hourly sweep would do anyway — but their return values then include it, so a sweep could report "2 commitments, 2 tasks" for a memo when both belonged to a mail thread. It happened to be honest here (both were genuinely from the recording, verified by `thread_id`), which is exactly how this class of mistake survives. The counts are now read back from the rows. The same trap was caught earlier in the build for `applyThreadUpdates`, which does take `linkIds`.

**Cleaned up afterwards:** both threads, 1 chunk, 1 meeting, 1 staged session, 2 commitments, 2 tasks and both audio files. One `meeting_attended` row was deleted from the append-only `activity_log` **by hand in psql, deliberately and once** — it renders on Richard's own contact profile under Activity, so leaving it would have put a meeting that never happened in front of him as history. The `INSERT`/`DELETE` rows for the test tasks and meeting were left where they are: they are true, they carry the old row in `metadata`, and tidying an audit log of accurate entries is worse than the noise.

**Verified:** 351 tests pass (26 new), `tsc` clean, build exit 0 with the route registered, lint unchanged at 23 pre-existing (none in the new files), the cron route answers its own `Unauthorized` rather than the gate's `Not authenticated` (so `middleware.ts` names it), 25 launchd agents loaded including `cron-voice-memo-sweep`, `bw-snapshot` rebuilt and re-signed and run **through launchd** — grant intact, two databases copied, `CloudRecordings.db` correctly reported absent rather than fatal — and the local-prefix `.or()` filter checked against the live corpus: 156 rows (155 texts, 1 note), no mail leaked.

⚠ **ONE THING REMAINS UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE: APPLE'S OWN SCHEMA.** The synthetic store uses the column names `readVoiceMemos` expects, which proves the pipeline and not the names. The container stays empty until Voice Memos.app is opened on the Studio, so those names are resolved from a candidate list against a schema nobody here has read — which is why a miss returns the real `pragma table_info` output and names the file to fix, rather than an empty answer that reads as "no recordings". Richard's three minutes are in §13. (DEPLOYED + MIGRATED)

**Done 2026-10-14 (a call about three deals updates three deals, and the matcher that found them was failing 9 times in 10):**

Richard, immediately after the entry below: *"sometimes our call will be talking about multiple different deals. Does this have the ability to parse out and update any important information on the particular project."*

**Measured before answering, and the premise turned out to be the normal case rather than an edge one: 9 of the 10 staged meetings name between 2 and 8 records each, median 5.** A broker hour or a portfolio review is inherently multi-deal. The recap had been parsing them out all along — `referenced_records` is a list with a per-record note, `tasks` carry a `record_hint`, and the confirm screen files one call onto several records at once. Two things were wrong underneath that, and only one of them was the thing he asked about.

**1. The matcher found almost nothing: 5 of 52 named deals resolved to a record.** The cause is one hand-picked number, and §12 already states the rule it breaks — a fuzzy threshold is measured against the real corpus, never chosen. `match_projects_by_name` ran at 0.3:

```
"Riverdale Site" → Riverdale — Cleveland-Cliffs (IL)   = 0.30303    ✓ matched
"Steelton Site"  → Steelton — Cleveland-Cliffs (PA)    = 0.290323   ✗ no candidates at all
```

Two names of identical shape, one letter of difference in the place name, opposite outcomes — and the blank pre-match was on a deal the platform holds 162 documents for. Lowering 0.3 moves the cliff to the next pair.

**The fix was not to write a matcher. `resolveMeetingTarget` already existed and already did this properly** — both tables, learned titles, an exact-name bar kept separate from a suggestion bar, an ambiguity refusal, and a stopword list tuned against this corpus including the industry words. It was wired to a meeting's TITLE and nothing else, while the deals a meeting NAMED went through the trigram threshold plus a bare `ilike` for opportunities, behind a *second* copy of `GENERIC_NAME_WORDS` that had already diverged. §12: a shared renderer wired to one surface is worse than no shared renderer — grep for one before building, and then for every surface that should be calling it. **5 of 52 → 20 of 52**, the trigram path and the duplicate list deleted, and 11 new matches re-read onto the sessions already sitting in the queue (`rematch-meeting-records.mts`, pending only — a confirmed session is the record of what a human was shown).

**⚠ Found on the first run of the better resolver: a compass direction is a qualifier, not a place.** "West Virginia Power Site", "West Virginia Data Center" and "West Virginia Portfolio" each resolved to **West Wendover** — wrong state, wrong deal — on the word *west*, while `virginia` matched nothing in the portfolio. The file's own comment keeps PLACE names out of the stopword list deliberately (Myton, Delta, Heber, Steelton are what distinguish these records), and a direction had been riding along inside that exemption. Both records here carrying one are identified by the word beside it, so nothing is lost. **23 matches with 3 wrong became 20 with 1.** The survivor is "Golden Dome Initiative" — the missile-defence programme — matching Alaska Golden Summit on *golden*; every guard tried for it also killed real matches, so it stays as a pre-tick to untick.

**⚠ Found while wiring it: the model's `kind` is a guess and a match is a fact.** The review screen seeded each target from the model's `referenced_records[i].kind` and the resolver's `matched_id` — two sources for one record. "Elite Solutions" is an `opportunities` row and arrives labelled `project`, so the confirm route would have sent an opportunity's uuid into its projects branch. `matched_kind` now travels with the match; the model's label never picks the table.

**2. Then the thing he actually asked about: every deal got the whole call.** The confirm step composed one `feedBody(meeting)` from the minutes and the fan-out loop wrote it to each record — and the prompt's own field header described that as the intent ("the update/note added to each record"). So Riverdale's feed carried the Steelton negotiation and the Weirton walk-through. §12 holds the field-level form of the same failure: one thread covering those three deals had newest-wins rewrite each deal's own address to "Steelton, Riverdale, Weirton". It is the describes-versus-mentions test, applied to a whole ENTRY.

Asked and answered (Richard chose the per-deal section, and chose to keep the confirm): prompt **`meeting-intake-1.2`** adds `discussion` per referenced record — everything the call said about THAT deal and nothing else, written to be read on that deal's page by someone who does not care about the others, and **null when the deal was only mentioned**. Verified first run on the real 56,197-character Steelton/Riverdale transcript, 127.8s:

```
✓ Steelton Site    485 chars  ~280 acres over two parcels, PPL at 420 MW ramping to
                              900 via new 230-kV lines, ballast solar on the capped
                              landfill, free slag aggregate, 3-month demolition
✓ Riverdale Site   395 chars  28 miles from downtown Chicago, four rail yards (UP, NS,
                              CNX, CSX), dark fiber, water treatment idled Aug 2025,
                              230 MW substation, ComEd procurement
· Indiana Site     NULL       named in passing — no paragraph
```

That last line is the part that matters most: the model was asked to return null for a deal it was only told about, and obeyed without tuning. A record entry is a claim that the call was about that record.

Two conditions make a slice safe rather than thin, and both are tested: the entry **says it is a slice** and names what else the call covered, and the whole call stays reachable — the minutes document is saved on every target in the same loop and now names the records in it. Decisions still reach every record, because a decision belongs to the call. And it **falls back to the whole call, never to nothing**, in the three cases that are one case (a session staged before 1.2, a target the reviewer added by hand, a deal judged mentioned-only); an empty entry would read as a call about nothing. The composers moved to `src/lib/meetings/feed.ts` so the rule is testable rather than only observable after a confirm — 7 tests.

**The queue was re-read under the new prompt** (`reextract-meeting-sessions.mts`, pending only, ~2 minutes of local model each, sequential because LM Studio serves one request at a time). All 7: **38 records named, 34 with their own paragraph, 4 correctly judged mentioned-only** (Eagle Mountain and the Steelton data room on the Tensor call, the Indiana site, ComEd's cold-storage property). The re-extraction also enumerated deals the first pass had folded together — 6→9 on the TensorIQ partnership call, 4→7 on the Zenthium portfolio review — and it re-matches in the same pass, because `match_candidates` is aligned to `referenced_records` **by index** and stale indices would open the review screen with one deal's record ticked against another deal's name. A second run reports nothing. `source_title` is untouched, so "Ber Wilson / Zenthium" is still the filing key on the call §13 flags.

⚠ **The cost, recorded rather than glossed:** the model is not deterministic, so the recaps now read differently — task counts moved in both directions (9→6 on Steelton/Riverdale, 8→11 on the Tensor call), and the TensorIQ sessions stopped listing "Elite Solutions" as a referenced record because this pass enumerated the DEALS rather than the counterparty, which lost an exact match while producing a better deal list. That is why re-extraction is a one-shot with a dry run and not a cron.

**Verified:** 325 tests pass, `tsc` clean, build exit 0, lint unchanged at 23 pre-existing, deployed and answering on the tailnet. (DEPLOYED + PUSHED)

**Done 2026-10-14 (a recorded call lands on the contact and the deal, not just in the corpus):**

Richard: *"when the iphone save a record call in our phone, it defaults to Notes. The title will always begin with "Call with". I would like to set up an way for you to read only those notes, grab the call transcript and update ber intelligence at both the contact level and the project level (or whatever makes the most sense). The transcript can really be summarized and stored to show activity on the project and log really important information discussed."*

The reading half shipped on 10-12 and works: `calls.ts` admits a note on iOS's own signal (a `Call with …` title plus audio) from any folder, whisper transcribes it on-box, and the transcript becomes an `email_threads` row that inherits all eight mail phases. So the session began by reading what that had actually produced on the live database rather than by building. Three gaps, each visible in one query:

1. **The project's feed said `source=email`, "Email — Call with Eric Tuaone".** `apply-phase.ts` branches on where a thread came from and had exactly two arms — iMessage, added 10-11, and everything else. A note fell into `else`. The migration that fixed this for texts (`20261011000003`) is the same fix, one source late: **when a function branches on provenance, every source that can reach it needs an arm, not just the one being added today.**
2. **`meetings` had no row for the call.** `search_meetings` and `get_meeting_content` read that table and nothing else, so the tools Ber AI reaches for when asked what was said on a call could not see it. The Meet importer writes that row; a phone call had no such door.
3. **Nothing reached the contact, and nothing ever had.** `Eric Tuaone` sat in the title, unused; `updates.mentioned_parties` came back `[]`. Measured: **9 meetings in the register and ZERO `meeting_attended` rows against any contact, for any meeting, ever.** `syncAttendeeActivity` keys entirely on `attendee.party_id`; no automatic path had ever set one, and only the hand-typed form at `POST /api/meetings` called it at all. Every Meet-imported call was invisible on the profile of everyone who had been on it.

**The shape of the fix is one adapter and one choke point.** A recorded call is handed to the machinery a Meet recording already goes through — `analyzeMeetingNotes` for the recap, `upsertMeetingFromImport` for the register, the review queue for the filing decision (§12: never fork a shared pass, add a caller). It deliberately skips the one step Meet takes that this must not: `fileMeetingDocument`. The transcript is already indexed in `thread_chunks` because it arrived as a thread, and filing it again would put the same words in the curated `chunks` index to compete with themselves — which is why `upsertMeetingFromImport` sets `index_ai: false` on its own row.

Attendee linking went INTO `upsertMeetingFromImport` rather than beside it, so the Meet path was fixed by the same change. `linkAttendees` stamps `party_id` from identity matches only (`exact_email`, `exact_name`); a `fuzzy_name` hit is the top trigram score with no ambiguity check — §12's unchallenged match — and stays a suggestion in the review screen. Backfilled with `scripts/one-shot/link-meeting-attendees.mts`: **7 meetings, 19 attendee links, 21 rows now on 8 contacts' profiles where there were none.** §12 again — fixing a producer changes nothing the reader sees.

**Who the call was with comes from iOS's title, and not from a similarity score.** The title is the best evidence on the artifact: the name is copied from the Contacts card, by somebody who already decided that person was worth storing, while the transcript may never say a surname. But **the name on the phone is not the name in the CRM** — measured on the one real call in this corpus, the note says `Eric Tuaone` and `parties` holds `Ericson Tua'one`. Exact match fails; `match_parties_by_name` scores them 0.473, a number that means nothing on its own, and §12 is explicit that a lone hit on a weak key is an unchallenged match rather than a unique one. So `call-party.ts` uses the structure of a human name instead: punctuation is deleted (not split on), a surname must match WHOLE and be at least four characters, a first name may be a prefix of something longer, a prefix alone is never enough, people are tried before organizations, and two candidates mean no match. The reason travels with the record — `eric → ericson; tuaone matches "Ericson Tua'one"`.

A call is written `scope='unfiled'` and `attachCallMeeting` moves it onto the deal when the thread router returns `linked` — the same line route-phase.ts already draws between a fact it was handed and a guess of its own. An `inferred` guess leaves the register alone, because the update feed is still asking the reviewer about it.

**⚠ Found: `ZCREATIONDATE1` IS NULL FOR EVERY NOTE IN THIS STORE — all 353.** Apple keeps the creation time in `ZCREATIONDATE3`; 1 and 2 are legacy columns that still EXIST, which is why selecting one returned no error and no value. `appleDate(null)` then fell back to the epoch, so **every note and every recorded call ingested since 10-12 was dated 1970** — on the thread's `first_at`, on the meeting row, and on the attendee's contact profile, where it rendered as "1969-12-31" (the epoch in Mountain Time). Coalesced, with a further fallback to the modification time, because 1970 is a value no reader can tell from a real one and it sorts to the top of every list ordered by date. The verified value for the one recorded call is 22:14:20 against a 22:30:20 modification — the sixteen minutes the call actually ran.

**⚠ Found: the sweep re-transcribed the same call on all four daily runs** — 30 seconds of whisper each time for an identical answer, and the recap pass added this session would have doubled it. The register is keyed on the note's stable identifier and a recording's audio never changes, so the question is now asked BEFORE whisper runs: **2:00 for the first pass, 0.25s for the second.**

**⚠ Found: `Call with <person>` was learnable as a project's filing key.** `source_title` is what the confirm step learns, and a title naming a PERSON names no deal — learning it would file every later call with a colleague, about anything at all, onto whichever deal the first one happened to concern, from its second occurrence onward. The identity-bearing-word floor does not catch it: `eric` and `tuaone` are perfectly distinctive words, which is the problem rather than the defence. `normalizeMeetingTitle` now refuses the form outright, anchored at the start so a deal title that merely mentions a call survives. It costs the auto-filing of a Meet invitation someone titled "Call with TensorIQ" — one click, once, against a misfiling that compounds silently.

**⚠ And found while writing the test for that: `project` was missing from `GENERIC_MEETING_WORDS`, and that list's own docstring used it as the example.** "Weekly Project Review Meeting … names no deal" — except every other word fell away and `project` was left standing as the identity-bearing one, so that title WAS learnable. `GENERIC_NAME_WORDS` in `analyze-meeting.ts` has held it all along, for the same reason: four live records are called "<place> Development Project". Neither of the two learned titles on the live table is affected.

**⚠ Found: the model lists COMPANIES as attendees, and our own company is a `parties` row.** Across the six imported transcripts the attendee lists name "Ber Wilson" three times and "Bloom Energy" once, each an exact name match against a real row with `is_organization = true`. The first backfill dry run would have recorded Ber Wilson as having attended four of its own calls. The flag decides, not the name — the same reason `meet-import.ts` drops our own company from filing candidates — and an organization is simply absent from the map the linker checks. **And the mirror of it: `matchExtractedParties` ANDs the company into its exact-name lookup, so an attendee listed under "Ber Wilson" against a party whose company reads "Ber Wilson LLC" matched nothing** — dropping that narrowing took the backfill from 7 links to 19, with name uniqueness checked at the choke point instead (that function's exact-name branch ends `.limit(1).single()`, which would hand back whichever of two Chris Walkers sorted first).

**⚠ Found: the contact's copy of a meeting is a projection, and it goes stale.** `syncAttendeeActivity` reconciled the party SET and never the metadata beside it, so after `attachCallMeeting` moved the call onto the Helper project, Eric's profile still read "not filed on a deal yet" and linked to the review queue. §12 — an orphaned projection looks perfectly live. It now rewrites a row whose stored copy disagrees (delete-then-insert, the pair of operations the function already performed on that table), compares field by field rather than by stringifying jsonb whose key order is not preserved, and `attachMeetingToRecord` re-syncs after a move. The same staleness applied to a reviewer retitling any meeting.

**⚠ Found: a text message read as "Document" on a project feed.** `SourceTag` had no entry for `imessage`, and its fallback is `SOURCE_CONFIG.document` — the same class of mislabelling the enum migration fixed in the database, surviving in the component that renders it. An enum member with no entry there is wrong-looking rather than missing, which is why it lasted. `imessage`, `call` and `note` now have their own tags, and the contact page no longer prints "Project meeting" for a scope of `unfiled`.

**Not built, deliberately:** a role-word filter for the attendee linker. The dry run linked a contact literally named **`Geologist`** (title: "29-year-old geologist") to the 10-12 water-rights call. That is a faithful consequence of the directory holding such a contact, and 12 of 76 people here have one-word names, so a two-token rule would cost twelve real contacts to fix one junk row. §12 — measure before building; the premise was that the linker needed a heuristic, and the measurement says the data needs a rename.

**Verified end to end on the live database**, not inferred: the call now carries a recap ("New York Life Public Infrastructure Development - Site Analysis & Capital Structure Planning"), a 5,954-character transcript, `kind='call'`, `scope='project'` on DUBHES Helper / Giovanni Resilience Campus, a staged session at `/intake?tab=meeting` holding iOS's own title as the filing key, and `meeting_attended` rows on Ericson Tua'one and Richard White dated 2026-09-21. `search_meetings` finds it and `get_meeting_content` reads it back. 318 tests pass, `tsc` clean, build exit 0, no new lint. (DEPLOYED + MIGRATED + PUSHED)

**Done 2026-10-12 (a recorded phone call becomes a transcript, and it needed neither Drive nor an Apps Script):**

Richard: *"the iphone auto creates the notes folder and names it however it does. How do I get that to automatically push up to the drive? That way pepper doesn't need to try and read my notes."*

Three measurements answered it, and the answer was that nothing needs to be pushed anywhere.

⚠ **THERE IS NO AUTO-CREATED FOLDER ON THIS ACCOUNT.** Folders present: `Notes`, `Recently Deleted`, `New Folder`, `Podcast episodes`. Both recordings sit in the DEFAULT folder. What iOS generates is the **note title** — `Call with <name>` — so title-plus-audio is the structural signal and a folder was never the thing to nominate. Only 4 of 352 notes carry audio at all (one real call, one 2025 screen-recording, the meditation tracks).

⚠ **THE RECORDING'S NOTE BODY IS 254 BYTES** — a title and an attachment pointer, with NO transcript. The audio IS the content, so pushing the text to Drive would have pushed nothing. And an Apps Script could not have reached the audio either: it runs in Google's cloud and cannot see Apple Notes. Getting the bytes out would need an Apple automation on the Mac or phone, and Shortcuts cannot extract a Notes attachment.

⚠ **AND THE AUDIO WAS ALREADY ON THIS MAC — my previous session's "Media holds ZERO files" was my own error.** I looked at `group.com.apple.notes/Media`; the real path is `group.com.apple.notes/Accounts/<id>/Media`. It holds **146 files**, including `Call with Eric Tuaone.m4a` (12.3MB) and `Call with Chelsea.m4a` (whose note has since been deleted, leaving the file orphaned). iCloud downloads Notes attachments **while Notes.app runs** — which it was not. Opening it moved the local store from **1 Oct to the same minute**, 348 notes to 352. That also confirms the staleness diagnosis from earlier in the day.

**So the shape is:** `bw-snapshot` copies Notes audio → the reader resolves a note's audio through the database → whisper transcribes on-box → the transcript becomes the note's body → every existing phase (summarize, route, append, commitments, embed) sees what was actually said. Nothing leaves the box, which is the whole reason this is better than the Drive route rather than merely equivalent to it.

**Audio extensions ONLY in the snapshot, and that is a privacy decision rather than a size one.** That Media tree holds family photos, screenshots and PDFs the platform has no use for; copying them into a directory the app CAN read would widen this binary's blast radius for nothing. 16 audio files, 214MB — of which most is meditation tracks, an accepted cost of keeping the allowlist dumb and free of database access.

⚠ **RESOLVED THROUGH THE FK CHAIN, NEVER BY FILENAME**, and this corpus proves why: `attachment → ZMEDIA → that row's ZIDENTIFIER / ZGENERATION1 / ZFILENAME` is exactly the on-disk layout. Three different notes each carry a `recording.m4a`, and `Call with Eric Tuaone.m4a` has TWO media rows in two directories because the file has two generations. A filename match would have been ambiguous on the one file that matters. Note the attachment row's own `ZIDENTIFIER` is **not** the directory — chasing that was the wrong turn, and the directory row is the one reached through `ZMEDIA`.

⚠ **MY FIRST MEMORY GUARD WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND MEASURING FIXED IT.** §12 says never run OCR and the chat model together — with the 22GB model resident, swap hit 21.5GB and `bw-ocr` was being KILLED, 2 documents in 20 minutes. I assumed whisper inherited that and gated on 2GB free.

- **"Free" is not the metric on this box.** With the chat model fully UNLOADED, free pages were still **135MB** — macOS holds the rest compressed and inactive (1.2M inactive pages, ~18.6GB reclaimable). A free-pages gate never opens, so the guard deferred every call forever while reporting a tidy reason for it. What actually moved on unload was *swap*: 20.7GB → 16.2GB.
- **Whisper is not OCR.** OCR's problem is rendering pages at 200 DPI. Whisper large-v3-turbo needs ~1.6GB and completed with the chat model fully resident: **29.7s** for a 16-minute call, against 13.9s with it unloaded. Both runs produced the same substance.

So the default is now to ATTEMPT, with a kill reported as a deferral carrying the remedy (`lms unload`, re-run, then `lmstudio-check.sh --fix`). The cost of trying and failing is one deferred transcript on the next sweep; the cost of refusing pre-emptively was the entire feature.

**Verified end to end on the real call.** 959 seconds of audio → 5,956 characters of transcript → one `email_threads` row at 6,170 characters, `pipeline='deal'`, `summary_state='pending'`. The content is exactly what the platform should hold: *"what we need to have put together so that we can get the PID for the public infrastructure development for New York Life… we have to meet with DA Davidson to do the capital structure… I already got Amy to do the broker's assessment"*, then the insurance, bonds and what the GC needs. ⚠ One artifact worth knowing: whisper fell into a repetition loop on a stretch of this audio (*"It's more defensive"* sixteen times), a known large-v3-turbo failure on certain passages. The bulk is clean; a repetition filter is not worth building for one occurrence.

**A call with no transcript is NOT stored.** Its body would be the title alone, which summarizes to nothing, indexes as noise, and then reads on the record as though the call had been ingested — the worst of the three outcomes. Deferred calls are reported and retried on the next sweep.

⚠ **AND THE REBUILD BROKE THE SNAPSHOT'S FULL DISK ACCESS, WHICH IS THE ONE THING RICHARD MUST FIX.** `scripts/build-snapshot.sh` warns in so many words that TCC keys the grant to the binary and that re-granting after every rebuild is the cost of the design. Verified live rather than assumed: after the rebuild, `launchctl kickstart` of the snapshot agent failed on **every** file — `0 database(s) copied, 2 FAILED` — including `chat.db`, so the TEXT sweep is affected too, not just Notes. My hand-runs succeeded only because this shell holds its own grant, which is exactly the trap the header describes ("the terminal you test from has its own grant, so a hand run succeeds while launchd's keeps being denied"). The snapshot is frozen at 10-12 09:00 until the grant is replaced. Promoted to §13.

**Also in this session:** the two doors are independent, which is what answers *"so Pepper doesn't need to read my notes"* better than Drive would — with `NOTES_FOLDER_NAMES` pointing at a folder that does not exist, the sweep reads **only** the recorded call and nothing else. 308 tests passing.

**Done 2026-10-12 (Apple Notes becomes a source, the recorded call turns out to have no bytes, and CLAUDE.md is cut by a third):**

Richard: *"How do we get connected to the notes. DO I need to have notes get pushed up into the Google Drive with an app script or something. We need those recorded calls to land in the right place and be ingested into the system."* And: *"Make the md much shorter if you can. There is probably some old baggage as we have iterated on this over and over."*

**The Apps Script question, answered.** No — and it would be worse on both counts. Apps Script runs in Google's cloud and cannot see Apple Notes at all; reaching them would need an Apple automation on the Mac or the phone to export into Drive, which is more moving parts AND would push private notes into the folder the nightly sync indexes as company knowledge. Reading on-box keeps it contained and lets the platform refuse what it should not hold. `bw-snapshot` already copies `NoteStore.sqlite` for exactly this.

⚠ **AND THE REASON THAT MATTERS MOST: 39 OF 332 NOTES (12%) HOLD CREDENTIALS IN PLAIN TEXT.** Measured before a line was written. `Ber Wilson Passcodes` carries Brighton Bank's passcode, the office front-door code, the Woodlands gate code, a GoDaddy customer number and password — and **the password to `info@berwilson.com`, which is Pepper's own mailbox**. Beside it: `ANTHROPIC_KEY = "sk-ant-api03-..."` in a note TITLE, `Clawdia AWS`, `Macu banking info`, `N8n lead client id`, `SSH terminal`. An ingested note is summarized, chunked and EMBEDDED into `thread_chunks`, retrievable by Ber AI and reachable by every outbound channel, and there is no un-embedding a secret you have already answered a question with. Pushing Notes to Drive would have done precisely that.

⚠ **AUTOMATIC CLASSIFICATION WAS BUILT, MEASURED AND THROWN AWAY — FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON, NOT A TUNING ONE.** The text sweep's classifier works because its strongest signal is WHO IS ON THE CONVERSATION: a CRM contact's phone number. **A note has no participants at all.** Scoring 334 real notes against every project, opportunity and contact name, with corpus-calibrated rare tokens exactly as the text sweep does, matched 101 notes (30.2%) — and essentially every one was false:

```
Costco                  -> matched 'box'
Movies/Shows to Watch:  -> matched 'richard'
Reptilian brain         -> matched 'economy'
Honey                   -> matched 'community', 'richard'
Crossing the chasm      -> matched 'technology'
```

§12 already says that sometimes the measurement says a threshold cannot work, and then the question is which signal actually exists. The signal that exists here is the one this platform already trusts everywhere else: **a human filing decision.** `GOOGLE_DRIVE_KNOWLEDGE_FOLDER_ID` works that way and §7's own note says nominating folders IS the control model. So `NOTES_FOLDER_NAMES` names the folders to read, unset means the sweep does nothing, and a note Richard has not filed there is never opened. The credential guard then runs INSIDE that folder as defence in depth.

**The guard fails closed and skips a note WHOLE** — title included, because a title like `Brighton bank 2484#` is itself the secret. Its reason names the RULE and never quotes the match, so a log file does not become the leak.

⚠ **AND THE GUARD'S FIRST TWO VERSIONS REFUSED REAL WORK.** 73 refusals -> 59 -> 39:
- **73:** the entropy rule read any 20+ character run as a key.
- **59:** URLs stripped first. A Drive file id is forty characters of exactly key-shaped text, and a work folder is full of links — an entropy rule that reads a URL as a secret refuses the very notes the feature exists for.
- **39:** a generated run must contain BOTH letters and digits. `website/host/deliver/what` and `projects/infographics` are ordinary words joined by slashes, and they were refusing `BW Task list Eric` and `Tasks` — two of the most work-relevant notes in the corpus.

**The decode.** A note's text is not text: `ZICNOTEDATA.ZDATA` is a gzip stream wrapping protobuf, and the readable note is one length-delimited field inside it (document(2) -> note(3) -> text(2)). The decoder walks it rather than scraping printable bytes, with no protobuf dependency — three nested fields and one varint reader. ⚠ **The check it cannot fake:** Apple stores the title separately in `ZTITLE1` and the first line of the body IS the title, so a correct decode must START with it. **333 of 348 decode (96%), 330 of 333 titles agree**, and the three "mismatches" are notes whose stored title concatenates two lines. A scraping decoder passes this on short notes and fails on any note holding a checklist, a table or an attachment — which is exactly the population that matters.

⚠ **I HIT THE WAL TRAP THAT `bw-snapshot`'s OWN HEADER ALREADY RECORDS.** Reading the bare `NoteStore.sqlite` reported this corpus as ending **2026-09-15 with 334 notes**. With the 63MB `-wal` it runs to **10-01 with 348** — and the only recorded call on the machine was in the part the main file could not see. The header says it in so many words ("reading NoteStore.sqlite without its 63MB WAL hid a call recording from three weeks earlier entirely"), written by the session that built the snapshot the day before. Reading the repo's own comment first would have saved the measurement.

⚠ **RECORDED CALLS CANNOT COME FROM NOTES ON THIS BOX, AND THAT IS NOT FIXABLE FROM HERE.** The Media directory holds **ZERO files**. Notes downloads attachment bytes lazily and only while Notes.app is running, and `bw-snapshot` copies databases, not media. So `Call with Eric Tuaone` (2026-09-21, the one recorded call in 348 notes — the rest of the audio is meditation tracks and 2025 voice memos) exists as a database row and nowhere on disk. Rather than pretend, a note's attachments are NAMED in the thread body with the reason they are absent and where to put audio instead. **The right place for a recorded call is Drive or `/intake?tab=meeting`:** whisper already transcribes audio attached to a meeting (`/api/meetings/[id]/transcribe`), and `meet-import` already COUNTS "recordings in Drive with no transcript" — it simply never transcribes them. Making that branch return the files and feed `transcribeAudio` is the next build and is now item 2 in §13.

⚠ **AND NOTES SYNCS ONLY WHILE Notes.app RUNS.** Notes.app was not running on the Studio and the local store was eleven days behind the phone, with no error anywhere. A stale corpus here is silent — the sweep reports success having read nothing new — which is §12's rule about a liveness check needing a clock rather than a count.

**Shipped:** `src/lib/notes/{decode,secrets,read,to-thread,sweep}.ts`, `/api/cron/notes-sweep` (named in `middleware.ts`), `scripts/verify-notes-decode.mts`, a launchd agent at :45 past the four snapshot hours (10 minutes behind the text sweep, since both read the same snapshot and LM Studio serves one request at a time). A note becomes an `email_threads` row prefixed `note:` — the same move the text sweep made, so summarize/route/append/embed/commitments/predecide all apply unchanged. **ONE note is ONE thread**, unlike a text: a chat is a stream that had to be cut into 6-hour sessions, where a note is already the unit somebody opened and named. The thread id carries the modification time, so an edited note re-summarizes rather than leaving a stale answer in place. 308 tests passing, 24 agents loaded.

**CLAUDE.md: 149,994 -> 98,551 characters (-34%), with 51,449 of headroom.**

Richard asked for it much shorter and named the reason: *"There is probably some old baggage as we have iterated on this over and over."* He also restated the purpose, which is now the second paragraph of the file: *"an intelligence platform to store and query information, along with a digital assistant — Pepper — which automates all of the data entry."* Two jobs; §13's next-work list is ordered against them.

⚠ **THE PRUNE CAME OUT OF §12, WHICH THE FILE ITSELF SAYS IS RICHARD'S CALL AND NOT A SESSION'S — HE MADE IT.** Measured first, because the file's own rule is that the bloat has never once been where the rule assumed: §12 was 70,216 characters (46.8%) across 178 rules; §13 was 27,399 (18.3%); §4 14,132; §7 10,172.

**Nothing was deleted.** All 178 rules moved verbatim, with their evidence, into **`docs/HARD-WON-RULES.md`** — the third such split, after the session history (09-23, at 606k) and the open items (10-01, at 143k). §12 now carries ~60 rules as the claim and the fix, at 20,318 characters: the ones a session is most likely to hit, chosen over the ones a script now asserts or a shared helper now enforces. The new file's header says plainly that a rule retired from CLAUDE.md is not a rule that stopped being true, and to grep there before concluding something has never bitten this project.

**The §12 rule queued yesterday is now in**, as an extension of *"filling a blank and overwriting a value are different acts"*: **which act is safe turns on whether the source DESCRIBES the field's subject or only MENTIONS it.**

**Done 2026-10-12 (Pepper writes to the CRM without asking, she can text from the box, and three of the four premises behind the feature were wrong):**

Richard's direction, verbatim: *"I want pepper to be aware of every single detail she can from looking at our emails, texts and recorded calls... I then want her to update the CRM with every detail. I would like her to get rid of older crappy data like old proposals, weak deal description etc... she can update it all automatically without our approval. The only thing she cant update automatically is something that we have done manually that isn't obvious that she could update it."*

That is a deliberate amendment to §11, the second one (the first was 2026-08-23, which let the sweep read both mailboxes on a schedule). The invariant §11 exists to protect — no project, opportunity, party or lead is CREATED without a human confirm — is untouched and is enforced in code below. What changed is that UPDATING an existing record no longer needs a press.

**What replaces the approval gate.** Not trust. Three properties `applyFieldUpdates` guarantees and no caller can opt out of:

- **Attributable.** Every write carries Pepper's own auth user (`ec89f3ee…`, the `info@` seat), so `log_activity()` records who did it rather than "system". `assertPepper()` runs at the top of the pass and THROWS if that seat has moved — a run that cannot attribute itself does not run, because the whole safety argument would be silently worthless.
- **Bounded.** `src/lib/provenance/fields.ts` is a whitelist of 40 columns across five tables. A field not named there cannot be machine-written at all, which keeps `projects.confidential` and the three `economics_*` rollups out of reach by construction rather than by care.
- **Legible.** The pass RETURNS what it changed, per field, with the before value — which is what the morning message reads out. A change nobody is told about is the failure mode this design must not have, and it is why a `confidential` project is skipped entirely: her report is an outbound channel a protected deal may never reach (§12), so a change she could not report is one she does not make.

**Richard's carve-out, in code.** "Overwrite anything except something human-entered that looks like it could be important (partner split percentages and things like that) — those ones just alert." That is a per-FIELD question, so it needed a per-field answer: `record_field_provenance` (one row per table/record/field, `written_by` human|pepper) and a `tier` on every registry entry. `guarded` fields — money, ownership splits, legally-effective dates, and the judgement calls a human makes by weighing what no email states — are proposed into `field_update_proposals` when a human typed them. `open` fields she owns.

⚠ **ABSENCE OF A PROVENANCE ROW MEANS HUMAN, NOT PEPPER.** Nothing written before today has a row, and `activity_log.field_changes` only carries a column diff since 09-30, so most existing values cannot be attributed either way. Reading absence as "she wrote it, so she may replace it" would have handed her every hand-curated figure on the first run. 14 tests on the decision table, and the three that matter are the three provenance states of a guarded field.

⚠ **THE ASYMMETRY THAT ONLY THE DRY RUN COULD HAVE FOUND, AND THE RULE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX.** The first dry run, with "newest evidence wins" on open fields, would have done this:

```
Steelton:   "215 S Front St, Steelton, Dauphin County, PA" -> "Steelton"
Riverdale:  "Riverdale, Cook County, IL (Chicago)"         -> "Steelton, Riverdale, Weirton"
Weirton:    "Weirton, Hancock County, WV"                  -> "Steelton, Riverdale, Weirton"
W Wendover: Sector government       -> real_estate
Whiskey:    Sector infrastructure   -> institutional
Zorro:      Sector infrastructure   -> technology
```

One thread covers all three Cleveland-Cliffs sites and is linked to each, so its `location` is all three names. Four projects would have been reclassified off a human's considered sector by a per-thread guess. **The rule: evidence that DESCRIBES the subject of a field may overwrite it; evidence that merely MENTIONS the subject may only fill it.** A person's title comes off their own signature block, so newest-wins is right there. A deal's location in a thread about three deals is incidental, and no amount of recency makes it authoritative. `tier` answers "whose value is this"; `fillOnly` answers "does this source actually know". After the fix: 74 writes became 57, then 17 once people were deduped, and **zero of them replace an existing value.**

⚠ **MEASURING INVERTED THE WHOLE FEATURE.** The premise was that deal records were the dirty thing. Measured: 19 projects hold **ONE** blank location, **ZERO** null sectors and **ONE** blank description. The dirt is the rolodex — **52 of 76 people had no title, 36 no email, 28 no company** — against 144 linked threads whose summaries name those people with their titles and addresses. So this shipped mainly as a contact enricher with deal fields as the small half, which is the reverse of the plan. 11 contacts filled on the first run: Merlin Corbin → Zenthium, Brook Stonebraker → Xmission, Ken Berg → Avenues Consulting, Taylor Englert → Englert Mining, Mark Welsko → CTO, WES.

⚠ **AND IT NEEDS NO MODEL CALL, WHICH ALSO ONLY MEASURING SHOWED.** Planned as one extraction per record — 26 calls, ~20 minutes of a single-threaded box, nightly. Then `email_threads.summary` turned out to be **jsonb**, already carrying `location`, `sector`, `key_facts` and a `people[]` array with name/title/company/email, because the sweep extracted all of it months ago. The pass is a read: **about three seconds for the whole portfolio.** §12 already says to check whether the data is already on the row before calling it an extraction problem; this is the second time that line has paid for itself (the first was `/decide`, which looked like schema work and was a UI change).

**Six defects found in the building, five of them mine:**

1. **The registry named four columns that do not exist** — `projects.client_name`, `projects.next_steps`, `parties.bio`, `milestones.title` — every one written from memory. The real columns are `client_entity`, `next_step` (singular, and only on `opportunities`), `relationship_notes`, `label`. An update naming a missing column fails at runtime inside an unattended pass, and the only symptom is a field that is never curated. `scripts/verify-provenance-registry.mts` now asserts all 40 against `information_schema` plus the three Postgres enums against `pg_enum`, via a new one-signature `enum_members()` RPC. 43 green.
2. **`projects.sector`/`stage`/`status` are real enums, so §12's filter rule applies to WRITES too.** A value outside the enum fails the whole UPDATE with `22P02` and a NULL row set — not the row — so one plausible-sounding `energy` from a model would have silently discarded every other field on that record's update and the pass would have reported writing nothing. `canWrite` refuses a non-member BEFORE the blank branch, so filling an empty enum column cannot sneak one past either.
3. **`parties` is GLOBAL, so enriching inside the per-record loop wrote Eric's row eleven times in one pass** with three different readings of his own title — "CEO", "Chief Executive", "Founder & Chief Executive" — and whichever record ran last won. Worse, Mark Welsko appeared twice inside ONE record with two different companies, because mentions were keyed on email-or-name and a person mentioned once with an address and once without is two keys for one human. Now deduped by the MATCHED PARTY, once, across the whole run, taking the newest non-empty value per FIELD rather than the newest mention wholesale (which had silently discarded a good email fill).
4. **It proposed `Richard White: Title="Advisor"`** — a model's incidental role guess for one thread, about to be written onto the reader's own contact record. Our own people are now never curated from mail: an internal title is an EMPLOYMENT fact that lives in `personnel` (§4) and is set by a human. Keyed on `team_members.party_id` **and** the `@berwilson.com` address, both, for the reason §12 gives about the Pepper self-loop — a guard on a display string is defeated by a rename that is itself a good idea.
5. **A text session's `gmail_thread_id` is PRESENT and prefixed `imessage:`, not null.** My first draft tested for null, so it labelled all 115 text sessions as email — and would have told a reader asking "where did she get that" the wrong answer about the source. `isIMessageThread` already existed for exactly this. §12: grep for the helper before writing the test yourself.
6. **`documents` has no `opportunity_id` and no `updated_at`.** An opportunity's files live in `opportunity_documents` (which also has no `excluded_at`), so a curator reading only `documents` would curate every opportunity as though it had no paperwork at all — the parallel-table split §12 already names, where `drive-sync`'s ownership check reading one of the two re-claimed an opportunity's file as company knowledge. Also checked rather than assumed: `meetings.meeting_date` is a DATE, not a timestamp.

⚠ **AND THE SAFETY CLAIM WAS FALSE UNTIL THE FIRST LIVE RUN TESTED IT.** "Every change is attributable and recoverable from `activity_log`" — measured immediately after 17 real writes across 1 project, 4 opportunities and 11 parties: **`activity_log` held exactly ONE row.** Two independent pre-existing reasons. `opportunities` and `parties` carry **no `log_activity` trigger at all** (checked against `pg_trigger`; `projects`, `milestones` and `project_spv_participants` have one), so 15 of 17 writes left no audit row whatsoever. And on `projects`, `field_changes` was NULL, because the generic column diff added 09-30 is gated to twenty governance tables — `documents`/`updates` carry hundreds of KB of text and diffing those would store both copies on every edit (§4). The fix is **not** to retype `log_activity()`: §12 forbids transcribing that 148-line function by hand, and this would be a change to twenty tables' audit trail to serve one pass. Instead the pass records its own `previous_value`, so reversibility holds by construction for every table the curator can touch, present and future. **The trigger gap on `opportunities` and `parties` is real and is logged as a finding rather than quietly fixed** — adding an audit trigger to the contact directory changes the log's volume for every human edit too, which is a decision rather than a repair.

**Idempotent, and asserted rather than hoped.** `scripts/verify-curator-idempotent.mts` runs the pass twice with `force` on both and fails if the second run writes anything. §12 requires that pairing by name, after the separation pass announced *"org chart marked departed"* on a second run having changed nothing. Verified: run 2 wrote 0.
