**Done 2026-09-30 (deal documents stopped answering as company knowledge, and a filing decision finally sticks; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's question: "On the Ber Wilson Profile I see alot of attachments falling into the knowledge base. Seems like every email attachment is landing there. Isn't that going to risk giving us data that isn't relevant to Ber Wilson? I would like attachment to land in the pertinent project they belong to so the AI can search them, but not sure this is structured properly. Maybe docs that don't know where they go land in a queue and they can be assigned to a project or deleted easily? Analyze this and tell me what you would do."**
- **The concern was right and the stated mechanism was wrong, which changed the whole fix.** `importThreadAttachments` opens with `if (link.record_kind !== 'project' && link.record_kind !== 'opportunity') return 0` — mail can never become company knowledge, and there is no company branch anywhere in the sweep. What Richard was looking at was the nightly **Drive knowledge sync**: **142 of 154 live `is_company` documents**, the other 12 hand-uploaded capability statements.
- **⚠ AND IT WAS WORSE THAN IT LOOKED. Company chunks were 1,239 of 6,536 — 19% of the entire searchable index** — and `filter_include_company` is an **OR branch**, set by `synthesize/route.ts:313` and `agent-tools.ts:735` whenever a question is scoped to a record. So every one of those passages widened every project question, and `getCompanyKnowledge()` hands them to `assessFit()` as *"RELEVANT BER WILSON EVIDENCE"*. The top of that corpus by volume was not capability evidence at all: **`Phase 1 Environmental report.pdf` 134 chunks, `W9126G26D0003 - Award.pdf` (a USACE award) 79, the IAN/WELSKO patent set 207 across four files, `Army NEW LEASE..pdf` 27, `Title commitment 2026.pdf` 23, and `4-badge-usage-sheet.html` — 54 chunks of logo usage guidelines.**
- **⚠ THE INVERSE PROBLEM IS THE BIGGER ONE AND NOBODY HAD SEEN IT: 903 email attachments are never imported at all.** 837 sit in 421 threads with no record link, 60 on lead-linked threads and 6 on steel-deal-linked ones, all of which that same guard returns 0 for. The gap was never over-filing. Deliberately left for a second pass — and the right shape is to stage the *reference* (thread, message, attachment id, name, size) and fetch only on a filing decision, because 903 files at 30–135s of local document AI each is days of compute on a box at 95MB free.
- **`drive_folder_path` was in hand all along and dropped from the row.** The sync passes `file.path` to its `arrivals` notification and never wrote it, while the project importer had recorded the same column since September — which is why 142 cards read as undifferentiated sludge with no origin. One line on the insert, one on the update, plus `getFolderName()` so the recorded path names the **nominated folder** and not just the subpath below it (`listFolder` returns paths relative to the folder it was handed, so a file sitting directly in one came back with an empty string).
- **Backfilled, and the leak named itself in one query.** `Corporate /M & A/` is a **per-deal subtree**: GET Turkiye 22 docs/42 chunks, Tooele Market & Manufacturing Reports 11/190, GridEdge Modular Datacenter 8/225, Tooele Business Documents 5/68, IAN 3/12, M&A/M&A 3/23, USACE Fort Johnson 2/88 — **648 of the 1,239 company chunks, 52%**. `Corporate` also holds genuinely company shelves (NDA NC 105, Fundraising 92, Board Meetings 16), which is why the answer is filing the documents rather than un-nominating the folder.
- **⚠ TWO TRAPS HAD TO BE FIXED BEFORE ANY CLEANUP COULD HOLD, AND BOTH LOOKED LIKE THEY WORKED.** **Delete and retire were each no-ops against a Drive-synced document.** A hard delete removed the row, and `known` is built from existing rows only — so the file looked new and was re-imported the same night. A retire set `superseded_at`, and `returning = !!prior?.superseded_at` calls `restoreDocument()` on it, *actively undoing the decision*. So the Trash button on `/company` was cosmetic: clean up those 142 cards and they are all back tomorrow.
- **The row is now its own tombstone.** `excluded_at` / `excluded_reason`: the row stays, so `drive_file_id` still blocks a re-insert through its unique index, and the sync skips it outright. **The check must come BEFORE the restore branch** — after it, it does nothing, because `returning` has already un-retired the row. Chunks are deleted so the file leaves retrieval; the bytes stay, so the call is reversible. **Verified against a real sync run:** excluded two documents, ran the full sweep — `skippedReasons: {'excluded by hand': 2}`, `superseded=0`, one row per Drive file, both exclusions held.
- **⚠ `ownedElsewhere` READ ONLY `documents`, NEVER `opportunity_documents`.** An opportunity's Drive files live in a different table that this ownership check never consulted, so a file already filed on an opportunity was re-claimed as company knowledge — one file, two rows, two sets of chunks. Latent at **0 collisions and only 2 opportunity docs from Drive**, and guaranteed to fire the moment filing to opportunities became possible, which is exactly what this change makes possible. Found by reading the check while writing the thing that would break it.
- **NOTHING RE-EMBEDS. Chunks are RE-POINTED, never rebuilt.** A stored vector is only meaningful against the model and the width that produced it (§12, 09-30) — but the *text* does not change when a document is re-filed, so the existing vectors stay exactly valid at their new address. A project move is one UPDATE of `project_id` + `is_company`; the opportunity move crosses tables. That is what keeps the whole job off the local model: rebuilding 142 documents at 30–135s each would have been hours of contended GPU for no change in the numbers.
- **⚠ IN THE CROSS-TABLE MOVE THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING.** `chunks.document_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so deleting the source row before re-pointing destroys the vectors the move exists to preserve. Insert the `opportunity_documents` row (carrying `drive_file_id`, so both importers recognise it as owned), re-point the chunks, *then* delete. The storage object is deliberately **not** copied — `storage_path` is only a key and both tables sign and remove by it verbatim, so re-using it avoids a copy and an orphan.
- **Round-trip tested on real data, 13 assertions, database left as found.** `GridEdge_DC_Investor_Deck bp 4.0.pdf` → GridEdge opportunity: 2 chunks reported and 2 re-pointed with `opportunity_id` set, `document_id` null, `is_company` false; source row deleted; storage path unchanged; zero orphaned chunks; reversed; then excluded (2 chunks gone, `excluded_at` set) and restored. **The reversal exposed my own gap** — the restore insert did not carry `extracted_text`, so the document came back with none. Re-ran the AI pass on it: 2,271 chars, 2 chunks, summary present, exactly as before. Corpus re-measured afterwards at **1,239 company chunks and 154 live company documents — identical to the start**.
- **The queue is COMPUTED, not stored, so it cannot disagree with the records it proposes against.** `bestMatch` + `loadTargets` are pure string and set work with no model call, and `/decide` already loads its rows server-side, so there is no producer pass, no staleness and no schema for proposals. **One pass backs both surfaces** — `/decide` filters it, `/company` renders all of it with the proposal offered as a chip. Verified: `summarizeDecideQueue().documents`, `findMisfiledCompanyDocuments()` and the filtered `loadCompanyKnowledge()` all return **38**, and the breakdown sums to the total (80+96+38+38 = 252).
- **A document with no match is not in the queue.** 154 candidates → **21 with a proposed home, 17 images**, and the other 116 are left alone. Reaching for the closest record is how real evidence lands on the wrong deal (§12); a capability statement genuinely has no deal home.
- **⚠ `bestMatch` READS `summary.deal_name` IN PREFERENCE TO ITS OWN `subject` ARGUMENT** — `summary?.deal_name ?? subject`. So a richer subject passed alongside a summary that has a `deal_name` is silently discarded. The adapter composed `file name + Drive folder` into the subject and set `deal_name` to the bare file name, which threw the folder away: the patents, the USACE award and the ESA all came back `NO MATCH` inside the function while matching at **0.99 in isolation with identical inputs**. Took an instrumented run to find, because every input I tested by hand was the one that worked. Fixed by composing ONE name and passing it to both. **17 proposals became 21, and 101 chunks became 298.**
- **`filing_confirmed_at` is what lets a computed queue reach zero.** Dismissing an unfiled document means *"it is right where it is"* — a real answer, not the absence of one. Without recording it, the proposal reappears on every page load however often it is dismissed, and a queue that cannot reach zero teaches people to accept rows to clear them.
- **`/company` is now the workhorse, because the matcher deliberately cannot reach the worst offenders.** The ESA, the USACE award and the title commitment name no record, so they are correctly left unproposed — which means manual triage has to be good. Each card now carries **its retrieval footprint** (*"134 passages"* — the fact the decision actually turns on, and it was nowhere on screen), **the Drive shelf it came off**, a one-click *File on <record>* where there is a proposal, a bounded record picker, and *Set aside*. Filing controls are never behind hover (§12) and the picker is width-capped because a native select sizes to its widest option.
- **Delete is offered ONLY on a document that did not come from Drive**, since on a synced one it is the futile path. `/company` also stopped listing retired rows inline — seven of them were reading as part of the corpus — and they are a collapsed count with the set-aside ones.
- **⚠ A MEETING WHOSE ONLY TARGETS WERE LEADS FILED ITS VERBATIM TRANSCRIPT AS COMPANY KNOWLEDGE.** `meeting-intake/confirm` fell back to `{ kind: 'company' }` when no project or opportunity matched, writing `is_company` chunks — so a broker call about a dozen sites nobody chose to pursue became evidence for scoring every future lead. Zero `is_company` transcripts exist today, so it is caught **before** it fired, and it was about to: one broker has ~25 more sites to show and that fan-out IS the signal to route to leads. Files as `is_reference` now — searchable and quotable, which is the whole point of filing it, without being a claim about the company's capabilities.
- **⚠ `certifications/upload` HAD NEVER ONCE WORKED, AND THE DATABASE PROVES IT.** The insert set **none** of `project_id` / `entity_id` / `is_company` / `is_reference` / `meeting_id` / `steel_deal_id`, under a comment reading *"no project_id or entity_id — company-level"*. `documents_scope_check` has demanded one of them since `20260803000001`, so every attempt violated it and returned a bare *"Insert failed"*. **Zero rows with `doc_type = 'certification'` exist.** One line.
- **New images are no longer taken into the corpus**, with a counted reason — 13 site photos and 4 logo SVGs were listed among the capability statements, and where OCR could read one it was embedded. **Confirmed live in the nightly cron minutes after deploy:** `skippedReasons: {"over 30MB": 3, "unreadable type: application/x-zip-compressed": 1, "image — not knowledge-base material": 1}`. Existing images stay until set aside, because the `unchanged` check correctly runs first.
- **Not done, and named rather than quietly skipped:** `content_sha256` is NULL on all 154 company documents, so hash-based duplicate detection (there are two copies of the IAN patents — one company, one already on the IAN Networks project folder) needs its own pass over storage. Board minutes still write `is_company` **chunks** while their document row is not `is_company`, so they are in the company retrieval corpus and absent from the `/company` list — 0 rows today. And the `Corporate /M & A/` subtree will keep producing new company-scoped deal documents until the documents in it are filed and the shelf is reconsidered; that is a curation decision, not a code one.
- **Two Claude sessions shared the repo for this whole session** (§12, and a fourth recorded occurrence). The tree did not typecheck when I started — `src/lib/leads/forward.ts` had been renamed to `handoff.ts` with its importer not yet updated — and `MapView` gained a required `railMode` prop mid-session that its caller did not have, producing errors in files I had never opened. Both resolved when they committed. Staged all 21 files **by name**; verified `src/types/database.ts` carried only my 15 lines before staging it.

- **Construction went to a project, and the platform knew that but never said so.** `promoteTargetFor` mapped construction→project, steel→steel deal, corporate→opportunity, dino→email. `ROUTE_DESTINATIONS` held the sentence and only the detail sheet rendered it, so the queue's own tabs answered nothing. Dino alone needs two of those. Adding `flooring` to the existing shape would have collided with all three axes at once.
- **⚠ AND IT WAS A CHECK CONSTRAINT, WHICH IS THE §12 TRAP VERBATIM.** `leads_route_check` listed five literals. A sixth typechecks, deploys, and then fails at **every INSERT** until someone remembers the constraint exists — while the triage prompt hardcoded the same five values *in prose*, so a new lane meant a migration, a constraint swap, a prompt edit and a rebuild. Four places, none of which fails loudly if you miss one. That, not effort, is the argument against hard-coding each trade as it comes up.
- **So the taxonomy is data.** `lead_categories`, one row per line of business, carrying everything that varies: `destination` (what it becomes), `routing_rule` (the sentence read to the model verbatim), `handoff_email`, `drive_folder_id`, `share_with`, `publish_sheet`, `tone`, `sort_order`, `active`, `system`. Adding a line of business is an INSERT.
- **`leads.route` keeps its name, its 1,437 rows and all eight indexes.** Only the CHECK is replaced, by an FK to `lead_categories(key)`. No data migration, no rename churn, and the landmine is gone at its root rather than documented.
- **THE KEY IS THE TRADE, THE LABEL NAMES WHO DOES IT.** `plumbing` labelled *"Dino Plumbing"*, not a key of `dino_plumbing`. If Dino ever stops doing plumbing that is a label and an address, not a re-keying of history — and `on update cascade` means even a genuine rename carries its leads with it. **Measured on a disposable transaction:** renaming `flooring` → `flooring_renamed` moved its lead, and renaming back moved it home.
- **`on delete` deliberately left at NO ACTION, which is what `active` is for.** A lane with leads **cannot be deleted at all** — verified live, `delete from lead_categories where key='construction'` raises 23503. Closing a lane is `active = false`: existing leads keep their label and stay readable, the model is no longer told it exists, and `resolveRoute` coerces any new arrival to `unknown`. Verified: `resolveRoute('dino')` → `unknown`, while the one dino-routed lead still renders as *"Dino (retired)"*.
- **Seeded with the five existing values first**, so all 1,437 rows satisfied the new FK the moment it was added, then `plumbing`, `hvac` and `flooring`. `dino` retires to inactive.
- **The triage prompt's routing block is GENERATED from the active lanes.** Rendered and read back before trusting it: seven lanes, `dino` correctly absent, the JSON shape's route union built from the same list. Two rules were added to carry the cases that actually decide this: **a trade inside a building project IS the building project** (a GC inviting bids on a school is construction even though the email lists twelve trades), and **who is buying tells you more than what is mentioned** (an owner wanting a rooftop unit fixed is a service lead even though the building is commercial).
- **The prompt version now carries a fingerprint of the category set** — `lead-triage-3.0+st41ze`. Without it, a lead routed before flooring existed is indistinguishable in `ai_queries` from one where the model saw flooring and declined, which is precisely the question to ask when a lane looks like it is under-firing.
- **⚠ THE MODEL IS ASKED WHAT THE WORK IS, NEVER WHERE IT SHOULD GO** — the 09-29 rule, applied rather than rediscovered. The model cannot see the database; the mapping from *"this is HVAC service"* to Brent's inbox is configuration set once. Which is also why the tool declaration for `list_leads` now carries **no `enum`**: declarations are a static array re-sent every request (30.2k chars of fixed overhead), so a stale enum would name a lane that must not be used and hide one that should. The executor matches leniently on key **or** label, and says so when it matched neither rather than returning an empty queue that reads as *"no leads"*.

- **The detail sheet now leads with the lane's OWN destination.** Four equal buttons is part of why **1,268 leads were scored and none was ever promoted**: every promotion re-asked a question the triage pass had already answered, so the reader answered none of them. The other destinations are one disclosure away — never a dead end, just no longer a quiz.
- **A handoff lane with no address says so in place and links to settings**, and `/decide` blocks Accept on it with the reason. Three distinct outcomes that must not collapse into one: a lane with a destination, an unsorted lead needing a human, and a lane that would fail on press. - **`/decide`'s `forward` action became `handoff`, and the button names its destination** — *"Hand off to Dino Plumbing"*. *"Send to Dino"* was accurate while Dino was the only exit and became a lie the moment a flooring lead could take the same one.
- **One read-only sheet per lane that needs one, plus `share_with`.** The sheet mechanism already existed for exactly this audience — and was hardcoded to steel and dino. **⚠ It was also shared with the DOMAIN only, which reaches nobody outside berwilson.com — that is most of this audience.** A flooring subcontractor was being published a list they could not open, with nothing anywhere reporting it. `shareWithAddresses` grants named outside addresses reader on the lane's sheet and its Drive folder, idempotently, asserted every run because a grant removed by hand in Drive is invisible from here (§12, 08-26).
- **⚠ SPLITTING A LANE ORPHANS ITS SHEET, FROZEN AT THE MOMENT IT CLOSED AND LOOKING PERFECTLY LIVE.** "Dino Leads" had been updated by that same morning's sweep. Orphans are now retitled *"(no longer updated)"* rather than trashed — the link keeps working for whoever has it bookmarked, and the title says what happened. **And the live set is built from the lanes that SHOULD publish, not the ones that succeeded**: built from the successes, one transient Drive error would retire a live lane and tell the reader to stop trusting it. Caught while writing it, against a comment that already said it must not happen.
- **Ran for real against live Drive:** *Steel Leads* updated in place (14 rows, not recreated — bookmarks survive), *Dino Plumbing Leads* / *Dino HVAC Leads* / *Flooring Leads* created, *Dino Leads* retitled. A second run retired nothing and created nothing — idempotent.
- **⚠ A CLASS STRING READ FROM THE DATABASE IS NEVER GENERATED.** The obvious design was a `badge` column holding the chip's Tailwind classes. Tailwind v4 emits only what it finds by scanning source, so those classes would produce an unstyled chip with no error anywhere. The database stores a tone **name** against a fixed palette in `src/lib/utils/leads.ts`, and the settings screen offers it as a dropdown rather than a text field for the same reason. The API rejects an unknown tone instead of defaulting it.

The runbook's own warning (*"If `npm run build` fails, do NOT kickstart"*) was followed in spirit and defeated by a pipe. The failed build had already removed `.next/BUILD_ID`, so the service exited 1 and `/login` answered 000. Restored by capturing `$?` from an unpiped build and gating on it, which is now the only shape to use.
- **The build that failed was the other session's, not this one's** — two Claude sessions share this repo (§12) and the second was mid-refactor on the company knowledge base and the map. - **⚠ `deploy/lmstudio-check.sh --fix` CANNOT FIX THE FAILURE THAT MATTERS MOST.** It found the embedding model **not loaded** — retrieval returns nothing while chat keeps answering, so Ber AI says *"I found no correspondence"* rather than erroring. `--fix` reloads the **chat** model only, so it corrected `parallel 4 → 1` and left the embedder absent, then reported ✗ again. Loaded by hand (`lms load text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b`, 609MB, 5.89s); the check now exits 0. Worth teaching `--fix` to load a missing embedder, since the check's headline failure is the one it cannot repair.
- **Verified after the deploy:** `npm run build` exit 0 checked unpiped, `launchctl kickstart`, `/login` 200 on localhost, `tailnet-setup.sh` green on all three endpoints with env matching, `lmstudio-check.sh` exits 0 (context 131072, parallel 1, both models, no `:2` duplicate). `git push` clean — `06fa6aa..f910f68`. Lint clean across all 36 changed files.
- **What was deliberately NOT built.** A per-lane Gmail label (`Handed off — Dino Plumbing`) would tell someone working info@ which team took a lead without opening the platform, and it multiplies labels and needs the label helper to become async — worth doing, not worth bundling here. Follow-up on a handed-off lead: `forwarded` is still terminal, so nothing tracks whether the trade ever replied; the cheap version is a filter on `status='forwarded'` by age, not a mini-CRM per trade. And `opportunities.drive_source_folder_id` still has no importer, unchanged by this.

**Done 2026-09-30 (an intake package can be sent to the project it is already about, carrying everything the run assembled; DEPLOYED):**
- **Richard's question: "on the intake form at the bottom I am see the leads/updates that you are gathering from emails. It looks great, the only issue I have is sometimes multiple are being created for the same project. So can you add a way to send it to an exisiting project or opprotunity? That way it takes all the captured information and updates the pertinent project?"**
- **The duplication is structural, not a bug in the matcher: the queue proposes one record per CLUSTER OF CORRESPONDENCE, not one per deal.** `dedupe.ts` already says so in its header and had already measured it — **8 proposals for Myton, 8 for data centres, 5 for GridEdge, 4 for West Wendover out of 104 real ones**. The nightly dedupe folds same-deal proposals into one another, but it can only fold a pending proposal into another *pending* proposal. Nothing could fold one into a record that already exists, which is the case Richard is looking at.
- **⚠ `merge` WAS THE ESCAPE HATCH AND IT THREW THE WORK AWAY.** The route shipped on 09-25 with a header explaining that handing `linkClusterToRecord` an EXISTING id *is* the merge — and that was all it did. The threads were tied to the record with `linked` certainty, and the report, the people, the tasks and the staged attachments the run had already assembled were **discarded silently**. From the chair that is indistinguishable from losing the run: the correspondence pointed at the right deal and the deal never heard what it said. `/decide`'s "Merge → X" button has been doing exactly this.
- **⚠ AND THERE WAS NO WAY FOR A HUMAN TO NAME THE TARGET.** `resolveMergeTarget` resolves only the name the *model* put in `predecision.merge_target_name`, whole-name, against the closed candidate list it was shown — correctly refusing to guess. Its own error message says *"open the review screen and choose"*, and **the review screen had no chooser**. So a package the model had not pre-judged as a merge had no route to an existing record at all.
- **One target parameter is the entire difference, so the pass moved rather than forking (§12).** The whole body of `api/email-ingestion/confirm` — people → parties → players, tasks, the provenance note, the report as an `updates` row + a `.md` document, attachment promotion, Drive publish, the cluster link — is now `src/lib/email-ingestion/apply-session.ts`, taking `{ mode: 'create' } | { mode: 'existing', kind, id }`. The confirm route is 58 lines and the merge route builds its default actions with the same `buildConfirmBody` the Decide queue uses. Forking it per destination would have meant a second creation path to keep correct forever, which is the 09-17 `runDocumentAiPass` failure that silently discarded 413,000 characters.
- **The review screen's toggle is now a destination, not a kind: New opportunity / New project / Existing record.** Choosing *Existing record* opens a search over every project and every open opportunity (by name or location), with one-click chips for whatever Ber AI already matched the package to — the `merge_target_name` first, then the scored `match_candidates`. Picking one routes through `switchKind`, not `setKind`, deliberately: attaching an opportunity-shaped extraction to a PROJECT with a bare `setKind` hands the fill pass an empty project form, and the blank columns it exists to fill stay blank.
- **⚠ ATTACHING FILLS BLANKS AND NEVER OVERWRITES, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO MODES.** The reason to attach rather than create is that a human already curated this record. So `name` is excluded outright (attaching must never rename a record someone else is working on), `projects.sector` and `opportunities.opp_type` are excluded because they are **NOT NULL on an existing row and therefore never blank** — "filling" them could only mean overwriting — and `stage`/`status` are excluded because where a deal sits in the pipeline is a judgement no email reports. What is left is six project columns and eight opportunity ones, filled only where NULL or whitespace, with the filled names reported back to the screen.
- **⚠ AN INSERT THAT WAS SAFE ONLY BECAUSE THE PARENT WAS BRAND NEW.** `project_players` carries `unique (project_id, party_id, role)` and, for the opportunity half, `uniq_project_players_opportunity … WHERE opportunity_id IS NOT NULL`. The confirm route inserted players with no error check, which was harmless against a record created three lines earlier and is a constraint violation the moment the target is an existing one. It cannot be an upsert either — **PostgREST has no way to name a partial unique index as a conflict target (§12)** — so the pass reads the record's current roll first, skips a person who already holds that role, and **counts the skips** rather than swallowing them.
- **Verified against the live database, twice, on disposable records.** Pass one: three blank columns filled (`description`, `estimated_value`, `client_entity`), an already-set `location` of *Ogden, UT* left alone against an incoming *Salt Lake City, UT*, the incoming name ignored, one player, one task, one `updates` row on the project's feed, one report document in storage, `created_record_ids` carrying `attached_to_existing: true` and the record's name. Pass two, a second session onto the same project: **`fields_filled: []`, `players_already_linked: 1`, one player on the record, location still *Loc 1*.** Everything the scripts made was deleted afterwards; no real record was touched.
- **The confirmed banner and the toast now name the destination**, because on an attach the only question the reader has is whether their existing project actually changed: *"Added to Delta Industrial Campus — 3 blank fields filled · 2 tasks · 4 documents"*. Re-opening the session says *"This package was added to …"* rather than the old generic "already confirmed".
- **`/decide`'s Merge → X now runs the same engine**, so the batch path carries the content too. `resolveMergeTarget` still refuses an ambiguous or invented name and still says to open the review screen — which, for the first time, is now true.
- **What was deliberately NOT built.** Attachment de-duplication against the target's existing documents: the honest test is the bytes, not the name (§12 — four title commitments share one file name within 1.1% of each other), and a name rule defaulting a file to unchecked would silently drop a genuinely different file. The staged files stay checked and the human decides; hashing is a separate pass. Also left alone: nothing on the `/intake` list itself changed — the destination choice belongs on the screen where the extraction sits beside the record's name.
- Verified live after the deploy: `npm run build` clean, `launchctl kickstart`, `/login` 200 on localhost and on the tailnet, `tailnet-setup.sh` green on all three endpoints, `lmstudio-check.sh` exits 0 (context 131072, parallel 1, both models). `git push` clean this time — `1bf6155..86bc549`.

**Done 2026-09-30 (a quarter of every vector was being thrown away, and the re-embed tool that would have caught it could not run; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's question, after loading the large Qwen model beside the small one in LM Studio: "How does it know which one to use? I thought that the lightweight one was to help read PDFs or something of that nature. Given my 36GB Ram studio, am I using the best model(s)? I dont care about speed on the LLM as much as accuracy. This is all about combing through data effectively. Do we lose on some of our learning when we switch models?"**
- **The two models do unrelated jobs and both must be loaded; neither has ever read a PDF.** `LOCAL_AI_MODEL` (`local.ts:33`) serves every reasoning call; `LOCAL_EMBEDDING_MODEL` (`local.ts:37`) turns text into search vectors. PDFs go through `unpdf`, and scans through Apple Vision OCR — **no model call at all**, which is exactly why the 36GB box can afford neither a vision LLM nor a bigger embedder. Loading only the embedder breaks all chat; loading only the 35B breaks all search while chat keeps answering, so Ber AI says *"I found no correspondence"* rather than failing.
- **The model choice was already right, and is the one thing this session did not change.** Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at Q4_K_M is the confirmed 36GB pick; it is also `vision: true`, tool-trained, and has a 262,144 ceiling. Q5_K_M/Q6_K weights plus a 131k q8_0 cache do not fit in 36GB, so the quantization is forced rather than chosen.
- **⚠ THE LOAD CONFIG HAD DRIFTED TO 173,824 AGAINST A DOCUMENTED 131,072, AND THE BOX WAS PAGING FOR A WINDOW THE APP CANNOT REACH.** Measured with `lms load --estimate-only`: **25.42 GiB at 131,072 against 26.80 GiB at 173,824**. The agent caps a conversation at `AGENT_CONTEXT_BUDGET_CHARS=300000` (~75k tokens) plus ~13k of fixed overhead ≈ **88k tokens**, so the extra 42k was unreachable — while the machine sat at **314MB free with 10.7 of 12GB swap in use**. The q8_0 K/V cache had survived the drift; `--parallel` had reverted to 4, as §12 predicted.
- **⚠ THE EMBEDDER RETURNS 1024 DIMENSIONS AND THE SCHEMA WAS `vector(768)`, SO `local.ts:569` DISCARDED A QUARTER OF EVERY VECTOR — ON EVERY CHUNK AND EVERY QUERY.** Verified against the live endpoint rather than assumed. Qwen3-Embedding is Matryoshka-trained, so the leading 768 slice *is* a valid embedding and nothing ever errored, warned, or looked broken: retrieval simply ran on 75% of the signal, on a platform whose stated job is combing through this corpus. A truncation being legal is not the same as it being free.
- **⚠ THE RE-EMBED TOOL COULD NOT HAVE PERFORMED A RE-EMBED, WHICH IS WHY NONE OF THIS SURFACED WHEN THE EMBEDDER LAST CHANGED.** `deploy/reembed.mjs` covered `chunks` and **never `thread_chunks` — the entire correspondence index, 6,498 rows** — so any model swap would have left two incompatible vector spaces in one database and printed a clean total. It also omitted the investor (9), party-enrichment (2) and research-report (3) chunks inside `chunks` itself, and did not filter `superseded_at`, so it would have **added 12 deliberately-retired duplicates** to an index that held none (§12).
- **⚠ AND IT SELECTED A COLUMN THAT DOES NOT EXIST, WHICH MEANT IT HAD BEEN INDEXING ZERO DOCUMENTS.** `select('… extracted_text, summary')` against `documents`, where the column is **`ai_summary`**. supabase-js hands that 42703 back on `error`; the script destructured only `data`. The first run of this session printed **`documents: 0/0`** and reported success — a zero from a broken query and a zero from an empty table are the same number on screen. Every select in the script now goes through one `sel()` helper that throws on `error` and **pages at 500** (PostgREST caps at 1000 silently, §12), and the per-phase counter separates `skipped: no text` from `FAILED`, because folding a correct outcome into a miss is the same unlabelled-count failure §12 already records.
- **Migration `20260930000001_embeddings_1024.sql` widens both columns.** A `vector(768)` cannot be cast to `vector(1024)`, so the rows must go first: drop both HNSW indexes, delete, `alter type`, recreate at identical `m=16, ef_construction=64`, and reset `email_threads.embedded_at` **in the same transaction** as the delete — or the table claims every thread is indexed while holding no chunks for any of them. **`match_chunks` and `match_thread_chunks` both declare `query_embedding vector` with no dimension, so neither needed recreating** — checked rather than assumed.
- **⚠ THE PLAN SAID TO RESET `opportunity_documents.embedding_status` TO `pending`, AND THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG.** Only `document-pipeline.ts:106` ever settles that column — the embed path never has (§12, 09-28) — so resetting it would have stranded **45 complete documents as "Indexing…" forever**. It describes the document AI pass, not the vector. Left alone.
- **Backed up first (§12), and read back before trusting it:** both tables dumped to `~/Backups/berwilson/pre-1024-migration-*.sql.gz`, 56MB, gzip integrity verified, 2 COPY statements confirmed present.
- **Run with the 35B unloaded, for the same reason OCR is (§12).** `lms unload` dropped wired memory **24G → 4.9G**; the 639MB embedder then held the machine and ran at a measured **8 chunks/sec (~125ms each)**. The embedder is the only model a re-embed needs.
- **`deploy/lmstudio-check.sh` is the new assertion, and it exists for the same reason `tailnet-setup.sh` does: the load config is LM Studio's state, not ours.** It reads the two model ids out of `.env.local` rather than repeating them, and fails on a missing model, a wrong context, or an identifier ending `:2` (a second 22GB copy resident — 41GB against 36GB of RAM, seen live). Added to the deploy runbook. Verified by running it against the deliberately-unloaded box: it named the missing chat model and exited 1.
- **What was ruled out, by checking rather than by taste.** A **cross-encoder reranker** is the obvious next accuracy win and **LM Studio has not implemented a rerank endpoint** — so it is a revisit, not an option. The **4B embedder** is genuinely better (MTEB multilingual **64.33 → 69.45**) and must stay resident beside a 22GB model on a 36GB box, so there is no room; it is a reason to want a bigger machine, not a change to make on this one.
- **Rebuilt and reconciled, rather than assumed.** `chunks` **6,002 → 6,535** (higher: the four phases the old script omitted now run). `thread_chunks` **6,498 → 6,214**, and the coverage reconciles exactly against 2,671 threads: **817 embedded + 989 spam-lead skips + 846 `relevance='noise'` excluded by design + 19 never summarized**. The two PDFs that failed to decode (`PLANS Hafoka Residence`, `ZPD_CONC_CottageB`) held **zero chunks in the backup too** — undecodable before and after, not a regression.
- **⚠ THE 284 MISSING CHUNKS ARE THE NOISE SCRUBBER, AND THE SPLIT IS WHAT PROVES IT.** Body chunks fell **2,398 → 2,131 (−11%)** while attachments held **4,100 → 4,083 (−0.4%)** — a body-only drop, which is the shape `scrubMailText`/`unwrapSafeLinks` make and not the shape lost mail makes. Measured decisively: chunks containing `urldefense|proofpoint|safelinks|mimecast` went from **399 to 1**. The old index predated the 09-27 scrubber for most threads, so this is less gateway junk competing with prose, not less correspondence.
- **Verified after the deploy, on the two cases §12 already names.** `match_chunks` returns the Alaska DNR mining lease at **0.686** for *"how many acres is the Alaska mining lease"*; `match_thread_chunks` returns *"Bid Invite: Hill AFB Multiple Award Construction Contract"* (0.687) and **"Site Visit - IDIQ @ HAFB"** (0.680) — the passage the 09-27 entry records as one a too-clever noise filter would have withheld. `zsh deploy/lmstudio-check.sh` exits 0 (context 131072, parallel 1, both models, Q4_K_M); `tailnet-setup.sh` green on all three endpoints; `platform.err.log` has written nothing since the 09:18:05 restart, its last entry being 2026-09-29.
- **⚠ `git push` WAS REJECTED 403 AND THE DEPLOY WENT AHEAD ANYWAY, WHICH IS CORRECT BUT WORTH KNOWING.** *"Permission to berwilsonai/berwilson-platform.git denied to **richmwhite1**"* — the stored credential is a different GitHub account from the one with write access. Pushing is **GitHub backup only** (Vercel was deleted 2026-07-07), so production is current and this commit is live; but **this session's work exists only on the Studio** until the credential is fixed, and so does every commit made since whenever this started.
- **The answer to "do we lose our learning": no for the chat model, totally for the embedder, and that asymmetry is the durable rule.** Nothing here is fine-tuned — every fact lives in Postgres — so a better `LOCAL_AI_MODEL` is an env edit with nothing relearned. A stored vector is only meaningful against the model AND width that produced it, so changing either invalidates `chunks` and `thread_chunks` together, with no incremental path.

**Done 2026-09-29 (a broker names a dozen sites in an hour: meetings can stage candidate deals as leads, and a lead can attach to the record it already belongs to; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's question: "Rebecca has over 25 she wants to show us, so I want to ingest these properly. Does it make sense to have potential opportunities go to the leads area and then I can create the opportunity or project from there? Perhaps direct to an existing project if it is lost? Most meetings will be around just one project so it makes sense to put the full transcript on the project and/or drive folder, but with Rebecca we are talking about so many!"**
- **The answer was already written in the codebase, in a comment nobody had connected to meetings.** `src/lib/leads/promote.ts` opens: *"A lead is deliberately NOT a project: 10 of 15 projects already sit in pursuit/capture/bid, and letting every ITB become one is what put $50B of notional pipeline into the dashboard."* Rebecca's sites are that shape exactly. The meeting review screen could only offer **New project** or **New opportunity**, so ingesting one of her calls meant either creating a dozen projects or losing the sites.
- **⚠ THE ONE STAGED MEET SESSION WAS THE WHOLE CASE, ALREADY ON DISK.** `Ber Wilson/Rebecca/Merlin Portfolio Review` names *Steelton Project*, *Texas Greenfield Sites*, *Riverdale Site* and *West Virginia Portfolio* — four referenced records, **none of which exists**, all four pre-ticked for nothing. And the two Elite Solutions meetings reported as "filed themselves" are still `pending`: filing the DOCUMENT and confirming the SESSION are different acts, and the 09-28 entry's wording invited the opposite reading.
- **What did NOT need building, which is most of it.** One meeting → many targets was already the design (the prompt says so in as many words: *"A single meeting usually touches SEVERAL existing projects and opportunities — do not force everything into one record"*). Confident matches are pre-ticked, unmatched ones offered as one-click suggestions, tasks tagged per target, and `isConfidentNameMatch` already requires a shared identity-bearing word so "Riverdale Site" cannot silently land on some other *Site*. The gap was one missing destination, not a pipeline.
- **Leads is now a third destination in the review screen.** Each unmatched suggestion is a split chip: **stage as lead** on the left, **create the record** on the right. Lead leads, deliberately — a lead that turns out to be real is one promotion away, while a project that turns out to be talk is already in the pipeline figure. The lead is seeded with the location, sector and value the meeting stated (three new optional fields on `referenced_records`, prompt `meeting-intake-1.0` → `1.1`), which is exactly what the fit assessment reads; `score_state: 'pending'` hands it to the existing score phase, which runs overnight on the idle model for nothing.
- **⚠ `kind` STAYS `project | opportunity` AND THE MODEL IS NEVER ASKED WHETHER A RECORD EXISTS.** Adding a `'lead'` kind to the extraction was the obvious move and is wrong: the model has no sight of the database, a call about a live project reads exactly like a call about a site nobody has heard of, and a mis-classification would skip trigram matching entirely. The model says what a deal IS; the human picks the destination, on the screen where the match result sits beside the name.
- **⚠ FOLLOW-UPS TAGGED TO A LEAD BECOME NOTE TEXT, NOT TASKS, BECAUSE `tasks.lead_id` IS A UNIQUE INDEX.** One task per lead, reserved for the bid-deadline sync latch — so a call raising three follow-ups about one site cannot have all three, and keeping one of the three silently would be worse than keeping none. They are written into the lead's first note under *"Follow-ups discussed"*, the UI says so in place (*"Kept on the lead as a follow-up note, not created as a task — it becomes a real task when the lead is promoted"*), and the target chip counts "follow-ups" rather than "tasks" so the number is not read as a promise of task rows.
- **`promoteLead` gains an `attach` target — Richard's "direct to an existing project".** `PromoteTarget` was `project | opportunity | steel`, all three of which CREATE. A GC re-inviting us to a job already being bid, a broker re-circulating a site already in the pipeline: real deal, existing record, and the only exit was to promote and then merge by hand, splitting the deal's documents and mail across two rows. Attaching posts the lead's evidence to the record and drains the lead, and is **deliberately additive** — stage, value, dates and owner are never touched. Somebody decided those; a later bid invitation is not a reason to overrule them. `recordKind` (not `target`) now drives the directory link, `promoted_*_id`, the thread link and the Drive publish.
- **⚠ `leads_source_check` ALLOWED ONLY `email | web_form`.** A meeting lead would have typechecked, built, deployed, and failed at every INSERT — §12's discriminator rule, caught by reading `\d leads` rather than by shipping it. Migration `20260929000001_meeting_leads.sql` widens it. Nothing else had to move: `thread_id` was already nullable and every Gmail-facing consumer already filters `.not('thread_id','is',null)`, which is how web-form leads have worked since 09-05.
- **⚠ `originNote` SAID "INBOUND LEAD FROM AN EMAIL ENQUIRY" FOR A LEAD WITH NO SENDER, NO MAILBOX AND NO EMAIL.** Found by reading the attach test's own output rather than by looking for it. That sentence is written onto the record as its description and outlives the lead — a provenance line that invents a provenance, which a reader has no way to tell is wrong. Now three-way, and checked per source: *"from an email enquiry"*, *"from the website deal form … via the berwilson.com deal intake form"*, *"from a meeting … raised on a call and staged for review"*. `linkSenderToDirectory`'s player roles went three-way with it (a broker is an *Introduced By*, not an *Inviting Contractor*).
- **A leads-only meeting has no record to hold its transcript, so `fileMeetingDocument` gained a company arm.** Twelve copies of one hour-long call, each claiming to be about one site, is worse than none. One verbatim copy on the company shelf — indexed, quotable — and the per-deal reading of it on each lead as its note. Verified: `is_company: true`, `embedding_status: complete`.
- **⚠ TWO BUGS FOUND BY DRIVING THE LIVE UI, NEITHER OF WHICH READING WOULD HAVE CAUGHT.** `.neq('status','archived')` on the attach-target query looked like ordinary hygiene: `project_status` **has no 'archived' member**, so PostgREST failed the whole query with `22P02` and the picker held opportunities only — silently, which is the one thing an attach picker must not do. (Had the value been valid it would still have been wrong: `projects.status` is nullable and `.neq` is not true for NULL.) And `?lead=<id>` seeds the open sheet from the 300-row queue ordered by bid date then fit score, **both `nullsFirst:false`** — so a lead with NEITHER sorts dead last and is the first thing the cap drops. That is exactly a freshly staged meeting lead, which the confirm step now redirects to by id: staged, correct, and the sheet would never open. Both fixed; the second also repairs the digest email's links whenever the queue is long.
- **Verified end to end against the live system, with synthetic `ZZ TEST` data and Rebecca's real session untouched.** Three leads staged from one meeting (`source=meeting`, `route=construction`, `score_state=pending`, location/sector/value carried, follow-ups routed to the right lead, **zero orphan tasks**); the redirect landing on `/leads` for a leads-only meeting and `/leads?lead=<id>` for a single one; the verbatim transcript on the company shelf with a chunk; and an attach onto both a project and an opportunity — record unchanged in both, evidence posted, lead drained, `promoted_*_id` set. Every `ZZ TEST` row, document and storage object was then removed and the removal confirmed by count.
- **What Richard should do with his own answer:** keep titling calls `Ber Wilson/<counterparty>/<deal>` — the last meaningful segment is the filing key. For Rebecca there is no single deal, so `Ber Wilson/Rebecca Merlin/Portfolio Review` and expect fan-out; that fan-out IS the signal to route to leads rather than to a record.
- **Not built, deliberately:** `leads` has no dedupe key for a meeting lead (it dedupes on `(thread_id, thread_item)` and a NULL thread is distinct from every other NULL). What prevents a double-stage is upstream — the confirm route reads its session `.eq('status','pending')` and a second confirm finds nothing. Worth knowing before anything else writes leads without a thread.

**Done 2026-09-29 (Ber AI stopped mid-thought on the best-evidenced questions: a 300s ceiling inside `fetch` that no setting in this repo could reach; DEPLOYED):**
- **Richard's report: "I am asking BI to help me make an offer based on all conversations and discussions with GridEdge and after thinking for a while it simply stops working."**
- **⚠ THE ERROR THAT REACHED THE SCREEN WAS THE SINGLE WORD `terminated`.** The last four entries in `platform.err.log` are `[agent] Stream error: TypeError: terminated` with `[cause] UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` — the GridEdge attempts. `AgentChat` throws the server's message with `noRecover: true`, which skips the recovery path and drops the placeholder message, so the turn vanished and left one meaningless word behind.
- **⚠ undici — THE HTTP CLIENT BEHIND NODE'S `fetch` — ENFORCES TWO 300s TIMEOUTS, AND NEITHER IS REACHABLE FROM THIS CODE.** Not from the `AbortSignal`, not from `LOCAL_AI_TIMEOUT_MS` (900s). The 2026-07 comment in `local.ts` records dodging the first (`headersTimeout`) by asking for `stream:true` so headers return immediately instead of after generation. That dodge hands the socket straight to the second: **nothing streams while LM Studio ingests the prompt**, undici reads that silence as a dead body, and kills the connection at five minutes. So the 600s first-chunk guard written on 2026-09-27 for exactly this wait **was never once reachable** — undici got there first, every time.
- **⚠ REPRODUCED EXACTLY, WITH NO MODEL INVOLVED.** A local server that flushes headers and then goes silent for 310s: **`fetch` FAILED after 302s: `terminated (UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT)`** — byte-identical to the production error — **while `node:http` completed at 310s**. A first version of the same test failed at 302s with `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT` instead, because `res.writeHead()` only *sets* headers and Node holds them until the first write; `res.flushHeaders()` is what makes a test server behave like LM Studio with `stream:true`. Worth keeping: the wrong version proved the *other* 300s ceiling, and both are real.
- **The fix is the transport, not a number.** `localChatStream` now POSTs over `node:http`/`node:https` (`postJsonStream`), which applies no timeout of its own, so the guards already in the file become the real limits — which is what they were written to be. The response is read through a small `ChunkReader` shape so the existing think-filtering, tool-accumulation and idle-guard loop are untouched. Raising an undici setting instead would have meant adding a dependency (§11) to configure a client we do not otherwise want. Embeddings stay on `fetch`: at a 120s cap they are nowhere near the ceiling.
- **⚠ THREE MEASUREMENTS, AND THE FIRST ONE WAS WRONG BECAUSE OF THE QUEUE.** Prefill uncontended: **21,025 prompt tokens → first token at 68.3s (~308 tok/s)**. The same test run behind an in-flight request read **29,121 tokens at 135.5s (~215 tok/s)** — LM Studio serves ONE request at a time (§12), so that number was measuring the queue, not the model. A full 131,072-token window is therefore ~425s of silence before the first token.
- **⚠ THE PREFIX CACHE IS WHY A ROUND IS NORMALLY FAST — AND SHRINKING THE CONVERSATION IS WHAT THROWS IT AWAY.** The same prefix re-sent returned its first token in **3.2s against 68.3s cold — 21x**. An agent round only re-pays full prefill when the prefix CHANGES, which is precisely what `AGENT_CONTEXT_BUDGET_CHARS` does when it stubs the oldest tool results: rewriting the middle invalidates the cache from that point, and the next round re-prefills ~88k tokens (~285s uncontended, over 300s the moment a cron holds the model). **So the failure was aimed, not random.** It landed on turns that gathered enough evidence to trigger shrinking — which is exactly "an offer based on all conversations and discussions with GridEdge". A short question never came near it, and the more thoroughly Ber AI did its job the more certainly it died.
- **The 600s first-chunk guard was itself marginally short, and would have started failing turns the moment the transport stopped failing them first.** At ~308 tok/s a full window is ~425s, and under contention more; raised to **900s**, sized from the measurement rather than chosen.
- **Every stream failure now names the wait it died in.** `localStallError` only rewrote aborts, so a socket death during prefill arrived raw. A non-timeout failure is now wrapped as `Local AI chat stream (no first token) failed: …` with the original as `cause`, so the next instance of this is one log line to diagnose rather than one word.
- **`LOCAL_AI_TIMEOUT_MS` changes meaning**: it was documented as a whole-call cap for a non-streaming completion, and there has been no non-streaming path since the 2026-07 change. It is now the cap on response HEADERS, which with `stream:true` arrive in 0.1s — a wait there means LM Studio is not answering at all, which is a genuinely different condition from a model that is thinking.
- **GridEdge has the evidence the question needs**: 10 threads, 297 chunks, 1 opportunity, 0 projects.
- **Not fixed, deliberately**: `lms ps` still shows `PARALLEL 4` (Richard's open item, 09-28). Caching is per-slot, so four slots let a cron land in the slot holding a conversation's cache and evict it — relevant to this bug, but it needs a model reload and the box was serving.

**Done 2026-09-28 (Meet recordings reached nothing: a folder renamed, a subfolder added, and a note the importer could not recognise; DEPLOYED):**
- **Richard's ask: "I am recording my meetings in Google Meet. They all land in a Google Meet folder. How do I most easily associate those files to the relevant project? Should I just move the file from there into the folder they belong to? Since you are syncing the drive with the local docs, will that do the trick?"** Then, against the recommendation not to move anything: **full treatment staged, auto-file the document on a confident title match, backfill the three existing meetings.**
- **⚠ THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION WAS "DON'T" — BECAUSE AN IMPORTER FOR THIS ALREADY EXISTED AND HAD RUN 192 TIMES WITHOUT EVER IMPORTING ANYTHING.** `cron-meet-import` fires eight times a weekday and has since 2026-08-28. Every one of its 192 logged runs reads `{"found":0,"imported":0,"noMeetFolder":["moose@berwilson.com","tuaone@berwilson.com"]}`. Aggregated over the whole log: `found 0, imported 0, alreadyImported 0, tooShort 0, failed 0`. The health probe was green, the cron was green, and the feature had never once done its job.
- **⚠ THREE INDEPENDENT MISSES, ANY ONE OF THEM FATAL, AND ALL THREE INVISIBLE FROM THE LOG.** (1) `findMeetFolder` matched the folder name `'Meet Recordings'` exactly; Richard's folder is named **`Google Meet`** — Google renamed it, and the code's own comment already said the name was locale-dependent without the code acting on it. (2) Meet now writes **one subfolder per meeting** (`Ber Wilson/TensorIQ/Elite Solutions - 2026/09/25 10:58 MDT`), while `listMeetTranscripts` queried `'<folderId>' in parents` — flat — so even the right folder would have returned nothing but folders. (3) It accepted only Google Docs whose name contained `Transcript`; the files are named **`… - Notes by Gemini`**. There are no video files and no separate transcript documents in the folder at all, so `recordingsWithoutTranscript` — the counter built precisely to distinguish "transcription is off" from "nobody had meetings" — also read 0.
- **⚠ MOVING THE FILES WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED FOR THE MEETINGS HE HAD ACTUALLY RECORDED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING.** The per-project importer is real and healthy (`importDriveFolder` + `syncProjectFolders`, hourly 08:20–18:20, 12 of 14 projects carrying a `drive_source_folder_id`), so dragging a file into a *project's* folder does file it. But two of the three recorded meetings are `Ber Wilson/TensorIQ/Elite Solutions`, and **Elite Solutions is an `opportunity`** — `opportunities.drive_source_folder_id` exists and **no importer reads it**. The file would have sat in the folder indefinitely. The obvious manual answer was also the one that silently fails.
- **⚠ THE FILE FORMAT IS BETTER THAN WHAT THE CODE WAS BUILT FOR, WHICH CHANGED THE DESIGN.** One `Notes by Gemini` Google Doc per meeting carries, in three tab sections the text/plain export flattens (`✍️ Quick notes` / `📝 Full notes` / `📖 Transcript`): an `Invited` line of real email addresses, a `Summary`, a `Decisions` section, a **`Next steps` section with owners already in brackets** (`[Ericson Tua'one] Send MOU: Draft the Memorandum of Understanding…`), a timestamped `Details` section, and then the **entire verbatim call**. Measured across the three: **82,191 → 10,949 recap + 67,268 transcript; 50,917 → 9,697 + 37,801; 54,075 → 8,373 + 42,695.** No Whisper, no OCR, no video download — the transcript is already text.
- **`splitGeminiNotes` (`src/lib/meetings/gemini-notes.ts`) sends the recap to the model and files the whole thing.** The recap is ~10KB of already-structured material in the exact shape the meeting-intake prompt wants. Feeding the 82KB export instead would also have walked into a live mismatch: `analyze-meeting.ts` imports `MAX_CHARS`, which is `GEMINI_MAX_CHARS` (200,000), while the runtime is local at `LOCAL_MAX_CHARS` (40,000) — an 82KB document passes the guard at the wrong size. The split sidesteps it rather than renegotiating the constant. Google's survey and disclaimer lines are stripped at the same time, for the reason `text-noise.ts` exists: they chunk and embed and then compete with prose.
- **⚠ `maxDepth: 1` RETURNED ZERO FILES AND `maxDepth: 2` RETURNED ALL THREE.** `listFolder` calls `walk(folderId, 1)`, so the folder it is handed is level **1**, not level 0 — "this folder and the meeting folders inside it" is 2. Reasoning about the recursion gave the wrong answer; running it against the live Drive gave the right one, in one probe.
- **⚠ `tuaone@` HOLDS THREE `…apps.shortcut` ENTRIES TO THE SAME THREE MEETINGS, AND THAT IS WHY FILTERING ON `GOOGLE_DOC` MATTERS FOR MORE THAN TYPE SAFETY.** When several participants are executives, Meet puts the real document in the organizer's Drive and a shortcut in everyone else's. Both mailboxes are swept, so the real document is always seen exactly once — and ignoring shortcuts is what stops one meeting being imported, summarized and staged twice. Verified live: moose@ 3 documents, tuaone@ 3 shortcuts → 0 taken.
- **The meeting title is the filing key, and it is walked OUTWARDS.** Richard titles calls as a path, so `meetingTargetFromTitle` tries segments right to left: `Ber Wilson/TensorIQ/Elite Solutions` → `Elite Solutions`. Not merely "the last segment" — one real title is `Ber Wilson/TensorIQ/Elite Solutions/Jaren Davis`, where the last segment is a **person** and the deal is one level up; walking outwards finds `Elite Solutions` in both shapes. Ber Wilson's own name is dropped from the candidates (both spellings — "Bear Wilson" appears in these very transcripts), because the company is never the deal.
- **The bar for filing automatically is an EXACT name match with exactly one hit across `projects` and `opportunities`** — stricter than the trigram matcher the review screen uses, deliberately, because this one decides an action with nobody watching (§12: ambiguity must mean no match; one hit on a weak key is an unchallenged match, not a unique one). Two records sharing a name refuses **and says which two**. A refusal and a miss both fall through to the review queue, which was always the designed path.
- **What is automatic and what is not.** The **document** is filed on a confident match: it is evidence, it is reversible, and withholding it until someone clicks means the transcript cannot be searched in the meantime. Tasks, contacts, decisions and records still require the human confirm step at `/intake?tab=meeting` — §11's invariant is untouched, and the session now arrives with the target **pre-selected** (`seedTarget` folds into `referenced_records` with its match pre-filled, so the reviewer does not hunt for a record the title already named).
- **⚠ `embedOpportunityDocument` INSERTS CHUNKS BUT DOES NOT SETTLE `embedding_status`, AND THE COLUMN DEFAULTS TO `pending`.** Filing to an opportunity — which is what both Elite Solutions meetings do — would therefore have left a document reading "Indexing…" forever, the exact failure `saveReportDocument`'s own comment warns about for a row nothing will come back to. Settled explicitly, with `error` on a throw. The project path is fine; `embedDocument` settles its own.
- **⚠ `drive_file_id` CARRIES A *PARTIAL* UNIQUE INDEX ON BOTH DOCUMENT TABLES, SO `ON CONFLICT` IS NOT AVAILABLE (§12).** Filing checks first and treats `23505` as "a concurrent run won", removing its own orphaned storage upload rather than leaving a file with no row. The same index means one Drive file can be filed on exactly **one** record: the minutes document still goes on every confirmed target, the verbatim goes on the first.
- **The verbatim is no longer lost for a meeting that could not be auto-filed.** The session retains the **whole export** as `raw_text` while the model reads only the recap (`retainText`), and the confirm route files it onto the record the moment a human names one. Without this, an unmatched meeting's transcript would have existed only in Drive — the recap document written at confirm is not the call.
- **`scripts/verify-meet-import.mts`: a read-only dry run that costs no model passes** and prints the intermediate steps rather than a total — which folder resolved and by which name, which documents would be taken, the title recovered from each, the recap/transcript split sizes, and the record each would file to or why it refuses. This exists because the failure it diagnoses is invisible from a coverage count (§12): a run finding nothing looks exactly like a quiet fortnight. **Its output on the live Drive: 3 documents visible, 2 would file themselves, 1 waits for a human.**
- **The `noMeetFolder` message now names the folder names it looked for**, so the next instance of this is one log line to diagnose instead of 192 silent runs.
- **⚠ THE BACKFILL THEN EXPOSED A SECOND BUG, IN THE PRE-SELECTION THIS FEATURE FEEDS — AND A SCORE THRESHOLD CANNOT FIX IT.** `matchReferencedRecords` applied **no floor at all**: whatever `findMatchingProjects` returned best became a pre-ticked target on the review screen. The Elite Solutions joint review opened with **Myton Development** selected, because the model had named "Eagle Mountain Development" and four live projects share the word *Development* (Heber Development, Myton Development, Tonga Development Project, American Energy Rail Corridor - Community Development). Measured: **"Eagle Mountain Development" → Myton Development 0.487** (wrong), Heber Development 0.436 (also wrong, 0.051 behind); **"Delta, Utah Campus" → Delta Industrial Campus — Daves Farms 0.390** (right). **The wrong match scores higher than the right one**, so there is no threshold that keeps one and drops the other.
- **What separates them is WHICH word matched, so that is what is now required.** `isConfidentNameMatch` demands at least one shared identity-bearing word, with a generic list (`development`, `project`, `site`, `campus`, `expansion`, `portfolio`, `corridor`, `industrial`…) excluded — the §12 domain rule applied to record names. **Place names are deliberately not generic**: Myton, Delta, Heber, Tooele and West Wendover are precisely what tells these projects apart. **Measured against the corpus: all 14 project names still pre-select themselves (zero regression), the 0.487 false positive is refused, the 0.390 true positive is kept, and exact hits stay at 0.900.** Records that fail it still appear as one-click suggestions, so nothing is hidden — it simply is not ticked on the reviewer's behalf. Scoped to `analyze-meeting.ts`, which is the only caller; proposal intake's matcher is untouched.
- **The already-staged row was rewritten, not just the generator (§12).** Re-applying the rule to the three pending sessions dropped exactly one pre-selection — `"Eagle Mountain Development" -> "Myton Development"` — and left Delta and Elite Solutions in place. A fixed matcher would have changed nothing the reviewer saw.
- **Backfill result: 3 found, 3 imported, 2 filed, 1 held, 0 failed, in 459s** (~2.5 min each, consistent with the doubled context window's prompt-processing price). The held one names its reason: *"Ber Wilson/Rebecca/Merlin visit: no record matches the title. Pick one in the review queue."* Extraction quality on the recap is high — the Elite Solutions call produced **4 tasks, 33 attendees, 3 decisions**, with the tasks reading `Draft & Exchange MOU`, `Submit Golden Dome White Paper`, `Develop Eagle Mountain Project Timeline`, `Compare Product & Supply Chain Lists` — the `Next steps` section, owners and all.
- **Both filed transcripts: `embedding_status = complete`, 43 and 28 chunks, non-null summaries.** Retrieval verified by query against the opportunity's chunks: *"How big is the Eagle Mountain site and how many megawatts?"* returns, at 0.571, *"Eagle Mountain Permitting and Power Management: Jonathan Houk inquired about the engineering and regulatory status … Jaren L. Davis to confirm that conceptual site plans …"* — a passage that existed nowhere in the platform this morning.
- **Idempotence verified: a second run is `{found: 3, imported: 0, alreadyImported: 3}` in 6s**, with session, document and chunk counts unchanged.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean on all changed files, `next build` clean, deployed with `launchctl kickstart`, `deploy/tailnet-setup.sh` asserted. No migration — every column used already exists.
- **⚠ Open, and handed back:** **the Merlin visit session is staged and unfiled** — it references *Steelton Project*, *Texas Greenfield Sites*, *Riverdale Site* and *West Virginia Portfolio*, none of which exist as records, so it needs a record created or a target picked at `/intake?tab=meeting`. **`opportunities.drive_source_folder_id` and `steel_deals.drive_source_folder_id` still have no importer** — this work routes opportunity documents around that gap rather than closing it. And a chatty transcript chunk competes with its own recap: the PUE figure ("1.18") is in the recap but the top three hits for *"what PUE does the waterless cooling design achieve"* are mid-call banter — retrieval finds the meeting, and an agent turn reads enough, but transcript prose is noisier than a document's.

**Done 2026-09-28 (a site plan that is not a picture: Delta's 929 acres, by parcel number, from the county's own GIS; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's ask: "I have some site plans for some of the projects. What is the best way to load them in there and how could we best use and display them?"** — with two photographs: a Millard County zoning map amendment exhibit for Daves Farms, and an unlabelled colour-coded pad layout for Heber. Then: *"yes please do"*, against a recommendation to create both projects and build the parcel layer for Delta first.
- **⚠ THE TWO SHEETS ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF OBJECT, AND TREATING THEM ALIKE WAS THE WHOLE TRAP.** The Delta exhibit is *data wearing a picture*: 11 parcel ids, acreages summing to 928.98, Agriculture → Heavy Industrial, at 39.234 N / 112.657 W — and its own disclaimer names the source of its geometry, "publicly available Millard County / Utah AGRC parcel geometry". Filed as an image it becomes storage: OCR'd into a wall of text, then answered only by a model reading a table back out of a photograph, which §12 already records getting a 69-row claim schedule wrong by seven. The Heber sheet genuinely *is* a picture — no survey basis, no coordinates, no legend — and forcing it into GIS would invent precision nobody has.
- **⚠ ALL 11 PARCELS EXIST IN THE PUBLIC CADASTRE, AND THE ACREAGES AGREE ON 10 OF THEM.** `Parcels_Millard_LIR` on Utah AGRC's ArcGIS FeatureServer answers `PARCEL_ID IN (…)` with GeoJSON at `outSR=4326` directly — no reprojection, no tracing. HD-5530 100.00, HD-5531-1 44.58, HD-5532 140.00, HD-5533-1 20.00, HD-5534-1 69.00, HD-5535 160.00, HD-5536 160.00, HD-5536-A 80.00, HD-5536-B-1 62.40, HD-5536-1-A 80.00 — every one matching the exhibit exactly. **The eleventh does not: HD-5534-A-1 is 13.00 acres on the application and 4.69 in the county's own records, a gap of 8.31.** Exhibit total 928.98 against a cadastral 920.67. Nobody had looked for that, and it surfaced on the first import because the importer compares rather than picks.
- **`project_parcels` stores BOTH acreages, deliberately.** `acres` is what the deal asserts; `assessor_acres` is what the county says. Collapsing them into one column would mean choosing a winner and losing the fact that anyone disagreed — which on a rezone application is precisely the fact worth keeping. The Land tab names them apart on screen ("Schedule acres · as the deal states it" / "County acres · as the assessor records it") and never sums them, per §12's one-quantity-one-definition rule.
- **⚠ `unique (project_id, opportunity_id, parcel_id)` WOULD HAVE ENFORCED NOTHING, AND THE SYMPTOM WOULD HAVE BEEN A SILENTLY DOUBLED SCHEDULE.** Following the shared-children convention (§4) means exactly one of the two parent columns is NULL on every row — and under Postgres's default rule two NULLs are never equal, so the constraint matches nothing, `ON CONFLICT` never fires, and every re-import stacks a second copy of all 11 rows beside the first. `unique nulls not distinct` (PG 15+; this box is 17.6). Caught before the first import by reasoning about the upsert, not by seeing it fail. **Verified by running the import twice: still 11 rows.**
- **⚠ THE CENTROIDS IMPORTED INTO THE INDIAN OCEAN, AND NOTHING WOULD EVER HAVE REPORTED IT.** The shoelace helper returned the trapezoid form `(x_j + x_i)(y_j - y_i)`, which is the same area with the **opposite sign** to the cross-product convention the centroid sum beside it uses — so both coordinates came out negated and HD-5530 stored as 39.24 S / 112.66 E, off the coast of Western Australia. The geometry itself is stored raw and draws perfectly, so the map looked right; only the fly-to target and the stored centroid were wrong. Found by printing the eleven rows back out of the database instead of trusting the importer's own cheerful *"11 parcels, 11 with county geometry"*. Re-verified with an explicit check that every centroid falls inside its own parcel's bounding box.
- **/map now draws land, not just pins.** Fill, outline and label layers under the existing corridor lines; parcels inherit the exhibit's own colours, so "the pink one" in correspondence is the pink one on screen. Labels appear at z12 with the acreage formatted host-side (MapLibre cannot put a thousands separator on a number, and a parcel reading "1400 ac" where it means "1,400" is a figure someone repeats wrong in a hearing). **Selecting a project with parcels now fits the camera to its LAND rather than flying to its pin at a fixed zoom** — which answers "how big is this" in the same gesture as "where is this". Excluded parcels are dropped from the map on purpose: drawing ground that was considered and rejected overstates the assemblage.
- **⚠ A LINT WARNING THAT WAS A DESIGN SIGNAL.** Defining `ensureParcels` in the component body made `ensureOverlays` un-inferrable as stable for the React Compiler's exhaustive-deps rule, which then demanded it as a dependency of two long-standing effects that had been clean for months — two new warnings from a function that had not been touched. The fix was not a disable comment: the parcel layer builder needs nothing from the closure but the map and the data, so it moved to module scope and took them as arguments. Lint back to zero on the file.
- **A Land tab per project** (`/projects/[id]/parcels`), appearing only when the project has parcels, with the schedule, the computed totals, the disagreement called out by name, and a paste-a-schedule importer covering all 29 Utah counties. `parseSchedule` takes what a county exhibit table actually copies as — tabs, commas, pipes or runs of spaces — and keeps a row whose acreage it cannot read, because a parcel of unknown size is a real state and dropping it would hide it.
- **⚠ THE TWO PHOTOGRAPHS WERE FILED WITHOUT AN AI PASS, ON PURPOSE.** `lms ps` at the time: the 22GB model **GENERATING**, swap at 12,338 of 13,312 MB, 135MB of free pages. §12 is unambiguous — never run OCR and the LLM at the same time on this box; that combination had `bw-ocr` killed mid-render and six readable documents written off as `skipped`. Both images are filed as `doc_type = 'site_plan'` with **hand-written summaries rather than NULL**, because a document with no summary is one Ber AI never opens (§12). Text extraction is left for a quiet window.
- **Also logged, not acted on:** `lms ps` shows `PARALLEL 4` again, which §12 records as the setting that reverts on an LM Studio reload and the one that actually costs memory. Left alone because the model was mid-generation; worth setting back to 1.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean on every changed file, `next build` clean, migration applied as `postgres` with explicit grants, deployed with `launchctl kickstart`, `deploy/tailnet-setup.sh` green on all three endpoints, live `/login` 200.
- **Open, and handed back:** the Heber sheet has no legend, so its pads carry no uses or acreages and the project has **no coordinates and does not appear on the map** — it sits in the Place Projects panel. Delta's exhibit says **Sheet 1 of 2** and sheet 2 is not on file. Both were photographed; the source PDFs would read cleanly with no OCR at all.
