**Done 2026-09-27 (Ber Intelligence could not read a deck, a phrase, or past a hex dump; DEPLOYED):**
- **Richard's ask: "Go through and clean up any bugs. Make sure our ber intelligence search specifically is working properly and searching emails, drive, uploaded docs etc..."**
- **⚠ THE METHOD WAS TO CALL EVERY RETRIEVAL TOOL AGAINST THE LIVE CORPUS, NOT TO READ THE CODE — AND EVERY REAL FINDING CAME OUT OF A RETURN VALUE.** Ten tools probed directly through `executeToolCall`, then two full agent turns. The code reads correctly in all four places that turned out to be broken. The first agent turn, for the record, was excellent: asked what Highland Title said about the Carbon County parcels, it read four title commitments across two ownership groups, tabulated the parcel numbers, 2026 taxes, oil-and-gas leases, unrecorded power leases and the solar CUP, and named the Mechanic's Lien Indemnity Agreement blocking policy issuance — in 390s over 10 tool calls. **Retrieval was not broken. It had holes, and the holes were invisible from the inside.**
- **⚠ POWERPOINT WAS NOT A SUPPORTED DOCUMENT TYPE AT ALL, AND TWO INVESTOR DECKS HAD NEVER REACHED THE PLATFORM.** `documentKind` branches on pdf/docx/xlsx/text/image and has no pptx case, so the nightly Drive sync classified `Ber-Wilson-Investor-Deck-Simple-Edition-20 (1).pptx` and `GridEdge_Investor_Engagement_and_Acquisition_Roadmap_5.0_080826.pptx` as "unsupported", skipped them, and **created no `documents` row at all**. Not unreadable — *invisible*: nothing listed them, no status came back for them, and `select … from documents where file_name ilike '%.pptx'` returned zero rows. The first of the two states the $88M raise across three milestone-gated closings, the CAGE code, the UEI and the Utah licence numbers. That is the company describing itself, and the fit assessment and every capability answer are supposed to be grounded in exactly that.
- **`extractPptxText` reads a deck the way the xlsx reader reads a workbook** — `fflate` over the OOXML, `ppt/slides/slideN.xml` in order, `<a:t>` runs joined within each `<a:p>` (PowerPoint splits one line into several runs wherever formatting changes mid-word), speaker notes kept because a deck's actual argument is often only written there, and the slide count stated up front for the same reason the sheet reader states its row count (§12 — never make the model count). **Measured: 28,865 and 16,404 characters, extracted in 19ms and 20ms.** The sync then imported both on the spot — 16 and 10 chunks, summaries settled — and `search_knowledge_base` now answers "how much are we raising and on what terms" with *"Families, funds, and strategic partners commit up to $88M in three closings"* at 0.547, straight out of the deck.
- **⚠ `skipped: 26` WAS SIX DIFFERENT OUTCOMES IN ONE NUMBER, AND IT SAT AT 26 EVERY NIGHT WHILE THE DECKS WERE MISSING.** `drive-sync` increments one counter from six branches — owned by a project, listed twice, over 30MB, unreadable type, no content returned, lost an insert race — so the log line said the same thing whether nothing was wrong or a deck was being dropped. It now records the reason alongside the count. Today's run reads **`{"over 30MB": 3, "unreadable type: application/x-zip-compressed": 1}`** and the mystery is gone. §12 already says a coverage count is the only honest signal for a feature whose failure mode is doing nothing; this is the corollary — an *unlabelled* count is not one.
- **⚠ `search_email_threads` MATCHED WHOLE PHRASES ONLY, SO "title commitment" ANSWERED NOTHING ON A CORPUS HOLDING FIVE HIGHLAND TITLE THREADS ABOUT TITLE COMMITMENTS.** `ilike '%title commitment%'` needs the two words adjacent, and no subject or summary puts them that way. The semantic tool found them instantly; the keyword tool returned `{"count":0}`, which a caller can only read as *"there is no such correspondence"* — the one wrong answer. It was also **hand-rolling its own `.or()` string**, in a codebase where `orIlike`/`orIlikeAnyWord` exist precisely because this class of bug has been fixed one site at a time three times. Now: the phrase first, then any-word through the shared helpers.
- **⚠ THE ANY-WORD FALLBACK WAS WORSE THAN THE BUG UNTIL IT WAS RANKED.** Ordered by date like the base query, "Hill AFB site visit" answered with three meeting-notes threads that merely contained the word "site", and the actual Hill AFB correspondence fell off the end of the limit. The fallback now over-fetches 4× and ranks by **how many of the asked-for words a thread actually carries** before truncating — a thread matching two words beats a newer one matching one. After: `Site Visit - IDIQ @ HAFB, Evanston, UTTR, etc` is first.
- **⚠ A HEX DUMP WAS THE TOP-RANKED PASSAGE ON THE CARBON COUNTY TITLE THREAD.** Asked "what did the title company say about the parcels?", `search_correspondence` returned, as hit #1 at 0.492, a chunk opening with 300 unbroken characters of hex — the tail of a spam-report link cut at a chunk boundary. Mail gateways (Proofpoint, Outlook ATP, Inky) leave encoded runs and 300-400 character link wrappers throughout a message, and chunked and embedded they rank like anything else. **New `src/lib/ai/text-noise.ts`**: `unwrapSafeLinks` recovers the real URL out of a wrapper (verified byte-for-byte on a Dropbox bid-package link), `stripOpaqueTokens` drops runs of 64+ characters carrying no `.` `:` `/` `@` — narrow on purpose, so every URL, path and hostname survives and only the base64/hex/JWT family goes. **Measured: 14.8% of the raw thread markdown across 1,000 threads.**
- **⚠ THE FIX CHANGED FROM WITHHOLDING TO SCRUBBING WHEN THE OFFENDING PASSAGE TURNED OUT NOT TO BE JUNK.** Behind those 300 characters of hex was Ericson writing to Highland Title about getting the title together — real evidence in the same chunk. Dropping the passage would have cost the answer; dropping the run costs nothing. `searchCorrespondence` therefore scrubs each passage on the way out rather than filtering it, which also reaches the ~6,000 chunks indexed before any of this existed **without a re-embed**.
- **⚠ `isLowSignalPassage` WAS TUNED THREE TIMES AGAINST THE CORPUS AND EVERY CLEVER VERSION COST REAL EVIDENCE.** Share of characters belonging to prose, below 35%: **withheld 11.6% of the index**, including "Site Visit - IDIQ @ HAFB", "Bid Invite: Chick-Fil-A #04616 - Remodel" and "View the RFP for Membrane Roofing" — mail is full of URLs and addresses, so a prose ratio reads a bid invitation and a certificate blob alike. Share of characters in short tokens, below 50%: **worse at 14.4%**, and it took the bid invitations again, because a BuildingConnected invite is mostly long per-trade links and those links are content. What works is the crudest measure available — **density of ordinary words, below one per forty characters** — with figures counted as words, because the second pass had withheld the life-insurance policy ledgers, where every cell is a number and not one is a word. **Final: 2.2% withheld, 0 false positives across 256 bid and title passages.** The reasoning is in the function's comment, because the next person to look at it will want to make it smarter.
- **⚠ A HYPOTHESIS THAT MEASURED OUT TO ALMOST NOTHING, RECORDED BECAUSE IT LOOKED SO CONVINCING.** `extractPortalLinks` pairs a link with the filename in the 300 characters before it, and a gateway-rewritten link is itself 300-400 characters — so the window is swallowed and the reference discarded. Measured over 1,000 threads: **74 carried Proofpoint-wrapped links and produced ZERO portal references between them**, against 49 from unwrapped mail. That reads as a large blind spot on exactly the mail most likely to carry a bid package, since a gateway means a company big enough to run one. Unwrapping inside `extractPortalLinks` (at read time, so it reaches mail already swept) took it from **49 to 51**. The 74 threads carry Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn and Zoom links out of signature blocks, not bid portals. The unwrap is right and stays — its value is the noise it removes, not the references it recovers.
- **⚠ A FINDING THAT WAS SIMPLY WRONG, AND HOW IT WAS CAUGHT.** Ten documents held substantial `extracted_text` and had no chunks — an 88,498-character Stockton Power Nexus proposal, a 36,775-character Myton Rail package, the Helper / Carbon County letters of support — and `needsAnotherPass` treats `skipped` as terminal, so nothing would ever come back for them. A backfill script was written. It then reported **0 candidates**, because it filtered `superseded_at is null` and the live query had not: **all ten are deliberately retired duplicates**, and every one has an indexed live twin (21, 4, 3, 50 and 4 chunks respectively). Deduplication was working exactly as designed. Script deleted. The generalisation is that `documents` must be read with `superseded_at is null` or it reports the graveyard as a gap.
- **⚠ A PRODUCTION FAILURE REPRODUCED IN THE PROBING: `Local AI stream stalled — no data for 180s`, twice in `platform.err.log`.** A real Ber AI turn — 19 tool calls, several 40,000-character document windows against the 131,072-token context — died on it after six minutes of work, with the model still reading. **One timeout was serving two completely different waits.** Nothing streams while the server ingests the prompt, and prompt processing scales with the prompt, so the silence *before* the first token grows with the conversation; the silence *between* tokens does not, because generation holds ~75 tok/s whatever the context. `local.ts` now waits up to 600s for the first chunk (`LOCAL_AI_STREAM_FIRST_CHUNK_TIMEOUT_MS`) and keeps the 180s gap cap after it, and the two failures are named apart in the log so "never started" is distinguishable from "stopped mid-answer". **Verified by re-running the identical question**: it previously threw at 180s after 19 tool calls; it now runs past that point and returns a complete two-part answer — the raise's use-of-proceeds table and the two leave-behind documents it comes from, then six named Carbon County title exceptions with the March 4 2027 commitment expiry and the mineral and water severances called out as the two that matter for diligence.
- **Coverage, measured, as the baseline for next time:** `documents` 411 rows, 378 with text, 378 summarized. `chunks` 5,826. `thread_chunks` 6,269 over 2,549 threads. Drive knowledge folders: 137 files seen, 131 unchanged, 4 skipped with reasons.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean on all six changed files, `next build` clean, deployed with `launchctl kickstart`, `deploy/tailnet-setup.sh` green on all three endpoints. Every fix re-probed against the live corpus after deploying.
- **⚠ Not fixed, found on the way:** **three IBC Building Code PDFs (2024 and two redline sets) exceed the 30MB knowledge-base ceiling** and are the only real content still absent from Drive — raising the cap on a 36GB box that already swaps is a decision, not a cleanup. **847 of 2,549 threads are still unembedded and 1,383 have never had the commitments pass** (the known overnight backlog, unchanged). `SNL_Letter_Englert_Results.pdf` still needs its password. And two `.eml` attachments (West Wendover Master Plan) are stored as `message/rfc822` with no text — readable in principle, two files in practice.

**Done 2026-09-27 (contact photos found on the open web, verified before they are believed; DEPLOYED):**
- **Richard's ask: "Is there a way for you to find the contacts picture on linkedin or from around the web and bring it into the system. Auto populating their profile picture? Best guess is ok."** Then, on being shown the measurements: *"yes build it. Use logo as a fallback… Lets just have the enrich button go gather the profile photo/logo. You can go ahead and batch the current profiles"* — which overrode the recommendation that a logo is wrong for a person, and is the reason a person falls back to their employer's mark.
- **⚠ EVERY SOURCE WAS MEASURED AGAINST THE REAL DIRECTORY BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN, AND THREE OF THE FOUR OBVIOUS ONES ARE DEAD ENDS.** Over the 37 parties carrying an email: **Google People API 1 hit, Gravatar 1 hit — and both were Richard himself.** The People path is the galling one, because it is *already wired and already consented* (`lookupContactByEmail`, `contacts` + `contacts.other.readonly`): `searchContacts` finds the person and returns nothing but `default: true` silhouettes, because Google stopped exposing third-party profile photos years ago. **Clearbit's logo API: 0 of 27 domains** — HubSpot retired the service; it returns nothing for every domain tested. Google's favicon service answers for **25 of 27**, but a favicon is a mark, not a face. The only route that produces real headshots is **the person's bio page on their employer's own website**, read through `og:image`.
- **⚠ GROUNDED SEARCH INVENTS URLS, AND THAT IS THE ENTIRE DESIGN CONSTRAINT.** Asked for two lawyers at the same firm it returned `bakerlaw.com/professionals/michael-w-moyer` (**200, a real 78KB headshot**) and `bakerlaw.com/people/artie-mcconnell` (**404**) — two different path patterns from one firm, so at least one was fabricated. It also returned `linkedin.com/in/artie-mcconnell`, which answers **999**. Nothing the model says is therefore stored on its word: every candidate is fetched, **the page must name the person** (first AND last), the image must decode and be portrait-shaped, and the host is checked against the domain their mail arrives from. The failure this exists to prevent is not a 404 — it is a *valid* page for a **different** Artie McConnell (§12: one match is not a unique match).
- **LinkedIn works, but only for genuinely public profiles, and it is second for that reason.** `satyanadella` returns 200 with a fetchable JPEG behind `og:image` from this box; a profile that is not fully public returns **999**, which the fetcher treats as a miss rather than something to retry. Kept as a source, never depended on.
- **`sips` does the image work — no dependency added.** It ships with macOS, reads webp, reports real dimensions, and re-encodes under the avatars bucket's 2 MB ceiling. Same pattern as whisper.cpp and `bw-ocr`: spawn it, nothing resident. **Dimensions are the cheap guard against a share card** — a 1200×630 banner is not a face however confident the model is. Headshots become JPEG, logos stay PNG so transparency survives on a dark background, and nothing is ever upscaled.
- **⚠ A COMPANY DOMAIN LEARNED FROM OUR OWN MAIL BEATS ASKING THE MODEL — AND MATCHING IT ON A SUBSTRING FILED THE WRONG COMPANY'S LOGO.** `Barnraisers Group LLC` has no email of its own, but Rick writes from `rick@barnraisersgroup.com` and his contact record names the employer, so `domainFromDirectory()` resolves it with no quota spent at all. The first version matched any keyword anywhere in the domain and **put `bfaenergy.com`'s logo on Bloom Energy**, because `bfaenergy` contains `energy`. A shared industry word is the one thing a company identifier must not be. The domain must now **START** with the organisation's leading distinguishing word (`barnraisersgroup` for Barnraisers, `caseut` for Case Utility, never `bfaenergy` for Bloom), industry words are stopwords, and a match on a contact's `company` field must account for **every** word of the name. Re-measured across all 15 org parties afterwards: 6 correct resolutions, 9 refusals, **0 false positives**.
- **⚠ THE `GEMINI_API_KEY` IS ON THE FREE TIER: 20 `gemini-2.5-flash` REQUESTS PER DAY.** This is not a demand spike and it is not new — it is the standing capacity of every web-research feature in the platform. It surfaced as `503 This model is currently experiencing high demand` (which cost **seven minutes for a single contact**, because the SDK has no timeout of its own and sits on a stalled request) and then plainly as `429 … quotaId: GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier, quotaValue: 20`. **Enrich Profile issues three searches per contact, so the button is good for roughly five contacts a day.** Three consequences shipped: a 45s ceiling on any one search; a daily-quota error is never retried (backing off six seconds against a 24-hour window is pure waste); and the backfill **stops after three quota strikes** rather than reporting 76 contacts as having no web presence.
- **⚠ A LOGO IS A CONCLUSION, AND IT CAN ONLY BE DRAWN FROM A SEARCH THAT RAN.** The first cut let a person fall back to their employer's mark whenever no headshot was found — including when the headshot search had **429'd and never executed**. That would have written `avatar_url` for every remaining contact, skipped them on every future pass (the script only looks at rows with no avatar), and silently capped the directory at logos on the one day the quota happened to be spent. A person now settles for a logo only when the search actually returned.
- **The backfill ran and stopped where it should.** `scripts/backfill-profile-photos.mts` — checkpointed per contact, because a deploy is a `launchctl kickstart` (§12) — filed **3 logos with no model call whatsoever** (Ber Wilson's own mountain mark at 180×180, Case Construction's wordmark, Barnraisers' site icon, all visually confirmed) before hitting the day's wall at contact 7 of 83. Nothing was lost: the 80 still without a photo are simply still in the queue, and re-running is free.
- **Both enrich buttons now gather an image.** `/api/parties/[id]/enrich` runs the photo search **in parallel** with the existing research pass (same person, same grounding — no extra wall clock) and shows the found image at the size it will be used, with the page it came from underneath and an explicit "No headshot found — logo instead" when that is what happened. `/api/entities/[id]/enrich` does the same for a vendor's `logo_url`. Provenance — source, page URL, the reason it was believed — is written into `enrichment_notes.profile_photo` so a wrong face is always traceable, and neither path ever overwrites a photo a human chose.
- **Hit rate is honest and low, by construction.** Of four real contacts probed by hand, two had a public headshot and two have no web presence at all; the gmail-domain half of the directory will mostly miss. Returning nothing is the correct answer there, and the script prints the reason for every miss so the tally is readable rather than mysterious.

**Done 2026-09-26 (UX/UI pass: the brief renders as a brief, the queue reads as facts, one attention number; DEPLOYED):**
- **Richard's ask: "review the user experience and the user interface. Is there anything you would do to make it an even better and more useful beautiful experience?"** He named three frictions when asked — **forms and data entry**, **too much to scan**, **make it more beautiful** — and set the appetite at "whatever makes it best".
- **⚠ THE REVIEW WAS DONE IN THE BROWSER, NOT ONLY IN THE CODE, AND THAT IS WHERE EVERY HEADLINE FINDING CAME FROM.** Three code audits ran in parallel and returned good material, but the five things worth fixing first were all things you can only see: a page showing literal `## Bottom line`, a queue of 197 rows of clipped prose, and three numbers on one screen that disagreed about how much needed attention. The token layer in `globals.css` and the nav in `lib/nav.ts` are genuinely good and were deliberately left alone.
- **⚠ THE EXECUTIVE BRIEF WAS RENDERING AS RAW MARKDOWN, AND THE COMPONENT THAT FIXES IT WAS ALREADY IN THE REPO, WIRED TO THE PRINT ROUTE.** `src/components/briefs/BriefMarkdown.tsx` parses headings, bold, bullets and the three severity markers, and its own header argues there must be ONE renderer because *"a brief printed for a meeting must be the same document that was read on screen"*. `/projects/[id]/brief/print` used it. The screen did not — `ProjectNarrativeBrief` dropped the raw string into a `prose prose-sm [&_h1]:text-base [&_h2]:text-sm …` wrapper under `whitespace-pre-wrap`, **so no `<h1>` element was ever produced and not one of those child selectors could ever match**. The styling had been written for a rendering that never happened. The printed brief was prettier than the screen one.
- **A second, divergent copy of the same renderer was inlined at `PortfolioBriefButton.tsx:121`** — exactly the two-renderers-of-one-document the shared component exists to prevent. Deleted. `AgentChat` had the same raw-string-in-a-`prose`-div shape and now renders through it too.
- **⚠ `[FACT]` AND `[JUDGEMENT]` APPEAR IN NO PROMPT — THE MODEL INVENTED THEM.** `RECORD_BRIEF_SYSTEM_PROMPT` rule 5 said *"Distinguish FACTS, ESTIMATES and JUDGEMENTS… but label it"* and gave no vocabulary, so the model chose brackets. `[CRITICAL]/[WATCH]/[INFO]` **are** specified — but only for *Risks and constraints*, which is why they leaked mid-sentence elsewhere. Fixed at both ends: the prompt now names the closed vocabulary, says provenance is expressed in prose ("proposed", "our reading is", "not recorded") and reserves brackets for the severity line (`record-brief-1.0` → `1.1`, and `stored_briefs.metadata.prompt_version` already tracks it); the renderer handles an unplanned tag rather than stripping it. **Stripping would be lossy and silently so** — a `[JUDGEMENT] the schedule will slip` rendered bare becomes a flat assertion of fact, the opposite of what the rule exists for. Known tags get a `Chip` in the canonical severity palette; unknown ones get a quiet `label-caps` micro-label, because `FACT` can recur three times in one paragraph and a full chip each time shouts.
- **⚠ THE BRIEF WAS INVISIBLE TO ANY BROWSER THAT HAD NOT PERSONALLY GENERATED IT.** Every brief the platform writes goes into `stored_briefs`; the panel's only source was `localStorage`. A second executive, a new laptop or a cleared cache saw an empty box — and so did anyone whose regeneration failed, because a failed refresh blanked the panel and discarded a perfectly good brief sitting in the database. **This is how it was caught: mid-session the panel went empty, and the logs said `Failed to load model "qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b". Engine protocol startup was aborted` / `Local AI stream stalled — no data for 180s`.** The server now reads the latest stored brief and passes it in; it refreshes only when what it holds is not from today (a regeneration is 30-60s of the local model and queues behind every other AI job, §12); a failed refresh is now a footnote under the last good brief rather than a blank.
- **⚠ `/decide` IS THE APP'S MAIN WORK QUEUE — 197 ITEMS — AND IT WAS A WALL OF PROSE.** Each row was three lines of model paragraph truncated mid-word, with the facts that decide the question buried inside the sentences: *"The $12M institutional school project in Mapleton, UT aligns…"*, *"~38,000 sf across two buildings"*. **The structured data was already loaded.** `leads` carries `estimated_value`, `location`, `sector`, `scope`, `bid_due_date`, `site_visit_date`, `rfi_due_date` and `solicitation_number` as columns, and `decide/page.tsx:49` already did `select('*')` — the `DecideItem` viewmodel flattened all of it to `title / subtitle / note` and threw the structure away. **Pure UI change, no schema work.** Rows now lead with a fact strip (`$12M · Mapleton, UT · Institutional`) and the prose is clamped to one line beneath it. `review_queue` rows genuinely hold nothing but a confidence and an explanation, so they keep two lines of prose and no strip — the row degrades rather than faking parity.
- **⚠ THE ROW SHOWED `pursue 82` AND THE LIST WAS SORTED BY THE SAME NUMBER — IN A FILE WHOSE OWN COMMENT FORBIDS BOTH.** `DecideClient.tsx:38` reads *"a fit_score carries ±20 points of noise and must not be sorted or thresholded on… never shown as a number"*. Five hundred lines below, `:555` rendered `{item.verdict}{' '}{item.score}`; `rank.ts:30` used `+ (i.score ?? 0)` as the final term of `decideWeight`; and `page.tsx:51` ordered the fetch by `fit_score` descending. **Four consecutive rows on screen read `pursue 85`** — the digits were discriminating nothing and the queue was being ordered by sampling noise. Verdicts now render through a label map (`Pursue`), the score is gone, and money is the tiebreaker: capped at 99 so it breaks ties *inside* a verdict band and can never leapfrog one.
- **⚠ THREE DIFFERENT ATTENTION NUMBERS WERE ON ONE SCREEN AT ONCE: 1, 99+ AND 197.** The sidebar's Dashboard badge summed overdue milestones + critical diligence + overdue tasks (inlined in `layout.tsx`); the KPI tile summed critical diligence + overdue milestones + expiring certs **+ the whole Decide queue**, then restated the queue in its own sub-label ("197 · 197 waiting to decide"); and `NeedsAttention`'s header badge summed nine sub-lists, three of them already `.slice(0, 6)`, so it under-reported by construction. **`computeAttention()` had no UI callers at all** — its only two consumers are `agent-tools.ts` and `pepper/assemble.ts`. New `countAttention()` in `src/lib/attention.ts` is the one definition, four cheap head counts, shared by the layout and the tile; deliberately **not** `computeAttention()`, which runs a dozen queries and includes `lead_reviews` — that would fold the Decide backlog back into the number that exists to be separate from it, and this runs in the root layout on every page. The queue is now stated as itself and linked; the `99+` cap was raised because 197 is four characters and it is the truth. The two numbers now agree on screen: **Needs Attention 1, matching the sidebar's 1, with "197 waiting to decide →" beneath it.**
- **⚠ A BARE EM DASH AT A VALUE'S OWN TYPOGRAPHIC WEIGHT READS AS A FAILED RENDER, NOT AS "NOT SET".** Three of six dashboard project cards, three of twelve kanban cards, `DELIVERY METHOD` on every project Overview, the `WEIGHTED PIPELINE` tile and four `<select>` placeholders all showed one. Gone: project cards say "No value set" in quiet type, the contract `<dl>` omits the row entirely, the selects say "Not set" / "Unassigned", and the weighted-pipeline tile — which was showing a dash plus a two-line instruction across a quarter of the KPI band — **collapses, because a KPI tile with no value is not a KPI tile**. `Commitments.tsx` already had the right instinct with "no date agreed" and a comment explaining it; this is that rule applied everywhere.
- **⚠ THE COMMITMENTS RAIL WAS NINE CONSECUTIVE ROWS OF RED: 227d, 218d, 117d, 116d, 101d, 72d, 72d, 71d, 60d overdue.** When every row is red the colour has stopped signifying. Past thirty days is history — still listed, still settleable, no longer shouting. And the unexplained `🕐 2d` repeating on every row was `ageLabel(created_at)`: how long ago the commitment was read out of the mail, not a deadline. Beside "227d overdue" a bare clock and a number communicated nothing; it now says "found 2d ago".
- **⚠ `formatValue` HAD THREE SHADOW COPIES AND A SIGN BUG.** `dashboard/ProjectCard.tsx:44`, `dashboard/HealthPanel.tsx:15` and the canonical one each picked their own precision, which is why the same figure read `$2.1M` on Projects and `$2.13M` on the Financing tab. The magnitude guards were unsigned, so `formatValue(-2_500_000)` fell through to the last line and returned **`"$-2,500,000"`**. Now one decimal at every tier with the trailing `.0` trimmed (`$12M`, not `$12.0M`), `Math.abs` for the tests, and the sign outside the currency symbol.
- **`/tasks`: the page title was printed twice, one line apart.** `AppHeader` derives "Team Tasks" from `nav.ts`, and the board rendered its own `<h1>` saying the same words directly beneath. The board's is gone (a scoped board still titles itself, because there it is not the page). It also lost `max-w-4xl` — **it was clipping every task subtitle mid-sentence while reserving ~400px of empty column beside it** — and its four record filters no longer stretch: a `<select>` sizes to its widest option, so the project list stretched one control to half the row and the four wrapped onto three ragged lines.
- **⚠ THE REPEATED TASK TEXT WAS STORED DATA, NOT A RENDER CHOICE.** Five of nine visible titles opened with the identical ten characters `Bid due — ` (`leads/tasks.ts:265`), and every subtitle was `Ber AI: PURSUE (82/100). <first concern>` (`whyLine`, `:120`) — the same forbidden score, frozen into a text column where it can never be re-read. Both generators now write facts (`est. $12M · Mapleton, UT · Institutional — <concern>`), and **the 7 existing rows were backfilled** after a `_bw_task_backfill_20260926` copy: fixing the generator alone changes nothing the reader sees, and the same column is what Pepper emails and what Google Tasks shows on the phone.
- **The projects kanban gave 300px each to stages holding nothing.** `Award 0` and `Mobilization 0` squeezed the three columns carrying all twelve projects into a third of the board and pushed the rest off-screen. An empty stage keeps its place — a funnel with a missing rung misleads — at 92px, without a `$0` total. `/intel` was a fixed `h-[650px]` inside a `max-w-5xl`, leaving dead space right and below on a laptop and putting the composer under the browser chrome on a phone; it is `100dvh`-based and full width now.
- **⚠ THE APP HAD NO `Input`, `Select`, `Textarea` OR `Label` PRIMITIVE — 278 RAW `<input>`S ACROSS 68 FILES, AND 29 LOCAL CLASS CONSTANTS.** 79% of controls carried a label that sat beside the field but was not tied to it, so clicking the word did not focus the box. **Five of the constants — `ProjectForm`, `OpportunityForm`, `ContactForm`, `InvestorForm`, `SteelDealForm` — were byte-identical.** New `src/components/ui/field.tsx` (`Field`/`Input`/`Select`/`Textarea`/`FieldDate`/`FormSection`/`FormGrid`/`FormActions`, ids and `aria-describedby` from `useId`) plus `src/lib/utils/field-classes.ts` holding the strings outside the `'use client'` boundary. **The five forms now import the shared strings rather than being rewritten** — ~120 controls moved onto 44px touch targets, `rounded-lg`, and `focus-visible:ring-3` in one commit with the markup untouched. That is the migration path, and it is why `tsc` stayed green throughout.
- **⚠ THE OLD FOCUS RULE WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT SHOWED ON EVERY CLICK.** 248 sites used `focus:outline-none focus:ring-2` — `focus:` fires on a mouse click too, so clicking into any field flashed a ring. Only 12 occurrences of `focus-visible:` existed in the whole app, all in `button.tsx` and five other files. The field kit follows `button.tsx`.
- **15 controls existed only on hover, including two deletes** — `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` with no tap affordance and, in twelve of them, no `focus-visible:opacity-100` either, so a keyboard user could focus a control they could not see. `DecideClient` already did this correctly; its pattern (`sm:opacity-0 … focus-visible:opacity-100`) is now applied across `ProjectsClient`, `ContactsClient`, `EntitiesTab`, `DiligenceTab`, `MediaGallery`, `ConversationList`, `DinoNotes`, `InvestorRequirements`, `EditRoleButton` and `RemovePlayerButton`.
- **Raw enums stopped reaching the screen.** New `enumLabel(value, map?)` in `constants.ts` — and **the fallback is the point**: `projects.contract_type` is *not* a controlled enum (the form offers FFP/CPFF/GMP while email intake and lead promotion write `joint_venture`), so a map-only lookup renders blank where a humanising fallback renders "Joint Venture". `CONTRACT TYPE: joint_venture` was on every project Overview. `reviewReasonLabel` routes through it, `NeedsAttention`'s `{dd.severity}` and CSS-`capitalize`'d reason are now a `Chip` and a label, and `/decide`'s `subtitle: … : r.source_table` no longer prints a bare table name.
- **One severity palette.** `dd_severity` had five — the canonical `SEVERITY_BADGE` plus local copies in `DiligenceTab`, `DependenciesTab`, `UpdatesTab` and `PasteInput` — and the canonical one was the minority (the only one making `critical` orange). `NeedsAttention` and `BriefMarkdown` now both draw from it.
- **⚠ THINGS THE AUDIT GOT WRONG THAT MEASURING CORRECTED.** `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` is **already active** via `eslint-config-next`, with six rules, none of which catch labels or icon buttons — so "enable it" was not the job. Running the candidate rules against `src` put `label-has-associated-control` at **101 violations in 22 files, not 68**, with six files holding 62 of them; and `control-has-associated-label` at **334**, which is the known-noisy rule — it flags `<Button>{ACCEPT_COPY[item.accept].verb}</Button>` because the name is not *statically* derivable. Not enabled. And `ProjectForm`/`SteelDealForm`, assumed to be the worst forms because they are the longest, are the **two best-formed in the repo** — `<section>` + `label-caps` + grid, every label with `htmlFor`, two a11y violations between them. `FormSection`/`FormGrid` were extracted *from* `ProjectForm` rather than invented.
- **⚠ WIZARDIZING THE TWO LONG FORMS WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED.** Both are `<form action={formAction}>` with `useActionState`. Splitting them means either hiding steps with CSS (a progress bar and nothing else, plus the browser's "required field is hidden" failure) or lifting 34 fields into client state and posting once at the end, which discards progressive enhancement and rewrites both action signatures. `ProposalIntakeWizard` is not the precedent it looks like: its steps exist because step 2 cannot run until step 1's upload returns an extraction — a data dependency, not a field-count remedy. `FormSection` ships with `collapsible`/`defaultOpen` instead, which gets the same perceived benefit with every field mounted.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean throughout, `next build` clean, `eslint` held at its **27-problem baseline (20 errors, 7 warnings)** — three new `no-unused-vars` from dropped `cn` imports were cleared before the count was accepted. Deployed with `launchctl kickstart` after each change and walked in Chrome at 1440px: `/decide`, `/dashboard`, `/tasks`, `/projects`, `/projects/[id]`, `/projects/new`, `/contacts/new`, `/intel`.
- **⚠ Not fixed, found on the way:** LM Studio was returning `Failed to load model… Engine protocol startup was aborted` and `Local AI stream stalled — no data for 180s` during the session (§12's `lms ps` check — the other 2026-09-26 session was unloading and reloading the model at the time). And `/contacts` is still 80 records in ~290px cards, six to a screen, some rendering an `<hr>` with nothing beneath it — the densest remaining scanning problem, and the next thing worth doing.

**Done 2026-09-26 (scanned documents read locally; the agent's limits lifted; DEPLOYED):**
- **Richard's ask: "tell me exactly what model to load into LM studio and I will do it… Also, I don't care how long it takes, I just want the most accurate answers as possible so please remove any limits from it doing so. If I need to do something on my end like expand the context window tell me what to expand it to."**
- **⚠ THE HONEST ANSWER TO "WHICH MODEL" WAS NONE, AND MEASURING THE MACHINE IS WHY.** Before recommending anything: `free` **0.3GB**, `wired` **25.8GB**, `compressed` 6.9GB, and **swap 17.2 of 18.4GB used** — with `llama-server` holding **19.71GB** of weights, Colima reserving **3GB** for the Supabase stack, and active swap-ins running ~6MB/s. A 7B VL model at Q4 is another ~6GB on a box already paging. Loading one would have bought slower, less faithful transcription and risked exactly the OOM kills §12 already records.
- **⚠ AND LOADING A MODEL WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED ANYWAY, FOR TWO REASONS IN THE CODE.** `callGeminiWithFile`'s local image branch sends to `localChatModel()` — the single `LOCAL_AI_MODEL` text model — so an image would have gone to Qwen3.6 and failed; there is no second model env var. And the scanned-PDF branch **throws `UnreadableDocumentError` before any image exists**: `extractPdfText` returns null and it gives up, so a scanned PDF could never have reached a vision model even if one were loaded. There is no PDF rasteriser in the repo. "Load a vision model" was never one step.
- **The platform already had the right tool, built for something else.** `bw-ocr` (`scripts/ocr/card-ocr.swift`) wraps Apple's Vision framework for the business-card scanner — no model, no RAM held resident, nothing leaves the machine. It could not take a PDF: ImageIO does not decode PDF, so the lease came back *"could not decode image (unsupported format?)"*.
- **⚠ MEASURED FIRST, AND THE MEASUREMENT SETTLED THE WHOLE QUESTION.** `sips` rendered page 1 of `Lease ADL421724.pdf` at a mere 611×784 and Vision read it — including **"containing approximately 665 acres, more or less"**, the figure Ber AI had been asked for three times and could not produce, plus the full legal description (*Fairbanks Meridian; Township 003 North; Range 001 East; Section 33 S1/2, S1/2NE1/4; Section 34 SW1/4, S1/2NW1/4, SW1/4NE1/4, S1/2SE1/4, NW1/4SE1/4; Fairbanks Recording District*) and the lessee's address. **Full document after the rewrite: 11 pages, 26,103 characters, 3 seconds.** No vision LLM was going to beat that.
- **`bw-ocr` now takes PDFs**, rendering each page through `CGContext` at a chosen DPI (`--dpi`, default 200; `--max-pages`, default 300). Details that are each a bug if got wrong: `.cropBox` not `.mediaBox` (mediaBox carries printer bleed that pads the render and shrinks the text); the page filled **white** first (a scan is often transparent where it is white, and Vision reads dark on light); `drawPDFPage` so `/Rotate` is honoured (a landscape scan stored rotated recognizes as nothing); and **exit 5 for "read it, found no text"** as distinct from 3 for "could not read the file" — a blank or purely graphical scan is a fact to record, not an error to retry forever.
- **Wired in as a fallback, not a replacement.** `transcribePdfText` still tries the embedded text layer first and only OCRs when there is none, so 285 documents that already had text are untouched. New `extractImageText` gives images the same path, and `documentKind` grew an `'image'` kind — images had been `'unsupported'`, so they were skipped outright. The summary path needed a fix to match: a scanned PDF's text now comes from OCR, so sending the file to `callGeminiWithFile` would render and recognize the whole scan a second time and then throw — it summarizes from the text already in hand.
- **`scripts/reindex-unreadable-documents.mts`** backfills anything with no text (`--kind`, `--project`, `--limit`, `--dry`), writing progress back after every document so an interrupted run resumes rather than restarts (§12 — a deploy is a `kickstart`), and surviving a single unreadable file instead of dying on it. **39 documents were in that state: 30 PDFs and 9 images** — `Army NEW LEASE..pdf`, `Eaquinta Operating Agreement.pdf`, `Sharkey_SettlementAgreement.pdf`, `Tax Notices.pdf`, two Welsko patents, `Five Star Subdivision.pdf`, the Wendover and Carbon County plat maps, and the Alaska assay letter and resistivity survey.
- **Limits lifted, as asked.** Agent rounds **12 → 30** and the wall-clock budget **4 → 30 minutes** (`AGENT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS`, `AGENT_TIME_BUDGET_MS`); the closing round still guarantees an answer at whichever limit is reached first, so "no limit" does not reintroduce "no answer". `LOCAL_PDF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` **240,000 → 2,000,000**: that figure dated from when a whole document was fed to the model at once, so it doubled as a context guard, and it had silently truncated — `SOO lode report.pdf` was stored at *exactly* 240,000 characters. Reads are windowed now, so the only thing it bounds is a text column and an embedding pass.
- **⚠ THE ONE LIMIT THAT CANNOT BE LIFTED BY FIAT IS THE CONTEXT WINDOW — AND HAND ARITHMETIC GOT ITS COST WRONG BY MORE THAN DOUBLE.** The GGUF metadata says 40 layers × 2 KV heads × (256 + 256) = 81,920 bytes per token, which puts f16 KV at 65,536 tokens at 5.00 GiB and 131,072 at 10.00 GiB. **`lms load --estimate-only` says otherwise, and it is the one that knows its own allocator: 23.30 GiB at 65,536 and 25.42 GiB at 131,072 — a delta of just 2.12 GiB**, with flash-attention and the MoE layout not allocating what the naive formula implies. It also returns the *identical* figure for `--parallel 1` and `--parallel 4`, so the four slots are not a memory cost — and a 28,018-token prompt verified fine against `--ctx-size 65536 --parallel 4`, so they are not slicing the usable window either. The recommendation to Richard is therefore small and exact: **+2.12 GiB buys 131,072 tokens**, quantizing the KV cache to q8_0 in the GUI offsets it if the box is tight, and `--parallel → 1` is tidiness rather than a lever. `AGENT_CONTEXT_BUDGET_CHARS` and `AGENT_DOC_WINDOW_CHARS` stay at their 65,536-safe defaults, documented to be raised *with* the LM Studio change and never ahead of it.
- **⚠ THE FIRST BACKFILL ATTEMPT PROVED THE MEMORY POINT BY FAILING, AND FAILED IN THE SESSION'S OWN WORST WAY — SILENTLY.** Run with the model resident, it managed **2 documents in 20 minutes** and marked six readable ones `skipped`: `R0170 (1).pdf` was written off as permanently unreadable and then OCR'd **105,063 characters** by hand a minute later. Cause: swap grew from 18.4GB to **21.5GB with 295MB free** while `bw-ocr` rendered an 18.5MB scan at 200 DPI, so the recognizer was being killed — and `ocrDocument` returned null for *both* "read it, found nothing" and "was killed", so the pipeline could not tell a blank scan from a machine out of memory. **New `OcrFailedError`:** exit 5 (no text) and exit 3 (cannot decode) return null as properties of the document; anything else throws, leaving the document retryable, and the backfill tallies those separately with the command to re-run.
- **The fix was to stop asking the two heaviest things to run at once.** `lms unload` dropped wired memory **25.36GB → 4.27GB** and swap **20GB → 7GB**; OCR needs no model at all, only the 639MB embedder. A new `--text-only` mode skips the 30-60s summary call, and the same backfill then did **28 of 34 documents in about 7 minutes**: `Lease ADL421724.pdf` 26,087 chars, `Eaquinta Operating Agreement.pdf` 100,827, two Welsko patents 122,473, `Army NEW LEASE..pdf` 47,013, the R0170/R0183/R0186 1880s survey records 102–152k each, `Sharkey_SettlementAgreement` 8,238, `Tax Notices.pdf` 6,076, and the plat maps and site photos in the hundreds. **6 genuinely carry no text** (blank or purely graphical) and one, `SNL_Letter_Englert_Results.pdf`, is **password-protected** — a real gap, now named rather than silent.
- **⚠ TWO MORE GAPS FELL OUT OF CHECKING THE END STATE RATHER THAN TRUSTING IT.** Five documents held text and had **zero chunks** — 293,229 characters invisible to retrieval, including `Email research — englertmining@gmail.com.md`, the file carrying the Alaska township grid; `--unembedded` found and fixed them (the chunks lookup pages at 1,000 rows, §12). And **a document with a NULL `ai_summary` is one the agent never opens**: `list_documents` and `get_record_brief` present a document *by* its summary, so with the lease extracted but unsummarized Ber AI still answered *"the lease ADL-421724 document is a scanned PDF the platform cannot read"* — while `get_document_content` with `find:"acres"` returned **"containing approximately 665 acres, more or less"** at offset 1,034 on request. The summary is not cosmetic, it is the signpost; `--missing-summary` fills the 29 documents the text-only pass left in that state.
- **End state: 324 of 340 live documents hold text (was 292), 5,736 chunks, and nothing with text is left unembedded.** The remaining 16 are the 6 blank/graphical, 9 calendar and raw-email files that carry no document text by design, and the one encrypted PDF.
- **Richard applied the LM Studio change; the window is now 131,072 with a q8_0 K/V cache, and `.env.local` sets `AGENT_CONTEXT_BUDGET_CHARS=300000` / `AGENT_DOC_WINDOW_CHARS=40000` to match.** ⚠ **The eject-and-reload introduced two problems that `lms ps` caught and nothing else would have:** a **second full copy of the model was resident** (`qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b:2`, two llama-server processes at 21.20GB and 19.71GB — **41GB against 36GB of RAM**, free memory 0.10GB), and **`--parallel` had reverted to 4** despite being loaded at 1. §12 already warned that a model id ending `:2` is the tell; this is the first time it was seen on a *GUI* reload rather than from `lms unload -y`. Unloading the duplicate settled it at one process, 22.22GB.
- **The doubled window is not free, and the cost is latency rather than memory:** document-summary calls on the long OCR'd records went from **40-50s to 110-135s** — prompt processing over a larger KV cache. Worth it for an agent turn that now carries 102k tokens of evidence; worth knowing before wondering why a cron got slower.
- **`LOCAL_SUMMARY_INPUT_CHARS` added but deliberately left at 30,000.** A summary's job is to say what a document IS so the agent decides to open it, and 30k characters answers that for a 150k-character survey record. Quadrupling it would quadruple the prompt on every document pass on a box that is already 22GB of model against 36GB of RAM.
- **Verified end to end, same question that opened the session — "Where exactly is this land located, and how many acres is it?" — 8 tool calls, 223s, 101,999 prompt tokens:** *"approximately **665 acres** across Sections 33 and 34, T3N, R1E… Fairbanks Recording District"*, with the legal description tabulated (S½, S½NE¼ / SW¼, S½NW¼, SW¼NE¼, S½SE¼, NW¼SE¼), the 69-claim total from the spreadsheet, and — read out of the OCR'd lease — **a 60-foot RS 2477 public easement running through the lease area that must remain open at all times**, a real constraint on surface disturbance that no one had surfaced. It still hedges the per-township claim split with "~" (48/12/2 against an actual 52/15/2) while the total of 69 is exact, which is the counting weakness the row-count line fixes only where a count is printed.
- **The lease's own `ai_summary` now opens with "approximately 665 acres in the Fairbanks Recording District"** — so the answer is visible at the signpost level, in `list_documents` and `get_record_brief`, without opening the file at all. That is the difference the `--missing-summary` pass made.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` clean, `eslint` at the pre-existing 27 (one `prefer-const` I introduced, fixed), `zsh scripts/build-ocr.sh` builds, OCR verified on the 11-page lease by hand and through the pipeline, all three backfill modes run to completion (34 text + 5 embeddings + 29 summaries), deployed with `launchctl kickstart`, `deploy/tailnet-setup.sh` green on all three endpoints.

**Done 2026-09-26 (Ber AI announced a search and then stopped: a five-round cliff with no answer behind it; DEPLOYED):**
- **Richard's report: "I just asked Ber intelligence to comb the alaska project documents and find me the location. It said it was combing them but then just stopped working. I want to make sure Ber Intelligence thoroughly searches all available data and does not stop until it completes its missions. Token usage should not be a constraint."**
- **⚠ THE TURN DID NOT CRASH. IT RAN OUT OF ROUNDS AND SHIPPED THE NARRATION AS THE ANSWER.** `runAgent` looped `for (let round = 0; round < 5; round++)` and then fell out of the bottom with whatever text had accumulated. `finalText` accumulated across **every** round — so when the model was still calling tools at round five, what got stored was the preambles from rounds one to four. Read straight out of `agent_messages` on conversation `53cfa78b`, three consecutive turns:
  - *"I don't have the specific acreage or precise location details in the summary data… Let me pull those."* — 6 tool calls, 38s.
  - *"Let me pull the actual claim list and lease document to get you the precise location and acreage."* — 6 tool calls, 21s. **99 characters, and that is the entire stored answer.**
  - *"Let me pull the JV Brief… The Felix PSA is the most detailed document, but it's truncated. Let me also check… The knowledge base and email search didn't surface the specific Alaska location data. Let me search more specifically…"* — **9 tool calls**, 60s, and still no answer.
  - Nothing told the model it was out of rounds, and nothing told Richard either. A budget cliff and the assistant giving up mid-sentence are indistinguishable from the chair.
- **⚠ AND A DOCUMENT COULD ONLY EVER BE READ 20,000 CHARACTERS DEEP.** `get_document_content` returned `raw.slice(0, 20000)` with `truncated: true` and **no parameter to ask for the rest** — no offset, no continuation, nothing. On this project that is 8% of `SOO lode report.pdf` (240,000 chars) and 26% of the Felix PSA (76,666). The agent said so out loud — *"the Felix PSA is the most detailed document, but it's truncated"* — and had nowhere to go with it. A legal description or an acreage schedule sits wherever it sits; reading the front of a contract is not reading the contract. "Thoroughly searches all available data" was impossible by construction, independent of the round budget.
- **⚠ AND THE ONE FILE HOLDING THE ANSWER WAS A FILE TYPE THE PLATFORM COULD NOT OPEN.** `documentKind` classified `.xlsx` as `'unsupported'`, so `Full Claim List.xlsx` was stored with a file and **zero extracted text** — Ber AI could see that a document by that name existed and nothing more. It holds exactly what was asked for: **50 State of Alaska mining claims by ADL number, Fairbanks Meridian, township (3N1E / 3N1W / 2N1E / 2N1W…) and quarter-quarter section.** The agent chased it twice in one turn and could not say why it was failing, because `list_documents` reported `has_full_text: false` with **no reason** — and "no text" reads as a transient miss, not as a permanent property of the file.
- **Four changes, in the order they matter.**
  - **The last round always runs with the tools removed.** This, not the round count, is the fix: on the closing round the model is handed a `[SYSTEM]` instruction and no tool declarations, so a function call is not a reply it can give and the only thing left to emit is the answer. The instruction makes a **partial** answer the required output — what was established, what was not, and which specific file or system holds the rest. A turn can no longer end on a preamble.
  - **Rounds 5 → 12, plus a 4-minute wall-clock budget** (`AGENT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS`, `AGENT_TIME_BUDGET_MS`). Generation is free on this box, so the round count is a runaway guard rather than a cost control; the time budget is what actually brings a long investigation in to land, by promoting the next round to the closing one.
  - **Narration no longer survives into the answer.** Text from a round that ends in tool calls is discarded: the server emits a new `reset` SSE event and `AgentChat` clears what it has rendered. Richard still watches it work — that is the only evidence anything is happening — but the message he reads afterwards is the answer, and it now matches what is stored rather than diverging on the next page load.
  - **A window, not a prefix.** `get_document_content` takes `offset` (with `next_offset` handed back) and `find: "<phrase>"`, which centres the window on the first match — the fast path to a clause, a township description or a payment table deep in a contract. Verified: `find: "ADL 421724"` against the 76,666-char PSA, and `offset` walking a document to its end.
- **⚠ RAISING THE ROUND BUDGET WITHOUT A CONTEXT GUARD WOULD HAVE TRADED ONE SILENT FAILURE FOR A WORSE ONE.** Measured on this box: the system prompt is **17,547 characters**, the company context **4,885**, and the 42 tool declarations **30,216** — about **13k tokens of fixed overhead on every request**, against a **65,536-token window** (`lms ps`). One 20,000-character document window is ~5k tokens, so **ten document reads fill the rest** — and a thorough investigation now makes more calls than that by design. So the oldest tool *results* are shrunk to a stub as the conversation grows (`AGENT_CONTEXT_BUDGET_CHARS`, 120k), keeping the six most recent intact. Messages are never removed, only their content replaced: an OpenAI-format `tool` message must keep following the `assistant` message whose `tool_calls` it answers. **It fired three times in the verification run — rounds 7, 8 and 9 — which is the measurement that says the guard was needed, not speculation.**
- **New: .xlsx extraction** (`extractXlsxText`). An .xlsx is a zip of XML; `fflate` inflates it (already in the tree, zero dependencies of its own, now an explicit dependency) and the sheet XML is read directly — shared strings, inline strings, cached formula values — into one markdown table per sheet. **The column letter in each cell's `r="C12"` reference is what places it:** a blank cell is simply absent from the XML, so reading cells in sequence without it shifts every value after a gap one column left, which silently mis-pairs a claim number with the wrong section. `scripts/reindex-spreadsheets.mts` backfilled the one affected document: **4,167 characters, 3 chunks embedded, 36s.** Only 1 of 315 live documents was a spreadsheet — but it was the one that answered the question.
- **⚠ AND THE FIRST VERIFICATION RUN CAUGHT AN ERROR I HAD JUST WRITTEN INTO THE PROMPT.** The new prompt rule listed "a scan, an image, a spreadsheet" as permanently unreadable and gave the example sentence *"the acreage is in Full Claim List.xlsx, which the platform cannot read yet"*. The agent produced that sentence almost verbatim — about a file that was, by then, fully indexed. **A prompt example is training data, and a stale one is a lie the model will repeat with confidence.** The rule now says to judge readability from `list_documents` and never from the extension, and its example names a file that genuinely is a scan.
- **`list_documents` now says WHY a document holds no text** — `unreadable_because`: image file, scanned/image-only PDF, unsupported type, calendar invite, raw email. The distinction the agent needs is permanent-vs-transient, so it reports the gap by name instead of re-fetching the same empty document. On the Alaska project that labels 9 of 22 documents, including `Lease ADL421724.pdf` and 3 other scanned PDFs.
- **Prompt: a FINISHING THE JOB section.** Never announce work instead of doing it (there is no one else to do it, and the reader cannot answer "go ahead"); exhaust list_documents → get_document_content → search_knowledge_base → search_correspondence → get_record_brief before calling anything absent; a long document is not read until you have read past the first window; end every turn on an answer.
- **⚠ AND ONCE THE AGENT COULD READ THE TABLE, IT COUNTED IT WRONG.** Asked how many claims the schedule holds, it read all **69 rows** and reported **62** — with its per-township split wrong too (43 / 17 / 2 against an actual **52 in T3N R1E, 15 in T3N R1W, 2 in T2N R1W**, verified by `awk` over the stored text: 69 rows, 69 distinct ADL numbers, no summary row). Counting rows of a long table is the one thing a language model is worst at and a line of code is exact at, and the count is the figure an executive repeats out loud. `extractXlsxText` now prints `69 data rows (first row is the header). This table is complete — use this count rather than counting the rows below.` above each sheet. Generic on purpose: the row count is arithmetic, the grouping by township is judgement, and only the first belongs in the extractor. **Re-verified after the change: 69 claims and 52 in T3N R1E — both correct**, the stated total having anchored the split as well.
- **Verified end to end against the question that failed**, same project, same phrasing: **17 tool calls across 10 rounds, 352s, 5 narration resets, the context guard firing 3 times** — and a Situation / Risks / Recommendation / Next Decision answer naming the Fairbanks Recording District and the Pedro Dome / Golden Summit trend, the 49 conveyed legal descriptions from PSA Exhibit A, and the acreage as an explicit gap with where to get it. Previously: 9 calls, 5 rounds, and the sentence *"Let me pull the JV Brief."*
- **And re-verified after the prompt correction: 4 tool calls, 93s** — `list_projects` → `get_record_brief` → `list_documents` → `get_document_content` on the claim list — returning the township-by-township breakdown, the named claim clusters (Pedro Dome, SOO North / True North, Serra Pelada, the Sheriff/Posse group), and the acreage as an explicit gap with where to get it (the seller's asset schedule, or BLM records by ADL number). The whole investigation collapsed from 17 calls to 4 once the file it needed was readable.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` clean, `eslint` — 27 problems, all pre-existing and none in a touched file (the documented count in §9 is unchanged).

**Done 2026-09-25 (a title company's documents reached nothing, and the attachment importer could never have run; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's report: "there are some emails from misty@highlandtitleutah.com providing title research. I don't see those docs being uploaded automatically to the helper deal or the Drive into the appropriate folders... Maybe logging the email is fine, but it would be nice if I could click it and open the email. Note: Highland Title will be working on multiple projects so it is good that the AI understand what project it belongs to based on the content of the email/documents."**
- **The mail was read. Everything after that failed, for three independent reasons.** Five threads from `misty@highlandtitleutah.com` were in `email_threads`, swept from `tuaone@`, summarized, clustered, `routed_at` stamped — carrying 14 non-inline attachments (preliminary reports, plat maps and invoices for Carbon County parcels 02-0138, -0139, -0140 and -0354). Zero `thread_links`, zero documents, zero updates, nothing in Drive.
- **1. The router had nothing to match on, and was right to refuse.** Subjects read `62831 | Parcel No 02-0138-0000 / Carbon County | NPS Holdings, LLC / Ber Wilson Company`, which shares **no token** with *DUBHES Helper / Giovanni Resilience Campus*. Its aliases are `Helper`, `Giovanni`, `DUBHES` — none present. Misty was not a `parties` row; neither NPS Holdings nor Eaquinta Land existed as a party or entity. So the four threads formed a NEW cluster ("Eaquinta Land LLC Parcel (Carbon County)") and staged a session proposing a **duplicate project** at 0.95 confidence, with `match_candidates` empty — so the merge path could not even be offered.
- **2. ⚠ THE ATTACHMENT IMPORTER WAS UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, FOR EVERY RECORD IN THE PLATFORM.** `importNewAttachments` sliced the thread at `applied_message_count` — and **every filing path except the router's own inferred match seeds that cursor at the thread's CURRENT length**: the hand-file button, `linkClusterToRecord` (so `/decide` confirm *and* the merge route), and the derived-link branch. Deliberately, and correctly, so filing a conversation does not replay years of mail into a record's feed as new activity. But it meant the attachment slice was **always empty**: a thread's existing documents could never arrive, and only a message landing *after* the link existed brought a file in. **Measured: 178 attachments sat on project- and opportunity-linked threads against 30 correspondence documents ever imported.** Filing Highland's threads by hand would have imported nothing at all.
  - Fix: `thread_links.attachments_through`, a **second cursor**, defaulting to 0 — which also backfills every existing link. The asymmetry is the point: *the text of old mail is not news, but a deed is still a deed.* The candidate scan now selects a link on **either** cursor (a caught-up link was previously skipped entirely, which is exactly what a freshly filed thread is), liveness is probed separately so an attachments-only pass still respects a closed record, and the cursor advances **per message** so a `kickstart` mid-run resumes rather than restarts (§12).
- **3. No clickable email.** `RecordCorrespondence` rendered subject · mailbox · date as dead text. The permalink helper (`gmailThreadUrl`, `authuser=` rather than a positional `/u/0/`) had existed since the leads work and was never wired here. The subject is now the link, with the 44px inset overlay, and the `why_filed` reason renders under it.
- **Learned identifiers — the answer to "understand what project it belongs to".** A title company works across many deals, so the SENDER can never be the key. What is durable is the **property**: a parcel number belongs to a piece of ground permanently, and the owning entity belongs to it for the length of a negotiation. New `record_identifiers` table; filing a thread by hand, confirming a session or merging one now records the parcels and owning entities that thread carried, and the router matches them **by containment as a fact (`linked`), exactly as it already matches a solicitation number** — not as a score needing review. Identifiers are **read** by the router and **learned only from a human filing decision**: a router that taught itself would compound, attaching a neighbouring parcel mentioned in a forwarded chain and then filing the neighbour's deal here.
  - **Retroactive by design.** `routeThreads` reads `routed_at is null`, so a thread already refused is never reconsidered — learning from thread one would leave its siblings where they were. `threadsMatchingIdentifiers` finds unlinked threads carrying the new identifier and re-routes them explicitly. **Verified live: filing 62831 taught `parcel 02-0138-0000` + `NPS Holdings, LLC` and pulled in 2 siblings automatically** (reasons: *"parcel 02-0138-0000"*, *"NPS Holdings, LLC is on this record"*); filing 62830 taught `Eaquinta Land LLC` and pulled in the fourth.
- **⚠ THE EXTRACTOR WAS MEASURED AGAINST THE WHOLE CORPUS, AND THE MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE DESIGN TWICE.** First run over all 2,492 threads produced **164 distinct party identifiers**, and the list was full of things that are on many deals by their nature: `Carbon County` (10 threads), `Murray City`, `City of West Wendover`, `Salt Lake Chamber`, `U.S. Army Corps of Engineers`, `Bank of Utah` — plus bare personal names from `summary.counterparty`: `Charles Manto`, `Steve McCleery`, and **`Richard White`, the reader himself**. Learning "Carbon County" onto Helper would file every thread about the county there. Two changes: `summary.counterparty` **dropped as a source entirely** (it answers "whose deal is this" with the wrong *kind* of answer), and a civic/geographic ban list. **Result: 164 → 15 distinct parties, all genuine private entities, and 4 parcels with zero false positives across 2,492 threads.** Only 26 threads carry any identifier at all — narrow and high-precision, which is the right trade for something that files without review.
  - Separately, `normalizeParty` stripped `holdings`, `group` and `trust` as legal suffixes. Those are NAME words: `NPS Holdings, LLC` reduced to `nps`, fell below the length floor and was discarded — so the owner of two of the four parcels was learned as nothing. Only genuine legal forms are stripped now, and periods are removed first so `L.L.C.` collapses to `llc` rather than `l l c`.
- **⚠ TWO MORE BUGS SURFACED ONLY BECAUSE FOUR SIBLING THREADS ARRIVED AT ONCE.** Both were invisible until a real parcel assembly hit the importer.
  - **The name-only dedupe silently discarded six real documents.** Every Highland thread attaches a `Title Commitment - AS.pdf` and a `Plat Map.pdf`, so three of each were skipped as duplicates. **And size cannot rescue it:** measured, the four title commitments are **1,091,743 · 1,093,633 · 1,097,014 · 1,103,229 bytes** — four different parcels within **1.1%** of each other — while the plat maps span 94,853 → 377,644. A tolerance wide enough for the re-encode case the name rule was written for (205,839 vs 211,664) discards these. Now deduped on a **SHA-256 of the bytes** (`documents.content_sha256`): identical bytes are a resend and skipped whatever the name; different bytes under a held name are imported and **renamed with the parcel** — `Title Commitment - AS (02-0140-0000).pdf`. The remaining error, a genuinely re-encoded resend across two threads, is now a visible near-duplicate rather than a silent deletion.
  - **A failed byte fetch advanced the cursor anyway.** Gmail meters by cost-units-per-**minute** (§12), so pulling four 1MB title commitments in a row is precisely when `fetchAttachmentBytes` returns empty — the loop `continue`d, the end-of-thread advance ran regardless, and the file was unreachable by any later pass. Caught live: the plat map for **02-0140-0000** vanished exactly this way. A failure now holds the cursor at the message before it.
- **Signature logos were being filed as project documents.** `image001.png` (56,496 bytes) and `image002.png` (14,317) arrive **inline** on Misty's original and as plain attachments on Eric's reply — Gmail re-attaches a sender's signature images with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, stripping the inline marker. This is the mirror of the existing §12 rule (Content-Disposition is authoritative, or Gmail-sent files are discarded as chrome). Both had been imported and filed into Drive. Now filtered on the **name**, which is what survives: `image001.png`, `ATT00002.png`, `oledata.mso` are generated by a mail client and never by a person — bounded to images under 200KB so a genuine phone photo still comes through. The two that landed were deleted and their Drive copies **trashed** (never hard-deleted — `canDelete` is false).
- **End state on DUBHES Helper:** all five Highland threads filed, **12 documents imported** — four title commitments, four plat maps and four escrow invoices, one per parcel, each named for its parcel — self-filed into the team's own Drive subfolders (*Land Legal*, *Previous Land Offers*), embedded and searchable by Ber AI. Correspondence posted to the project feed. The duplicate-project card in `/decide` resolved as **merged into Helper** rather than creating a second record. Two plat maps are scanned/image-only so no text was extracted — they need a vision model loaded in LM Studio, noted as an open item.
- **⚠ PRE-EXISTING FINDING, NOT INTRODUCED HERE: the apply phase has no concurrency guard.** A manual run and the hourly cron both saw `applied_message_count = 0` and each posted the same email. **Measured across the whole `updates` table: 15 `source_ref` groups hold duplicates, dating back to 2026-05-04 and including 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-22** — long before today. Today's three were removed; the underlying race is logged as an open item rather than fixed in passing, because the correct guard (claim-then-post) trades a duplicate for a possible loss and deserves its own pass.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean on every touched file, `next build` clean, both migrations applied as `postgres` (grants confirmed present on `record_identifiers` — §12), deployed with `launchctl kickstart`, `deploy/tailnet-setup.sh` green.

**Done 2026-09-24 (a lead promoted to the Steel CRM disappeared; DEPLOYED):**
- **Richard's report: "I had a lead come through and I sent it to the Steel CRM. The problem is it just disappeared. It should have gone and created an opportunity in the steel CRM with all the information possible. In an ideal world it then just gets quoted by clicking our quoting tool."**
- **⚠ THE RECORD WAS CREATED, WAS CORRECT, AND WAS VISIBLE TO NOBODY.** `steel_deals` held the deal — *Bid Solicitation & Site Walk · Silo Park Place Adaptive Reuse*, Kier Construction, $8M, stage `quote`, created 11:53:58, Drive folder published, the lead marked `promoted` and its thread linked. Nothing had failed. But `SteelPipelineBoard` defaults `scope` to **`'mine'` whenever the viewer is linked to a `team_member`**, and `'mine'` filters on `deal.salesperson_id === myMemberId` — while `/api/leads/[id]/promote` **never sent a `salesperson_id`**. `LeadDetailSheet.promote()` posts `{ target }` and nothing else. So the deal was created **unassigned**, and an unassigned deal is in nobody's book: not Richard's, not Eric's, not the default view of either. **Measured across the whole table: 2 of 7 steel deals had no salesperson, and both were invisible to every viewer who opened the page** (the other being *Hawaii home*).
- **The one-field-over comparison is the tell.** The same route already defaults `capture_lead` to `viewer.teamMemberName` for exactly this reason — *"an owner-less pursuit is the thing this replaces"*. The steel branch took `opts.salespersonId ?? null` and no caller ever passed one.
- **⚠ AND THE QUOTE BUTTON COULD NOT HAVE BEEN PRESSED EITHER.** `quoteReadiness()` blocks on **square footage, a priced material line, the owner, the site address, the scope summary, a named estimator, and company contact details**. The promoted deal carried the owner and nothing else — `site_address`, `scope_summary`, `salesperson_id`, `next_step` and `next_step_date` were all NULL — **while the lead itself already held two of them**: `location` = *470 West 600 South, Salt Lake City, UT 84101* and `scope` = *"Adaptive reuse of two adjacent buildings including demolition, structural metal framing, roofing, HVAC, MEP, and finish trades."* A promotion that reports success and then hands over a disabled button is the same failure as the invisible card, one screen later.
- **Three changes.**
  - The promote route **defaults `salesperson_id` to whoever clicked**, beside the `capture_lead` default it mirrors.
  - `promoteLead`'s steel branch **carries `site_address` from the lead's location, `scope_summary` from its scope, and the bid date into `next_step_date`** under a named next step (*"Price the steel package and return a quote"*). The bid date is the reason the deal is urgent; without it the card sorted to the bottom of its own column under `next_step_date ?? '9999-99-99'`.
  - The board grows an **"unassigned" attention chip**, counted over **every** deal and **bypassing the owner scope when active** — a chip computed on the scoped set could only ever reveal what the scope had already discarded. A deal in nobody's book can no longer be hidden from everybody.
- **The swallowed deal was backfilled from its own lead** (owner, address, scope, next step + the 2026-09-22 site-walk date), so it is now in Richard's pipeline with two honest blockers left: **square footage and a priced line**. Neither is inventable — the email never states a building size. Confirmed the quoting tool itself is fine: `company_profile` carries email and phone, and `steel_quotes` already holds 2 generated quotes.
- **Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` clean, deployed with `launchctl kickstart`, `deploy/tailnet-setup.sh` green on all three endpoints.
- **Note on the ask's wording:** "created an opportunity in the steel CRM" — the Steel CRM has no `opportunities`; its record type is a `steel_deal`, which is what promotion creates. Nothing is missing there.
