**Done 2026-09-24 (Pepper — a morning note addressed to a person, and one stack to approve; DEPLOYED):**
- **Richard's ask: "how to best take advantage of our local LLM, automations and other things that an executive assistant would do on behalf of the executive team. We would like to refer to the Intelligence layer as 'Pepper'. She is here to help manage the company."**
- **⚠ MEASURING FIRST SAID THE BOTTLENECK HAD MOVED, AND THAT MORE EXTRACTION WOULD MAKE IT WORSE.** `email_intake_sessions` held **80 staged deals waiting on a click, 67 of them older than two weeks, the oldest from 12 July** — and the model had already decided every one: **74 `create`, 6 `merge`, NOT ONE `dismiss`, average confidence 0.93 with every row at or above 0.85.** Plus 38 unresolved review items and 77 live leads: **~195 decisions for two people.** Meanwhile `commitments` held **220 open obligations** read out of mail, and the local engine ran at **~5% of a day** (3.3–8.5% typical, 17.3% on the heaviest of ten days), with **19:00–04:00 completely untouched** and every batch job crammed into 05:00–07:00. The scarce resource is not GPU and not extraction. It is a human saying yes.
- **⚠ AND NOTHING THE PLATFORM LEARNED WAS ADDRESSED TO ANYBODY.** One Google Chat space receives the weekly brief, the daily digest, lead announcements and document arrivals; `team_members` has **no notification-preference column**; the only per-person channel in the system is the Monday task digest. `computeAttention()` computes **eleven categories** of what is falling through the cracks and **had no reader at all** — its only callers were its own route and an agent tool, so a human saw the itemised list only by thinking to ask the AI. (`risk_scores` is still in that position: computed nightly at 01:00, rendered nowhere but a freshness card.)
- **Two corrections to CLAUDE.md, both measured.** The pursuit profile is **no longer thin** — 5 target sectors, 10 geographies, 3 delivery methods, 3 contract types, 615 chars of differentiators, 653 of disqualifiers, 570 of past performance, 9 certifications, $20M bonding — so "refine the pursuit profile" as highest-leverage work #1 is largely **done**; only `min_project_value` / `sweet_spot_value` / `max_project_value` are still null. And `/decide` already accepted rows in place, so batch approval was an extension of an existing surface, not a new one.
- **New: Pepper's morning note** (`src/lib/pepper/*`, `/api/cron/pepper-note`, weekdays **06:50**) — one email per executive, in the second person: what you owe, what you are owed, your day with the counterparty context an assistant would have looked up, the portfolio's cracks, and ONE closing line on the queue. **Email rather than the Chat space**, for the reason the task digest already carries its list inline: the platform is tailnet-only and a note that needs a login is a note nobody reads from a truck. This is also what finally gave `computeAttention()` a reader.
- **⚠ `commitments.owner_name` IS FREE TEXT AND CANNOT CARRY ATTRIBUTION ON ITS OWN.** The live distribution for `side='us'`: `Ericson Tua'one` 22, **`Ber Wilson` 19 — the company, not a person** — `Eric` 10, **`Bear Wilson` 9 (the company again, misspelled)**, `Ericson H. Tua'one` 4, `Richard White` 4, `Erikson Tua'One` 2, `Richard M White` 2, `Eric Tua' One` 1, **`Hola` 1**, and **31 nulls**. Four spellings of one man and a Spanish greeting. `contact_aliases`, which would have been the natural place to resolve this, **is empty — 0 rows** — so nothing was built on it. **The thread's MAILBOX is the key that actually works**: complete on every row, deterministic, and it answers the question being asked. So the name is tried first against a strict bar (a token of 4+ characters, unique to exactly one member, ambiguity refuses per §12) and the mailbox decides when it does not. **Verified against all 220 open rows: Richard 60, Eric 148, 12 company-level, 61 of them resolved by name rather than mailbox.**
- **⚠ WHICH SIDE THE COMMITMENT IS ON DECIDES WHETHER THE NAME MEANS ANYTHING AT ALL.** For `us` the owner is the internal person who took it on. For `them` it is the **counterparty being waited on** — so resolving it to a teammate produces nonsense, and one live row proves it: *"Ensure team access to Google Drive business plans — Moose"*, side `them`, which under a naive read lands on Richard's waiting-on list as something Richard owes himself. `them` now consults the mailbox alone.
- **⚠ THREE BUGS FOUND BY READING THE FIRST REAL NOTES, NOT THE CODE.**
  - **`Tua'One` normalized to two tokens too short to match.** The apostrophe was being replaced with a space, yielding `tua` + `one`, so **three of the four spellings of Eric's surname resolved to nobody.** Apostrophes are now deleted rather than separated, before other punctuation.
  - **Printing the reader's own name back at them invented a third party out of the recipient.** *"Review and sign the GridEdge MNDA — extraction named: Richard White"*, rendered into Richard's own note, came back from the model as **"Richard White is waiting"**. When the owner IS the reader the name is not information; the line now says the item is theirs.
  - **All five attention slots went to ONE project waiting on the SAME people for the same 143 days** — five phrasings of one stalled Box Elder conversation ("Response from Governor Cox", "Response from Box Elder Commissioners", "Response regarding the proposal", twice more) — while the rest of the portfolio silently lost its place. Capped at two per project per category; the re-run gave a slot back to a bid closing in six days.
- **⚠ THE SECTIONS HAD TO BE CAPPED, AND THE CAP HAD TO BE HONEST.** Eric's ledger alone is **89 owed and 58 awaited**, which rendered to an **18,349-character prompt** asking for a note under 300 words — a long prefill on a model that serves one request at a time, to produce something nobody could act on. Capped at 12 a section, ranked **overdue first (most overdue first), then due soon, then undated oldest first** — undated rows are kept because **185 of the 220 open rows have no agreed date at all** and dropping them would hide most of a real ledger. The overflow is passed through and stated ("and 77 more not shown"), and **the subject line reports the TRUE count, not the listed one**: Eric's reads *89 commitments outstanding* over twelve printed rows, because "12" over a ledger of 89 is a small lie told every single morning.
- **⚠ A NEW CRON ROUTE IS UNREACHABLE UNTIL `middleware.ts` NAMES IT.** The first live call answered `{"error":"Not authenticated"}` — the middleware's words, not the route's. The gate runs first, so the route's own `CRON_SECRET` check never executes. It typechecks, builds, registers, and then **401s at 06:50 every weekday into a log nobody reads**. Added to the allowlist beside the other twelve crons; verified afterwards that an unauthenticated call now returns the route's own `Unauthorized`, i.e. it still fails closed.
- **⚠ PEPPER NOW SENDS AS HERSELF, BECAUSE THE FIRST REAL NOTE CAME FROM RICHARD.** `sendMail` defaults to `PRIMARY_MAILBOX`, so the note arrived From **"Ber Intelligence <moose@berwilson.com>" — Richard's own address**, making a note written *to* him look like mail he had sent himself. `info@` is a real seat (`team_members` already holds *Pepper Potts / info@berwilson.com*) and its token was checked against Google's `tokeninfo` endpoint — **it genuinely grants `gmail.send`**, not merely "should". `notify()` gained `from`/`fromName` so the seam stays the only thing that knows how a channel sends. Read back out of the mailbox afterwards: **From "Pepper <info@berwilson.com>"**.
- **New: batch approval on `/decide`** — multi-select, **"Select the N Ber AI is sure about"** (pre-decision confidence ≥ 0.85), and a runner that accepts **strictly one at a time** with visible progress. Sequential is not a UI preference: each accept writes a record with its people, tasks and attachments and publishes documents to Drive, against a box whose model serves one request at a time. **A failure does not stop the run** — the rest of the batch is good work and the failed rows stay in the queue — and **only rows that actually succeeded are marked done**, because a row vanishing without being written is worse than one that never moved. **§11 is untouched: a human still confirms; they confirm seventy at once instead of seventy times.**
- **Measured what the button will actually offer**, using the page's own `buildConfirmBody()`: of **81 pending sessions, 75 `create`, 6 `merge`, 0 `dismiss`, every one at confidence ≥ 0.85, and 77 accept-ready.** The four that are not are the already-known sessions whose correspondence never states a record name (*"Needs a project name — the correspondence never states one"* ×2, opportunity ×2). So one confirm drains the entire correspondence backlog.
- **⚠ The select-all toggle compared counts across different filters.** Selection survives a filter change on purpose (you can gather a batch across tabs), so `selected.size >= selectable.length` said "Clear" on a tab where nothing was ticked, as soon as the two numbers happened to coincide. Compared row by row now.
- **Verified end to end on the DEPLOYED build, not a dev process.** `tsc` clean, `next build` clean with `/api/cron/pepper-note` registered, eslint clean on every new and changed file. Dry run: **2 candidates (Pepper's own seat correctly excluded), 0 sent, 0 failed, and NOTHING written to `notification_log`**. Real send: **1 sent, logged `pepper_note|email|sent`**, and an immediate second run returned **`skipped: "already sent today"`** without making a model call. **The message was then read back out of `moose@` by the Gmail API** — subject *19 commitments outstanding* (12 printed + 7 omitted = 19 ✓), body carrying "Good morning", "First thing" and the Pepper footer, HTML escaping intact. `notification_log` grants were checked against `information_schema.role_table_grants` **before** trusting a green run, because that same guard failed silently from 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-24 while reporting success.
- **Timing is a correctness constraint here.** 04:30 lead sweep → 06:30 weekly brief → **06:50 this** → 07:00 digest. Measured per note on the real ledger: **123s, 131s, 170s** on ~2,800-token inputs, so two people is ~250–340s and fits the ten-minute gap with margin. **A third executive would not fit** — the answer then is an earlier slot, never a parallel one.
- **Deliberately NOT built:** re-adding calendar writes (`src/lib/leads/calendar.ts` is dead code for a reason — 107 leads wrote events and 100 dates were already past with nothing to clean them up); any new extraction pass (the queue is human-bound, not model-bound, and the build log is right that manufacturing model work is the recurring mistake); any write authority for Pepper over records; and a per-person notification-preference column, which two people do not need.
- **Left for later, in order:** Pepper's **ears** — email `info@` a question from a phone and have her answer in-thread over the agent's 42 read-only tools, sender-allowlisted to the two executives; **draining the overnight backlog** (1,333 of 2,442 threads have never had the commitments pass, 841 are unembedded, against an engine free 19:00–04:00 — finishing existing passes, not inventing new ones, and checkpointing per unit because a deploy is a `kickstart`); **the chase list** (107 commitments are owed *to* us — draft the chase in `info@`, never send it); **meeting prep unasked** (`/api/ai/meeting-prep` exists but fires only from a button); and **closing the directory**, which knows 36 of the 652 people the company emails while volume climbs — 250 threads active in June, 646 in August, **1,199 in September**.

**Done 2026-09-24 (a stack of business cards, scanned at once, reviewed once; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's ask: "I have multiple business cards to upload and don't want to wait for each one. I would like to upload multiple photos and have you put each one through the ingestion process completing their profile, company information, relevance towards Ber Wilson."**
- **Measured the cost before changing anything, and the wait was the whole complaint.** `ai_queries` holds **18 calls at `prompt_version = 'card-intake-1.0'`** — two per card, so **nine cards have ever been scanned** — **averaging 44s and peaking at 96s each**. A card is therefore ~90s of model time plus grounded search, and `ScanCardButton` held a modal dialog open for all of it, in series. **A stack of twelve is ~22 minutes of a phone screen that sleeps after thirty seconds.** The feature was good for the one card you are handed at a meeting and unusable for the handful you come home with.
- **New: `/intake?tab=cards`** — drop the photos, walk away, review the stack once (`CardBatchUpload` → `/api/contacts/scan-card/ocr` → `/api/contacts/scan-card/batch` → `/intake/cards/[id]` → `/api/contacts/scan-card/batch/confirm`). Staged as an `email_intake_sessions` row with `intake_kind = 'cards'`, reusing the running→pending→failed contract People Intake and Email Research already prove. **The Scan Card button on the Directory gained `multiple`**, so picking more than one photo there hands off to the same batch rather than opening a dialog it cannot honour; one photo still behaves exactly as before.
- **⚠ `intake_kind` CARRIES A CHECK CONSTRAINT AND THIS IS NOW THE THIRD TIME.** `('email','meeting','people')` — so `'cards'` would have typechecked, built, deployed, and then failed at every INSERT. Checked against `pg_constraint` before writing the route, widened in migration `20260924000004`, and the constraint re-read afterwards to confirm all four kinds. §12 already says this; it is worth saying that following the rule cost thirty seconds and ignoring it costs a deploy.
- **⚠ THE CARD SCANNER NEVER ASKED WHETHER THE PERSON WAS ALREADY IN THE DIRECTORY. IT BLIND-INSERTED, ALWAYS.** Scan the same person's card twice — a year apart, or twice at one conference — and you get two `parties` rows, which is exactly the failure a batch makes twelve times more likely. Meanwhile People Intake had a careful matcher sitting in `profile-intake.ts` doing precisely this job. **Extracted to `src/lib/contacts/directory-match.ts` and used by both doors** (§12: never fork a shared pass — add a target), so "already have them" means one thing platform-wide: email is identity and wins outright; a name that is not unique comes back `ambiguous` with its candidates and **no chosen id**, and the review screen asks rather than merging two people.
- **A matched row defaults to filling the existing contact in, never overwriting it.** Verified against a fixture: a record whose `title` was null and whose `phone` read `555-9999` took the card's title and **kept its own phone**, tags merged, the note appended rather than replaced (somebody's own writing), and **exactly one party still held that address**. Cleaned up afterwards — this is production, so the fixture was created, asserted and deleted, 0 residue.
- **Splitting recognition from research is what makes the wait tolerable, and it is a privacy improvement too.** Apple Vision is local and instant, so `/api/contacts/scan-card/ocr` reads each photo on its own, one request per image: **an unreadable photo says so within a second, while the card is still in your hand**, instead of twenty minutes later. It also keeps a dozen 6MB phone photos from arriving as one 70MB body on a box that has been OOM-killed before (§12). And by the time anything slow starts, **only text is in play — the photographs are already gone**, which was already true of the single scan and is now true for longer.
- **The batch returns in 140ms and writes its row after EVERY card**, which buys three things at once: progress is a real count ("1 of 2 researched"), `updated_at` moves so the 15-minute stale-`running` guard cannot trip on a long batch that is in fact healthy, and **a batch interrupted by a `launchctl kickstart` still hands over the cards it finished**. The recognized text is stored on the session, so **"Finish them" re-reads only the unfinished cards and costs nobody a second photograph** — which matters because a deploy *is* a kickstart, and the batch's own background pass dies with it.
- **Cards are processed strictly in series because LM Studio serves one request at a time** (§12) — overlapping them would only queue them somewhere nothing can show it. **What a batch genuinely saves is research: company lookups are cached across the stack.** Measured on a live three-card run — two people from Okland Construction and one from Big-D — **`research_reused: 1`, with the two Okland cards sharing an identical 27 sources**, i.e. the second colleague's research was free. **327s for three cards (109s each), all three `ready`, 0 failed.**
- **One write path, shared.** `src/lib/contacts/card-save.ts` carries create / fill-in / skip, and both the single confirm and the batch confirm call it — the single route shrank to 47 lines. It takes its Supabase client as a **required parameter** rather than reaching for `actorAdminClient()` itself: a user-initiated write attributed to "system" in the activity log is the §12 bug, and taking it as an argument also keeps the module free of request-scoped imports. The batch confirm saves each card on its own, so **one bad row never costs the reader the other eleven** — a failed row comes back named, the rest have already landed, and the session stays open rather than closing over a card that did not save.
- **Verified end to end on the DEPLOYED build with a real minted session, not a dev process.** `tsc` clean, `next build` clean with all four new routes registered, eslint clean on every new and changed file. Authenticated render check: **`/intake?tab=cards` 200** with the drop zone present; **`/api/contacts/scan-card/ocr` round-tripped two real images** (Vision returned the full card text, correctly dropping the blank lines); a real two-card batch **returned `{session_id, cards: 2}` in 0.14s** and the review page rendered its live state (`["reading","queued"]` → "1 still being researched", "Nothing is ready yet") without a reload. Test sessions deleted afterwards.
- **Deliberately NOT built:** attaching a scanned stack to a project or opportunity (People Intake does that because a cast belongs to a deal; a conference stack does not, and nobody asked); storing the photographs (the whole posture of this feature is that the image never persists, and a batch is not a reason to change it); pipelining research for card N+1 against the model call for card N (measurable gain, real complexity, and the wait is already unattended); and raising the cap past 30 cards.

**Done 2026-09-24 (People Intake — profile a whole cast from the mail already on file; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's ask: "enter a person's email address and have Ber Intelligence scrub through emails to gather all information needed to populate their profile, so I don't have to type it in" — named against a live deal in Eagle Mountain (Seth Lloyd, Trevor Burton, a "Cliff" at Avant, a land owner Jerren Davis, and the firm Tensor whose "reps are to be found out soon"), and asked for those profiles associated to the deal.**
- **⚠ MEASURING FIRST CHANGED THE WHOLE SHAPE OF THE BUILD: THE EVIDENCE WAS ALREADY ON THE BOX AND NOBODY WAS READING IT.** `email_threads` holds **2,436 threads, 2,372 summarized, 652 distinct participant addresses**, with `participants` GIN-indexed and `raw_markdown` carrying the rendered conversation. Queried before writing any code, the corpus already had **every person he named**: `seth.lloyd@elitesolutions.tech` (7 threads), `trevor.burton@` (4), **both TensorIQ reps he said were unknown — `sterling@tensoriq.io` and `jonathan@tensoriq.io`** — and the land owner as `jarenldavis@gmail.com`. One stored thread contains, verbatim, `Trevor Burton / Elite Solutions / 801-231-5995`. **So this was never a Gmail-integration job; it was a missing front door.** No new table, no new sweep, no new AI provider.
- **The gap was precise.** `/api/parties/[id]/enrich` — the Enrich Profile button — does Google Contacts plus three grounded web searches and **never reads the mailbox**, and it requires a party record with a name already typed, which is the opposite of what was asked. `/api/email-research/run` does read the mail beautifully but aims at producing an *opportunity*; people fall out as a side effect.
- **New: `/intake?tab=people`** (`ProfileIntakeForm` → `/api/contacts/profile-intake/run` → `/intake/people/[id]` → `/api/contacts/profile-intake/confirm`), staged as an `email_intake_sessions` row with `intake_kind = 'people'`, reusing the running→pending→failed contract the Email Research run already proves. Five stages, each degrading rather than failing: **parse seeds** (`Name <email>`, bare address, bare name, a pasted To:/Cc: line, `(role hint)` in parentheses, split on delimiters that are not inside brackets) → **resolve stored mail** → **top up from Gmail** for anyone the cursor-based sweep has not reached → **one local-model pass per person** → **the existing web enrichment**. Then the fan-out: everyone else on those threads, offered as cast candidates.
- **⚠ `intake_kind` CARRIES A CHECK CONSTRAINT (`'email' | 'meeting'`), so 'people' would have typechecked, deployed, and then failed at every INSERT** — the 09-19/09-23 failure mode exactly. Checked before writing the route, widened in migration `20260924000003`, and every write the confirm route makes was then **proven in a rolled-back transaction** (party with tags/notes/enrichment jsonb, alias upsert, entity + `party_entities`, `project_players` against an opportunity *and* against a project, session close). `ALL WRITES OK`, rolled back, 0 residue.
- **⚠ `/api/parties/associate` HAS BEEN 500ING ON EVERY CALL IT HAS EVER RECEIVED.** `contact_aliases`' uniqueness lived only in `uq_contact_alias`, a UNIQUE INDEX on **`lower(alias)` — an EXPRESSION** — and PostgREST's `onConflict: 'alias'` names a column, so Postgres answered `there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification`. **Proven with a probe insert before touching it, not inferred.** A UNIQUE CONSTRAINT cannot be declared on an expression, so the fix is a generated stored `alias_key` column carrying a real constraint; verified case-insensitively (two spellings → one row) and the redundant expression index dropped. All alias writes now go through one `upsertAliases()` which also refuses aliases that identify nobody — a bare first name maps two people to whoever was written last, which is worse than no alias.
- **⚠ `email-ingestion/confirm` WAS WRITING OPPORTUNITY PLAYERS INTO A TEXT NOTE, its own comment asserting "opportunities have no player link table".** They have had one since `20260923000002` (nullable `project_id` + nullable `opportunity_id`, exactly-one check) — so every person confirmed onto an opportunity since then landed in `opportunity_notes` and the record's Players tab stayed empty. Six-line fix; the roll-call note is kept alongside the real links because it reads well in the feed.
- **⚠ THE FIRST LIVE RUN PRODUCED A CONFIDENTLY WRONG CONTACT, AND THE REFUSAL RULES EXIST BECAUSE OF IT.** "Cliff (Avant Executive)" matched **exactly one** Cliff in 2,400 threads — `cab11c@acu.edu`, **Cliff Barbarick, an academic at a university with no connection to the deal** — and because it was a unique match the resolver took it. **One match is not a unique one; it is an unchallenged one.** A single given name now never auto-resolves, and the row says what it found and why it will not use it. There are no Cliffs at goavant.net at all: the twelve Avant people in the mail are Jason Jones, Calvin Vass, Chip Hoisington, Peter Callowhill, Ross Thompson and seven others. The role hint is used only to NARROW an existing candidate set, never to widen one.
- **⚠ AND IT FILED A CONTACT AS "To: Cliff Barbarick".** The name capture runs back to the previous delimiter, which in rendered mail is a quoted header's `To:` or the whole `### 2026-09-08 17:34 —` message heading — so both became part of people's names, along with `Email:sterling` from a `<mailto:>` link in a signature block. Cleaned, with labels, headings, `mailto:` and colon-bearing captures all rejected.
- **⚠ THE CAST FAN-OUT WAS DROWNED BY TWO PARTY INVITATIONS.** The first run returned **40 candidates**, almost all strangers from t-mobile.com, invitenetworks.com and motustech.tech — because Seth Lloyd's threads include two **"FW: AVANT Mobility Solution Lunch & Learn"** blasts with **35 and 36 recipients**. Measured the distribution before picking a rule: **2,391 of 2,436 threads have five participants or fewer**, and the largest real deal conversation has 11. Above 15 a thread is a distribution list, not a conversation, and its recipients are not a cast. Re-run returned **8 people, every one of them real**: Todd Gorringe (Elite), Calvin Vass, Chip Hoisington, Peter Callowhill, Ross Thompson (Avant), **Sterling Orr and Jonathan Houk (TensorIQ — the reps he said were unknown)**, and **`jarenldavis@gmail.com`, the land owner**. Ranking is colleague-of-a-seed first, then thread count, because "who are the other side's people" is the question actually being asked.
- **⚠ THE PARTICIPANT SCAN WAS CAPPED AT 1,000 ROWS AND SILENTLY READ 40% OF THE CORPUS.** PostgREST's ceiling, self-inflicted with an explicit `.limit(1000)`, and the symptom was that the correctly-spelled "Jaren Davis" could not be resolved *at all* while everything else worked. Paged, and it resolves. **This is the third time this rule has cost time; it is in §12 and I still wrote the bug.**
- **Near misses are suggested, never applied, and the threshold is calibrated rather than chosen.** "Jerren Davis" (his spelling) scores **0.60** against `jarenldavis@` on a character-bigram Dice coefficient; scored against all 652 addresses, `Seth Loyd`→0.93, `Chip Hoisington`→0.87, `Trever Burton`→0.82, `Peter Callowhil`→0.73, and `Michael Zzzzson`→nothing at all. 0.58 catches the real case; it also admits the odd false friend (`Robert Smith`→`tsmith@` at 0.67), which is the right trade **only because there is no auto-resolve on this path** — the reviewer reads "closest in the mail" and ignores it.
- **Confirm writes what a contact record alone cannot: the association.** Party create-or-fill (an existing contact's typed fields are never overwritten, only gaps filled — the Enrich Profile policy, and the note is appended rather than replaced because the existing one is somebody's own writing), aliases so the next extraction finds the person instead of duplicating them, employer find-or-create + `party_entities` in the same shape the card scanner and manual Add Contact produce, `project_players` against the chosen project **or opportunity**, and `embedPartyEnrichment` so Ber AI can answer "who is the land owner on Eagle Mountain?". Every link is idempotent — re-confirming cannot double-link. **Nothing is created before the human presses Confirm; §11 untouched.**
- **Two shared passes gained a target instead of a fork** (§12): Google Contacts + web research moved out of the enrich route into `src/lib/contacts/web-enrichment.ts` so both doors run one pass (the route shrank 158 lines), and the sweep's `persistThreads` gained `storeFetchedThreads()` so a targeted Gmail search's threads enter the corpus properly — summary_state pending, picked up by the next summarize phase — rather than being read once for one screen and thrown away.
- **Also built:** the cast has a **"Profile the selected"** button that feeds the ticked addresses into a fresh run, which is the actual two-pass workflow — the first pass finds who is on the deal, the second reads their mail properly. And a **"Profile from Email"** button on the Directory toolbar, the third door in beside Add Contact and the card scanner.
- **Verified against the DEPLOYED build in the browser, not a dev process.** Ran the four names Richard gave, mail-only: **"2 of 4 people were profiled from 7 email threads, and 8 other people appear in the same correspondence."** Seth Lloyd → Elite Solutions, **801-231-2587**, role *project introducer*, title blank with the placeholder reading "not in the mail" (honest rather than invented). Trevor Burton → 4 threads, defaulting to **Update existing → Trevor (same email address)**. Cliff and Jerren Davis → refused, each carrying its reason. `tsc` clean, `next build` clean with all three new routes registered, eslint clean on every new and changed file (the two survivors in touched directories are the documented pre-existing §9 noise). **The staged session was deliberately left un-confirmed for Richard** — confirming creates real contacts and that is his call, not mine.
- **Deliberately NOT built:** auto-profiling on a schedule (the point of the human step is that a profile read out of mail is evidence, not a record); a `people` nav destination (it is an intake mode, and this platform keeps removing destinations); merging `team_members`/`entities` into `parties` while in the neighbourhood (§9 says only if the split causes real pain, and it did not here); and writing commitments found during profiling into `tasks` (§11, same argument as 09-23).
- **⚠ AND `npm run gen-types` IS A HARD-DISABLED STUB, while §4 told every session to run it after every migration.** It is literally `echo … && exit 1` (it used to run `--linked`, which points at the retired cloud project), and `SUPABASE_DB_URL` — documented in §7 as the replacement — is **referenced nowhere in the repo**. So the generated types have been frozen for some time and six live tables are absent from them (`email_threads`, `mailbox_sync`, `thread_clusters`, `thread_links`, `leads`, `commitments`). Nothing was broken by this — the convention that already exists (`sweepDb()`'s untyped client carrying hand-maintained row interfaces) is what this session followed — but §4 was instructing every future session to perform an impossible step and then presumably to improvise. **§4 and the §7 env line now state reality and say what to do instead. Repairing gen-types against the self-hosted DB is a real, small, un-done job.**
- **⚠ Richard's manual step: one session is waiting at `/intake?tab=people` with Seth Lloyd and Trevor Burton ready to confirm.** Attaching them to the existing **Elite Solutions** opportunity (already at stage `negotiating`) is one dropdown. There is still no Eagle Mountain record; the Attach dropdown will create nothing, so make that project or opportunity first if the cast should land on it.

**Done 2026-09-24 (simplification pass — a table with no grants, a bell with no audience, and three dashboard panels that could never show anything; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's question: any ways to simplify the platform and create a better user experience?** Measured the live system rather than reading the build log, and the answer was not a code-size answer: **there are zero orphaned components** (every prior cleanup held), so the weight is in information architecture and in features that quietly do nothing.
- **⚠ FIRST, A MEASUREMENT TRAP WORTH KNOWING: `pg_stat_user_tables.n_live_tup` IS A STALE ESTIMATE AND IT LIED ABOUT HALF THE SCHEMA.** It reported `projects` at **1** (really 15), `parties` at 6 (really 81), `risk_scores` at 110 (really 947), `email_intake_sessions` at 13 (really 140). Every conclusion in this entry would have been wrong. **Rule: count with `count(*)`, never `n_live_tup`, when the number is going to drive a decision.**
- **⚠ `notification_log` HAD NO API GRANTS AND HAD FAILED EVERY CALL SINCE THE DAY IT SHIPPED (2026-08-18).** PostgREST answered `42501 permission denied`, and the cause was ownership: the table is owned by **`supabase_admin` while every other public table is owned by `postgres`**, so it fell outside the default privileges that grant anon/authenticated/service_role — and `postgres` then could not grant on it either (`WARNING: no privileges were granted`). Two silent consequences: the task digest's **once-per-day idempotency insert always failed**, and because its error was discarded the run still reported a successful send while the guarantee never held (a second cron fire in one day re-sends it); and `/settings/health` reads that table for its Task Digest card, so **that card was structurally incapable of ever reporting a successful send**. Fixed by reassigning the owner and granting (migration `20260924000001`); verified the same insert went **42501 → 201** and the read **403 → 200**, then the probe row deleted (0 residue). The caller now logs a failure to record the send instead of swallowing it — that discarded error is the whole reason this hid for five weeks. **Swept every other table: exactly one was affected, so this is not systemic — but applying a migration as anything other than `postgres` reintroduces it.**
- **⚠ THE NOTIFICATION BELL HAD NO AUDIENCE, AND THE NUMBER IS UNAMBIGUOUS: 52 rows written across 8 days, 0 EVER READ, 0 ever dismissed.** It could not have been otherwise — the bell lives inside a tailnet-only platform most of the company cannot reach, while the same events have been mirrored to Google Chat since 09-22 and Chat is where they actually get read. Removed: `NotificationBell`, both `/api/notifications` routes, the per-page unread count in the shell, the `/api/notifications` allowlist entries in four roles, and the `notifications` table (**52 rows backed up to `~/berwilson-data/backups/notifications-predrop-*.sql.gz` and read back before dropping**; nothing referenced it — no FKs in, no triggers, no views).
- **⚠ AND THE MORE SERIOUS HALF: CHAT MIRRORING WAS OPT-IN PER CALL SITE, SO TWO SOURCES REACHED NOBODY AT ALL.** Only **2 of the 4** `notifyTeam` callers paired their bell write with `broadcastEvents` — so a **dev-note bug report** and a **below-floor quote needing executive approval** wrote an unread bell row and nothing else. Both had been completely silent since they shipped. The fan-out now lives **inside `notifyTeam`**, so no caller can forget it and no future one can either: a second channel a caller may forget is a channel that will be forgotten. `devNoteRecipients()` and `notificationRecipients()` are deleted — a Chat space has one audience, so per-person recipient resolution and actor exclusion no longer mean anything.
- **⚠ VERIFIED THE SINGLE CHANNEL WORKS *BEFORE* DEPLOYING, because making Chat the only channel means a broken Chat is total silence.** A real event announced through `notifyTeam` to the live space returned `announced: 1`.
- **Three dashboard panels deleted, each on measurement rather than taste** — the right rail goes from **five stacked panels to two**. **`ClosingSoon` rendered unconditionally while 0 of 15 projects have EVER carried a `bid_due_date`**, so it was permanently empty dead space at the top of the morning read. **`VerticalRollup`** was a four-row breakdown of fourteen projects for two executives who know the portfolio by heart. **`RiskOverview`** was a synthetic 0-100 score — the same argument that retired the synthetic health score from `HealthPanel` on 07-03. All three were dashboard-only (no other consumer), so the components are deleted rather than hidden.
- **⚠ RICHARD EXISTED TWICE, AND IT SPLIT HIS OWN NOTIFICATIONS DOWN THE MIDDLE.** Two auth logins (`info@` signed in 09-24, `moose@` on 09-23) mapped to two `team_members` rows — "Richard" (moose@) and "Info" (info@, no contact link). Measured blast radius: notifications split **12 / 21** so his unread count depended on which account he used; all 14 tasks sat on the "Richard" row, so signing in as info@ showed him **none of his own work**; and the per-person weekly report generated a page for what is actually a **mailbox** — the one the platform itself sweeps, labels and archives. **Richard's call: info@ becomes "Pepper Potts", the seat a real executive assistant will use when hired** — so the two identities are separated rather than merged, and the roster now reads Richard / Eric / Pepper Potts. `active` and the admin role were deliberately **left alone**: deactivating a login he had used that same day risks locking him out for cosmetic gain, and `/settings/users` parks the seat in one toggle when he wants it (an inactive member still signs in but resolves to `member`).
- **Measured and deliberately NOT changed, because the evidence says the queue is not a UI problem any more:** `/decide` holds **196** items (79 staged deals + 79 leads + 38 review rows) and that number sits on every page. Conversion over three months is **0 of 1,268 leads ever promoted or forwarded** and **5 intake sessions confirmed, ever**. But 09-23 already made every row one-click, so the cause is elsewhere: one counter merges a **live feed** (41 bid invitations arrived in the last 14 days, ~20/week), a **slow queue** (12 staged deals with fresh mail, ~5/week) and a **tail** of ~143 items whose mail is 15-180 days old. A feed is skimmed and a queue is cleared; merging them guarantees a permanent number. And the conversion action is disproportionate: the 79 open leads are genuinely good Utah GC solicitations (Stout, Kier, XCEL, U of U Arapeen, Camp Williams, UDOT, Walmart Depot — the filter works, 892 correctly binned as marketing), but **73 of 79 carry no bid date** and `promoteLead` creates a full `projects` row at stage `pursuit` that then lands in pipeline value, the map's unplaced list, the weekly report and `list_projects`. `promote.ts`'s own docstring says letting every ITB become a project is what put $50B of notional pipeline on the dashboard. **Richard chose not to build this yet; recorded here because the shape of the fix is "give a bid invitation a proportionate action" — `quoting` / `passed` on the lead, no record created — not "make the queue easier".**
- **⚠ AND AN AGE-OUT ON STAGED SESSIONS IS STILL THE WRONG TOOL — re-checked rather than assumed.** The 09-22 argument recorded in `predecide.ts` holds: a bid invitation is perishable, a staged acquisition is not, and the old-mail sessions include Anniston Army Depot Microgrid, USACE IDIQs and Golden Dome. Measuring *mail* age rather than *session* age changes the numbers (26 of 79 sessions sit on mail over 60 days old) but not the conclusion.
- **Also measured, not acted on:** the local model is **1.7% busy** (57.3 GPU hours over 143 days), and **78% of all 4,651 AI calls are the mail pipeline** (thread summary 1,166, lead triage 1,309, fit assessment 790, doc summary 387) while the human-facing surfaces are barely touched — **Ber AI has taken 38 questions in three months**, record briefs 9, meeting intake 9, card scanner 12, weekly brief 3. Fit assessment alone is ~11 GPU hours computing a score with ±20pt sampling noise (measured 08-26) and a **0% action rate**. Dormant modules: **investors last touched 07-15** with `investments` still at 0 (deliberately spared — `raises` holds the hand-entered $88M tranche plan, per the 09-22 rule to check what a table CONTAINS), org chart 07-28, meetings 2 rows last 08-12. Small dead weight found and left for a follow-up: **`portfolio_briefs` (0 rows, 0 code references — superseded by `stored_briefs`, which holds 61 portfolio briefs)**, two `_score_snapshot_*` debris tables (56 rows, 0 references), the Ber AI thumbs control (`api/eval/rate` still writes, its reader was deleted 09-22, **0 of 4,651 calls rated**), and `risk_scores` inserting ~12 rows/day forever with only the latest ever read (947 rows / 14 projects / 80 days).
- **Verified:** `tsc` + `next build` clean; eslint **at its documented 20-problem baseline (14 errors / 6 warnings), unchanged** — both survivors in touched files confirmed pre-existing by stashing. Deployed twice, tailnet serve asserted both times. Authenticated render check on the **deployed** build with a real minted session: `/dashboard` 200 with all three panels confirmed absent and Commitments + Needs Attention still present, `/tasks` `/dev-notes` `/settings/health` 200, **no bell markup on any of them**; `/api/notifications` and `/api/tasks` 401 unauthed, pages 307. **0 residue** — auth users still 3 (no stray created by `generateLink`), `dev_notes` still 0, the probe rows deleted.
- **⚠ Richard's manual step: sign in as `moose@berwilson.com` from now on.** `info@` is Pepper Potts' seat — logging in there will greet you as her and show you her (empty) task list. Both are working admin logins today; nothing was deactivated.
- **⚠ HOUSEKEEPING — a concurrent Claude session split `CLAUDE.md` into `docs/BUILD-LOG.md` during this session** (commit `65ace22`). No conflict: this session staged its 16 files **by name**, never with `-A`, per the standing rule.
