**Done 2026-09-23 (a daily email digest to Google Chat, and a commitment ledger to remind from; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's ask: read all our email each day, TL;DR at the top then key updates in priority order, posted to a Google Chat group he and Eric are in — plus "would you include key changes in BI itself?" and reminders of events and deadlines. He wants a virtual executive assistant.** His picks (AskUserQuestion): deal mail **plus** new scored bid leads; **one heartbeat room** (daily digest, weekly brief and lead alerts all to the new space); **digest stored in BI plus a commitment ledger**; **6:30am weekdays** (built at 7:00am — see the plist, the offset is deliberate).
- **⚠ MOST OF IT WAS ALREADY BUILT, AND MEASURING SAID SO BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN.** Chat is wired (`notify()` + `GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL`, with `_<KEY>` fallback), every email is already read/triaged/summarized hourly, and the weekly brief already posts TL;DR-first. So the digest reads CONCLUSIONS, not mail: **one model call per day, not one per email.** Live volume is ~50-90 threads/day of which only **3-13 are substantive** (deal or operational) — the rest is marketing the filters already discard.
- **⚠ BUT THE REMINDER HALF HAD ALMOST NOTHING TO REMIND FROM, and that reframed the whole build.** Counted before designing: **0 milestones with a future date, 0 projects with a bid due date, 9 open tasks carrying one (1 overdue)**, 6 leads with a bid date. A reminder engine on that data would have been silent — which is worse than absent, because it teaches you the platform has nothing to say. **The deadlines are real; they live in correspondence**, which the sweep has been extracting as `open_items` all along ("Mike Ostermiller to sign NDA", "Attend Friday 1:00 PM EST meeting") with **nothing ever reading them**. Hence the ledger.
- **New `commitments` table + `email_threads.commitments_at`** (migration `20260923000006`, **APPLIED**). Each row is an obligation read out of mail with the three things `open_items` lacked: **which side owes it** (us vs them — "we owe them pricing" and "they owe us the NDA" demand opposite actions, and a flat list cannot tell them apart), **a real date** resolved against the conversation's own date, and **whether it is still open**. `commitments_at` is cleared wherever `routed_at`/`embedded_at` are, so a thread that gains a reply is RE-READ — the newest message is exactly where an obligation gets discharged.
- **⚠ DELIBERATELY NOT ROWS IN `tasks`**, same argument the dev-notes build made hours earlier: `tasks` is the company's WORK board and feeds the weekly report, the daily brief, `/decide` and the per-person workload chips. A commitment is a MACHINE READING of an email, not agreed work; putting it there would distort every one of those surfaces and breach §11. **§11 is untouched — nothing here creates a record.** Promoting a commitment to a real task stays a human action.
- **⚠ MOST THREADS NEVER REACH THE MODEL, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT AFFORDABLE.** A thread whose summary lists no open items is stamped and skipped with **no AI call** — the summary pass already read that whole conversation and found nothing outstanding, and paying 30-50s for a second model to disagree with the first is a bad trade at portfolio scale. Measured live: **6-8 of every 12 threads skipped**, and the model reads a 12k-char TAIL rather than the 40k-char body, so a call costs well under half a summary.
- **⚠ THE EXTRACTION REFUSES MORE THAN IT EXTRACTS, verified on real threads.** Both GridEdge threads (whose only open item was *"Next steps following MNDA execution are pending"*) and both e-signature notifications produced **zero** commitments — vague and automated, exactly as the prompt demands. What it did produce was correct, including the date resolution: *"Attend the 1:00 PM EST meeting on Friday, September 25"* → `2026-09-25`, **confirmed to actually be a Friday**. A synthetic `us`-side case resolved *"by next Wednesday"* sent on Wednesday the 23rd → the 30th, **and left the second commitment's date NULL because none was stated** — the never-invent-a-date rule holding while the other item in the same message did have one.
- **⚠ A REWORDED COMMITMENT RESOLVED ITSELF AND CAME BACK AS A NEW ROW — found by re-reading ONE thread twice, and the original design was wrong about how rare it is.** Identity was an exact normalized-text key, and the first real re-extraction produced `"oct 1"` for `"october 1"` and dropped the word `"delegation"`, so **2 of 2** commitments auto-resolved and reappeared with **their outstanding age reset to zero** — the single signal a follow-up list exists to carry. The original comment called this "a small annoyance"; measurement says it is the common case. Reconciliation now falls back to an **overlap coefficient** match among the handful of rows on that same thread — the same measure and the same reasoning the thread router uses (Jaccard punishes the longer phrasing for being longer). **9 unit cases: both real drift pairs score 1.00, three genuinely different obligations score 0.00** — the 0.6 threshold sits in a wide gap, not on a knife edge.
- **⚠ AND MY FIRST TEST OF THE HUMAN-VERDICT RULE WAS INVALID, which is how the drift got found at all.** `maxThreads: 1` picks the newest pending thread, not the one un-stamped, so the run read a different thread entirely and the verdicts survived only because nothing touched them. Re-run properly by parking every other pending thread behind a findable sentinel timestamp: **`done` and `dismissed` both survived a genuine re-read of that exact thread with their settlement stamps intact, `autoResolved: 0`**, and the one new row scored 0.33 against the nearest existing one — correctly distinct. Sentinel fully reverted (2381 threads restored, 0 left).
- **The digest** (`/api/cron/daily-digest`, `src/lib/digest/`): assembles substantive threads, newly scored leads, open commitments, bids closing, tasks due, today's meetings and the Decide count, renders them into one block where **absence is stated explicitly** ("no date agreed") so the model repeats it instead of quietly omitting a date, then composes TL;DR-first. Stored BEFORE delivery, so a Chat outage costs the post and never the digest. **One per day** — a retry or a double-fire refuses with the existing brief_id, verified live.
- **⚠ `stored_briefs.brief_type` CARRIES A CHECK CONSTRAINT** and a new value fails at INSERT, not at compile time — the exact 09-19 failure where `opportunity_id` typechecked, deployed, and then every insert failed while the route logged it and returned the brief anyway. Widened in the migration and **proven in a rolled-back transaction**: `daily_digest` accepted, the four old types still accepted, a bogus one still refused.
- **⚠ THE DIGEST IS WEEKDAYS AT 7:00am, NOT 6:30.** Two reasons, both structural: the 4:30am lead sweep and the hourly email sweep have both run by then so it reads mail already summarized and commitment-extracted; and Monday's weekly brief fires at 6:30 while **LM Studio serves one request at a time**, so overlapping them would queue the digest behind a ~90s brief and burn its own curl budget waiting. No weekend entries — a Saturday digest over 16-28 threads of near-zero deal content is how a channel teaches people to skip Monday's; Monday reaches back across the weekend instead.
- **Dashboard gains a Commitments panel** (we owe / waiting on, one-click settle with revert-and-toast, 44px hit area via an `-inset-3` overlay so completing on a phone does not shift the rows below). Settling stamps who and when; **reopening clears both**. `PATCH /api/commitments/[id]` is admin-only by default-deny and carries its own guard anyway, since `matchesPrefix` is not method-aware. Verified live: 400 on a bad status naming the allowed values, **404 on an unknown id rather than a 200 that did nothing**, done→settled_by stamped from the SESSION, reopen→both cleared.
- **Two health cards, because both failures are silent by construction.** Daily Digest Cron (4-day threshold, not 36h — the digest is weekdays only, so a 36h bar would report a false failure every weekend and train the reader to ignore a red card). Commitment Extraction reports open count and backlog, and its detail **names both causes of a large number** — a first run after deployment legitimately has every summarized thread to read — and says to check whether the number is FALLING between sweeps.
- **Verified against the deployed build, not a dev process:** 401 unauthed on the cron and on a bad secret, 401 on the commitments PATCH, 307 on the pages; a real digest generated through the route (107s), stored with model/latency/metadata, **delivered to Chat**, and the second run correctly refusing; both new health cards rendering authenticated; the Commitments panel rendering on the dashboard. **And the phase proven to run in the serving process** — `ranPhases` includes `commitments` and a live run reported **`updated: 2, created: 0`**, which is the fuzzy-match fix working in production (before it, that same run would have read `created: 2, autoResolved: 2`). `tsc` + `next build` clean; eslint **back to its documented 20 (14 errors / 6 warnings)** after removing an unused import I had added. **All test data removed — 0 residue** across commitments, sentinel stamps and settled_by.
- **⚠ HOUSEKEEPING — THIRD RECORDED OCCURRENCE: a concurrent Claude session ran `git add -A` at 17:58 and swept this session's in-flight `middleware.ts` edit into its own commit** (`5a72d5b`, "feat: the new Ber Wilson logo…"). Nothing was lost and the tree is correct, but that message does not describe the allowlist line. History deliberately NOT rewritten — the other session was live in the same folder. **This session then staged its own 17 files BY NAME rather than with `-A`**, which is the practice to follow whenever two sessions share this repo.
- **⚠ Richard's manual steps:** (1) **create the "Ber Wilson Updates" space and replace `GOOGLE_CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL` with its webhook**, then restart — all three senders (weekly brief, daily digest, lead digest) fall back to that variable, so one swap moves everything and nothing else needs touching. (2) The commitment backlog is ~1000 threads on first deployment and drains over a day or two through the hourly sweep; the health card is amber until it does, and the test is whether the number FALLS. (3) Unchanged from this morning: 27 opportunity documents still unindexed, `GOOGLE_DEAL_INTAKE_FOLDER_ID` still unset, 4 staged sessions still need a name typed.
- **Deliberately NOT built:** auto-creating tasks from commitments (§11, and it would put model output on the work board); a commitments page of its own (the dashboard panel plus the digest is the whole surface — a 19th nav destination for something read in context is the clutter this platform keeps removing); per-record commitment sections on project/opportunity pages (the rows already carry scope and link back, so this is a loader away if it is ever wanted); and a second daily send in the afternoon (his pick was one morning message).

**Done 2026-09-23 (new logo everywhere — app chrome, home screen, favicon, PWA; DEPLOYED, no migration):**
- **Richard's ask: update the logo on everything, including the icon he sees when he saves the app to his iPhone home screen — "I would like it to display this awesome black logo."** He supplied the 1024x1024 black-field lockup (cream wordmark + coral/gold/teal chevron, "BUILDING FUTURES").
- **Every asset is GENERATED from one checked-in source by `scripts/build-logo-assets.py`** (Pillow; `assets/ber-wilson-logo-source.png`), so the set is rebuildable rather than hand-cut. The supplied artwork is already a square icon, which is exactly what a home-screen icon wants — so `apple-touch-icon`/192/512 use its composition verbatim. **iOS takes the home-screen icon from `apple-touch-icon`, never from the manifest**, so that link is the one that actually does what he asked.
- **⚠ THE BLACK TILE CANNOT BE USED IN THE APP CHROME, so the lockup is keyed off its field.** A hard black rectangle reads as a box on the navy sidebar and a slab on a white print letterhead. **Keying is done against the brand PALETTE, not by unpremultiplying luminance**: every brand colour's max channel is well below 255 (cream 238, coral 203, gold 197, teal 155), so the obvious `alpha = max(r,g,b)/255` leaves solid fills 15-25% see-through. Matching each pixel to its nearest brand colour and taking alpha from the luminance ratio restores clean, fully-opaque shapes with correct antialiasing.
- **⚠ THE LIGHT-SURFACE LOCKUP IS NOT THE DARK ONE RECOLOURED — the company already had one, and it differs.** `assets/steel-quote-template.docx` (`word/media/image1.png`) carries the light-background lockup used on quotes a customer signs, and the brand renders the chevron's **third stroke black on light and teal on dark**. Recolouring the cream to ink would have put a second, subtly different logo on every app print letterhead sitting next to those quotes. That asset is now checked in as `assets/ber-wilson-logo-light-source.png` and is the light variant.
- **⚠ THE FAVICON IS THE CHEVRON ALONE, found by rendering it rather than assuming.** At 16px the full lockup's wordmark collapses into two grey smears — legible as "something is there", not as Ber Wilson. The chevron survives 16px cleanly. Every larger icon keeps the full lockup.
- **⚠ `/site.webmanifest` HAD BEEN 307'ing TO `/login` SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN.** The middleware matcher exempts `svg|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp` and `favicon.ico` but not `.webmanifest` — and **a browser fetches a manifest WITHOUT credentials** unless the link says otherwise, so the install name, icons and standalone display have never once been read. Exempted (it carries no data a login protects: app name, description, icon paths). Verified 200 `application/manifest+json` unauthenticated, with pages still 307 and APIs still 401.
- **⚠ THE COLLAPSED SIDEBAR OVERFLOWED BY 21px, measured not eyeballed.** The rail is 56px with 32px inside its padding; the chevron at `h-6` is 46.5px wide and sat beside a 27px button. Measured in a faithful CSS replica of the rail before touching the component. **The chevron now IS the expand control** rather than sitting next to one — which is also the better read, since a chevron logo beside a chevron-right icon is two chevrons arguing in one 56px row. At `h-4` it is 31px in a 32px slot. (The old code hid this: it declared `width={28} height={28}` on a 1.84:1 image, so `object-contain` letterboxed it into a 24px square.)
- **Also**: a **maskable** 512 icon (the lockup inset to 58% so it survives Android's circular adaptive-icon crop, which takes roughly the middle 72%); `background_color` → `#0a0a0a` so the PWA splash matches the icon (`theme_color` left navy — it tints browser chrome and still matches the sidebar); icons declared with true intrinsic dimensions, because `w-auto` derives width from the declared aspect ratio and the old `120x65` was a 1% squash.
- **⚠ `favicon.ico` MUST BE SAVED FROM AN RGBA IMAGE.** Pillow stores the 256px entry as an embedded PNG and Next's image decoder rejects a PNG-in-ICO with no alpha — `next build` fails outright with "The PNG is not in RGBA format", not at runtime.
- **Verified on the deployed build over the tailnet, not just typechecked:** all nine assets 200 with the right content types; the head tags emitting manifest + favicon + both PNG icons + apple-touch-icon; the manifest readable unauthenticated while `/dashboard` 307s and `/api/tasks` 401s; five authenticated pages rendering with the correct variant each (**print pages carry only `logo-light`, confirming the chromeless layout is intact**); both themes exercised on the login card; and the sidebar's collapse→expand round-trip clicked in the live app. `tsc` + `next build` clean; eslint **at its documented 20-problem baseline, unchanged**.
- **⚠ Richard's manual step: iOS caches home-screen icons hard.** The existing shortcut will keep the old icon — remove it from the home screen and re-add it from Safari (Share → Add to Home Screen) to pick up the black logo.
- **⚠ HOUSEKEEPING: a concurrent Claude session was editing this repo throughout** (a commitments / daily-digest feature, its migration already applied). Only the logo files were staged — `git add -A` would have absorbed their in-flight work, as it has twice before. Richard chose to deploy anyway, so **the running build contains that session's work as of 17:58**; the logo commit itself (`5a72d5b`) is clean.

**Done 2026-09-23 (debug pass — a comma broke six searches, a tool throw killed the agent turn, and the offsite backup had been failing for a week; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's ask: go through and debug the whole system.** The build gauntlet was already clean (tsc 0, eslint at its documented 20, `next build` clean, no Finder duplicates) and **all 93 authenticated routes render 200 with no error markers**, so everything below came from exercising the deployed platform against live data — the tool layer, the cron logs, the backup logs, the DB — rather than from reading it.
- **⚠ A COMMA IN A SEARCH TERM SILENTLY RETURNED NOTHING, IN SIX PLACES INCLUDING THE ⌘K BOX.** PostgREST `.or()` takes a **logic tree**, not a list of values: it parses the string and reads `,` as the separator between conditions. So `steel, framing` becomes two malformed conditions and the whole query dies with `failed to parse logic tree` — and **every caller swallowed that into "no results"** (`data ?? []`). Affected: `search_updates`, `search_parties`, `search_meetings`, `search_tasks`, the recipient lookup in draft generation, and the **steel branch of `/api/search`**, so typing a comma in ⌘K dropped that whole result type with a 200 and no sign anything went wrong.
  - **This had already been fixed one site at a time twice** — `search_email_threads` on 2026-08-28, the thread-link scan before it — each time locally, each time leaving the rest. It now lives in **one helper, `src/lib/utils/postgrest.ts`**, which does both things that are needed: **quotes the value** so a comma inside it is a comma, and **strips what a quoted value still cannot carry** (`( ) " ' \` and `,`), because PostgREST offers no escaping to fall back on. **Rule: any `.or()` whose value comes from user or model input is built through `orIlike`/`orIlikeAnyWord`.**
  - **Verified end to end on the deployed build**: `Mira, Vista` now returns the steel deal it always should have; a full Ber AI turn asking for `"steel, framing"` called `search_updates` and came back with **10 real updates in 37s, zero tool errors**, where before it would have been told "no results" and said so confidently.
- **⚠ TWO AGENT TOOLS THREW INSTEAD OF ANSWERING, AND THE THROW KILLED THE WHOLE TURN.** `query_project_data` dereferenced `args.fields` and `search_updates` dereferenced `args.query` with no guard, so the model omitting or nulling a required parameter raised a `TypeError` — and **`runAgent` explicitly falls back to `{}` when tool-call JSON is malformed** (its own comment says "run the tool with none"), so this is a routine path, not an exotic one. Neither of the two `executeToolCall` sites was wrapped, so the user saw **the assistant fail rather than a tool fail**, which is both worse and much harder to diagnose.
  - Fixed at both levels, deliberately: the two tools now return `{ error }` like the other forty, **and `runTool` guards both call sites** so no tool added later can do it either. A model can recover from an error result; it cannot recover from a dead turn. **Verified: 99 argument-fuzz variants across all 42 tools — empty args, null-valued required args, each required arg omitted in turn — 0 throws** (was 6).
- **⚠ THE OFFSITE BACKUP HAD FAILED 6 OF THE LAST 8 NIGHTS AND THE HEALTH PAGE SAID "BACKUPS RUNNING" THROUGHOUT.** `probeBackups` only ever stat'd the **local** artifacts, which were written perfectly every night — so the half that protects against losing the Studio was invisible. Confirmed independently from the mini's own directory listing: copies for Sep 11-15 and Sep 22, **nothing for Sep 16-21**.
  - **⚠ THE CAUSE WAS THE TAILNET MOVE, NOT A SLEEPING MINI — checked rather than assumed.** The failures start **exactly on 2026-09-16**, the day the tailnet moved to the berwilson.com Workspace org and every node was renumbered; the script still held `100.74.2.126` and timed out. It was then switched to the MagicDNS short name, which **does not resolve under launchd** (`Could not resolve hostname richards-mac-mini`, five times in the error log). The mini reports `sleep 0` and **7 days uptime** across the whole window, so the obvious "it was asleep at 2:30am" explanation is wrong and is recorded as wrong in the script.
  - Fixed by resolving through **`tailscale ip -4`** — no resolver involved, and it reads the *current* address rather than a hardcoded one, which is what the original comment was rightly insisting on.
  - **⚠ AND THAT FIRST FIX BROKE IT A DIFFERENT WAY, CAUGHT BY RUNNING IT RATHER THAN READING IT.** Dialling the literal IP gave `Host key verification failed` — `known_hosts` holds **4 entries for the hostname and none for any address**, exactly as the script's own comment warned, and `BatchMode=yes` cannot prompt. **`-o HostKeyAlias=richards-mac-mini -o CheckHostIP=no`** keeps both properties: connect by address, verify the key by name. Proven with the exact invocation before re-running the real backup.
  - **Offsite now has its own health card**, fed by a marker the script writes, because it fails independently of the local backup and is the half that matters if the Studio is lost — the 2026-08-25 loss of `~/berwilson-data` showed that is not hypothetical. Retries added too (6 × 5 min), documented as **belt-and-braces for a dropped link, not the fix**: the push is ~1GB at a measured **~17 MB/min over the tailnet**, so it is in flight for the better part of an hour.
  - **Proven end to end on the real thing, not simulated:** the full backup re-run pushed **db + storage + secrets to the mini on attempt 1**, wrote the marker (`{"ok":true,...,"secrets":true}`), and cleaned up its local encrypted copies (0 left). All four card states then exercised — ok / failing / 4-day stale / corrupt marker — and the real marker restored afterwards. **The failure message deliberately does NOT blame the mini being asleep** (the first guess, which measuring killed); it names the two causes that actually occurred and the log line that distinguishes them.
  - **⚠ WORTH KNOWING, cost an hour of confusion: DO NOT EDIT A SHELL SCRIPT WHILE IT IS RUNNING.** Correcting a comment in `backup.sh` mid-run shifted the byte offsets zsh reads from, and the still-executing copy resumed at a garbage position and died with `backup.sh:140: unmatched "` — on a **133-line file**. Everything material had already completed, and both copies are byte-identical and `zsh -n` clean, but the error looks exactly like a syntax bug that is not there.
  - **`backup.sh` was not version-controlled anywhere.** The disaster-recovery script was a single unbacked-up file on the one machine it protects. Committed as `deploy/backup.sh` with a header saying the live copy is `~/supabase-selfhost/backup.sh` and that the two are synced by hand.
- **⚠ THE LEAD SWEEP REPORTED FAILURE ON EVERY SINGLE RUN WHILE COMPLETING ITS WORK.** `launchctl list` showed exit **28** (curl timeout) — but 8 leads were created and 25 updated that morning, because Next does not abort a handler on client disconnect. `budgetMs` governed only the model-bound phases while **label, tasks, notify, sheets and hygiene ran after it** and added their own time (hygiene alone carried a flat 10 minutes), so a 50-minute budget produced 60-minute runs past the client's 3500s. Same shape as the weekly-brief cron fixed on 09-22. `RUN_BUDGET_MS` now bounds the **whole** run and hygiene draws from what is left rather than adding to it.
- **⚠ AND IT WAS EATING THE WEEKLY BRIEF.** LM Studio serves one request at a time (`parallel 1`), and at 5:30am the sweep was still issuing `lead-triage` calls at **06:02-06:22 on Monday 2026-09-21** — one of them taking **529s against a 90s norm** — when the brief cron started at 6:30. The brief timed out at 6:38 and **no brief was written that week**; the only portfolio brief for Sep 21 was hand-generated at 16:10. Sweep moved to **4:30am**, which with the 45-minute ceiling leaves a clear hour. (The brief's own `-m`/`maxDuration` fix from 09-22 is in place but **has never been exercised** — next Monday is its first real run.)
- **⚠ `dd_items.status` WAS NULLABLE AND FIVE SURFACES FILTERED IT WITH `.neq()`.** PostgREST renders that as SQL `<>`, which is NULL — and therefore not true — for a NULL status, so a **critical or blocker diligence item with no status set would be invisible to the dashboard badge, `/api/attention`, the weekly brief, risk scoring and meeting prep simultaneously**. Latent only because the table is currently empty. Migration `20260923000003` makes it NOT NULL, matching the `default 'open'` the column already carried and what every writer already does; the schema now enforces what every reader already assumes.
- **A real user action failed today and was reported as a server fault.** `Add dd_item failed: invalid input value for enum dd_severity: "high"` — the vocabulary is info/watch/critical/blocker, `severity` is a Postgres enum, and the route passed it straight through, so a client mistake came back as a **500 carrying the raw Postgres text**. Validated at the edge now (400 with the allowed values, verified live). **`category` is deliberately left unvalidated** — it is plain `text` by design and deal intake files unknown keys under Other.
- **⚠ THE HEALTH PAGE COULD NOT SEE OPPORTUNITY DOCUMENTS AT ALL.** `probeDocumentIndexing` read the `documents` table alone, so it printed **"Every document is settled"** while 28 `opportunity_documents` — the whole M&A file for the Englert / Gold mine deal — had never been indexed and one had been stranded in `processing` since 09-22. CLAUDE.md has carried that backlog as a manual item for days while the health page actively contradicted it. Now counts both tables, allows one in-flight pass **per table** rather than one overall, and names the opportunity-specific remedy, since an opportunity document has **no nightly retry** to fall back on. It now correctly reads `27 documents never finished indexing`.
- **Swept clean, measured not assumed:** every `.select()` in the tree re-verified column-by-column against the live schema (**0 drift** — all 16 regex hits were adjacent-query false positives); **0 orphans** across every major FK (chunks→documents/projects, thread_chunks, thread_links, tasks→assignee, leads→thread, documents→project); all seven opportunity-parity scope constraints hold with **0 violations**; no `::` casts in any PostgREST filter; every other `.neq()` target confirmed NOT NULL. All 24 major pages render 200 authenticated with no error markers. **Security posture verified live rather than by reading config**: self-signup genuinely refuses (`signup_disabled`, auth users unchanged at 3 — worth testing because the compose maps `DISABLE_SIGNUP`→`GOTRUE_DISABLE_SIGNUP` and only the container knows which it reads), no secrets tracked in git, all Google scopes granted on all 3 mailboxes.
- **Healthy and deliberately left alone:** the email sweep (8-450s per run, `moreWork:false`, all phases at 0 remaining — the 802 "unembedded" threads are **exactly** the 764 noise-classified plus the 38 unsummarized, i.e. the designed exclusions, not a gap); LM Studio at a single copy, 65536/parallel 1, no drift; local backups; all 8 Supabase containers; both tailnet listeners.
- **⚠ WORTH KNOWING: 44 `review_queue` rows carry `resolved_at` with NO `resolution`**, all `inferred_email_match` from 2026-09-18..21 — the 09-22 bulk reclassification stamped the timestamp without recording a verdict. Every surface treats them as resolved (`/decide` and `/review` both filter on `resolved_at`), so nothing is broken and nothing is hidden; only the audit trail is silent about what was decided. **Deliberately NOT rewritten** — guessing a verdict and writing it into 44 audit rows is worse than a gap that is visibly a gap.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean and **eslint at its documented 20-problem baseline, unchanged** (14 errors / 6 warnings, all pre-existing `set-state-in-effect` / `no-img-element` / `purity`); `next build` clean; 8 unit checks on the filter helper; 99-variant tool fuzz; a real agent turn on the deployed build; the ⌘K comma case, the dd-items 400/200 pair (**probe row deleted, `dd_items` back to 0**), and the new health cards all exercised over HTTP against the running production build. Deployed twice, tailnet serve asserted both times. **All test data removed — 0 residue.**
- **⚠ Richard's manual steps:** (1) **27 opportunity documents are still unindexed** and now say so on `/settings/health` — `node --experimental-strip-types --import ./deploy/register.mjs --env-file=.env.local scripts/reindex-opportunity-documents.mts` makes the Englert / Gold mine deal searchable. (2) `GOOGLE_DEAL_INTAKE_FOLDER_ID` is still unset, so deal intake is off. (3) One team member has no Google Tasks mailbox configured. (4) `deploy/backup.sh` and `~/supabase-selfhost/backup.sh` are synced by hand — copy across after editing either.

**Done 2026-09-23 (anyone can report a bug from the page it happened on; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's ask: developer notes in the bottom left so users like Eric can report a bug or request a feature; the logged request works like a task that can be checked off; log the activity for auditing.**
- **⚠ THE PEOPLE MOST LIKELY TO HIT A BUG ARE THE ONES WITH THE LEAST ACCESS, so `/dev-notes` and `/api/dev-notes` are allowlisted for EVERY role** — the first feature in `permissions.ts` besides the notification bell to be. A feedback channel gated to admins has no reporters. Everyone READS the whole list (seeing what is already filed is what stops one bug arriving five times); the routes decide what each viewer may CHANGE, and carry their own guards rather than trusting the middleware — `matchesPrefix` is a prefix match and is **not** method-aware, so allowlisting the read also admits every mutation underneath it.
- **⚠ THE BUTTON OPENS A DIALOG INSTEAD OF NAVIGATING, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN.** A bug report is worth roughly what its context is worth, and the reporter is the one person who usually cannot say precisely which screen they were on. `DevNoteDock` reads `usePathname()` **at open time, not at submit** (a reporter who navigates mid-write would otherwise file the page they ended on) plus the user agent, and states on the form exactly what is being attached on their behalf. Sidebar footer on desktop, the More grid on mobile; both dispatch one `open-dev-note` window event, the same seam the quick-upload sheet already uses.
- **⚠ DELIBERATELY NOT A ROW IN `tasks`.** A dev note behaves like a task — owned, worked, checked off — but `tasks` is the company's WORK board: assigned to team members, tagged to projects/opportunities/objectives, and rolled into the weekly report, the daily brief, `/decide` and the per-person workload chips. Platform feedback filed there would appear as portfolio work in every one of those surfaces and quietly distort them. Same behaviour, separate ledger.
- **Checking off is one click on the row, not a status buried in a detail view** — a report that takes four clicks to close stays open. Optimistic with revert-and-toast (a row that silently un-ticks reads as handled when it was not), and the 44px hit area is an `-inset-3` overlay so completing on a phone does not shift every row below it under the next tap, matching the 08-27 mobile pass. Settling stamps who and when; **reopening clears both**, or a reopened report carries a closer who has not looked at it since.
- **Priority is admin-only and the reporter's own attempt is ignored, not rejected.** Everyone's bug is urgent, and a triage field anyone can set stops being a triage field. The reporter's other escalation attempts are refused outright: the POST route stamps `reporter_id`/`reporter_name` from the SESSION and never the body (verified live — a request naming someone else and a foreign `reporter_id` still filed as the sender), and PATCH on someone else's report is a **403**.
- **`resolution` closes the loop.** Without it a settled report simply vanishes from the open list, which reads as ignored rather than fixed. The admin writes what was done and the reporter reads it back on the row.
- **⚠ `log_activity()` IS ATTACHED HERE, unlike objectives / investors / dino / org-structure, whose migrations all say it "dereferences new.project_id, which this table doesn't have".** That was true of the ORIGINAL trigger; the current version (2026-07-04) reads the column through `to_jsonb(new)->>'project_id'`, which yields NULL for a table with no such column. **Verified against the live database in a rolled-back transaction BEFORE attaching** — INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE on a project-less probe table all log cleanly. Worth knowing for the next module: that comment is stale, not a live constraint.
- **⚠ AND THE TRIGGER WOULD HAVE LOGGED THE CHECK-OFF WITHOUT SAYING WHAT MOVED.** `log_activity()` only builds `field_changes` for tables it names explicitly (projects, dd_items, milestones, compliance_items), so ticking a report would have written a bare `UPDATE` — an audit row that records that something happened and refuses to say what. Migration `20260923000005` adds a `dev_notes` branch tracking status/priority/kind. It was generated by **dumping the live `prosrc` and splicing the branch in rather than retyping the function**, then diffed after applying: the only change to every other table is one blank line. Routes write through `actorAdminClient()`, so the log names the person rather than 'system' — **verified live: the INSERT is attributed to the reporter's own email, and the check-off logs `{"status":{"old":"open","new":"done"}}`**.
- **A report nobody is told about sits in a table nobody opens** — the silent-queue failure this platform has hit repeatedly. Filing raises a bell notification, **to ADMINS ONLY** (`devNoteRecipients`): it is addressed to whoever fixes the platform, and fanning one person's UI complaint to everyone is how a bell stops being read. Best-effort throughout — a notification must never fail the report that produced it. The sidebar shows an open count to admins only, for the same reason: a number nobody can act on is decoration on everyone else's screen.
- **Verified against the live deployed app with real minted sessions, not fixtures: 35 checks, all passing.** A throwaway **non-admin** account was created for it, because all three real logins are admins and the non-admin path — the entire point of the feature — would otherwise be untested. Covered: 401/307 unauthenticated; a member filing, checking off, reopening and reading the page over HTTP (with the bottom-left button present in the member's shell); every escalation refused (403 on priority, 403 on another's report, 403 on delete, spoofed reporter ignored); five validation rejections (400/400/400/404/400); notification raised to admins and **not** to the reporter; and the activity rows read back at each step. Pure-function checks confirm all five roles reach both surfaces with no adjacent-prefix leak. **All test data removed — 0 residue** across dev_notes / activity_log / notifications, team_members back to 3 and auth users back to 3. `tsc` + `next build` clean; eslint **at its real measured baseline of 20 problems (14 errors, 6 warnings), unchanged**.
- **⚠ HOUSEKEEPING: a concurrent Claude session ran `git add -A` mid-build and swept this work into its own commit** (`09a8793`, "fix: the offsite failure message…"), with the two migrations landing in `11d714f`. Nothing was lost and the tree is correct, but neither message describes this feature. History was deliberately NOT rewritten — the other session was active in the same folder. **This is the second recorded occurrence; when two sessions share this repo, `git add -A` will absorb the other's in-flight edits.**
- **Deliberately NOT built:** a comment thread on a report (the `resolution` field closes the loop without a second table; add comments if back-and-forth actually proves necessary), screenshot attachment, email or Chat delivery of new reports (the bell is the channel, and the `notify()` seam is there if it is ever wanted), and any AI pass over the reports — there are none yet to triage.

**Done 2026-09-23 (opportunities carry the same child records as projects; DEPLOYED + MIGRATED):**
- **Richard's ask: "Opportunities should have all the same fields as projects (documents, players etc…) so we can add the appropriate information."** An acquisition needs the people on the deal, a diligence checklist, a capital structure, the entities involved and a timeline at least as much as a construction project does — and there was nowhere to put any of it.
- **⚠ FIVE CHILD TABLES WERE HARD-WIRED TO `project_id NOT NULL`, so the only way to record a deal's players or diligence was to INVENT A PROJECT.** `project_players`, `milestones`, `dd_items`, `financing_structures` and `entity_projects` each now take a nullable `opportunity_id` beside `project_id` with a `num_nonnulls(...) = 1` check; `compliance_items` and `research_artifacts` take it as `<= 1`, because a NULL there already means a company-level obligation rather than a missing scope. **The shape is the one `tasks` (06-27) and `documents` (meetings, steel deals) already use — NOT parallel `opportunity_players` / `opportunity_milestones` tables**, which would fork every query, route and component; forking is exactly what cost this codebase the `runDocumentAiPass` drift and nine copies of `formatDate`.
- **⚠ THE UNIQUE CONSTRAINTS STOPPED GUARDING THE MOMENT `project_id` WENT NULL.** `project_players` carries `unique(project_id, party_id, role)` and `entity_projects` `unique(entity_id, project_id, relationship)` — and Postgres treats NULLs as distinct, so the same person could be added to a deal twice in the same role with the constraint sitting right there. Matching **partial** unique indexes on the opportunity side close it (verified live: the second identical player returns **409**, not a duplicate row).
- **⚠ `milestones.stage` WAS A POSTGRES ENUM, AND ONE ENUM CANNOT CARRY TWO PIPELINES.** Widened to plain `text` (`using stage::text`, existing values survive verbatim), following the convention every vocabulary added since opportunities/steel/leads already uses. `MilestonesTab` now takes `stages` / `stageLabels` / `advance` as **props** rather than importing the project vocabulary, so a deal's milestones group under its own 6-stage pipeline and "advance" PATCHes `status` the way a project's PATCHes `stage`. **Checked first that nothing else reads the column** — across the whole `src` tree only that one grouping expression did.
- **⚠ AN ENUM CHANGE MADE `project_id` NULLABLE IN TWO PLACES THAT ASSUMED OTHERWISE, AND `tsc` CAUGHT BOTH.** The timeline is the project Gantt and now skips deal milestones explicitly. The calendar does the opposite and **shows them**: a milestone with a target date is a deadline whoever owns it, so `CalendarEvent` gained an optional `href` and an opportunity milestone links back to `/opportunities/[id]/milestones` instead of a `/projects/` URL that would 404.
- **The opportunity detail page is a tabbed record now, not a nine-section scroll.** `ProjectTabBar` became `RecordTabBar` (base path + tab list as props) and both records share it, so the "show the tabs that have rows, hide the rest under More" rule from 09-22 applies to deals for free — **verified live: a bare opportunity shows Overview/Notes/Documents, and after one row landed in each table the bar grew Players, Milestones, Financing, Diligence and Entities & Vendors, each carrying its count.** The players table was lifted into one `RecordPlayers` rather than copied.
- **⚠ THE BRIEF PRINT VIEW SITS OUTSIDE THE ROUTE GROUP, DELIBERATELY.** `(detail)/layout.tsx` wraps the tabs; `brief/print` is its sibling, so a document carried into a meeting does not come out with a tab bar across the top. (Worth knowing: `projects/[id]/brief/print` **is** wrapped by the project layout and does get the header and tabs — pre-existing, untouched, and the same route-group move would fix it.)
- **The brief and Ber AI can see the new data, or it would be invisible where it matters most.** `assembleOpportunityBrief` reads all five children and reports them through formatters **extracted from the project assembler rather than copied** — verified on real rows: MILESTONES, DUE DILIGENCE, CAPITAL STRUCTURE, COMPLIANCE and PEOPLE ON THIS RECORD all render, and the project brief still renders its own unchanged. `query_opportunity` returns players/milestones/diligence/capital_structure, and its own description says so. Absence is stated too: the gaps block now calls out an untracked deal timeline, an empty diligence checklist and a missing capital structure.
- **⚠ THE EVIDENCE-DOCUMENT PICKER IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT ON A DEAL'S COMPLIANCE ITEMS.** `compliance_items.evidence_doc_id` is a foreign key to `documents`, and an opportunity's files live in `opportunity_documents` — offering them would have produced a 23503 on save. Caught by reading the constraint rather than by running it; the item's notes can name the file until that FK is widened.
- **Every write route now decides scope in one place** (`src/lib/records/scope.ts` `scopeFromBody`, mirroring the database's exactly-one rule at the edge so a bad body is a 400, not a 500) and guards it through one `canAccessRecord`. Four of the five routes had **no viewer check at all**, relying on the middleware allowlist; they carry their own now, per the 09-22 posture that the layer whose job is not to trust the one above should not.
- **Verified against the live database and the deployed app, not fixtures:** every constraint exercised in rolled-back transactions (both-scopes refused, neither refused, duplicate refused, cascade leaving **0 orphans**); all 12 opportunity routes rendering **200 authenticated** with the brief print confirmed chromeless; all 8 project routes re-checked for regression; a full round-trip creating a player, milestone, diligence item, capital structure, entity link and compliance item through the real API, then the deal deleted — **every table back to its exact pre-test count, 0 residue**; project-scoped writes re-run and reverted; 307 unauthenticated on pages and 401 on the API over the tailnet. `tsc` + `next build` clean; eslint **at its real measured baseline of 20 problems (14 errors, 6 warnings), unchanged** — note CLAUDE.md had been claiming 27.
- **Deliberately NOT built:** the project-only scalar fields (solicitation number, contract type, delivery method, bid/award/NTP dates, win strategy, incumbent, competitors) — a deal already has the equivalent of each that means anything to it (probability, thesis, lead, counterparty, target close), and bid-and-build fields on an acquisition would be noise on a form; an investor roll-up on the deal's Financing tab (`investments` target the parent company or a **project**, never an opportunity, so there is nothing to sum); and a `updates`-style feed on opportunities (progress Notes is that feed, and the tab is labelled Notes for exactly that reason).

**Done 2026-09-23 (the queue can now be finished from the queue — 0 of 193 items were actionable in place, now 189; DEPLOYED, no migration):**
- **Richard's ask: a cleaner, simpler UX, and put as much of the time-consuming work as possible on the local model. Measuring inverted the second half of the question.**
- **⚠ THE LOCAL MODEL IS 93% IDLE BECAUSE IT HAS FINISHED, NOT BECAUSE NOTHING WAS ASKED OF IT.** 1,752 calls / 23.2 busy hours across 14 days = **6.9% utilisation**, statistically unchanged since the 6.3% measured on 08-25 despite everything built since. The last several hourly sweeps report `moreWork: false` with **every** model-bound phase at zero — summarize 0, apply 0, embed 0, predecide 0. There is no backlog to chew. **Adding a model phase here would have been manufacturing work**, and this codebase has already removed three such passes after measurement (09-22).
- **⚠ THE PLATFORM PRODUCES DECISIONS AND CONVERTS ALMOST NONE OF THEM, AND THE CAUSE WAS THE UI, NOT THE RECOMMENDATION.** `/decide` held **193 items** (79 leads of which 71 `pursue`, 76 staged sessions of which 69 `create`, 38 flagged matches). Conversion: **5 intake sessions confirmed ever** against 136 decided — and 52 of the 56 dismissals were the model's own auto-dismiss, so a human has settled almost nothing — and **0 leads promoted or forwarded out of 1,268 scored**. `promoteLead()` had shipped on 08-25 and **had never once run in production**.
- **⚠ THE MODEL HAD ALREADY DONE THE WORK AND THE SCREEN MADE YOU DO IT AGAIN.** A representative pending session carries a complete project: name, `pursuit`, `government`, **$625M**, contract type, delivery method, a real description, 4 people with roles and emails, 3 tasks with assignees and due dates, `suggested_record: "project"`, confidence 0.95. Nothing left to type. To agree you had to leave `/decide`, open a 25-input form on another route — **which dropped the `predecision` on the way in**, so the verdict you were shown vanished at the moment you needed it — scroll, and press Create. Average correspondence behind one session is **12,327 characters**, so re-forming the judgement costs ~12 minutes. 193 items at that price is why nothing converted.
- **⚠ `merge` WAS A LABEL WITH NOTHING BEHIND IT.** Pre-decide has returned `disposition: 'merge'` with a `merge_target_name` since it shipped, and `/decide` and `/intake` both rendered it — while there was **no merge control in the review form and no merge branch in the confirm route**. Six sessions sat on a recommendation whose only available action was to dismiss it. The machinery existed and had simply never been called this way: `linkClusterToRecord` ties a session's threads to a record with `linked` certainty and the apply phase then posts the correspondence and imports attachments — confirm has called it since day one, **with the id of a record it had just created**. Handing it an EXISTING id is the merge. New `POST /api/email-ingestion/merge`, ~30 lines over existing code.
- **Resolving the merge target is a string comparison, not a judgement, and deliberately so.** `match_candidates` already carries `project_id` + `project_name` and the model chose from that closed list, so a name it returns either IS a candidate or was invented — and inventing is exactly the case that must not resolve. `resolveMergeTarget` matches the WHOLE name case-insensitively (never a substring), and **refuses when two candidates share one**, the same ambiguity rule the thread router holds. All 6 live merge sessions resolve to real existing projects; 11 unit cases cover the refusals.
- **⚠ REVIEW ROWS ARRIVED UNDECIDABLE, AND THE TEXT THEY NEEDED WAS ALREADY IN THE ROW.** 38 items rendering as "Inferred email match" with no title, no note and no verdict — while `review_queue.ai_explanation` has held a complete sentence naming the record all along (*"Matched to this project by same deal name — Myton Rail. Approve to post it and index it…"*). The page simply never selected it. No model involved; the rows now title from the matched project and carry the explanation.
- **One definition of what a session would create** (`src/lib/email-ingestion/defaults.ts` `buildConfirmBody`). It existed twice in spirit and nowhere in fact — the review form derived it from the extraction in four rules and the only way to act was to render that form. The confirm route's own `ConfirmBody`/`PartyAction`/`TaskAction` types moved here and the route imports them, so the request shape has exactly one declaration. Two copies of a mapping this load-bearing is how the 09-17 `runDocumentAiPass` fork drifted and silently discarded 413,000 characters.
- **⚠ THE READINESS GATE IS DETERMINISTIC BECAUSE MEASURING KILLED THE MODEL VERSION.** A "is this draft complete" pass was designed and dropped: run over all 76 live sessions, **65 of 69 `create` sessions already carry a name for their suggested kind and exactly 4 do not**, and a name is the only thing the form hard-blocks on. Value is absent on 51 of 65 and sector on 7 — both optional at the schema and in the form, so treating either as a blocker would send a human to a form with nothing to do. A model call would have re-decided what a `!= null` answers. **The 4 blocked rows show their reason and offer no Accept**, so there is never an Accept that 400s.
- **Accept from `/decide`, symmetric with the existing dismiss.** intake `create` → the existing confirm route with the draft; intake `merge` → the new merge route; lead → `promoteLead` at the target its route already implies; review → `{resolution:'approved'}`. Accept confirms once and dismiss does not — the asymmetry is the point, since setting aside is reversible and creates nothing while accepting writes a record, contacts, tasks, documents and publishes to Drive. **The draft is FETCHED on click rather than shipped with the page**: a full draft is a couple of kilobytes and most rows are never accepted.
- **⚠ CLAUDE.md §11 IS UNTOUCHED AND THIS IS THE REASON IT STILL HOLDS.** Nothing here creates a record automatically. The click IS the human review the invariant requires; what changed is that it lands where you are standing instead of three pages away. The review screens remain for when you want to edit first, and now show the recommendation that sent you there.
- **The lead promote target comes from the route the triage already chose** (`promoteTargetFor`): construction→project, steel→steel, corporate→opportunity, dino→forward. **`unknown` deliberately maps to null** — a lead the triage could not place is exactly the one a human should place, and a one-click guess between four record types would misfile deals silently. Live: 72 construction, 6 steel, 1 corporate.
- **The weekly brief now says the queue exists.** Richard's own answer to why zero leads converted was that he had not been looking, and nothing ever told him — arrivals are announced once through a latch that correctly never repeats, and the accumulated pile was never mentioned again. `summarizeDecideQueue()` shares `countDecideItems`' filters and the page's `decideWeight` (extracted to `src/lib/decide/rank.ts`, pure, imported by both), so the brief cannot claim a different queue or a different top item from the screen it links to. **Verified agreeing exactly: 193 = 193.**
- **Verified against the live database, live Drive and the deployed app — not fixtures.** 11 unit cases on the merge resolver plus `buildConfirmBody` run over all 76 real sessions with per-session shape assertions (including that no party is set to `link` without an id). Then **full round-trips on real records, each reverted**: an intake accept created a project with **14 players, 5 tasks, an update, a document, 51 chunks and 8 thread_links seeded at their real message counts** (9, 1, 14 — not zero, so history cannot re-post); a merge linked one thread with `linked` certainty at 3 of 3 and **left projects at 15, because merging creates nothing**; a lead promoted with both the firm and the estimator linked as players; a review approve posted and indexed 13 chunks. Every refusal path exercised (409 re-merge, 400 non-merge, 404 unknown, 400 no id, **401 unauthenticated**, 409 draft-on-confirmed). **All four reverted to exact pre-test counts — 0 residue across projects/parties/tasks/updates/documents/chunks/players/thread_links**, both test Drive folders trashed, and the test lead's Gmail label restored to match the other 71. `tsc` + `next build` clean; eslint **at the documented 27 baseline, unchanged**.

It refuses a bare `List-Unsubscribe` link (that is meant for a human and may be a preferences page, where a blind POST can do something else), refuses `http` and `mailto`, and will not follow a redirect off the sender's origin.

And **moose@/tuaone@ already had priority** — they are the only mailboxes that get summarized, clustered and staged. The junk was in the two mailboxes he called cleanest: **743 of 1,054 deal threads (70.5%) were newsletters** — pumpkins, oil-change reminders, Mark Miller Toyota review replies — each costing a 25-50s local-model call to reach that verdict.

Recognition needs the **name AND an internal sender together** — the address alone matches genuine mail between the two executives, the name alone could be spoofed from outside. **Every** message must be platform-sent, so a human replying to a digest reopens the thread. Drafted replies are deliberately NOT stamped (`buildRawMessage.fromName` is opt-in): a draft is written for a human to send under their own name.
- **Gmail-side exclusions now cover the DEAL sweep, not just leads.** `leadExclusions()` → `mailExclusions(pipeline)`; `buildQuery` already accepted them and `fetch-phase` was passing them only for `'lead'`. **Measured over 90 days: 963 → 753 threads, 210 never fetched, stored or read (~2h of local-model time).** Split is lopsided and worth knowing: **moose@ drops 1 of 152; tuaone@ drops 209 of 811** — the marketing is almost all in tuaone@. It also gives the deal mailboxes the same one-gesture escape hatch info@ has: a Gmail filter applying `bw-filtered` retires a repeat sender with no code change.

Both look like chrome; both are real signal. The bar for a new rule is that the class **cannot** carry deal signal, not merely that it usually does not.
- **ONE definition of "live"** (`src/lib/records/live.ts`) replaces four places that had drifted: apply-phase posted correspondence onto any record, Drive filing filed into any record, the publish reconcile published any record, and only `project-folder-sync` filtered at all — in JS, on two of the three dormant statuses. **The JS filter is preserved and its comment now says why: `status=not.in.(closed,lost)` is NULL for a NULL status and PostgREST drops it**, and one project has no status set. A **dormant link is KEPT and `applied_message_count` is NOT advanced**, so reviving a record replays what it missed (mail arriving while a pursuit is parked is usually why it gets un-parked) — but `last_applied_at` IS stamped, or a dormant link would sort to the front of every batch forever and starve the live records behind it. Explicit human "Publish to Drive" bypasses the gate (`includeDormant`); the automatic passes do not.
- **⚠ THE APPLY BATCH COULD NEVER REACH MOST OF ITS OWN BACKLOG — found by running it, not by reading it.** A caught-up link was skipped inside the loop **without its `last_applied_at` moving**, so it kept its place at the front of the order forever; the same 100 links were re-read every run and everything behind them was unreachable. That is also why attachment-bearing threads never imported their files. The delta is a **cross-table comparison PostgREST cannot express**, so the batch is now chosen in two steps: a light paged scan in the batch's own order — **deliberately without `raw_markdown`**, which is every conversation's full body — then the full embed for the chosen ids. `pendingFound` reports the real backlog rather than the slice. **Drained live: 44 → 0, 5 attachments imported and indexed, 0 documents left pending or errored.**

- **Richard's question: anything else to simplify and streamline.** Measured the live database rather than reading the build log, and the answer was not a code-size answer.
- **⚠ THE PLATFORM GENERATES DECISIONS FASTER THAN ANYONE MAKES THEM, AND NOTHING CONVERTS.** Of **1,216 leads ever scored, ZERO have ever been promoted** to a project, opportunity or steel deal; **97 pursue/consider leads expired unreviewed**; intake stands at 5 confirmed against 73 pending; the Decide queue held **282 items**. The leads are *good* — Hill AFB B509, U of U Arapeen, a UDOT PEMB routed to steel, fit 72-85 — so this is a drain problem, not a filter problem.
- **⚠ AND THE DRAIN COULD NOT REACH MOST OF THE QUEUE: `expireStaleLeads()` filtered `.not('bid_due_date','is',null)`**, so a lead with NO bid date could never satisfy it — and **69 of the 73 open pursue leads carried no bid date**. Its own comment claimed it "drains the queue"; for the overwhelming majority the rule never fired. Measured further: only 24 of those 69 threads even mention a deadline, because a bid invitation keeps its dates behind a plan-room login. They are structurally undatable, so an age-out is the ONLY thing that can ever close them. `drainLeadQueue()` keeps the dated rule and adds three: undated leads age out at 30 days, `pass` leads close as `ignored`, and a job posted twice collapses. **Live: 99 open → 76, idempotent on re-run, 0 promoted/forwarded touched, all 23 changes re-labelled in Gmail.**

- **⚠ THE DEDUPE ESTIMATE IN THE PLAN WAS WRONG AND MEASURING KILLED IT.** Titles that *look* duplicated ("Ground-Up Development" vs "Construction", "RFI Responses" vs "RFI Clarifications") are not, and a fuzzy matcher would sometimes merge two genuinely different bid packages. Exact normalised title within one route collapses **3 groups, 4 rows** — small, and deliberately so: a surviving duplicate is one click to dismiss, a silently closed distinct bid is lost. Sky Mountain Golf appears under **six** normalised keys because six different GCs invited us; not merging those is correct.
- **⚠ AN ALIAS MATCH IS NOW `linked`, NOT `inferred` — the single biggest cut to the review queue.** Setting "Also known as" is a person stating in advance that mail calling the deal that name belongs there: a filing decision expressed as a rule. Staging it for review asks the same question twice, which is the argument `/api/thread-links` already makes for hand-filed links. **All 75 unresolved review rows were this one reason, unread since 2026-09-09**, and 73 of 106 inferred links were aliases. Solicitation-number matches likewise (an identifier, not a similarity). Guards unchanged and re-verified by unit test: the **whole** alias must appear, and `AMBIGUITY_MARGIN` still refuses when two records share one. **Review queue 75 → 31**, and what remains is genuine name-similarity worth a human. **Decide 282 → 181.**

Measured on a real question ("Sandpoint cottage permit set and lateral takeoff for 15 homes") the top three hits were **a URL tracking token at 0.740, a signature block at 0.697 and a message header at 0.673**, with the answer nowhere in the top eight. 197 chunks removed; the same query now returns the actual cottage permit drawing, and the mail still leads `search_correspondence` at 0.706. **Nothing lost, both halves better.**
- **⚠ NINE `formatDate` COPIES, EIGHT WITHOUT THE TIMEZONE FIX THAT EXISTS BECAUSE IT WAS A BUG.** Two of the eight formatted DATE columns — `tasks.due_date` through `dueLabel`, and `objectives.target_date` on the steering board — so **a task due the 1st rendered as the 30th** west of UTC. One implementation now, with `empty`/`year` options that exist only to preserve what each screen already displayed. `formatBytes` had six copies and three behaviours, so 800 bytes read "800 B" on one screen and "1 KB" on another. `ConversationList`'s copy is renamed `formatRelative` — it returns "Yesterday", so it was never the same function.
- **⚠ TWO NOTES TABLES TOOK THE AUTHOR'S NAME FROM THE REQUEST BODY** and shipped a "Your name (optional)" box to fill it, so a note could be posted under anyone's name. The other four stamp it server-side with a comment saying why. Fixed.
- **⚠ THE OPPORTUNITY UPLOAD ROUTE WAS THE LAST FORK OF THE DOCUMENT AI PASS**, against an explicit rule in `document-pipeline.ts` ("never fork this pass per table; add a target"). It summarized before storing the extracted text inside a bare `catch {}` — the 2026-09-09 failure that cost 413,000 characters. **Rewiring it surfaced a live bug: `runDocumentAiPass` RETURNED 'complete' without ever writing it.** `embedDocument` sets `embedding_status` as a side effect; `embedOpportunityDocument` does not, and the column only reached that table on 2026-09-21 — so **no opportunity document had ever been marked complete** (34 pending / 3 processing / 0 complete), which the health card reads as passes dying. Status is now settled by the function rather than by whichever embedder it called; 10 rows that had finished but were never marked are corrected. **27 genuinely unindexed opportunity documents remain and are now visible as such.**
- **⚠ 56 API GUARDS PASSED WHEN THERE WAS NO VIEWER AT ALL.** `getViewer()` returns null for an unauthenticated request, so `viewer && !viewer.isAdmin` was false exactly when nobody was there. Nothing was exposed — the middleware 401s first, verified live — but it is the wrong default for the layer whose job is not to trust the one above. 44 plain checks, 12 compound (narrowing preserved), 8 early returns. **The 28 routes with no in-route guard were DELIBERATELY LEFT**: cross-referencing every one against `ROLE_API_PREFIXES`, exactly 3 are reachable by a non-admin (`/api/objectives*`, for `executive`) and that is intended. The invariant that safety rests on a restrictive allowlist — and that `matchesPrefix` is **not method-aware**, so allowlisting a read grants every mutation under it — is now written where it will be read.

Tabs with rows show with their count; the rest wait under More. The tab components are untouched — hiding is reversible. The tab you are standing on always renders, or picking an empty one made it vanish from under you.
- **The weekly brief cron reported failure on every success.** It was the only one of thirteen agents not at exit 0. Most project folders have no subfolders at all (Myton, HAFB, Vallejo, Hafoka, Mira Vista, Camilla); the ones that do use sets specific to that deal — Tooele Steel House has `Business Documents | GET Turkiye Cold Form Steel Acquisition | USACE Fort Johnson Contract 20MM Design Build`, IAN has `Partners & Acquisitions`, West Wendover has `Due diligence`. **A single hard-coded taxonomy would have been wrong for 14 of 15 projects.** Hence hybrid (Richard's pick): classify against the record's OWN folders, and create a standard set only where there are none.

Confirmed the 09-16 finding generalises: on a SHARED drive `drive.file` governs which files the app may touch afterwards, while adding a child is the impersonated user's own right. **`canDelete` is false, so cleanup trashes rather than deletes.** Also verified `ensureFolder`'s find-half returns the right folder on the shared drive, so it will **not** create duplicates there — that had never been exercised, since the steel-quote feature only ever uploaded.
- **⚠ FOLDERS ARE LINKED AT THE BUSINESS-LINE LEVEL, NOT THE PROJECT LEVEL — found by running it, not by reading the schema.** DUBHES points at `Helper - Utah`, whose single child `PQC Giovanni Campus ` is the folder actually holding the taxonomy. Filing against the link as given would have offered "PQC Giovanni Campus" as the one candidate and never reached Deeds or Land Legal at all. New `resolveFilingRoot`: **a folder holding NO files and EXACTLY ONE subfolder is a shelf, not a filing choice** — there is no decision to make there, so step through it (bounded at 3 hops). A folder with files of its own is somewhere people already file, so it stays put however many subfolders it has. Verified against all six linked projects: Helper and Trump City descend correctly, **Stockton (7 loose files plus two subfolders) correctly does not.**
- **⚠ THE LOOP GUARD IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART, and `import.ts` had predicted this exact day in a comment:** *"the day a project's source folder and its published folder are the same one, every published file would return as a duplicate of itself."* Verified against the real skip sets: `published` is built from `drive_published_id NOT NULL **AND drive_file_id IS NULL**`, so stamping only `drive_published_id` would **not** have protected anything. A filed document therefore stamps **all three** — `drive_file_id`, `drive_modified_at`, `drive_published_id` — and the importer finds it in `known` and short-circuits. **The timestamp matters as much as the id**: `driveFileUnchanged(null, …)` is false, so a row filed without it is re-downloaded, re-summarized and re-embedded every night. `uploadToFolder` never requested `modifiedTime`; it does now. **Proven live: `added=0, unchanged=1, updated=0`, one row, stable across repeated imports.**
- **The classifier refuses rather than guesses.** `chooseFolder` accepts a folder name **only if it is verbatim one of the candidates** — no fuzzy matching, no trimming into a match (near-misses in this codebase have historically been trailing-space bugs). Below `FILING_CONFIDENCE = 0.7` it goes to **`_Unsorted`**, because a document misfiled into a folder the team trusts is worse than one waiting to be sorted: nobody goes looking for a file they believe is already filed. A **deterministic filename pass runs first** so routine documents cost no model call at all, and it defers the moment two candidate folders match — ambiguity is the thing the whole module exists to refuse. Measured live against the real PQC taxonomy: broker opinion → `Independent RE Brokers Market Analysis` (0.95), geotech → `Pre Construction` (0.90), `Scan_0043.pdf` → `_Unsorted` (0.10), and an HR handbook correctly refused outright. Model calls are **5–18s**, not the 30–60s feared, because the prompt is small.

Non-documents (`.ics`/`.vcf`, `text/calendar`) are now skipped; the denylist is deliberately narrow, since a `.dwg` is unreadable to the platform and still absolutely a document. (2) **Platform-generated summaries were being filed into folders a human curated** — `Email research — Helper.md` was headed for `Master Proposal - Land Development` at 0.70. They now go to `_Unsorted` whenever the taxonomy is the team's own. **`isStandardSet` compares the folder set by content rather than trusting the `created` flag**, which is true only for the very first document filed and would have made the first generated summary behave differently from every later one.
- **Opportunities could not be linked to a Drive folder at all** — the column existed on projects and steel_deals and was simply missing here, so the M&A deals (exactly where loose documents arrive by email) could not participate. The check now says precisely that and names the restart to try. **Verified by reproducing the real state** — and the first attempt at that test silently passed, because the `set_updated_at` trigger bumps `updated_at` on the very write that un-routes a thread; reproducing it needed `session_replication_role = replica`. **A test that cannot fail is not a test.**

The tempting move is to detect and penalise these "semantic magnets" — either by prose ratio or by distance from the corpus centroid. **Both were wrong, and measuring showed why:** a <0.10 prose filter would have dropped 321 chunks including the platform's own generated investor snapshots and real data tables, and the chunks *closest to the centroid* turned out to be **the executive brief, the capability statement and the credentials section** — the most important company documents in the index, near the centroid precisely because the whole corpus is about Ber Wilson.
